# stage0

---

Good. We will discuss only **Stage 0: Product Portfolio and Business Model**, but define in full the requirements the product layer and service layer must meet in order to realize that business model later; we will not go into code-level questions such as ASP.NET/Aspire, database tables, or RPC interfaces.

Given the architecture you have already settled on, I think the most suitable business model for ArcForges is neither traditional SaaS nor Open Core, but:

# **Open-source Local Software + Paid Managed Cloud + Metered AI**

That is:

> **All local features of the desktop Apps are free, and all the code is open source.**
> **Local Agents, cross-App Agent scheduling, BYOK, and local models are also free.**
> **What ArcForges charges for is the official managed services: sync, cloud storage, cross-device, remote Agents, managed AI credits, background tasks, and, in future, team collaboration.**

This model is highly consistent with your existing architecture: ArcChat is a complete chat product and the local Agent Hub; ArcNotes, ArcSlate, and ArcScope are all independent, autonomous processes that must keep working on their own even if ArcChat or Cloud is absent.

Let me put my conclusion up front:

> **This route is technically feasible and commercially sound.**
>
> And I think it suits ArcForges better than "cripple features in the free version, unlock the advanced ones in Pro".

---

# 1. First divide the ArcForges product layer into 3 layers

The entire product system should be:

```text
                   ArcForges
                       │
        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
        │              │              │
   Local Apps      ArcForges Cloud    Arc AI
       Free           Subscription      Metered / Quota
    Open source         Managed            Optional
        │              │              │
 ArcChat           Sync            Managed AI
 ArcNotes          Storage         Model Routing
 ArcSlate          Remote          Credits
 ArcScope          Backup          Cloud Agent
 ArcCanvas         Web/Mobile      BYOK Cloud
 ArcMusic          Collaboration
```

The single most important principle here is:

## **Software and services are completely separated.**

Users should never end up feeling:

> "After I stop subscribing, ArcSlate can no longer cut videos."

Instead it should be:

> "After I stop subscribing, ArcSlate still works in full; only the official ArcForges cloud sync, cloud storage, and official AI services stop."

This would make ArcForges' open source positioning very clean.

---

# 2. ArcChat's role in the entire product system

ArcChat is no ordinary "chat software."

Eventually it should be:

> **ArcForges Local Agent Center**

For example, locally:

```text
                     ArcChat
                       │
                   Arc Agent
                       │
              Capability Registry
                       │
        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
        │              │              │
     ArcNotes       ArcSlate       ArcScope
        │              │              │
  Knowledge Tools   Video Tools   Telemetry Tools
```

Users can do without ArcChat entirely:

```text
open ArcSlate
Cut video
save
Export
```

No problem.

Also possible:

```text
open ArcScope
Connect devices
Analyze data
Export report
```

Completely independent.

But after ArcChat:

> "Analyze the last hour of ArcScope data."

Agent calls ArcScope.

Then:

> "Compile the exceptions into a complete technical report."

Agent calls ArcNotes.

Then:

> "Cut out the malfunctioning part of the relevant demonstration video."

Agent calls ArcSlate.

Finally:

```text
User
 ↓
ArcChat
 ↓
Agent
 ↓
Multiple majors App
```

I recommend this ability:

# **Free forever.**

Because this is the core ecological growth mechanism of ArcForges.

The more Arc Apps a user installs:

> ArcChat is stronger.

ArcChat is stronger:

> The more willing users are to install other Arc Apps.

So never put:

> "Agent calls other apps"

Put it behind the Pro subscription.

This should become a core free capability of ArcForges.

# 4. How does ArcForges make money?

I think there are four sources of long-term charges.

## ① ArcForges Cloud

This is the most stable subscription revenue.

Includes:

* Cloud Sync
* Cloud Storage
* Version History
* Backup
* Cross-device
* Web Access
* Mobile Access
* Remote Desktop Agent
* Cloud Knowledge Index
* Cross-App Cloud Context
* Cloud Task
* Notification

What users pay is:

> **"I do not want to maintain the server myself."**

This has nothing to do with whether the code is open source or not.

Users can:

```text
git clone ArcForges Server
↓
Deploy yourself
↓
Buy it yourself PostgreSQL
↓
Match it yourself R2/S3
↓
Assign your own domain name
↓
Back up yourself
↓
Update yourself
```

Free.

But the vast majority of users are willing to:

> Pay $5 a month and let ArcForges do it all.

This is a very mature business model.

Joplin also provides open source products, self-hosted solutions and official Joplin Cloud. The current official cloud prices range from €2.99/month Basic to €5.99/month Pro and €9.99/month 100GB; Obsidian's local application is free, while the official Sync is currently $4/month paid annually or $5/month paid monthly; AFFiNE also adopts the route of coexistence of local/FOSS and official managed cloud. ([Joplin][1])

So:

# **Around $5/month is completely based on the market.**

# 6. How much storage should be provided for $5.99 Cloud?

I currently recommend the first version:

# **50 GB Shared Cloud Storage**

Not 50GB per App.

is:

```text
ArcForges Account
       │
       └── 50 GB
            │
    ┌───────┼────────┐
    Notes   Chat    Slate ...
```

One of the reasons is that Cloudflare R2's current Standard pricing is only **$0.015/GB-month** and does not charge public egress bandwidth; it also provides S3-compatible API. Even if 50GB is fully occupied by users, the cost of pure object storage itself is not high. Of course that includes requests, databases, compute, backups and support, so you cannot simply equate the R2 storage price with your full cost. ([Cloudflare Docs][2])

On the existing market:

* Joplin Pro: 30GB, €5.99/month;
* Joplin 100GB: €9.99/month;
* Standard Notes Professional: 100GB, $120/year;
* AFFiNE Pro: 100GB, $6.75/month. ([Joplin][1])

So:

> **$5.99 + 50GB + the entire ArcForges ecosystem**

It's competitive.

---

# 7. But never promise "unlimited storage"

Especially ArcSlate.

A user might:

```text
4K Video
100 GB
500 GB
1 TB
```

If you say:

> ArcForges Cloud $5.99 unlimited storage

Sooner or later the business will explode.

Notesnook itself made it clear when it adjusted prices in 2025 that truly unlimited files/images storage was not sustainable in the long term, so it later changed to a tiered storage solution. ([Notesnook Blog by Streetwriters LLC][3])

So by default ArcSlate should:

```text
Project Metadata      Cloud
Proxy/Thumbnail       Cloud
Small Assets          Cloud
Raw Media             Local by default
```

Users need full cloud media:

> Use additional Storage Packs.

For example later:

```text
+100 GB
+500 GB
+1 TB
```

Charged separately.

# 8. Is R2 the most suitable for ArcForges?

## Normal ArcForges Cloud: I choose R2

For:

* Notes
* Chat
* Documents
* Attachments
* Reports
* Thumbnails
* Project metadata
* Sync objects

I think:

# **Cloudflare R2 is a very suitable first choice right now.**

Reason:

1. S3-compatible;
2. No egress bandwidth fees;
3. $0.015/GB-month;
4. Natural integration with other Cloudflare infrastructure. ([Cloudflare Docs][2])

---

## But in the future, massive video archives will need to be compared again.

For example 1TB pure storage:

The standard storage price of R2 is significantly higher than Backblaze B2's current starting price of about $6.95/TB/month; B2 also provides free egress of about 3 times the average storage volume per month, and charges are based on volume after that. ([Backblaze][4])

So I would reserve:

```text
ArcForges Storage Abstraction

Hot / Sync Data
        ↓
       R2

Large Media Archive
        ↓
R2 / B2 / future provider
```

Stage 0 does not require the decision to only R2 forever.

**Current default: R2.**

# 9. How much does Vector Search cost?

I recommend:

## Local Vector Search

Free forever.

```text
ArcNotes
↓
Local Embedding
↓
Local Vector Index
```

---

## Cloud Vector Search

Contained in:

> ArcForges Cloud

There is no separate charge.

Cloudflare Vectorize is now GA and is billed according to queried/stored vector dimensions; the current paid Workers tier includes a certain amount. In the official example, the estimated cost for 50,000 768-dimensional vectors and 200,000 queries per month is about $1.94/month, and there is no egress fee. ([Cloudflare Docs][5])

So for ordinary personal knowledge bases, it can be completely used as one of the background costs of Cloud Subscription.

Users do not need to see:

```text
Vector Dimensions Balance
```

This is an internal cost.

This is the most critical part of ArcForges.

```text
                 Arc Agent
                    │
      ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
      │             │             │
   Local AI        BYOK       Arc Managed AI
```

## A. Local AI

Free.

For example:

* Ollama
* LM Studio
* Local OpenAI-compatible

ArcForges does not charge a fee.

## B. BYOK

I suggest two categories here.

### Local BYOK

# Free forever.

User fills in:

```text
OpenAI API Key
Anthropic API Key
Gemini API Key
xAI API Key
OpenRouter Key
```

Use ArcChat directly.

User pays model manufacturer.

ArcForges:

> $0.

---

### Cloud BYOK

Here you can charge reasonably.

For example, the user wants to:

```text
mobile phone
 ↓
ArcForges Cloud
 ↓
Cloud Agent
 ↓
User's own Anthropic API Key
 ↓
perform tasks
```

Although you do not bear the Token cost, you do bear:

* Cloud Server
* Agent Orchestration
* Queue
* Remote Session
* Scheduling
* Storage
* Database
* Logging
* Reliability
* Rate Limit
* Security
* Monitoring

So:

> **BYOK users still require ArcForges Cloud $5.99.**

This is very reasonable.

But I suggest:

# No additional commission will be charged for BYOK Token.

That is:

```text
Cloud Subscription
$5.99

+

User's own API cost
```

instead of:

```text
Cloud Subscription
+
User's own API cost
+
ArcForges Collect again 10% Token Fee
```

The user experience will be much better.

OpenRouter itself has proven that BYOK charging platform fees can exist in the market: its current policy is to waive platform fees for the first 1 million BYOK requests per month, and then charge 5% of the cost of the same model/Provider on OpenRouter. ([OpenRouter][6])

But ArcForges does not have to follow suit.

Your profits come from Cloud Subscription.

# 12. What AI backend do I recommend?

I do not recommend:

> All OpenRouters.

It is also not recommended to:

> All Workers AI.

I think the best combination is:

# **Cloudflare AI Gateway serves as the main entrance and control layer**

Below:

```text
                    AI Gateway
                        │
       ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
       │                │                │
   Workers AI       Direct Provider    OpenRouter
       │                │                │
 Cheap/Open        Frontier Models    Long Tail/Fallback
 Embedding         OpenAI             New Models
 Whisper           Anthropic
 Small LLM         Gemini
                   xAI
```

The current core functions of Cloudflare AI Gateway include analytics, cache, and rate limiting, and the core functions are currently free; it supports providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, DeepSeek, Workers AI, and OpenRouter. ([Cloudflare Docs][7])

This is perfect for ArcForges.

---

## Where are Workers AI used?

I recommend using:

* Embedding
* Reranker
* Whisper/STT
* Small model
* Quick classification
* Summarization
* Low-cost Agent subtasks

The current price of Workers AI is very low, for example, some embedding models are about $0.012/M input tokens, and Whisper is about $0.0005/audio minute; LLM is also priced separately by model. ([Cloudflare Docs][8])

Great for a lot of background "small tasks".

But do not lock ArcForges into Workers AI.

Models are updated and retired.

---

## Frontier Models

For example:

* GPT
* Claude
* Gemini
* Grok

Priority:

> Direct Provider Account

Via AI Gateway.

This way you control:

* Provider
* Cost
* Rate Limit
* Routing

---

## OpenRouter

I positioned it as:

> **Fallback + Long-tail Model Provider**

Because it's great for supporting large numbers of models quickly.

But if all ArcForges Managed AI goes through OpenRouter, you will naturally bear platform fees: OpenRouter currently has a 5.5% fee for purchasing credits; BYOK also has a 5% platform fee for exceeding the free request limit. ([OpenRouter][9])

Cloudflare Unified Billing itself also charges a 5% fee for purchased third-party AI credits. ([Cloudflare Docs][10])

So the long-term business optimal is generally:

```text
High traffic mainstream model
→ Direct Provider

low cost model
→ Workers AI

new model / niche model / Fallback
→ OpenRouter
```

Then all:

> AI Gateway unified observation.

This is by far my most recommended combination.

# My final stage 0 advice

I will officially make it:

> **ArcForges is a completely open source, local-first AI-native professional desktop software ecosystem.**
>
> **All local products and local Agent capabilities are free forever.**
>
> **ArcChat is a free Local Agent Hub with capabilities provided by individual Arc Apps.**
>
> **Commercial revenue comes from official ArcForges Cloud, managed AI, storage expansion and future team services.**
>
> **BYOK Local is permanently free; Cloud BYOK is included in Cloud subscription, and no additional Token commission is charged.**
>
> **Managed AI uses a quota system and never promises Unlimited.**
>
> **Cloudflare R2 as default plain object storage; large-scale video media will allow separate storage tiers in the future.**
>
> **Cloudflare AI Gateway serves as the AI control plane; Workers AI performs low-cost tasks; the mainstream Frontier Model is directly connected to the Provider as much as possible; OpenRouter is used for long-tail models and fallbacks.**
>
> **In the first phase, only one `ArcForges Cloud ≈ $5.99/month` Family Bucket cloud service will be sold, so there is no rush to unsubscribe via the App.**

I think this is currently the option that **best balances all four concerns: technology cost, open-source philosophy, user appeal, and long-term commercial sustainability**.

When the next stage enters **Stage 1: ArcForges Account / Identity**, you can fully define on this business model: **User, anonymous local user, account, device, Session, Cloud Account, Organization, Subscription, AI Wallet, Storage Quota, BYOK Key, cross-device login, and the complete product process of "can be used without logging in" and "cloud service after logging in"**.

# stage1

---

Okay, now consider **Stage 1: ArcForges Account / Identity / Device / Session / Workspace** as a **complete product requirements** that can truly guide all subsequent clients, Cloud, Billing, AI, Sync, and Remote Agent.

This stage is very critical, because if the Account model is only based on "email + password + user table" at the beginning, then add:

* Multiple Apps
* Multiple devices
* Self-host
* Team
* Cloud Sync
* BYOK
* Managed AI
* Remote Agent
* App Store / Google Play
* Billing
* API
* Organization

There will almost certainly be rework.

Your existing architecture has been clarified: **The authoritative source of cloud accounts, organizations, and devices is ArcForges Cloud, and each desktop App is independent and available offline; mobile/Web passes the Cloud, and remote desktop capabilities must also be authorized by the device. **So Account cannot just "log in to the system", but should be the **basic layer of identity and ownership** for the entire ArcForges Cloud.

---

# Stage 1 Final Core Conclusions

Let me first directly give you the solution that I think is most suitable for ArcForges:

> **ArcForges local software does not require an account.**
>
> **ArcForges Account only appears when users require official Cloud, Managed AI, Cloud BYOK, Sync, Remote, Web/Mobile and other services.**
>
> **The official ArcForges Account uses the first-party identity system and does not regard third-party accounts such as Google, Apple, and GitHub as the core of the identity.**
>
> **Suggested login method for the first moderator: Email + Passkey.**
>
> Email OTP is responsible for first-time verification and recovery, and Passkey is responsible for daily login.
>
> **The first version does not even require Google Login.**
>
> Self-host completely owns its own user system and does not rely on arcforges.com.
>
> Differentiate from day one:
>
> **User ≠ Workspace ≠ Device ≠ Session ≠ Subscription ≠ Entitlement.**

This last one is the most important.

---

```text
           │     ├── Email

Workspace
```

All official ArcForges products use the same Account.

---

## An account should not be a prerequisite for launching a local app

Opening ArcNotes for the first time:

```text
Open ArcNotes
     ↓
Create notes directly
```

Opening ArcSlate for the first time:

```text
Open ArcSlate
     ↓
Cut video directly
```

Open ArcScope for the first time:

```text
Open ArcScope
     ↓
Connect devices
```

All should not appear:

> Sign in to continue

This is a product principle that I believe must be adhered to.

Because your core commitment is:

> **Local software is free and fully functional.**

Only if the user clicks:

* Enable Sync
* Backup to Cloud
* Use Arc AI
* Remote Access
* Continue on Mobile
* Continue on Web

Only then appeared:

> Sign in to ArcForges

Apple itself has long emphasized that apps without obvious account-based functions should not force users to register without reason; and your local functions clearly do not rely on accounts, so this design not only provides a better experience, but is also more consistent with the entire product logic.

---

# 3. "Local user" should not pretend to be a cloud Guest Account

This is an easy mistake to make.

Do not secretly create it when the user first starts:

```text
Anonymous Cloud User
```

Also do not:

```text
Guest Account
```

The correct way should be:

```text
Local Profile
```

It's just:

> The local application identity on the current device/OS user.

Does not exist on the server.

For example:

```text
Local Profile
├── Local Settings
├── Local Documents
├── Local Agent History
├── Local BYOK
└── Local Vector Index
```

When the user later logs into ArcForges:

```text
Local Profile
      +
ArcForges Account
```

The two are related.

But:

> Logging in does not mean uploading.

For example, the user locally has:

```text
2000 Notes
300 GB Video
```

After logging in, you cannot suddenly:

> Synchronizing 300 GB...

The user must be given an explicit choice:

```text
Enable Sync for ArcNotes?
Yes / Later

Upload ArcSlate media?
Metadata only / Selected media / Never
```

This is a very important product principle.

---

# 4. Workspace must exist from the first day

Even if you only have individual users for the first year, I recommend:

> **All cloud data belongs to Workspace, not directly to User.**

After user registration, you will automatically receive:

# Personal Workspace

For example:

```text
Ryan's Workspace
```

Inside:

```text
Chat
Notes
Storage
Knowledge
AI
Sync
```

So:

```text
User
  ↓ owns
Personal Workspace
```

The team will come out later:

```text
User
 ├── Ryan Personal
 ├── ArcForges Team
 └── QmlSharp Team
```

No need to change the data model.

---

## Workspace is the true cloud boundary

Future:

```text
Personal Workspace
├── 50 GB Storage
├── 500 AI Credits
└── Personal Data

ArcForges Organization
├── 1 TB Storage
├── 10000 AI Credits
├── 10 Members
└── Shared Data
```

It's very natural.

---

# 5. Account, Workspace, and Billing must be completely separated

Very important.

Do not design:

```text
User.SubscriptionId
```

The correct logic should be:

```text
User
  │
  └── Workspace

Billing Account
      │
      └── Subscription
             │
             └── Entitlement
                    │
                    ▼
                Workspace
```

Reason:

Today:

> Ryan buys himself Cloud.

Tomorrow:

> ArcForges pays 30 employees.

The day after tomorrow:

> Users belong to three Organizations.

If Subscription is always bound to User:

Get messed up immediately.

---

# 6. Login method: I recommend that the first version be very restrained

I think the best combination is:

# Email + Passkey

instead of:

```text
Email
Password
Google
Apple
GitHub
Microsoft
Discord
WeChat
...
```

There is no point in having 8 logins in the first place.

---

# 7. Passkey should become the main login method for ArcForges

This direction is mature enough in 2026.

FIDO's definition of passkey is password replacement technology: it uses public and private keys instead of shared passwords, has phishing-resistant characteristics, and can be synchronized between devices, or it can be a device-bound credential. ([FIDO Alliance][1])

So ArcForges can design:

First time registration:

```text
Enter Email
    ↓
Email Verification Code
    ↓
Account Created
    ↓
Create a Passkey?
    ↓
Yes
```

Later:

```text
Sign in
  ↓
Use Passkey
```

The user experience is:

> Windows Hello
> Touch ID
> Face ID
> Confirm via mobile phone
> PIN

Instead of remembering the ArcForges password.

---

# 8. What role should email play?

Email should be responsible for:

### Account Discovery

Tell ArcForges:

> Who am I.

### Initial Verification

First registration verification.

### Recovery

Recover when all Passkeys are lost.

### Security Notification

For example:

* New device login
* Email changed
* Passkey added
* Recovery initiated
* Device revoked

---

## I recommend using Email Code instead of relying heavily on Magic Link

For example:

```text
Verification Code

384921
```

Because ArcForges is:

* Windows
* macOS
* Linux
* Mobile
* Web

Magic Link often encounters:

> Click the link to open the default browser
> But I am logged in to ArcNotes Desktop

Also deal with deep links.

Verification codes are the most common.

Later, it can be provided at the same time:

> Click to verify

as a convenience feature.

But it cannot be relied upon.

---

# 9. I recommend that the first version does not even require a password.

Official ArcForges Cloud:

```text
Email OTP
+
Passkey
```

enough.

This does not:

* Forgot Password
* Password Reset
* Password Breach
* Credential Stuffing

This whole set of questions.

Passkey itself has no shared password secret held by the server, and FIDO explicitly emphasizes its advantages in resisting phishing and avoiding password database breaches. ([FIDO Alliance][1])

---

## But Self-host should retain other login capabilities

Official Cloud can:

```text
Passkey
Email OTP
```

Self-host:

```text
Local Password
Passkey
OIDC
Enterprise Provider
```

Because some companies:

> Public email is not allowed.

Or:

> Already have Keycloak/Entra/Okta.

So do not let the identity domain assume:

> Email OTP is required for everyone.

Authentication Provider should be an extensible concept.

---

# 10. Does the first version support Google/Apple Login?

My suggestion:

# No rush.

V1:

```text
Continue with Email
Continue with Passkey
```

That's enough.

The main reason is not technology.

Instead:

### 1. Chinese users will not rely on Google

Email + Passkey is more globally neutral.

### 2. Avoid the complexity of account merging

For example:

```text
a@gmail.com
Google Login

a@privaterelay.appleid.com
Apple Login

a@gmail.com
Email Login
```

It may become three Accounts.

### 3. App Store Rules

Apple's current 4.8 stipulates that if an app uses a third-party/social login such as Google, Facebook, or ([Apple Developer][2])

So:

```text
First-party Email
+
Passkey
```

It's a very clean starting point.

In the future, if user data indicates:

> Google Login conversion is significantly higher

Add together:

```text
Apple
Google
```

---

# 11. Authentication Identity must be separated from User

This must be decided from the first day.

Do not:

```text
User.Email = Identity
```

Instead:

```text
User
├── Identity: Email
├── Identity: Passkey #1
├── Identity: Passkey #2
├── Identity: Apple
└── Identity: Google
```

The same person can:

```text
3 Passkeys
1 Email
1 Apple
1 Google
```

But only:

```text
1 User
```

After this:

> Add login method
> Remove login method
> Change email
> Add Apple
> Add Google

The user's identity will not be changed.

---

# 12. Passkey must allow multiple

For example:

```text
Ryan's Account

Passkeys
├── Windows Hello
├── iPhone
├── MacBook
└── YubiKey
```

Users can:

* Rename
* View created time
* View last used
* Remove

Never assume that:

> An Account = a Passkey.

---

# 13. Recovery must be designed from the first version

Passkey is safe.

But users may:

> Lost mobile phone
> The computer is broken
> Apple Account lost

So there must be Recovery.

I recommend:

```text
Primary Recovery
Email

Secondary
Recovery Codes
```

Users can generate:

```text
10 one-time Recovery Codes
```

Then clearly prompt:

> Store these somewhere safe.

---

## Do not do Security Questions

For example:

> What was the name of your primary school?

Not required at all.

---

# 14. High-risk operations require Step-up Authentication

Even if the user is already logged in:

The following actions should also reauthenticate:

* Change Email
* Remove all Passkeys
* Generate Recovery Codes
* Delete Account
* Add Cloud BYOK
* Reveal/replace sensitive secret
* Enable Remote Agent
* Revoke trusted devices
* Create high-privilege API Token
* Transfer Organization ownership

Process:

```text
Normal Session
      ↓
Sensitive Action
      ↓
Passkey / Fresh OTP
      ↓
Continue
```

This is called Step-up.

A lot of safety rework can be avoided later.

---

# 15. Device and Session must not be confused

ArcForges specifically requires the Device model.

Because you have:

```text
Remote Agent
Mobile
Desktop
Multiple Apps
```

Suggested concepts:

# Device

A long-lived trusted installation environment.

For example:

```text
Ryan's Desktop
Windows
Taipei

Ryan's MacBook

Ryan's iPhone
```

Device has:

* Name
* Platform
* Created
* Last Seen
* Trust Status
* Remote Enabled
* Revoke

---

# Session

Session is:

> The current login status of an app.

For example:

```text
Device
 Ryan Desktop

Sessions
 ├── ArcChat
 ├── ArcNotes
 ├── ArcScope
 └── Browser
```

Sessions can expire.

Device still exists.

---

# 16. We also need an App Installation concept

This is unique to ArcForges.

Suggested model:

```text
Device
  │
  ├── ArcChat Installation
  ├── ArcNotes Installation
  ├── ArcSlate Installation
  └── ArcScope Installation
```

Then:

```text
Runtime Instance
```

Just start it once:

```text
ArcScope.exe PID 1234
```

`AppId / InstanceId` in your existing architecture is a runtime local routing identity, while Cloud also needs a long-lived Device/App Installation dimension; you cannot treat a process instance as a device identity.

Final relationship:

```text
User
 ↓
Device
 ↓
App Installation
 ↓
Runtime Instance
```

This will be particularly important as a Remote Agent in the future.

---

# 17. Device should not be strongly bound by "hardware fingerprint"

Do not rely on:

* CPU Serial
* Motherboard ID
* MAC Address

to identify the device.

Because:

* VM
* Reinstall the system
* Hardware replacement
* Privacy

Everything will go wrong.

Product logic should be:

> User authorization generates a Device Identity.

The device can:

```text
Rename
Revoke
Re-register
```

---

# 18. Arc Apps on the same device should have a unified login experience

User logs into ArcChat for the first time:

```text
ArcChat
Sign in
```

Then open ArcNotes:

The ideal experience should be:

> Continue as Ryan?

instead of:

> Enter Email again.

That is:

# ArcForges Device SSO

But there is a principle:

> ArcNotes cannot rely on ArcChat to log in.

Because you have determined that each product operates independently.

So what should be achieved is product experience:

```text
ArcChat absent
    ↓
ArcNotes still signs in

ArcChat present
    ↓
Reuse existing trusted account
```

rather than architecture dependency.

---

# 19. Logout must distinguish four actions

It cannot just be:

> Log out

It is necessary to distinguish:

### Sign out of this App

```text
ArcNotes logout
```

ArcChat is still logged in.

---

### Sign out of this Device

All Arc Apps:

```text
Cloud sessions revoked
```

Local data is retained.

---

### Revoke Device

From another device:

```text
Ryan Desktop
Revoke
```

Stop:

* Sync
* Remote
* Cloud Access

---

### Sign out everywhere

Clear all sessions.

But the Account still exists.

---

# 20. Local data must not be deleted after logging out.

This is very important.

For example:

```text
ArcNotes
5000 local notes

Sign out
```

The result should be:

```text
Local notes remain
Cloud sync stops
```

instead of:

> Data removed.

ArcForges is Local-first software.

---

# 21. Remote Agent must be based on Device Trust

Future:

```text
iPhone
  ↓
ArcForges Cloud
  ↓
Ryan Desktop
  ↓
ArcChat
  ↓
ArcScope
```

Must meet:

```text
Account
   ↓
Trusted Device
   ↓
Remote Enabled
   ↓
Allowed Capabilities
```

Default:

# Remote = Off

User clear:

> Enable Remote Access on this PC

Then you can:

```text
Allow:
[x] ArcNotes
[x] ArcScope
[ ] ArcSlate Export
```

High-risk capabilities can still:

> Require local confirmation.

Your existing architecture has also made it clear that the remote bridging of desktop ArcChat should actively have the desktop actively establish a public internet connection and undergo user-visible device authorization, approval and revocation, so Device Trust must be modeled in the Account stage.

---

# 22. Workspace Context is extremely important to Agent

Future users:

```text
Personal Workspace

ArcForges Company Workspace
```

Users said about ArcChat:

> Summarize recent projects.

Agent must know:

```text
Context = Personal
```

Or:

```text
Context = ArcForges Organization
```

Data must not be automatically searched across Workspaces.

Therefore:

```text
Agent Session
   ↓
Active Workspace
```

It should be a strong border.

Cross-workspace operations must be explicit.

---

# 23. Organization is reserved from the first day, but V1 does not need to be opened.

Model:

```text
Organization
├── Owner
├── Admin
├── Member
└── Guest
```

Future:

* Shared Notes
* Shared AI
* Shared Storage
* Shared Agent
* Shared ArcScope reports

All under Organization Workspace.

---

## User exits the company

Should:

```text
Remove Membership
```

instead of:

```text
Delete User
```

Personal Workspace is not affected at all.

---

# 24. Organization Owner delete account

You must first:

> Transfer Ownership

Or:

> Delete Organization

It cannot be deleted directly.

This should be considered from the Account deletion stage.

---

# 25. Billing identity cannot be matched by email

Very important.

Later Lemon Squeezy:

```text
Payment email
```

May be:

```text
finance@company.com
```

Login:

```text
ryan@gmail.com
```

Never:

```text
payment.email == user.email
```

to determine who the subscription belongs to.

Must:

```text
Purchase
 ↓
Billing Account
 ↓
Workspace
```

Email is just a contact method.

So the user later modifies the Email:

> Subscriptions will not be lost.

---

# 26. Cloud BYOK Secret does not belong to Identity

BYOK should belong to:

```text
Local BYOK
→ Device

Cloud BYOK
→ Workspace Secret Vault
```

instead of:

```text
User.Profile.ApiKey
```

In this way, Organization can:

```text
Anthropic Organization Key
```

Shared by the entire Team.

and:

> Personal BYOK does not leak to the Organization.

---

# 27. Official Cloud and Self-host must be different Realm

This is another very important design.

Do not assume:

> ArcForges Account IDs are unique worldwide and apply to all servers.

should be:

```text
Realm
   +
UserId
```

For example:

```text
Official Cloud
user: 123

https://cloud.company-a.com
user: 123
```

These are two different identities.

---

## Self-host does not require an official ArcForges Account

Users can:

```text
Download ArcForges Server
 ↓
Deploy
 ↓
Create Local Account
```

No access at all:

```text
arcforges.com
```

This is how open source self-hosting should behave.

---

## App should support Server Profiles

Future:

```text
Cloud Accounts

ArcForges Cloud
Ryan

My Home Server
Ryan

Company Server
ryan@company
```

These may be different identities.

V1 UI can only support:

> One Official Cloud + One Self-host

But the underlying concept must support multiple Realms.

---

# 28. Do not automatically Federation

In the future, we can support:

```text
Self-host
Sign in with ArcForges
```

But only optional OIDC Federation.

Self-host cannot be made to rely on official ArcForges.

Otherwise:

> The official Cloud is down, and self-hosting cannot be logged in.

It goes against the logic of self-hosting.

---

# 29. Be cautious when merging accounts

In the future, users may generate two Accounts:

```text
Account A
email@example.com

Account B
Sign in with Apple
```

You cannot see that the emails will be merged automatically.

Correct way:

> User login A
> Clear Link Identity

Or:

> Merge Accounts

The identities of both parties need to be re-verified.

---

## Merge should not simply merge everything

should be handled separately:

```text
Identity
Personal Workspace
Subscription
AI Credits
Organization Membership
Devices
```

So I suggest:

> V1 does not need to provide full Account Merge.

But the data model must allow for future implementation.

---

# 30. Account Profile should be as few as possible

ArcForges is not a social network.

Account Profile only requires:

* Display Name
* Avatar
* Primary Email
* Locale
* Timezone

Not required:

* Username
* Real Name
* Phone
* Birthday
* Gender
* Address

Billing Address is handled by the payment process.

User Profile should not be placed.

---

# 31. Do not use global Username

There is no need to do:

```text
@ryan123
```

Unless ArcForges has a public community in the future.

Otherwise it will bring:

* Name squatting
* Rename
* Trademark
* Abuse

Purely extra complexity.

---

# 32. Phone/SMS is completely unnecessary in the first stage.

I do not recommend that the first version of ArcForges Account requires a mobile phone number.

Reason:

* Global SMS costs
* Country differences
* SIM Swap
* China/overseas number
* The user is unwilling to provide

Email + Passkey is enough.

---

# 33. Users must have a Security page

ArcForges Account Portal should at least have:

```text
Security

Email

Passkeys
├── Windows
├── iPhone
└── YubiKey

Recovery Codes

Devices

Active Sessions

API Tokens

Security Activity
```

---

# 34. Security Activity Users must be able to see

For example:

```text
Jul 20
New device signed in
Windows · Taipei

Jul 18
Passkey added
iPhone

Jul 12
Cloud BYOK changed

Jul 10
Remote access enabled
Ryan Desktop
```

In particular, ArcForges has Remote Agent.

This is very important.

---

# 35. Important security notices cannot be opt-out.

For example:

* New login
* Email changed
* Passkey removed
* Recovery used
* Remote access enabled
* Account deletion requested

Should always be informed.

Marketing Email:

Must be individually Opt-in/Opt-out.

Cannot be mixed together.

---

# 36. Account status must be richer than Active / Deleted

At least conceptually it requires:

```text
Pending
Active
Restricted
Suspended
DeletionPending
Deleted
```

For example:

### Restricted

AI abuse.

Cloud AI disabled.

But users can still log in to export data.

### Suspended

Serious violation.

Official Cloud discontinued.

But:

> Local ArcNotes / ArcSlate should not be locked remotely.

This is consistent with your business model.

---

# 37. Account deletion must be completely designed from the first day

Because after MAUI is launched in the future, Apple requires that apps that support account creation must allow users to initiate deletion within the app; Google Play also requires an in-app deletion entrance, and also requires an external web deletion entrance. ([Apple Developer][3])

So ArcForges must have:

```text
App
Settings
Account
Delete Account
```

and:

```text
arcforges.com/account/delete
```

---

## The deletion process should be

```text
Request Account Deletion
        ↓
Step-up Authentication
        ↓
Explain Consequences
        ↓
Export Data option
        ↓
Confirm
        ↓
Deletion Pending
```

Then:

* Disable new Cloud writes
* Cancel/stop renewal according to billing rules
* Revoke Sessions
* Revoke Devices
* Revoke API Tokens
* Revoke Remote Access
* Delete Workspace Data
* Delete Vector Index
* Delete Cloud BYOK
* Delete resources
* Process accounting records that are legally required to be retained

Apple clearly requires deletion of the account itself and associated data that does not need to be retained according to law; Google also requires that account deletion cannot just "freeze the account." ([Apple Developer][3])

---

# 38. Local data does not belong to "account deletion"

For example:

User deletes ArcForges Account.

On the computer:

```text
~/Documents/ArcNotes
```

It should not be deleted automatically.

Should:

```text
Official Cloud Account deleted

Local files remain
```

Unless the user explicitly:

> Delete local data too.

This is the key to being Local-first.

---

# 39. Subscription cancellation ≠ Account deletion

It must be distinguished:

```text
Cancel Subscription
```

Just:

> Cloud Entitlement drops after expiration.

And:

```text
Delete Account
```

It is:

> Delete Cloud Identity/Data.

The two processes cannot be mixed.

---

# 40. API Token reserved from the first day

In the future ArcForges is likely to have:

```text
CLI
Automation
Third-party Agent
Integrations
API
```

Therefore Account should be reserved:

# Personal Access Token

But Token must:

* Named
* Scoped
* Expirable
* Revocable
* Last Used visible

For example:

```text
GitHub Integration
scope:
notes.read
notes.write

Expires:
90 days
```

Cannot do:

```text
permanent Master API Key
```

---

# 41. Do not mix Human User and Machine Actor

Future:

```text
Human
Ryan

Agent
ArcChat Agent

Service Account
CI Bot
```

operations may occur.

The audit record should be:

```text
Actor
├── User
├── Agent
├── Device
└── ServiceAccount
```

This way you will not find out later:

> All action logs show Ryan.

---

# 42. Complete scope of the first version of Account UI

I think there should be at least:

## Account

```text
Profile
Email
Locale
Timezone
```

## Security

```text
Passkeys
Recovery Codes
Sessions
Devices
Security Activity
```

```text
Storage

```

```text
Sync
Devices

```

## Billing

Discussed at a later stage:

```text
Plan

AI Credits
```

## Data

```text
Export

```

# 43. The Account UI in Arc App should remain lightweight

Do not implement the complete Account Portal in every App.

In ArcNotes:

```text
Account
Ryan
ArcForges Cloud

Storage 12 / 50 GB

Manage Account →
```

Points:

> Manage Account

Open the Unified Account Portal.

All complications like this:

* Passkeys
* Billing
* Devices
* Recovery
* Delete

Centralized management.

---

# 44. Account Portal is the formal product component of Stage 1

So the entirety of ArcForges actually already has:

```text
Desktop Apps

ArcForges Cloud

ArcForges Account Portal
```

Portal is not just an official website page.

It is an official product.

Future:

```text
account.arcforges.com
```

Or:

```text
arcforges.com/account
```

I prefer the latter, the brand is more unified.

---

# 45. The final login experience of ArcForges Account that I recommend

## new user

```text
Open ArcNotes
    ↓
Use locally
    ↓
Enable Sync
    ↓
Enter Email
    ↓
Enter Verification Code
    ↓
Create ArcForges Account
    ↓
Create Passkey
    ↓
Personal Workspace created
    ↓
Choose what to sync
```

---

## New equipment for old users

```text
Install ArcChat
    ↓
Sign in with Passkey
    ↓
Device registered
    ↓
Personal Workspace available
    ↓
Choose Cloud data to download
```

## No Passkey

```text
Use another method
    ↓
Email Code
```

Then prompt:

---

# 46. I suggest that Stage 1 directly determine the product principle.

### 1

**No account required for local use.**

### 2

**ArcForges Account is a unified account for all products.**

### 3

**User and Workspace are separated.**

### 4

**Workspace is the boundary where data, quota, AI, and entitlement belong.**

### 5

**Billing Account is separated from User.**

### 6

**Device and Session are separated.**

### 7

**Device is separated from Runtime Instance.**

### 8

**Email + Passkey is the official Cloud primary identity method.**

### 9

**V1 does not need to be Password.**

### 10

**V1 does not have to do Google/Apple Social Login.**

### 11

**Self-host Identity is completely independent of Official Cloud.**

### 12

**Local data never silently uploads after login.**

### 13

**Sign out never deletes local data.**

### 14

**Subscription expiration never disables local App functionality.**

### 15

**Remote Agent is turned off by default and bound to Trusted Device.**

### 16

**Agents and data always have a clear Workspace Context.**

### 17

**Account deletion, Subscription cancellation, and Workspace deletion are three different operations.**

---

```text
│   ├── Recovery

│
├── Workspace
│   ├── Personal
│   └── Organization
│
├── Device
│   └── App Installation
│       └── Runtime Instance
│
├── Session
│
├── Trusted Device
│
├── Remote Access Grant
│
├── API Token
│
├── Actor
│
├── Billing Account
│
├── Subscription
│
├── Entitlement
│
├── Storage Quota
│
├── AI Wallet
│
└── Secret Vault
```

Pay attention to what follows here:

```text
Billing Account
Subscription
Entitlement
Storage Quota
AI Wallet
```

For now we are only **settling the identity ownership relationships**; the concrete business rules are left to the later Billing stage.

---

# my final judgment

The most important architectural decision in Stage 1 is not "what does the login page look like" but:

> **ArcForges Account is only responsible for "who you are".**
>
> **Workspace is responsible for "whose data belongs to".**
>
> **Device is responsible for "which device can represent you".**
>
> **Session is responsible for "where are you logged in now".**
>
> **Entitlement is responsible for "what official services you can use now".**
>
> **Billing is responsible for "who pays for these services."**

Completely separate these six things. From **Individual User → Family Bucket → Mobile/Web → Remote Agent → Team → Enterprise → Self-host**, there is basically no need to overturn the Account basic model.

And I will clearly choose **Email OTP + Passkey, no forced account, no forced password, V1 does not do Social Login, official Cloud and Self-host Realm separation** as the official direction of ArcForges Stage 1. This is the solution that I think has the lowest long-term rework risk under your product route.

# stage2

---

OK, now we have officially decided on **Stage 2: ArcForges official website, product portal and Account Portal**.

This stage is not about "making an official website", but about defining the **only official entrance system** for ArcForges to the outside world. In the future, downloads, product introductions, open source, accounts, Cloud, AI, subscriptions, documents, support, status, and account deletion will all be hung on this layer. If you just build a Landing Page now, it will be dismantled later.

The boundaries of your existing products are already very clear: each desktop product runs independently and completely, ArcChat is the local Agent/Hub, the Cloud is responsible for accounts, devices, synchronization, AI and remote capabilities; the Web only connects to the Cloud. This premise determines that the official website and Account Portal cannot become "another ArcChat/ArcNotes in the browser", but should focus on **product discovery + download + cloud management**.

# 26. There are several pitfalls that must be avoided from the beginning when visiting mainland China.

Do not rely heavily on the official website:

* Google Fonts
* Google Analytics
* reCAPTCHA
* Google-hosted JS
* Facebook Pixel

Fonts and core static resources are hosted by yourself.

Cloudflare Turnstile can be used first to prevent form bots; its working mode is that the browser generates a challenge token and the server verifies it again. ([Cloudflare Docs][5])

But one thing needs to be clear:

> **Using the ordinary Cloudflare global network does not mean having a local CDN in mainland China.**

Cloudflare officials made it clear that the cross-border network in mainland China may have higher latency and reliability issues; its mainland China network is an independent subscription of Enterprise, and deploying domain names in mainland China also involves ICP. ([Cloudflare Docs][6])

So the reasonable route for the first stage is:

> Global Cloudflare + Chinese website + no reliance on blocked third-party resources.

First, make sure that mainland users can "use it normally."

In the future, the number of users in China will be really huge. Let us discuss this separately:

> Mainland China node/ICP/independent regional deployment.

Do not be upfront about the enormous complexity of Enterprise China Network now.

# 27. Official website performance requirements should become formal product requirements

Marketing official websites should not require users to download several MB of WebAssembly before seeing Hero.

Regardless of what C# web technology you end up using, the product requirements should be:

> **The public marketing page must be fast and indexable above the fold, and the content can be rendered normally even when JS/WASM is not fully started.**

Core Web Vitals can be targeted directly:

* LCP ≤ 2.5 seconds
* INP ≤ 200ms
* CLS ≤ 0.1

Aim to reach at least 75% of user visits. ([web.dev][7])

Account Portal can be more application-oriented.

The official website does not work.

# Stage 2 I recommend formalizing the decision

Final web product layout:

```text
arcforges.com
Marketing + Products + Pricing + Download
Open Source + Changelog + Support + Security

account.arcforges.com
Account + Workspace + Cloud + AI
Storage + Devices + Remote + Billing + Data

docs.arcforges.com
Product Docs + Self-host + Developer Docs

status.arcforges.com
Independent Cloud Status

api.arcforges.com
Reserved Cloud API
```

Core principles:

> **The official website is responsible for discovery and downloading.**

> **Account Portal is responsible for managing the Cloud and is not responsible for editing user content.**

> **ArcChat Mobile is responsible for chat, remote agent and desktop task progress, not Account Portal.**

> **Downloading never requires an account.**

> **All products have unified but independent product pages.**

> **The official website clearly explains Free Local and Paid Managed Cloud from the first day.**

> **Open source and Self-host are first-class citizens, but the official Cloud is the default convenience option.**

> **Status is independently hosted.**

> **Chinese users do not rely on blocked resources such as Google; mainland China's dedicated infrastructure will be determined based on the actual number of users in the future.**

> **Account, security, account deletion, billing and other high-privilege functions are all centralized in Account Portal.**

In this way, when Stage 3 starts to discuss **Payment/Subscription/Lemon Squeezy/Paddle/Stripe/China User Payment/Merchant of Record/Refund/Tax/Webhook/Checkout**, you can directly connect to the complete path of `Pricing → Checkout → Account Portal → Entitlement` that has been determined without having to re-change the website structure.

# stage3

---

OK, Stage 3 can now be officially settled on **Waffo Pancake as the main Billing Provider**.

We are not discussing how to write specific C# classes here, but we are settling in one pass **the complete set of requirements that the later code, backend, website, Account Portal, Cloud, AI, and finance operations must implement**. The goal is that switching payment platforms, adding Teams, adding Storage, or adding Apple/Google Billing later never forces a rewrite.

---

# Stage 3: Billing/Payment/Subscription/Entitlement

## Final technical and commercial positioning

ArcForges' commercial relationships are formally defined as:

```text
ArcForges
│
├─ Local Software
│    $0
│    Free forever
│
├─ ArcForges Cloud
│    monthly payment / Annual payment
│
├─ ArcForges Cloud Pass
│    One-time fixed term purchase
│
├─ Arc AI Credits
│    One-time recharge
│
└─ Future
     Storage Add-ons
     Team
```

Payment layer:

```text
ArcForges
    ↓
Billing Domain
    ↓
Waffo Pancake Provider
    ↓
Waffo Checkout / MoR
```

instead of:

```text
ArcForges User
    ↓
directly equal to Waffo Customer
```

This layer of isolation is very important.

---

# 1. Officially choose Waffo Pancake, but not make Waffo the business database of ArcForges

## Waffo Responsibilities

Waffo Pancake is the Merchant of Record.

The legal contract subject is currently **Waffo.com Limited** registered in Hong Kong. As a seller to the end consumer, Waffo can be responsible for payment processing, billing, invoicing, VAT/GST/Sales Tax, refund payment process, chargebacks, and payment-related customer support. Developers are still responsible for product quality, delivery, product support, their own income/corporate taxes, local operations and reporting, etc. ([Waffo Pancake][1])

Therefore:

### Waffo is the authoritative source for this stuff

* Was payment actually made?
* Actual payment amount
* Payment currency
* Amount of tax
* Payment status
* Waffo Subscription Status
* Refund
* Chargeback
* Invoice
* End customer payment method

### ArcForges is the authoritative source for this stuff

* Who is the user?
* Whose Workspace is it?
* Is ArcForges Cloud available?
* Cloud expiration time
* Storage Quota
* AI Allowance
* Purchased AI Credits
* Remote Agent permissions
* BYOK Cloud permissions
* Team Entitlement
* User product status

So it can never occur:

> `Waffo subscription == active → the client directly considers Pro`

Must:

```text
Waffo
 ↓
ArcForges Billing
 ↓
Entitlement
 ↓
client
```

a.

Therefore, WeChat Pay's rates have entered the formal fee system. ([Waffo Pancake][4])

# 5. A Waffo document inconsistency problem was discovered here, and the system must defend against it.

This is worth noting.

As of now:

**WeChat Pay is already listed in the Fee Schedule. ** ([Waffo Pancake][4])

But Waffo's `Supported Countries` page still only puts:

* Visa/Mastercard
* Apple Pay
* Google Pay

Listed as current buyer payment methods. ([Waffo Pancake][5])

And Waffo's own SaaS guide on June 14 even stated that Pancake "does not support WeChat payment" at that time. ([Waffo Pancake][6])

This does not contradict the July 2nd update you posted - **apparently the product is live and some of the older documentation has not yet been synced.**

But it reveals a characteristic of Waffo, which is still a young product:

> There may be short-term version differences between documentation and actual capabilities.

So ArcForges adds one from day one:

# `BillingProviderCapabilities`

concept.

For example:

```text
SupportsRecurring
SupportsOneTime
SupportsWechatOneTime
SupportsDynamicPricing
SupportsPlanSwitch
SupportsPartialRefund
SupportsCustomerPortal
SupportsCurrencyUSD
SupportsCurrencyEUR
...
```

It cannot be hard-coded in business logic:

```text
if Waffo:
    WeChat = true
```

Provider capabilities change as the platform evolves.

Instead of promising:

# 8. Tax must be paid completely to Waffo Checkout

Do not ArcForges yourself:

```text
if Germany:
    VAT = 19%
```

Not at all.

As MoR, Waffo is responsible for the calculation, collection and payment of VAT, GST and Sales Tax that need to be borne by it; Waffo's public statement covers US sales tax, EU VAT/OSS, UK VAT and other market compliance. ([Waffo Pancake][5])

Therefore:

```text
ArcForges
→ offer goods + Suggested price + Tax Category

Waffo
→ The decision is final Checkout Tax / Invoice
```

ArcForges Pricing Page must state:

> Final price and applicable taxes are determined at checkout.

Do not copy Waffo's tax logic yourself.

Cloud and AI Credits:

# Anonymous purchases are not allowed.

Users must first:

```text
Sign in ArcForges
      ↓
Choose Workspace
      ↓
create Checkout
      ↓
Waffo
```

Because payment must ultimately know:

> To which Workspace should the rights be issued?

# 10. `buyerIdentity` Never use Email

The official Waffo API specifically supports merchant-controlled `buyerIdentity` and explicitly recommends using authenticated checkout when the customer's identity is already known; it can accept internal User IDs, not just Emails. ([Waffo Pancake][8])

So ArcForges must:

```text
buyerIdentity
=
ArcForges Stable Billing Identity
```

For example internally:

```text
billing_user_xxx
```

Do not:

```text
buyerIdentity = user@gmail.com
```

Because the email will change.

# 11. Checkout Metadata must establish a complete business association

Waffo Checkout supports:

* metadata
* merchant external ID
* buyerIdentity
* successUrl
* billing details

The metadata will be returned to the webhook along with the event. ([Waffo Pancake][8])

Therefore every Checkout is associated with at least:

```text
BillingAccountId
WorkspaceId
OfferId
PriceVersionId
CheckoutAttemptId
PurchaseIntentId
```

Then:

```text
Waffo Order
      ↓
these ArcForges Internal IDs
```

Even if:

* User changes email address;
* Account merge;
* Workspace transfer;
* Waffo Customer changes;

No orders will be lost.

# 12. If Checkout returns successfully, you must not activate Cloud directly.

Must:

```text
User payment
 ↓
Waffo Success Page
 ↓
Redirect ArcForges
 ↓
“Confirming payment......”
```

Then wait:

```text
Waffo Webhook
 ↓
ArcForges Verify
 ↓
Entitlement Grant
```

The successful jump itself:

> Not a payment authority.

Otherwise the user can forge the URL.

---

# 13. Webhook is the main event source, but it cannot be the only recovery method

Waffo webhooks currently support:

* `order.completed`
* `subscription.activated`
* `subscription.payment_succeeded`
* `subscription.updated`
* `subscription.canceling`
* `subscription.uncanceled`
* `subscription.canceled`
* `subscription.past_due`
* `refund.succeeded`
* `refund.failed`

Official requirements include signature verification, fast return of 2xx, asynchronous processing, and event idempotence; Webhook can be retried up to 3 times, that is, up to 4 attempts in total, and will be marked failed afterwards. ([Waffo Pancake][8])

So ArcForges must implement product layer requirements:

### Provider Event Inbox

Save:

```text
Provider
EventId
EventType
ReceivedAt
Raw Payload
Verification Result
Processing Status
Retry Count
```

### Idempotent

Same one:

```text
eventType + eventId
```

Can only affect business status once.

### Regular Reconciliation

For example, regular inspections:

```text
ArcForges Subscription
vs
Waffo Subscription
```

Found:

> Waffo Active
> ArcForges Suspended

Automatic repair.

Losing a webhook once cannot cause the user to permanently lose the subscription.

# 14. The Waffo Subscription life cycle cannot directly become the ArcForges life cycle

Waffo's current status includes:

```text
pending
active
trialing
past_due
canceling
canceled
expired
closed
```

([Waffo Pancake][2])

ArcForges should be normalized to its own:

```text
Pending
Active
Grace
CancelScheduled
Ended
Suspended
```

Also retain:

```text
ExternalProviderStatus
```

For diagnostic purposes.

Then change to Creem/Paddle/Apple:

> ArcForges does not require re-changing all business logic.

---

# 15. Payment failure and Grace Period

Waffo enters after renewal failure:

```text
past_due
```

It clearly states that this is a recovery/retry state and does not mean immediate termination; the platform can continue to retry and the user can update payment information. ([Waffo Pancake][2])

ArcForges default rules:

### Payment failed on the first day

Enter:

> Grace

Still:

* Sync
* Storage Read/Write
* Remote Agent
* Cloud BYOK

Normal.

But:

> New Managed AI Monthly Allowance is not reissued.

---

### Grace Maximum Recommendation 7 Days

If still not restored:

```text
Cloud write → suspended
Remote Agent → suspended
Managed AI → suspended
Cloud BYOK → suspended
```

However:

* Account can log in;
* Data can be exported;
* Billing can manage;
* All local apps are normal;
* Local BYOK OK.

After that, Waffo successfully deducted the money:

> Automatic and immediate recovery.

The length of Grace must be configured and not hard-coded into the Provider.

---

# 16. Cancel subscription

`canceling` by Waffo:

> The subscription has been canceled but will continue until the end of the current period.

And before the end, you can Reactivate to restore the original billing cycle. ([Waffo Pancake][2])

So the ArcForges page must show:

> Cancellation scheduled
>
> Cloud remains active until Aug 21, 2026.

instead of:

> Canceled

Users can also:

> Resume subscription

until the end of the cycle.

# 17. An important limitation: Currently Waffo has not actually launched Upgrade/Downgrade yet.

The official API documentation has defined:

```text
Change Subscription Product
```

But currently returns:

In other words, the package switching API has not been officially launched yet. ([Waffo Pancake][2])

Therefore ArcForges V1 **Never rely on this feature**.

Currently:

```text
Monthly → Annual
```

Correct experience:

> Cancel monthly at period end
> Then purchase annual at the end of the period.

The background model is still reserved:

```text
PlanChangeIntent
```

Wait for Waffo GA to get in.

# 20. Rules of AI Credits

Suggestions:

### Subscription Allowance

* Reissued every cycle
* No rollover
* Void when due

### Purchased Credits

* Can be accumulated
* Recommended validity period of 12 months
* No cash withdrawal
* Not transferable
* Not redeemable for cash

### Promotional Credits

* Independent expiration time
* Non-refundable

# 21. The product description of AI Credits on Waffo is very important

Because Waffo prohibits unregulated crypto, speculative NFT and other financial/virtual asset-related businesses. ([Waffo Pancake][9])

So do not describe it as:

> Arc Wallet
> Digital Currency
> Token

A better formal description:

> **Prepaid usage credits for ArcForges Managed AI services. Credits have no cash value, cannot be withdrawn, transferred or traded.**

This way it's clear:

> SaaS usage balance

Not a financial asset.

---

# 22. Refund rules must be adapted to Waffo

Waffo one-time payment refund ticket current rules:

* The refund process can be entered within 14 days after payment;
* Support full or partial refund;
* Refund Ticket has pending / approved / rejected / processing / succeeded / failed status. ([Waffo Pancake][10])

In terms of costs:

* Additional `$1` per refund
* The original transaction fee will not be refunded. ([Waffo Pancake][4])

---

# 23. ArcForges Refund Policy

## Cloud Pass

Apply within 14 days of purchase.

If of little practical use:

> Full Refund

If it has been used extensively:

* Large amounts of Cloud Storage
* Lots of AI Allowance
* A large number of Remote/Cloud services

A partial refund or rejection may be decided in accordance with the policy and local mandatory consumer laws.

---

## AI Credits

### completely unused

Allowed:

> Full Refund

### used part

Priority:

> Partial Refund = Unused portion of the corresponding value

Waffo supports Partial Refund. ([Waffo Pancake][10])

---

## Subscription

Subscription can be canceled normally:

> Renewal will stop after the current cycle ends.

Waffo's current refund ticket system is mainly for one-time payments; the normal path for Subscription is cancel-at-period-end, but Waffo, as a MoR, can still refund itself under legal, consumer protection or payment risk requirements. ([Waffo Pancake][10])

So do not make promises in the UI:

> Subscription is never refundable

The correct one is:

> Cancel subscription
> Request billing support / refund separately.

---

# 24. Rights must be rolled back after a refund occurs

Not just:

```text
Order.Refunded = true
```

For example, AI Credits:

```text
Refund $25
 ↓
Correspond Credit Lot Undo the remaining part
```

Cloud Pass:

```text
Refund
 ↓
Cancel correspondence 365-day Entitlement Grant
```

Here's why:

> Entitlement must document the source.

---

# 25. Chargeback must preserve evidence from the first day

Waffo's current Chargeback cost is:

* First chargeback: `$25`
* Representment: `$10`
* Pre-arbitration: `$25`

The terms stipulate that when the chargeback exceeds 1% of the transaction volume and at least 10 transactions within the 30-day window, it can be considered excessive, and the platform can also take measures at a lower level due to major risks. ([Waffo Pancake][4])

Therefore, every commercial order needs to keep the most basic:

```text
Order
Checkout
Terms Version
Refund Policy Version
Account Identity
Workspace
Entitlement Granted
Login Activity
Cloud Usage
AI Usage
Support History
Cancellation Request
Refund Request
```

These are called:

# Commercial Evidence

Not to spy on users, but to be able to prove when a chargeback occurs:

> The item was actually delivered.

Enter the Waffo Portal.

# 29. Merchant review: ArcForges must meet complete conditions in advance

Waffo Store must undergo a business review before officially launching Live Payments.

Current clear requirements:

* The product has actually been launched;
* The website is publicly accessible;
* It cannot just be Coming Soon;
* Product description is clear;
* Pricing is clear;
* Privacy Policy;
* Terms of Service;
* Real and available Support Email;
* Fake reviews and false numbers are not allowed;
* Products must not infringe trademarks;
* Not a prohibited product;
* Typically review takes 1–3 business days.

([Waffo Pancake][12])

So before applying for production review:

```text
arcforges.com
/products/chat
/cloud
/pricing
/privacy
/terms
/support
```

At least all must be real pages.

# 30. ArcForges belongs to Waffo's Restricted Category, please take the initiative to explain

Waffo currently handles:

> Subscription Services

Place in the "Allowed with additional review" category and require:

* Clear cancellation terms;
* Automatic renewal is expressly agreed to.

It also lists AIGC as a category requiring additional review. ([Waffo Pancake][9])

Therefore, the review materials should proactively state:

> ArcForges is an open-source desktop productivity software suite.
> Local software is free.
> The paid product is an optional managed cloud service providing synchronization, storage, remote access and managed AI usage.

Do not just write:

> AI Agent Platform

If it is too vague, it will easily trigger more serious risk control.

Especially:

* AI video generation

But currently:

> ArcChat Agent + Managed LLM

This can be explained directly during the review.

If generative media services are added in the future, the original review should not be automatically overwritten by default.

# 32. Mainland's personal KYC and withdrawal plans are officially confirmed

Currently Waffo's personal identity authentication explicitly supports:

* Nationality = CN
* Mainland China National ID
* 18-digit ID number
* Chinese Legal Name must be exactly the same as the ID card

A payout account cannot be added until identity authentication is completed. ([Waffo Pancake][13])

# 33. Withdrawal method

Now explicitly supported:

# Mainland bank card

and:

# Alipay

All are settled using RMB CNY. ([Waffo Pancake][14])

So you do not need to:

* Hong Kong bank card;
* Payoneer;
* National PayPal;
* USDC.

This is Waffo's greatest value to you.

# 34. Cash withdrawal operation strategy

Current rules:

* Minimum `$20`
* About 10 working days after sale clearing
* After cleared, you can apply on demand
* Usually arrives within 1–3 working days
* Withdrawal fee `1%`
* Minimum `$10`

([Waffo Pancake][14])

So:

# Do not withdraw small amounts frequently.

The operating rules are directly determined:

> **The accumulated amount is approximately `$1,000+` before withdrawing.**

Because:

```text
1% × $1000 = $10
```

At this time, the minimum `$10` will no longer increase the effective rate.

---

# 35. Both Alipay and bank cards should be bound

Waffo allows multiple payout accounts, with the option of selecting a default account. ([Waffo Pancake][15])

So:

```text
Primary
Mainland bank card

Secondary
Alipay
```

Or vice versa.

I prefer:

# Bank card Primary

# Alipay Backup

Because Waffo itself clearly stated that Alipay may require the submission of transaction background materials during large cross-border settlements; if the review is troublesome, you can use a bank card instead. ([Waffo Pancake][14])

---

# 36. A set of "Cash Withdrawal Certificate Package" must be kept for a long time

Because Alipay's large-amount review may require:

* Waffo Developer Terms
* Transaction/Settlement Export
* Customer Invoice
* ArcForges Pricing Page

The official Waffo documentation clearly lists these materials. ([Waffo Pancake][14])

So it is automatically archived every month:

```text
Settlement Report
Invoices
Order Export
Payout Record
Waffo Statement
Pricing snapshot
```

It will be useful for future domestic tax, bank or Alipay audits.

---

# 37. Waffo's own risks must also enter the system design

The Waffo company itself is not a small team with no background: it will complete a new round of financing of more than US$15 million in 2026, co-led by Illuminate Financial and Gaorong, with participation from HSBC and BAI Capital; Illuminate Financial itself has also publicly confirmed its investment. ([illuminatefinancial.com][16])

But:

> **Pancake This do-it-yourself MoR product line is really young.**

Its official Developer Terms version is **2026-06-03**, and we now also see that the Upgrade/Downgrade API is `501 Not Implemented`. ([Waffo Pancake][1])

Therefore:

# You can choose Waffo as the main platform.

But:

# Billing Domain cannot be bound to Waffo.

---

# 38. Provider Abstraction is required

Conceptually:

```text
BillingProvider
├── WaffoPancake
├── Creem     future
├── Apple     future
├── Google    future
└── Other     future
```

All external IDs:

```text
ProviderCustomerId
ProviderOrderId
ProviderPaymentId
ProviderSubscriptionId
ProviderProductId
```

Only Provider Mapping can exist.

ArcForges:

```text
OfferId
SubscriptionId
EntitlementId
```

Always your own.

---

# 39. Do not let Waffo Product ID appear on the client

The client only knows:

```text
ArcForges Cloud Monthly
```

instead of:

```text
PROD_4cW....
```

User clicks to buy:

```text
Client
 ↓
ArcForges Server
 ↓
find current Provider Mapping
 ↓
Waffo Product
 ↓
Checkout
```

If you change platforms in the future, you will not need to change a single line of business logic on the client side.

---

# 40. API security model

Waffo's official API is:

* HTTPS JSON
* Server API uses RSA-SHA256 signature
* The private key is only stored on the server;
* Test and Production Key are separated;
* Timestamps must remain within the allowed time window;
* WRITE OPERATION REST;
* Queries mainly use GraphQL. ([Waffo Pancake][8])

Therefore, the product requirements are determined directly:

> **Any Waffo Merchant Secret / Private Key is never allowed into ArcChat, ArcNotes, MAUI or the browser.**

Only exists:

# ArcForges Cloud Backend

Clients always create checkouts through ArcForges Server.

---

# 41. All purchases must support Idempotency

The Waffo API itself supports `X-Idempotency-Key`, and the current write operation can use idempotent Key. ([Waffo Pancake][17])

Therefore:

User double-clicks:

> Buy

Two orders cannot be generated.

Internal:

```text
PurchaseIntent
 ↓
CheckoutAttempt
 ↓
IdempotencyKey
```

The same PurchaseIntent can only create one valid Checkout.

---

# 42. Dynamic Pricing can only be determined by the server.

Waffo `priceSnapshot` can temporarily override product prices, and its official documentation clearly requires:

> Can only come from trusted servers, user client is not allowed to decide. ([Waffo Pancake][8])

So in the future:

```text
AI Overage
Enterprise Quote
Storage Overage
```

Dynamic prices are possible.

But:

```text
ArcChat client
```

Definitely not allowed to pass:

> I want to pay `$0.01`

Then the Server is handed over to Waffo as is.

---

# 43. Test and Production must be completely isolated

Waffo has an independent Test Mode:

* Fake transaction
* Fake money
* Independent data
* Webhooks are fully testable
* API behavior consistent with production

API Key is also separated by test/prod. ([Waffo Pancake][18])

Therefore phase 3 must exist:

```text
Development
→ Waffo Test

Staging
→ Waffo Test

Production
→ Waffo Production
```

Never:

> The test environment uses Production Key.

---

# 44. The mobile version maintains the previous plan and does not purchase through Waffo App.

ArcChat Mobile is just the Companion App.

Apple currently explicitly allows free standalone companion apps to access paid web services that have been purchased on the Web, as long as the app itself has no purchase functionality and does not guide users to external purchases. ([Apple Developer][19])

In principle, Google Play requires Play Billing for digital services such as Cloud software, storage, and productivity. If you do not participate in a specific alternative/external payment program, you cannot direct users to external payments within the app. ([Google Help][20])

So V1:

### ArcChat Mobile can

* Login
* View Plan
* Use existing Cloud
* Use existing AI Credits
* View Remote Agent
* View Desktop Task

### Not available

* Buy Cloud
* Buy Credits
* Waffo Checkout Link
* "Go to the official website to buy cheaply"

Purchases all occur:

# Web

This is the safest.

---

# 45. No trial in the first edition

Although Waffo supports Free Trial and has cross-merchant Trial Abuse Protection, the 7-day Trial may also incur authorization verification costs. The official Fee Schedule even indicates that the first cycle of the 7-day trial may incur a net loss of approximately `$0.50`. ([Waffo Pancake][2])

ArcForges itself has:

> All local free.

So there is no need to do:

> Cloud Free Trial

The first stage is direct:

```text
Local = Free Forever
Cloud = Paid
```

On the contrary, it is clearer.

In the future, there will be data to prove that Trial can significantly improve conversions, and then increase.

---

# 46. Do not build a complicated preferential system in the first stage.

Starting:

```text
Free Local
$5.99 Monthly
$59 Annual
$59 Pass
AI Credits
```

That's enough.

Do not start with:

* Coupon
* Referral
* Affiliate
* Student Discount
* Lifetime Deal
* Complex promotional credit

It's not that it cannot be done in the future, but there's no need to add Billing State first.

---

# 47. Business systems must ultimately have these domain objects

Although the specific code will not be discussed now, it must be fully expressed later:

```text
Billing Provider
Provider Capability

Billing Account

Offer
Product Scope
Price Version
Regional Price

Purchase Intent
Checkout Attempt

Order
Payment

Subscription
Subscription State
Plan Change Intent

Cloud Pass

Entitlement Grant
Entitlement Revocation

AI Credit Lot
AI Credit Reservation
AI Credit Settlement

Refund
Refund Request

Dispute
Chargeback

Provider Event
Provider Mapping

Reconciliation

Invoice Reference

Commercial Evidence

Payout
Settlement
Finance Statement
```

These concepts exist from the beginning, and the entire business system will basically not be reconstructed due to changing payment platforms.

---

# 50. Stage 3 officially finalized

Now I will formalize phase 3 as:

## **Primary MoR**

# Waffo Pancake

## Merchant

# Mainland China personal identity

## Store

# A `ArcForges` Store

## Payout

# Mainland Bank Card Primary

# Alipay Backup

## merchandise

```text
ArcForges Cloud Monthly    $5.99 recurring

ArcForges Cloud Annual     $59 recurring

ArcForges Cloud Pass       $59 one-time / 365 days

Arc AI Credits             $10
Arc AI Credits             $25
Arc AI Credits             $50
```

## Chinese users

# WeChat payment focuses on:

* Cloud Pass
* AI Credits
* Disposable Storage Pack of the Future

Currently 3.9%, no fixed fees.

## Equity

# ArcForges takes it into your own hands.

Waffo is always only responsible for:

> Money / Subscription transaction / Invoice / Tax / Refund / Dispute

## V1 explicitly does not rely on

* Waffo Upgrade/Downgrade
* Native Usage Metering
* Team Seat Billing
* Complex Proration

## Risk control

* Provider abstraction
* Webhook inbox + idempotency
* Periodic reconciliation
* Complete order/subscription export
* Business evidence retention
* Regular withdrawals
* Keep the second MoR accessible later

---

## The final stage 3 online threshold

Stage 3 is truly Production Ready only when all of the following are completed:

**Mainland ID card KYC → Store Business Review → Mainland bank card/Alipay binding → One real Card payment → One real WeChat payment → One real Subscription → One real renewal → One cancellation and recovery → One refund → Webhook duplicate/missing recovery test → The first RMB bank card withdrawal → The first Alipay withdrawal.**

Especially the last two real withdrawals.

Before the actual RMB arrives, we can only say:

> **Technology integration successful.**

Only after the account is actually received can we say:

> **ArcForges' payment business closed loop is completed.**

This set of Stage 3 can now serve as the formal requirements baseline for subsequent Billing, Entitlement, AI Credits, Account Portal, and Cloud business functions.
