# stage4

---

Now onto **Stage 4: Unified Entitlement – "What happens after you pay the money"**.

This stage is actually more important than the payment itself.

Stage 3 addresses:

> Did you receive the money successfully?

Stage 4 addresses:

> **Because of this money, which Workspace will get which cloud capabilities, how much storage, and how much AI quota within what time frame; what will happen after refunds, cancellations, failed renewals, and repeated purchases?**

This layer must be completely in the hands of ArcForges itself. **Waffo Pancake only provides business facts and does not directly determine ArcForges functional permissions**.

---

# 1. Determine the final structure first

I recommend that the entire business permission chain be fixed to:

```text
Waffo Pancake
    │
    │ Payment / Subscription / Refund facts
    ▼
ArcForges Billing
    │
    │ converts commercial facts
    ▼
Entitlement Grants
    │
    ▼
Entitlement Resolver
    │
    ▼
Effective Entitlements
    │
    ├── Cloud access
    ├── Storage quota
    ├── Sync
    ├── Remote Agent
    ├── Cloud BYOK
    ├── Managed AI allowance
    └── Purchased AI credits
```

The client always only asks:

> **ArcForges: What permissions do I have now?**

instead of:

> Waffo: Is my Subscription active?

This is the core principle of Stage 4.

---

# 2. The true meaning of Entitlement

Do not reduce Entitlement to:

```text
IsPro = true
```

This is the easiest design to rework later.

ArcForges has at least four completely different categories of benefits.

## 1. Capability

Whether a Cloud feature is available.

For example:

```text
cloud.sync
cloud.remote_agent
cloud.byok
cloud.vector_search
cloud.version_history
cloud.web_access
```

Result:

```text
Enabled / Disabled
```

---

## 2. Quota

How many resources the user can use.

For example:

```text
cloud.storage
```

The result is not:

```text
true
```

Instead:

```text
50 GB
```

Future:

```text
50 GB base
+ 100 GB add-on
= 150 GB effective quota
```

---

## 3. Allowance

The quota is given periodically and cannot be used anymore after it is used up.

For example:

```text
managed_ai.monthly_allowance
```

Each Billing Period:

```text
500 Arc AI Credits
```

Resend in the next cycle.

This comes with Cloud Subscription.

---

## 4. Consumable Balance

Really purchased consumable resources:

```text
Purchased AI Credits
```

For example:

```text
$25
→ 2500 Arc AI Credits
```

It is the balance.

Not a simple Entitlement flag.

---

So:

# **Entitlement ≠ Feature Flag**

Feature Flag means:

> Has this function been released for the product?

Entitlement means:

> Is this Workspace eligible to use it?

For example:

```text
Feature Flag:
Remote Agent = GA

Entitlement:
Workspace A = Enabled
Workspace B = Disabled
```

Must be separated.

---

# 3. Entitlement must belong to Workspace, not User

Stage 1 has been determined:

```text
User
 ↓ membership
Workspace
```

So paid benefits should also:

```text
Workspace
 ↓
Entitlements
```

instead of:

```text
User.IsPro
```

This is very important.

Today:

```text
Ryan
 ↓
Personal Workspace
 ↓
ArcForges Cloud
```

Later:

```text
Ryan
 ↓
ArcForges Team Workspace
 ↓
Team Subscription
```

Ryan's own Personal Workspace can be Free.

Corporate Workspace is Paid.

The two do not conflict at all.

---

# 4. Billing Account is purchased and Workspace is used to obtain benefits.

The complete relationship should be:

```text
Billing Account
      │
      │ pays
      ▼
Commercial Purchase
      │
      │ grants
      ▼
Workspace
      │
      ▼
Entitlements
```

So:

> who pays

and:

> who uses

Not the same concept.

Future payment from company financial staff:

```text
finance@arcforges.com
```

But what is actually used is:

```text
ArcForges Team Workspace
```

There is no need for financial users to own that data themselves.

---

# 5. The first version of the official Entitlement Catalog

Entitlements for the first phase of ArcForges Cloud can now be formalized.

## ArcForges Local

Entitlement is not required at all.

All local capabilities are present by default:

```text
local.apps               Free
local.agent              Free
local.cross_app_agent    Free
local.byok               Free
local.ai                  Free
local.storage             Free
local.vector_search       Free
```

Do not let these things go into business Entitlement.

Otherwise, it will be easy to misoperate into:

> The Billing service is down → Local functions cannot be used.

Absolutely cannot happen.

---

# 6. ArcForges Cloud Base Entitlements

Cloud Subscription or Cloud Pass should get unified:

# `ArcForges Cloud`

Rather than monthly payment, annual payment and Pass each producing different functions.

That is to say:

```text
Monthly
Annual
12-Month Pass
```

Just:

> **Purchase methods vary**

What is obtained is:

> **Same Cloud Entitlement Bundle**

---

## First Edition Bundle

Suggestions:

```text
cloud.access                  Enabled

cloud.sync                    Enabled

cloud.storage.bytes           50 GB

cloud.backup                  Enabled

cloud.version_history         Enabled

cloud.search                  Enabled

cloud.vector_index            Enabled

cloud.remote_agent            Enabled

cloud.cloud_byok              Enabled

cloud.web_continuity          Enabled

cloud.mobile_continuity       Enabled

managed_ai.allowance          N credits / billing period
```

The product specifications can be modified later, but the domain model does not need to change.

---

# 7. Do not hardcode the Bundle directly into the code

Cannot:

```text
if plan == Cloud:
    storage = 50GB
    remote = true
    ...
```

To exist:

# Entitlement Bundle Definition

Similar concepts:

```text
ArcForges Cloud v1
├── cloud.access = true
├── cloud.sync = true
├── storage = 50GB
├── remote_agent = true
├── cloud_byok = true
└── ai_allowance = 500
```

Later:

```text
ArcForges Cloud v2
├── storage = 100GB
...
```

It is a commercial policy for old users to keep 50GB and automatically upgrade to 100GB.

No need to modify the entire Entitlement system.

---

# 8. Why the Entitlement Bundle must also be versioned

Waffo Pancake's own Product adopts a versioned design: product updates will create a new version, and existing Subscriptions will retain the original version; price modifications only affect new purchases. ([Waffo Pancake][1])

ArcForges itself should adopt the same principle.

For example:

### 2026

```text
Cloud Bundle v1
50 GB
500 AI Credits
```

### 2027

```text
Cloud Bundle v2
100 GB
300 AI Credits
```

At this point you can decide:

### Automatically upgrade old users

```text
v1 → v2
```

Or:

### Grandfather

```text
Existing = v1
New users = v2
```

Entitlement layer can handle it.

---

# 9. Entitlement Grant is required

This is one of the most important data concepts throughout Stage 4.

Do not just maintain the end result:

```text
Storage = 150 GB
```

Must know:

> Where does this 150GB come from?

So to exist:

# Entitlement Grant

For example:

```text
Grant #1
Source: Cloud Annual Subscription
Capability: cloud.access
Valid:
2026-07-21 → 2027-07-21
```

and:

```text
Grant #2
Source: Cloud Annual Subscription
Quota:
storage +50 GB
Valid:
2026-07-21 → 2027-07-21
```

Later:

```text
Grant #3
Source: Storage Add-on
Quota:
storage +100 GB
```

Final Resolver:

```text
50GB
+
100GB
=
150GB
```

---

# 10. All Grants must have sources

Sources include at least:

```text
Subscription
CloudPass
StorageAddOn
PurchasedCredit
Promotion
AdminGrant
TeamPlan
Migration
Compensation
```

For example, if a Cloud failure occurs:

> Compensate users for 7 days of Cloud.

Cannot be secretly:

```text
ExpirationDate += 7
```

Instead it should produce:

```text
Compensation Grant
+7 days
Reason: Incident 2026-08-05
```

A later audit will reveal what happened.

---

# 11. Grant should be as unmodifiable as possible

This is the key to not having to rework in the long run.

Assumptions:

```text
Grant
2026-07-21 → 2027-07-21
```

A chargeback occurs.

Do not just change it to:

```text
2026-07-21 → 2026-07-25
```

A better model is:

```text
Original Grant
+
Revocation
```

That is:

```text
Entitlement Grant
      │
      └── Entitlement Revocation
```

This way you will always know:

> Why did you get it?

> Why was it lost later?

Especially suitable for:

* Refund
* Chargeback
* Fraud
* Admin correction
* Account migration

---

# 12. What is really given to the client is Effective Entitlements

The client does not need to understand:

```text
Subscription
Grant
Revocation
Add-on
Promotion
```

These are all server internal business logic.

What the client gets is a copy of:

# Effective Entitlement Snapshot

For example:

```text
Workspace: Personal

Cloud:
  Active

Storage:
  50 GB quota
  12.4 GB used

Sync:
  Enabled

Remote Agent:
  Enabled

Cloud BYOK:
  Enabled

Managed AI:
  Monthly allowance remaining: 320

Purchased AI:
  2,500 credits

Valid through:
  2027-07-21
```

---

# 13. It is best to give the client a clear Entitlement Reason

For example:

```text
remote_agent:
  enabled: false
  reason: subscription_expired
```

Instead of just:

```text
false
```

Reasons can be:

```text
available
no_entitlement
subscription_expired
payment_grace
quota_exceeded
temporarily_restricted
workspace_suspended
feature_unavailable
```

In this way, the UI can correctly prompt:

> Cloud subscription expired

instead of:

> Something went wrong.

---

# 14. Do not let each app calculate its own rights and interests

This is a very big pit.

Cannot:

```text
ArcNotes:
if subscription == active

ArcChat:
if Waffo == active

ArcScope:
if cloud plan != free
```

All must be unified:

```text
ArcForges Cloud
      ↓
Entitlement Resolver
      ↓
Effective Entitlements
```

Each app only consumes results.

---

# 15. How Waffo Monthly and Annual generate Grant

Waffo's current subscription status includes:

* `pending`
* `active`
* `trialing`
* `past_due`
* `canceling`
* `canceled`
* `expired`
* `closed`

Moreover, `past_due` is a recovery state, which does not mean that the service should be discontinued immediately; during `canceling`, users still have access rights to the current payment cycle. ([Waffo Pancake][2])

So you cannot directly:

```text
Waffo active = entitlement ON
Others = OFF
```

---

# 16. The real basis for Subscription Entitlement

The core is not:

```text
Subscription.Status
```

Instead:

# `Paid Through`

For example:

```text
PaidThrough = 2027-07-21T10:00Z
```

Just:

```text
Now < PaidThrough
```

Cloud benefits still exist under normal circumstances.

Therefore:

## active

Normal.

```text
Entitlement valid to CurrentPeriodEnd
```

---

## canceling

Still normal.

```text
Entitlement valid to CurrentPeriodEnd
```

Waffo explicitly states that cancellations are only effective at the end of the current period and there is no immediate cancellation option. ([Waffo Pancake][2])

So:

> `canceling` ≠ Use prohibited.

---

## canceled

You cannot just see `canceled` and turn it off immediately.

Must check:

```text
PaidThrough
```

Because the state semantics of different Providers may be different in the future.

---

# 17. What to do with past_due?

This is the easiest design error.

Waffo explicitly recommends treating `past_due` as:

> Renewal requires recovery

instead of:

> Stop service immediately. ([Waffo Pancake][2])

So ArcForges enters itself:

# Grace

For example:

```text
Entitlement State:
Grace

GraceUntil:
+7 days
```

---

## Grace in

Suggestions:

### Reserve

* Sync
* Storage
* Download
* Backup
* Remote Agent
* Cloud BYOK

### Do not regenerate

* New Cycle Managed AI Allowance

Reason:

> If the renewal is not successful, the next cycle of AI resources cannot be distributed for free.

---

# 18. Grace is not deleted after expiration, but Restricted

Enter:

# `CloudRestricted`

At this time:

```text
cloud.sync.write      Disabled

cloud.storage.upload Disabled

cloud.remote_agent   Disabled

cloud.cloud_byok     Disabled

managed_ai           Disabled
```

But should continue to allow:

```text
cloud.login          Enabled

cloud.read_existing  Enabled

cloud.export         Enabled

billing.manage       Enabled
```

At least for the subsequent data retention period.

Do not:

> Payment failed → User data is locked instantly.

---

# 19. Subscription restored successfully

Waffo:

```text
past_due
→ active
```

ArcForges:

```text
Grace / Restricted
→ Active
```

Effective Entitlements are restored immediately.

Not required:

* User logs in again
* Reinstall
* Contact customer service manually

---

# 20. Do not re-create "Permanent Duplicate Permissions" when the renewal is successful.

The correct way should be:

First time:

```text
Subscription Grant
Valid:
Jul 2026 → Aug 2026
```

After renewal:

```text
same commercial entitlement source
PaidThrough:
Sep 2026
```

Or form a series of traceable cycle Grants.

I prefer to keep it internally:

```text
Subscription Entitlement
+
Billing Period Grants
```

This way:

### long term capability

Represented by Subscription Source.

### AI Allowance per cycle

Each successful payment is created independently:

```text
Allowance Grant
```

These are two different things.

---

# 21. AI Monthly Allowance must be generated according to Billing Period

For example, in the future:

```text
Cloud = monthly value $2 of Managed AI allowance
```

Monthly payment:

```text
Monthly renewal successful
→ Create a Allowance Lot
```

Annual payment:

Do not:

```text
Send once 12 All months AI Credits
```

Otherwise, the user's annual purchase payment is:

> Burn all the AI for the whole year in one day

Will increase your cost risk.

Correct way:

```text
Annual Subscription
    ↓
every month Anniversary
    ↓
Issued this month Allowance
```

Although the payment is once a year.

Entitlement Scheduler generates allowance on a monthly basis by itself.

---

# 22. Annual and Monthly Cloud benefits are the same

Do not do:

```text
Monthly:
20 GB

Annual:
50 GB
```

At least not in the first version.

Annual business awards should be:

> Discount.

It's not about artificially creating product differences.

In this way, users will not have their data permissions changed due to changing Billing Cycle.

---

# 23. How Cloud Pass generates Entitlement

This is Waffo One-Time Product.

The authoritative status of successful payment in Waffo payment status is `succeeded`; the refund status is maintained separately from Payment Status. ([Waffo Pancake][3])

After success:

```text
Cloud Pass Purchase
       ↓
Entitlement Grant
       ↓
365 days
```

For example:

```text
StartsAt = purchase confirmation

EndsAt = StartsAt + 365 days
```

---

# 24. Handling of Continuous Pass Purchases

WeChat users are likely to use it like this:

```text
2026 buy once
2027 buy again
```

Even:

```text
Currently there are 6 months
see promotion
Buy another year in advance
```

The formal rules should be:

```text
newStart =
max(CurrentPaidThrough, PurchaseTime)

newPaidThrough =
newStart + 365 days
```

So:

> No remaining time is lost.

---

# 25. It is recommended to set the maximum prepayment period of Pass

For example up to:

# 3 years

Not infinite:

```text
buy once 20 portion
→ 20 year Cloud
```

Because:

* Cloud costs will change
* Business prices will change
* Product may be adjusted
* Refunds and migrations are complex

So it is recommended:

> Cloud Pass accrues up to 36 months into the future.

No further purchases are allowed after this time limit.

---

# 26. Subscription and Pass should not exist at the same time

Stage 3 has already mentioned this, and here it officially falls to Entitlement.

if:

```text
Subscription Active
```

Do not allow:

```text
Buy Pass
```

if:

```text
Pass Active
```

The user decides to change to automatic renewal:

Subscription purchases may be allowed, but preferably:

# Subscription starts when Pass ends

rather than immediately overlapping.

The first version is simpler:

> Wait until the Pass is close to expiration before opening Subscription.

Avoid simultaneous decisions from two sources `PaidThrough`.

# 27. However, Entitlement Resolver must be able to handle multiple sources

While the UI discourages overlap, the underlying layer must support:

```text
Subscription
+
Compensation
+
Promotion
```

For example:

```text

Compensation +7 days
```

Resolver gets:

```text
Effective paid through Aug 8
```

This capability will also be needed when migrating the payment platform in the future.

# 28. Entitlement combination rules must be clear

Different types cannot all use the same algorithm.

## Boolean Capability

For example:

```text
remote_agent
```

Usually:

# ANY

As long as there is a valid Grant:

```text
Enabled
```

---

## Additive Quota

For example Storage:

```text
Base 50GB
+ Add-on 100GB
= 150GB
```

Use:

# SUM

## Maximum

Possible future:

```text

```

Basics:

```text
5
```

Team:

```text
20
```

This uses:

# MAX

Instead of adding together we get 25.

## Replace / Priority

For example:

```text
SupportLevel
Free < Priority < Enterprise
```

Take:

# highest priority

---

## Balance

AI Credits:

Not Entitlement Resolver computes a static number.

By:

# Ledger

Calculate available balance.

# 29. Quota and Usage must be separated

For example:

```text
Storage Entitlement:
50 GB

Storage Usage:
12 GB
```

These are two completely different data domains.

Cannot save:

```text
StorageRemaining = 38GB
```

as the only fact.

Because if the user purchases more:

```text
+100GB
```

It should change naturally:

```text
Quota 150GB
Usage 12GB
Available 138GB
```

# 30. What to do if the Storage exceeds the quota?

Later the Subscription expires or the Add-on is canceled:

May occur:

```text
Current Usage:
120GB

New Quota:
50GB
```

Never:

> Automatically delete 70GB.

Correct status:

# Over Quota

```text
Storage Usage:
120 GB

Quota:
50 GB

New uploads:
Blocked

Existing files:
Readable

Downloads:
Allowed

Delete:
Allowed
```

User deleted below 50GB:

> Resume writing.

This is the rule that must be adhered to in the future.

# 31. AI Credits cannot use simple Balance

Officially adopted:

# Credit Ledger + Credit Lots

```text
Subscription allowance
500
Expires Aug 1

Lot B
Purchased
2500

Lot C
Compensation
200
```

Then each AI consumption:

```text
Debit
```

# 32. AI consumption order

Recommended:

### first priority

The earliest free Allowance to expire.

### second

Promotion / Compensation.

### third

Purchased Credits.

That is:

# Earliest-expiry-first

Let users try not to lose the amount that is about to expire.

However, the consumption order of Purchased Credits must also be based on the earliest expiring Lot.

# 33. AI balance must support Reservation

A complex Agent:

```text
ArcChat
→ model
→ tool
→ model
→ tool
→ model
```

May be consumed dozens of times in a row.

If there are three tasks at the same time:

```text
Balance = 100
```

Check all at the same time:

> 100 > 50, can run

Eventually it might be:

```text
-50
```

So need:

```text
Available
Reserved
Consumed
```

For example:

```text
100
 ↓ reserve 40
Available = 60
Reserved = 40
```

Mission ends:

```text
actual consumption 31

Consume 31
Release 9
```

# 34. Negative balances are absolutely not allowed by default.

# 36. Cloud BYOK belongs to Cloud Entitlement

Because:

```text
→ ArcForges Cloud
```

ArcForges is responsible for:

# 37. Remote Agent must also meet two conditions at the same time

It does not mean you can be remote automatically if you have Cloud.

Must:

```text
remote_agent = enabled

AND

Device Setting:
```

```text
Effective Remote Access
=

AND
```

# 38. The same is true for Feature Availability

```text
AND

AND

AND
```

# 39. Entitlement cannot serve as Authorization

This is very important.

For example:

Cannot explain:

That is:

```text
this Workspace Can I use this product capability?

Authorization:
current Actor Can I access this specific resource?
```

The two must be separated.

# 40. Entitlement Snapshot must have a version

```text
1842 available
```

Push is just:

The true state remains from:

Read again.

Because Cloud occasionally breaks.

For example:

```text

```

> No subscription.

Suggestions:

For:

Client-side caching is just a UX optimization.

# 45. Actual link after purchase is completed

Now it can be fully defined:

```text
User
 ↓
Waffo Checkout
 ↓
Payment succeeded
 ↓
Waffo Webhook
 ↓
Provider Event Inbox
 ↓
Billing verifies Order / Payment
 ↓
Commercial Purchase recognized

 ↓
Entitlement Resolver recomputes Workspace
 ↓
New Entitlement Snapshot
 ↓
EntitlementVersion++
 ↓
SignalR notification
 ↓
ArcChat / Portal refresh
```

Waffo's authenticated checkout can be bound to the stable `buyerIdentity` controlled by the merchant; the official also clearly recommends using authenticated checkout when the user's identity is already known, rather than relying on Email. ([Waffo Pancake][4])

This makes the mapping of Waffo Order to ArcForges Account/Workspace more stable.

# 46. Be sure to avoid "blindly granting the Webhook as soon as it arrives"

Webhooks are triggers.

Not unconditional belief.

Processing order:

```text
signature valid?

known provider?
 ↓
known Waffo Store?
 ↓
known product mapping?
 ↓
known PurchaseIntent / buyerIdentity?
 ↓
payment state valid?
 ↓
already processed?
 ↓
Grant
```

Waffo officials clearly state that webhooks may be delivered repeatedly and require the production environment to persist deduplication records. ([Waffo Pancake][5])

```text
↕
```

```text
No Grant
```

or exceeds the valid time.

### Security/Resilience

Only after these are passed will it be truly complete.

---

# Stage 4 Finalization

ArcForges should use:

# **Grant-based Unified Entitlement System**

Core structure:

```text
Commercial Fact
      ↓
Entitlement Grant / Revocation
      ↓
Resolver
      ↓
Effective Entitlement Snapshot
```

Waffo is only responsible for providing:

```text
Payment
Subscription
Refund
Commercial lifecycle
```

ArcForges always decides for itself:

```text
Cloud
Storage
Sync
Remote Agent
Cloud BYOK
Managed AI
AI Credits
```

and officially adheres to:

* **Local capabilities do not enter commercial entitlement.**
* **The rights and interests belong to Workspace, not User.**
* **Monthly / Annual / Pass get the same Cloud Bundle.**
* **Cloud Bundle versioning.**
* **Entitlement uses Grant + Revocation instead of directly changing it to `IsPro`.**
* **Boolean, Quota, Allowance, and Balance are handled separately.**
* **AI uses Credit Ledger instead of a simple Balance.**
* **Storage Quota is separate from Storage Usage.**
* **Downgrading never automatically deletes user data.**
* **Subscription Cancel does not immediately revoke rights.**
* **Waffo `past_due` Enter ArcForges Grace instead of immediately stopping the service.**
* **Cloud BYOK is a paid Cloud capability; Local BYOK is permanently free.**
* **Remote Agent requires both business Entitlement and user Device Consent.**
* **Entitlement is completely separated from Authorization and Feature Flag.**
* **The client only consumes ArcForges Effective Entitlement Snapshot.**
* **Webhook + Reconciliation double insurance.**
* **All Entitlement changes are explainable, auditable, and recoverable.**
* **Provider is replaceable. In the future, Waffo, Apple, Google, and Paddle will only be responsible for generating new Entitlement Sources.**

In this way, the **Waffo Pancake payment layer** of stage 3 and the **ArcForges Entitlement layer** of stage 4 have been truly decoupled.

No matter whether you add **Cloud Storage, Managed AI, Team, single App Cloud, mobile payment or change MoR** later, there is no need to overturn the basis of commercial permissions.

# stage5

---

Now enter **Stage 5: Application Distribution, Installation, Updates**.

At this stage I suggest separating four things outright: **"where the source lives", "where the binaries live", "where users install from", and "where updates come from later"**. That way, adding Microsoft Store, GitHub, WinGet, macOS, and Linux later will never overturn the release system.

# Give the final conclusion first

The overall solution for which ArcForges is best suited is:

> **GitHub = source code + Release image + build traceability**
>
> **Cloudflare R2 = Official Installation and Update CDN**
>
> **Velopack = Windows/macOS/Linux desktop installation and automatic update framework**
>
> **Microsoft Store = additional official distribution portal for Windows, not the only distribution source**
>
> **WinGet = Additional installation entry for Windows**
>
> **macOS = Direct distribution from the official website + Developer ID + Notarization**
>
> **Linux = AppImage direct distribution**
>
> **ArcChat Mobile = Apple App Store / Google Play respective native distribution and updates**

For Windows I would especially recommend:

# **Official website Velopack `Setup.exe` + Microsoft Store releases the same Win32 EXE/MSI installer**

Instead of maintaining it initially:

```text
Website EXE
+
Store MSIX
```

Two completely different installation and update systems.

The Microsoft Store now officially allows Win32 applications to directly submit existing `.exe` or `.msi`, and the publisher hosts the installation files themselves; in this mode, the Store is not responsible for automatically updating existing users, allowing the application's own updater to continue to update. Perfect for ArcForges using the same set of Velopacks. ([Microsoft Learn][1])

---

# 1. There is no conflict between open source and Microsoft Store.

This is settled first.

**Open Source describes source code licenses and source code availability.**

Microsoft Store / Official Website / GitHub Releases describes:

> Where can I get the officially compiled and trusted binary?

So it's totally fine to:

```text
GitHub
├── Source Code
├── Tags
├── Build Workflow
└── Release binaries mirror

Microsoft Store
└── Official signed ArcChat installer

arcforges.com
└── Official direct installer
```

Users can:

### Ordinary user

Directly:

> Microsoft Store / arcforges.com

### Open source users

Directly:

> GitHub clone → compile yourself

There is no contradiction between the two.

On the contrary, for open source projects, official Store packages and signed installation packages are very important, because ordinary users should not compile it themselves in order to use open source software.

---

# 2. Do not let GitHub take on all the responsibilities at the same time

GitHub Releases **can completely store installation packages**.

Official current restrictions:

* A Release can have up to 1,000 assets;
* Individual files must be smaller than 2 GiB;
* There is no limit on the total size of Release;
* Release There is no limit on download bandwidth. ([GitHub Docs][2])

So:

> There is no problem putting ArcChat, ArcNotes, ArcScope and other installation packages on GitHub Releases.

But I **do not recommend using the GitHub API directly as the sole source for production auto-updates**.

The reason is that Velopack's `GithubSource` anonymous GitHub API requests will be subject to the GitHub unauthenticated API limit of **60 requests/hour/IP**. This problem may be encountered in companies, campuses, proxies/VPNs, or when multiple users share a public IP. ([Velopack][3])

So it's better to split it into:

```text
GitHub Releases
        │
        │ public mirror
        ▼
Users can manually download

Cloudflare R2
        │
        │ production distribution
        ▼
downloads.arcforges.com
updates.arcforges.com
```

---

# 3. Put the official installation package and update files on R2

This is highly consistent with the overall route we chose Cloudflare earlier.

For example:

```text
downloads.arcforges.com
updates.arcforges.com
```

Bottom layer:

```text
Cloudflare R2
```

R2 Current:

* Standard Storage `$0.015/GB-month`
* Internet egress is free;
* You can bind your own Custom Domain;
* Custom Domain can connect to Cloudflare Cache. ([Cloudflare Docs][4])

So it's perfect for tons of free desktop software downloads.

---

## formal directory logic

For example:

```text
downloads.arcforges.com/
    chat/
      1.4.2/
        windows-x64/
        windows-arm64/
        macos-arm64/
        macos-x64/
        linux-x64/

    notes/
    scope/
    slate/
```

All historical releases:

# Immutable

Once:

```text
ArcChat 1.4.2
```

After release:

> You can never secretly change files with the same URL.

Repairs can only be made by:

```text
1.4.3
```

Because:

* Microsoft Store checks the installation URL;
* WinGet will verify SHA256;
* The user may save the checksum;
* GitHub Release provenance needs to be consistent;
* The updater must be able to restore historical versions correctly.

---

# 4. Officially choose Velopack

Under the current C#/Avalonia/Native AOT product system, I think:

# **Velopack is currently the most suitable installation + update infrastructure.**

It now natively supports:

* C#
* Windows
* macOS
* Linux
* Installer
* Automatic updates
* Delta Update
* Release Channel
* Self-hosted HTTP Update Source
* GitHub Releases
* Downgrade
* Release Notes

Moreover, MIT is open source and is still actively maintained; the official repository will continue to be released in 2026. ([GitHub][5])

---

## Why not Squirrel.Windows

Squirrel is one of the important predecessors to Velopack, but the latest official release of the original Squirrel.Windows is still stuck in 2020, and the repository itself has publicly stated that it needs more maintainers. More importantly:

> It is Windows-only.

ArcForges is:

```text
Windows
macOS
Linux
```

There is no need to maintain different update frameworks for three systems. ([GitHub][6])

---

# 5. There is no principle conflict between Velopack and Native AOT

Velopack eats:

> Your final publish output directory.

The application is not required to rely on the .NET Runtime on the machine.

For Native AOT:

```text
dotnet publish
       ↓
Native executable + dependencies
       ↓
Velopack package
```

That's it.

Velopack itself even explicitly recommends that self-contained applications no longer let the Installer bootstrap the .NET Runtime. ([Velopack][7])

Therefore:

> **ArcForges Native AOT distribution and updates do not require the .NET Runtime to be installed.**

This is right in your direction.

---

# 6. Windows: The final recommended distribution system

I recommend that Windows officially use four entrances:

```text
                    ArcChat Windows
                          │
       ┌──────────────────┼────────────────────┐
       │                  │                    │
arcforges.com       Microsoft Store          WinGet
       │                  │                    │
       └──────────── signed Setup.exe ─────────┘
                          │
                    Velopack install
                          │
                 ArcForges Update Feed
```

Additionally:

```text
GitHub Releases
```

Provide a public image of the same Release.

---

# 7. Windows official website main installation package: Velopack Setup.exe

Default:

```text
ArcChat-Setup.exe
```

Use:

# Per-user install

Install to something like:

```text
%LocalAppData%\ArcForges.ArcChat
```

No administrator rights are required.

Velopack's default Windows Setup is a per-user installation and does not require elevation; if the enterprise requires a machine-wide installation of Program Files in the future, it can also generate an MSI. ([Velopack][8])

This is great for regular personal desktop software.

---

# 8. Microsoft Store: I recommend the "Unpackaged Win32" route

The Microsoft Store now offers two Win32 routes:

### A

MSIX

### B

Post the original directly:

```text
.exe
.msi
```

Microsoft has supported the latter mode since 2021 and it is still officially supported now. ([Microsoft Learn][1])

For ArcForges:

# I choose B.

That is:

```text
Microsoft Store
    ↓
ArcChat
    ↓
ArcChat-Setup.exe
    ↓
Velopack
```

---

# 9. Why is it not recommended that the first version of Store use MSIX?

MSIX itself is fine.

It provides:

* Package Identity
* Clean install/uninstall
* Store-hosted update
* Differential update
* Some Windows Package Identity features. ([Microsoft Learn][9])

But if:

```text
Official website = Velopack
Store = MSIX
```

You immediately have two sets:

```text
Installation location
update logic
Package Identity
uninstall behavior
Version release process
Store Review life cycle
```

In the future, the test matrix will also become:

```text
Windows Direct
Windows Store
```

Two substantially different Builds.

Currently, ArcForges has no core requirement to rely on MSIX Package Identity.

So:

> **There is no gain worth introducing a second installation system now.**

---

# 10. There is another huge advantage of using Win32 Store Listing

Microsoft clearly states:

For MSI/EXE published in Microsoft Store:

> The Store is not responsible for automatically updating users who have already installed it;

Apps can continue to use their own in-app updates. ([Microsoft Learn][10])

This means:

```text
Website user
Microsoft Store user
WinGet user
```

All can finally be accessed:

# ArcForges / Velopack Update System

Very clean.

---

# 11. But Windows requires code signing

There is no saving here.

MSIX for the Store is automatically re-signed by Microsoft; however:

> **When publishing EXE/MSI in Store, the publisher must sign it with Authenticode themselves.**

Direct downloading from the official website requires code signing, otherwise SmartScreen and Antivirus will easily cause alarms. ([Microsoft Learn][11])

So ArcForges is officially released:

# All Windows executables/installers must be signed + timestamp.

---

# 12. How to sign up for Windows under your mainland identity?

Microsoft's own Azure Artifact Signing Public Trust currently:

* Organization: United States, Canada, EU, United Kingdom;
* Individual: United States, Canada.

So as a mainland individual, you cannot currently use it as your default choice. ([Microsoft Learn][12])

So you need to use:

# CA-issued Individual Code Signing Certificate

For example SSL.com now explicitly offers **IV Code Signing**:

> Individual developers can apply and do not need to register a company.

And supports Authenticode and CI/CD cloud signing. ([SSL.com][13])

However:

> **Whether the mainland ID card can pass the current KYC of a specific CA must be actually confirmed before formal purchase.**

Do not wait for the day the software is released to apply.

---

# 13. There is another practical problem: the signature will show the personal name

Personal IV Certificate:

```text
Publisher:
<your real name>
```

instead of:

```text
ArcForges
```

Likewise, the Microsoft Store currently:

* Individual developer → Publish in an individual name;
* Company developer → Published under the corporate legal entity name. ([Microsoft Learn][14])

So if in the future you want both the system and the Store to display:

# ArcForges

As a verification Publisher:

Ultimately it is best to register a legal corporate entity.

But this is not a starting hindrance.

The app name can still be:

```text
ArcChat
ArcNotes
ArcScope
```

Only Windows Signature Publisher may display your personal real name initially.

---

# 14. Microsoft Store developer accounts are now affordable

Latest process as of 2026:

> The Store onboarding registration fee is currently eliminated for both Individual and Company new registration processes.

Individuals use government ID cards + selfies to complete verification; companies require business and domain name verification. ([Microsoft Learn][15])

So:

> **There is no need to deliberately not list it on the Store because of "open source software".**

This is a basically free channel for additional customer acquisition and trusted installs.

---

# 15. But do not use your personal Store Account to occupy the brand casually

There is an important long-term question here:

Microsoft currently clearly states:

> Individual developer account **cannot be directly converted to Company account**.

If you want to publish as a company in the future, you need to create a new Company developer account. ([Microsoft Learn][16])

So my advice:

### If there is no company in the short term, and accept Publisher to display personal name

You can open Individual.

### If you are sure that you will start an ArcForges company in the near future and you care about Publisher brand consistency

You can wait until the company entity is ready before officially launching it on the Store.

There is no need to wait for the official website and GitHub.

---

# 16. WinGet should also be officially supported

Every Windows App:

```text
ArcForges.ArcChat
ArcForges.ArcNotes
ArcForges.ArcScope
...
```

Submit to:

```text
microsoft/winget-pkgs
```

Microsoft's official WinGet repository itself is a publicly maintained manifest on GitHub; PRs are automatically verified and then entered into the public WinGet repository. ([Microsoft Learn][17])

So the user:

```powershell
winget install ArcForges.ArcChat
```

Future:

```powershell
winget upgrade ArcForges.ArcChat
```

Very suitable for developer users.

---

# 17. WinGet is still not a substitute for its own Update System

Do not rely on:

> The user will actively run `winget upgrade`.

ArcForges itself still requires:

# Automatic Update

WinGet is just:

> Discover / Install / Package-manager upgrade channel.

The same version, the same installation package, and the same SHA256.

Avoid:

```text
WinGet Yes 1.4.0
Website Yes 1.5.0
Store Yes 1.3.0
```

Such a long-term maintenance disaster.

---

# 18. macOS: No Mac App Store required for first launch

I'll be very clear:

# **The first phase of macOS will be distributed directly from the official website.**

Format:

```text
.pkg
```

Bottom layer:

# Velopack

Then:

* Developer ID Application signature;
* Developer ID Installer signature;
* Apple Notarization;
* staple notarization ticket. ([Apple Developer][18])

---

# 19. Why is Mac App Store not recommended currently?

Mac App Store:

# Force App Sandbox.

Apple officially states that this is a requirement for submission to the Mac App Store. ([Apple Developer][19])

ArcForges product features include:

* ArcChat Local Hub;
* Multi-App process discovery and communication;
* Agent calls other apps;
* ArcScope device capabilities;
* Local file;
* Subsequent expansion tools.

These will have significantly more friction with a strict sandbox.

In addition, Velopack itself makes it clear:

> macOS App Sandbox is not supported because the updater must replace the `.app` bundle and may require operations `/Applications`. ([Velopack][20])

So Mac App Store means:

> Maintain another set of sandbox-specific build + Store updater.

Same problem as Windows MSIX.

The first stage is completely unnecessary.

---

# 20. The official version of macOS is professional enough

Officially supported by Apple:

```text
Website
+
Developer ID
+
Notarization
```

As a standard distribution method outside of the Mac App Store. ([Apple Developer][21])

User downloads:

```text
ArcChat.pkg
```

Gatekeeper can verify:

> Developer ID
> Apple Notarized

The experience is already at the level of formal commercial software.

---

# 21. Cost of macOS

To use:

* Developer ID;
* Notarization;

Requires Apple Developer Program.

Current:

# `$99 / year`

Moreover, this membership is also required for the ArcChat iOS version in the future, so it is not just an additional payment for the desktop. ([Apple Developer][22])

---

# 22. Linux: AppImage as the first official format

Linux I choose:

# **AppImage**

The reason is very practical:

* Not bundled with Debian;
* Not bundled with Ubuntu;
* Not bound to Fedora;
* No system-wide package manager is required;
* Works great with NativeAOT/self-contained;
* Velopack can be generated directly;
* You can also update yourself.

Velopack officially uses self-updating `.AppImage` on Linux. ([Velopack][23])

For example:

```text
ArcChat-linux-x64.AppImage
```

And in the future:

```text
ArcChat-linux-arm64.AppImage
```

---

# 23. Flatpak is not recommended in the first stage

The Flatpak itself is very good.

But it defaults to Sandbox:

* Cannot see the normal Host file;
* Processes outside the Sandbox cannot be seen;
* The device cannot be accessed by default;
* D-Bus and system resource access are restricted. ([Flatpak][24])

This is useful for:

### ArcNotes

The problem is relatively minor.

But for:

### ArcChat

Requires Local Agent + other Apps.

### ArcScope

May require serial port, USB, device node.

A lot of Flatpak permissions / portals will be needed.

Therefore:

> In the first stage, it is not worthwhile to make all apps Flatpak in order to "support a Linux store".

In the future, we will do this separately for suitable products:

```text
ArcNotes Flatpak
```

Absolutely.

---

# 24. Do not maintain DEB + RPM + Snap + Flatpak at the same time in the first stage.

Otherwise a Release:

```text
Windows EXE
Windows MSI
Windows MSIX
macOS PKG
macOS DMG
Ubuntu DEB
Fedora RPM
AppImage
Flatpak
Snap
```

You will find:

> The product has not been developed much, and the installer is being repaired every day.

First stage:

```text
Windows → Setup.exe
macOS   → PKG
Linux   → AppImage
```

enough.

# 25. GitHub Actions is the correct "packaging factory"

So to answer your original question:

> "Can I package it on GitHub or send it to Microsoft Store?"

It's not really a choice.

Correct structure:

```text
GitHub Actions
       ↓
Build / Test
       ↓
Native AOT publish
       ↓
Velopack package
       ↓
Code Sign / Notarize
       ↓
Release Artifacts
       │
       ├── R2
       ├── GitHub Releases
       ├── Microsoft Store submission
       └── WinGet manifest
```

GitHub is:

# Build/Release Automation Platform

Microsoft Store is:

# Distribution Channel

Completely two different levels.

---

# 26. Mac Runner must be used for macOS packaging

Velopack can generate Windows/Linux packages across systems, but macOS packages depend on:

* `codesign`
* `xcrun`
* `productbuild`

Must be generated in macOS environment. ([Velopack][25])

So CI Matrix:

```text
windows runner
→ Windows Native AOT + package + sign

macos runner
→ macOS Native AOT + package + sign + notarize

linux runner
→ Linux Native AOT + AppImage
```

This is also the most reliable mode.

# 27. Each App must have an independent Release life cycle

This is consistent with your product architecture.

Cannot:

```text
ArcForges 1.4
```

All apps must then be updated together.

Should:

```text
ArcChat  1.5.2
ArcNotes 2.1.0
ArcScope 1.3.7
ArcSlate 0.9.0
```

Each one:

* Independent installation;
* Independent uninstall;
* Independent updates;
* Standalone Release Notes;
* Standalone Stable/Beta;
* Independent Store listing.

ArcChat does not become an installation manager for other apps.

For example:

# 32. Each Release must form a unified Release Record

The true source of truth for the entire system going forward:

```text
Release

Product
```

# 33. All Release Artifacts must be verifiable

Because ArcForges is an open source project, this is especially worth doing well.

GitHub Artifact Attestations can be created for Release binary:

cryptographic provenance between, and public repo can use Sigstore public transparency log. ([GitHub Docs][27])

```text
SHA256SUMS
```

Windows:

I recommend to regular users:

# 37. Delta Update is very suitable for large apps like ArcSlate

Velopack will automatically generate:

```text
full package
delta package
```

And if:

* Too many deltas;
* The sum of Delta is greater than Full;
* Delta application failed;

Will automatically fallback to Full package. ([Velopack][29])

This is very suitable for larger volumes in the future:

* ArcSlate;
* ArcImage;
* Native dependencies.

# 38. How to deal with Critical Security Update

This must be designed in advance.

For example, a version:

> Remote Agent has a critical authentication vulnerability.

Older versions cannot be allowed to permanently connect to the Cloud.

The correct way is:

```text
Local Application
Still able to launch and use local features

Cloud:
MinimumSupportedVersion = 1.5.2
```

Old client connection:

```text
Your version is no longer supported for ArcForges Cloud.
Update to continue using Cloud services.
```

Restrictions only:

* Cloud Sync
* Remote Agent
* Managed AI
* Cloud BYOK

Unable to upgrade due to Cloud security:

> Users cannot even open local ArcNotes.

This is consistent with the entire Local-first business model above.

# 39. You must wait for all channels to be updated before forcing Cloud Minimum Version

The Microsoft Store in particular has certification and release delays.

So the release order must be:

```text
Build
 ↓
R2
 ↓
GitHub
 ↓
Store certification
 ↓
WinGet
 ↓
Confirm that main channels are available
 ↓
Only improve at the end MinimumSupportedVersion
```

Otherwise:

> Store users are asked by Cloud to update, but the Store does not have a new version yet.

This must be prohibited.

---

# 40. Bad versions must be Haltable immediately

Release system requires:

```text
Draft
Testing
Available
RollingOut
Stable
Halted
Deprecated
```

If `1.5.0` goes terribly wrong:

```text
Halt 1.5.0
```

Updater is no longer available to new users.

---

# 41. Rollback must also be reserved

Velopack currently explicitly supports:

> downgrade to a lower version.

If the latest version of the feed is lower than the installed version and downgrade is allowed, you can download the Full package to fallback. ([Velopack][30])

But for actual production, I recommend:

### General questions

Send immediately:

```text
1.5.1
```

Revert the 1.5.0 code.

### extremely serious problem

Only use server-directed rollback.

Avoid version history clutter.

---

# 42. Failure to update cannot destroy user data

This must become a hard rule:

# An Executable Directory is never a User Data Directory.

Velopack Windows update will replace the entire `current` directory; macOS/Linux will also replace App Bundle/AppImage. ([Velopack][29])

Therefore:

```text
Application binaries
```

with:

```text
Documents
Settings
Database
Logs
Credentials
Workspace
```

There must be complete separation.

---

# 43. Uninstall cannot delete user data by default.

User:

> Uninstall ArcNotes

Should be removed:

* Binary
* App shortcut
* Updater
* Installer metadata

But keep:

* Notes
* Projects
* User files

Can additionally provide:

> Also remove local application data

Explicitly checked by the user.

---

# 44. Cross-version data migration must be independent of the installer

Updater:

> Only responsible for installing new versions.

App starts a new version for the first time:

```text
DataSchema 4
→ DataSchema 5
```

Managed by the app itself.

And:

# Migration must consider rollback compatibility.

At least:

* Backup first;
* destructive migration clear version boundary;
* The data cannot be turned into a state that cannot be opened in the previous version due to an update failure.

This is not the installer's responsibility.

---

# 50. Microsoft Store does not serve as a commercial payment system

The design of stages 3 and 4 continues here:

Store App:

# Free

After downloading:

* Local functionality free;
* The user already has an ArcForges Account and can log in;
* Cloud Entitlement still comes from ArcForges;
* Billing is still from Waffo Web.

Microsoft Store is just:

# Distribution.

It does not enter:

```text
Billing
Subscription
Entitlement
```

This keeps the entire business system very clean.

The Microsoft Store also currently explicitly allows PC apps to use their own commerce platform, so the separation itself aligns with its PC Store distribution model. ([Microsoft Learn][32])

---

# 51. Core domain concepts that must be possessed in stage 5

The subsequent system must at least express:

```text
ProductRelease

ReleaseVersion
ReleaseChannel
ReleaseStatus

Platform
Architecture
PackageFormat

ReleaseArtifact

DownloadArtifact
UpdateArtifact

PackageIdentity

SigningIdentity
SigningStatus
NotarizationStatus

ArtifactHash
ArtifactAttestation
SBOM

MinimumOSVersion
MinimumCloudVersion

UpdatePolicy

UpdateFeed

DistributionChannel
├── Website
├── GitHub
├── MicrosoftStore
├── WinGet
├── AppStore
└── GooglePlay

StoreSubmission
StoreSubmissionStatus

Rollout

ReleaseNote

CompatibilityRange
```

It still does not mean creating a database table with these names.

Instead:

> The entire Release System must express these facts.

---

# 52. Stage 5 Scenarios that must be completely tested

Before going online, verify at least:

### Install

1. Fresh Windows install.
2. Ordinary Windows users do not have administrator rights.
3. Microsoft Store install.
4. WinGet install.
5. macOS signed/notarized install.
6. Linux clean AppImage.
7. x64.
8. ARM64.

### Update

9. Stable → Stable.
10. Stable → Beta.
11. Beta → Stable.
12. Full update.
13. Delta update.
14. Delta failed fallback Full.
15. Updates while the app is running.
16. Updates when multiple Arc Apps are running simultaneously.
17. The computer restarts during the update.
18. The network is disconnected.
19. Update package hash error.
20. Update feed is temporarily unavailable.

### Failure

21. Bad version of Halt.
22. Rollback.
23. The new version failed to start.
24. Data migration failed.
25. Disk full.
26. Antivirus lock file.
27. macOS notarization failure.
28. Certificate expired/renewal.
29. Release signing key compromise.

### Compatibility

30. OS is too old.
31. Schema error.
32. Cloud minimum version.
33. Cloud updates cannot be forced when the Store version has not yet been reviewed.

### Uninstall/Reinstall

34. Uninstall retained data.
35. Reinstall recognizes old data.
36. Deletion of all data is explicitly confirmed.
37. Uninstalling multiple apps does not affect each other.

# Stage 5 Finalization

I think the most suitable solution for ArcForges is:

> **GitHub Actions takes care of building and publishing.**
>
> **GitHub Repo continues to be the authoritative source for open source code.**
>
> **GitHub Releases stores official Release images and provenance.**
>
> **Cloudflare R2 + `downloads.arcforges.com` / `updates.arcforges.com` become official binaries and update CDN.**
>
> **For Windows/macOS/Linux, choose Velopack.**
>
> **Windows uses signed `Setup.exe` and publishes on the official website, Microsoft Store Win32 listing, WinGet and GitHub.**
>
> **Store MSIX is not used in the first stage to avoid the generation of a second Windows packaging/update system.**
>
> **Windows official Release must be signed with Authenticode; the Individual Code Signing route is used in the mainland individual stage, and will be migrated to ArcForges Organization signing identity after the company is established in the future.**
>
> **macOS is distributed directly from the official website `.pkg`, Developer ID + Apple Notarization; it will not enter the Mac App Store yet.**
>
> **Linux uses self-updating AppImage and does not maintain Flatpak/Snap/DEB/RPM in the first phase.**
>
> **Each Arc App has independent installation, independent version, and independent update; the so-called "Family Bucket" will only make a thin Bootstrapper in the future, and will not classify all Apps into a single entity.**
>
> **Stable / Beta / Development three-tier release.**
>
> **Ordinary updates do not block the use of local software; Cloud can require Minimum Client Version only when there are security compatibility requirements.**
>
> **Release Artifact is forever immutable and comes with SHA256, signatures, SBOM and GitHub build provenance.**
>
> **The client always gets updates through `updates.arcforges.com`, and it is unknown whether the underlying layer is R2, GitHub or other storage in the future.**

The biggest advantage of this solution is: ** open source, direct installation from the official website, Microsoft Store, WinGet, changing CDN in the future, setting up a company in the future and changing the signature identity will not force you to rewrite the application installation and update system.**

# stage6

---

Now entering **Stage 6: ArcChat serves as the entrance to the entire ArcForges ecosystem**.

At this stage, I think we need to resolve a fundamental issue first:

# ArcChat should be more than just "Avalonia for AionUi"

It should end up being:

> **ArcForges' local Agent Command Center / AI Operating Surface.**
>
> Users can use it as a normal AI Chat or hand it a "target"; ArcChat then schedules professional applications such as ArcNotes, ArcScope, and ArcSlate to complete tasks based on the current Project, installed Arc Apps, permissions, models, and device status.

This has an inheritance relationship with the direction of AionUi, but ArcForges has an extra layer of core advantages that AionUi does not have:

> **Your professional apps are first-class citizens in their own right, and each is an independent and complete product.**

Therefore, the design of ArcChat should be built around "**Unified entrance → Find the most suitable professional capabilities → Scheduling → Tracking → Deliver results → Return to professional App**" instead of constantly cramming all professional functions into Chat.

---

# 1. I first completely studied the current AionUi

The current main branch of AionUi has developed to `2.1.38`, the Changelog date is **2026-07-20**, and functions such as task-oriented prompts, Agent/Assistant search, Skill search, and Cron queue protection have been rapidly added recently. In other words, it is still a rapidly evolving Agent Desktop product and is not suitable for copying the current UI screen by screen.

It is no longer an ordinary Chat Client. Its core capabilities include:

* Built-in Agent;
* File reading and writing, Web, tool calling;
* A large number of external agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.;
* Parallel Agent;
* Team Mode;
* MCP;
* Skills;
* Scheduled Tasks;
* WebUI/remote;
* File Workspace;
* Artifact Preview;
* Extension System.

AionUi itself now clearly calls the product **Cowork platform, not chat client**.

Its Extension can already contribute ACP Adapter, MCP Server, Skill, Channel Plugin, Theme, Assistant, Settings and other content.

The Hub Catalog further expresses contribution types such as ACP Adapter, MCP, Assistant, Agent, Skill, Channel, WebUI, Theme, and Model Provider.

Therefore, the most valuable thing about AionUi that ArcChat can learn from is not its Electron UI, but:

> **The product idea of "an Agent Host can bring together Agent, Tools, Skills, Remote, Workspace, and Automation into one portal".**

---

# 2. But ArcChat should not directly copy the five things of AionUi

This is one of the most important trade-offs in Stage 6.

## 1. Do not turn "more than 20 Assistants" into the core of the product

AionUi currently has 21 built-in professional assistants, including PPT, Word, Excel, Academic Paper, Financial Model, etc.

ArcForges should not go:

```text
Cowork
Researcher
PPT Agent
Video Agent
Note Agent
Telemetry Agent
Image Agent
...
```

This Assistant Zoo.

Because you already have:

```text
ArcNotes
ArcSlate
ArcScope
ArcImage
...
```

These are truly professional applications.

ArcChat should be:

> **A small number of Agent Profiles + a large number of professional App Capabilities.**

More on that later.

---

## 2. Do not copy AionUi's "preview/edit all files by yourself"

AionUi's current Preview Panel already supports PDF, Word, Excel, PPT, code, Markdown, HTML, pictures, Diff, and supports multi-tab pages, editing and historical versions.

This makes sense for AionUi.

But ArcForges already has a professional app.

So ArcChat should use:

# **Thin Preview + Rich Handoff**

For example:

```text
Agent create ArcNotes Documentation

ArcChat
┌────────────────────────────┐
│ technical analysis report                │
│ [Brief preview]                  │
│                            │
│ Open in ArcNotes →         │
└────────────────────────────┘
```

instead of:

> Implement an ArcNotes editor in ArcChat.

The same goes for videos.

ArcSlate output:

```text
Task output
Video Project
Duration 04:32
3 clips modified

Open in ArcSlate →
```

ArcChat is only responsible for:

> See, understand, follow, jump.

Professional editors always come back to professional apps.

---

## 3. Do not use YOLO / Full Auto as the default experience

AionUi currently explicitly provides YOLO Mode / Full-Auto, which can bypass Agent permission prompts in one go.

Advanced users will appreciate this capability.

But ArcChat is the Agent Center of the entire desktop ecosystem. In the future, it may:

```text
Delete Notes
Modify Slate Project
control equipment
Send external content
remote operation
```

Therefore you cannot put:

> Allow Everything

Default as normal user.

Should make a real **Risk-aware Agent Permission System**.

Detailed later.

---

## 4. Do not use chat channels such as Telegram / Feishu / DingTalk / WeChat as the main route

AionUi currently supports remote channels such as WebUI, Telegram, Feishu, DingTalk, and WeChat.

But you've already determined:

> **ArcChat Mobile is the official mobile companion.**

So the ArcForges first-party experience should:

```text
ArcChat Mobile
        ↓
ArcForges Cloud
        ↓
Desktop ArcChat
```

This compares to:

```text
Telegram
WeChat robot
Feishu Robot
```

Taking care of security authorization, task steering and agent approval is cleaner.

These can later serve as connectors.

But not the core remote portal to ArcChat.

---

## 5. Do not regard "supporting dozens of CLI Agents" as the core selling point

AionUi currently supports a large number of Agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot, Cursor Agent, Qwen Code, etc., and uses ACP and other methods for unified interfaces.

ArcChat can support it.

However:

# **It should be Advanced Integration, not ArcChat's Product Center.**

The biggest difference between ArcChat should be:

> **Built-in Arc Agent + ArcForges App Ecosystem**

instead of:

> The most comprehensive CLI Agent Launcher.

---

# 3. ArcChat final product positioning

I suggest it be formally settled as:

# **ArcChat = Chat + Agent + Task Center + App Capability Hub**

Four identities.

```text
                     ArcChat
                        │
       ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
       │                │                │
      Chat             Agent           Tasks
       │                │                │
Normal AI dialogue   Complete a full goal   Background task management
                        │
                        ▼
                 Arc Capability Hub
                        │
       ┌────────────────┼─────────────────┐
       │                │                 │
    ArcNotes         ArcScope          ArcSlate ...
```

But users do not need to understand these schemas.

What the user sees should be very simple:

> **Ask something or get something done.**

---

# 4. What logic should the main interface of ArcChat look like?

I recommend that first level navigation ends up with only:

```text
Home

Projects

Tasks

Automations

Apps

----------------

Recent Chats
Pinned Chats

----------------

Account
Settings
```

Do not create more than twenty first-level menus.

---

# 5. Home is the real "ArcForges entrance"

Open ArcChat:

The center is not empty Chat History.

should be:

```text
              What do you want to do?

 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Ask or describe a task...                 │
 │                                           │
 │ +  @Context        Chat / Agent      ↑    │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────┘


      Suggested from your ArcForges apps

  Analyze latest ArcScope session

  Summarize today's ArcNotes

  Continue yesterday's report

  Organize these files
```

The latest version of AionUi has also begun to add task-oriented default prompts, indicating that it is also developing from a "chat entrance" to a "task entrance".

---

# 6. I suggest retaining two clear modes

## Chat

Normal conversation:

```text
explain this problem
summarize this text
Discussion plan
```

App operations with side effects will not be generated by default.

---

# Agent

The user expresses the goal:

```text
Analysis of last night ArcScope abnormal data,
Organize the conclusion into ArcNotes report.
```

ArcChat:

```text
Understand
    ↓
Plan
    ↓
Use Apps
    ↓
Execute
    ↓
Deliver
```

Anthropic's current Claude also puts Chat and Cowork in the same Home, and you can choose to enter a normal conversation or a complete Agent task through the mode; Cowork will plan, split tasks, display progress, and allow users to steer midway. ([Claude Help Center][1])

This mode is perfect for ArcChat.

---

# 7. Automation should not become the third Composer Mode

I do not recommend:

```text
Chat | Agent | Automation
```

This is getting more and more complicated.

Automation is:

> How Agent Tasks are executed.

For example:

```text
every morning 9 point analysis ArcScope Last night's data.
```

After Agent understands:

> Create Automation?

Then enter Automation.

---

# 8. A Project concept must be established

But note:

Stage 1 already exists:

# Workspace

It means:

> Cloud data ownership boundaries.

So definitely do not call it Workspace anymore.

I recommend calling it in ArcChat:

# **Project**

For example:

```text
Project: ArcScope Device Research
```

Instead of copying all the data in Project, save it:

```text
Instructions

Context references

ArcNotes notebook reference

ArcScope project/session reference

ArcSlate project reference

Local folder references

Relevant conversations

Relevant tasks
```

---

# 9. Project should be a "reference collection", not a second data warehouse

This is key to avoiding huge data chaos later on.

Do not:

```text
ArcScope data
→ copy Arrive ArcChat

ArcNotes
→ copy Arrive ArcChat
```

Instead:

```text
ArcChat Project
       │
       ├── Reference → ArcNotes Notebook
       ├── Reference → ArcScope Session
       ├── Reference → ArcSlate Project
       └── Reference → Local Folder
```

Each App is always its own data authority.

ArcChat is just:

> Context Orchestrator.

Claude Cowork currently also introduces Projects, using independent files, context, instructions, and memory to organize long-term tasks. ([Claude Help Center][2])

But ArcForges should go further:

> **Project can reference objects from other professional apps, instead of everything turning into Chat files.**

---

# 10. Apps cannot just "register Tools"

This is the most worthwhile place for you to design completely in advance.

An Arc App should contribute at least six things to ArcChat.

# 1. Actions

Operations for human use.

For example ArcScope:

```text
Start Capture

Open Latest Session

Export Report
```

Users can call it directly from the Command Palette.

---

# 2. Agent Capabilities

It is used by Agent and may not be directly displayed to ordinary users.

For example:

```text
QuerySignalRange

FindAnomalies

CompareSessions

GenerateTelemetryReport
```

---

# 3. Context Providers

Tell ArcChat:

> What the current user is looking at.

For example:

```text
ArcScope
CurrentSession
SelectedChannels
SelectedTimeRange
```

ArcNotes:

```text
CurrentDocument
CurrentSelection
CurrentNotebook
```

---

# 4. Artifact Handlers

What results can the app handle.

For example:

```text
ArcNotes:
NoteDocument

ArcSlate:
VideoProject
Timeline
Clip

ArcScope:
TelemetrySession
Report
```

In this way, the Agent knows after getting the Artifact:

> Which app should be handed over to.

---

# 5. Suggested Tasks

For example, after installing ArcScope, Home appears automatically:

```text
Analyze latest telemetry

Compare two sessions

Create device report
```

This is much better than ArcChat hardcoding all the suggestions itself.

---

# 6. Deep Links / Open Targets

Agents can ultimately:

```text
Open this report in ArcNotes

Open this timestamp in ArcScope

Open this clip in ArcSlate
```

---

# 11. Here you can learn from a very good design of Raycast

Raycast clearly differentiates between:

### Command

Users can proactively discover and launch.

### Tool

The AI can be called, but does not necessarily appear in the normal command list. ([Raycast API][3])

Its AI Extension is also:

> After Extension adds tools, AI can understand and call these tools. ([Raycast API][4])

ArcChat should be further developed into:

```text
Arc App
│
├── Actions             User call
├── Agent Capabilities  Agentcall
├── Context Providers   giveAgentcontext
├── Artifacts            Professional objects
└── Suggested Tasks     Homediscover
```

This would be simpler than:

> "App exposes tools"

Much more complete.

---

# 12. Capability must be richer in description than ordinary Tool

At least in a product sense, each Capability must describe:

| information                   | Purpose             |
| -------------------- | -------------- |
| Identity             | unique ability identity         |
| Description          | Agent understands when to use |
| Inputs               | what is needed           |
| Outputs              | What to return           |
| Read/Write           | Whether to modify data         |
| Destructive          | Is it possible to corrupt data?       |
| Idempotent           | Is it safe to repeat?       |
| Undoable             | Whether it can be undone          |
| Long Running         | Is it a long-term mission?         |
| Cancellable          | Is it possible to cancel          |
| Requires UI          | Do I have to open the app?     |
| Background           | Can it be done in the background?       |
| Local/Remote         | where can it be executed        |
| Required App Version | Compatibility            |
| Required Entitlement | Do you need Cloud     |
| Permission Class     | Permission level           |

This is not a code implementation detail.

This is the **product agreement** of whether ArcChat can truly reliably schedule dozens of apps.

---

# 13. MCP has now proven that this metadata is very important

The current stable MCP specification already has Tool Annotations:

* `readOnlyHint`
* `destructiveHint`
* `idempotentHint`
* `openWorldHint`

and concepts such as Tool Task Support. ([Model Context Protocol][5])

But MCP officials are very clear at the same time:

> These annotations are just hints; if the server is not trusted, the host cannot treat these statements as security guarantees. ([Model Context Protocol Blog][6])

Therefore ArcChat should:

### ArcForges Official App

Its signature and Capability Metadata:

> can be considered a credible statement.

### Third-party MCP

Metadata:

> Just as a reminder.

Actual permissions are still determined by ArcChat itself.

---

# 14. Capability must have Trust Level

I recommend being there from day one:

```text
Official ArcForges

Verified Third Party

Local Developer

Remote / Untrusted
```

Risk strategies are different.

For example:

```text
Official ArcNotes
readOnly=true
```

ArcChat can automatically allow this if appropriate.

A casually installed MCP Server claims:

```text
readOnly=true
```

This does not allow full permissions to be obtained.

---

# 15. The order of Agent calling must be formally determined.

This is particularly important.

# First priority: Native Arc Capability

For example:

```text
Need to modify ArcNotes
→ ArcNotes capability
```

Instead of mouse clicking the ArcNotes UI.

---

# Second priority: Trusted Connector/MCP/API

For example:

```text
GitHub
Google Drive
Web API
```

---

# Third priority: Computer Use

There's really no API:

```text
Screen recognition
Click
keyboard
```

Only used.

Anthropic's current Cowork computer-use strategy also selects the most accurate tool first; when a connector exists, the Connector is given priority, and the screen is directly manipulated last. ([Claude Help Center][7])

The same principle should apply to ArcChat.

---

# 16. Computer Use is allowed, but it should not be used as the V1 core.

In the future, of course:

```text
control no Arc integration software
browser automation
Old professional software
```

This will take ArcChat beyond ArcForges App.

However:

> Computer Use is more fragile, harder to verify, and more prone to Prompt Injection and misoperation than Structured Capability.

So it should belong to:

# Advanced Fallback

Not ArcChat core architecture.

---

# 17. Permission system: ArcChat must be stricter than AionUi

I propose to formally define five levels of risk.

| level | Type                | Default         |
| -- | ----------------- | ---------- |
| R0 | Read/Query           | automatic         |
| R1 | reversible local modifications          | Allowed within Task   |
| R2 | Delete, overwrite, irreversibly modify       | Must confirm       |
| R3 | Send/publish/affect the external world    | Must confirm and preview    |
| R4 | Credentials, security, system-level, high-risk device operations | Strong confirmation / local confirmation |

---

# 18. Specific examples

## R0

```text
Search ArcNotes

Read ArcScope session

Inspect video metadata
```

Normally it can be executed automatically.

---

## R1

```text
Create a new ArcNote

Add a new non-destructive marker
```

Can:

> Allow for this task

---

## R2

```text
Delete Note

Overwrite project

Delete file
```

Confirm every time.

Claude Cowork also currently requires explicit user authorization before files can be permanently deleted. ([Claude Help Center][1])

---

## R3

```text
Publish
Send Email
Post content
Upload public file
```

You must first:

# Preview → Confirm → Execute

---

## R4

```text
Change credential
Install system component
Modify security configuration
High-risk device operation
```

This machine strongly confirms.

Remote is not approved by default.

---

# 19. The scope of Allow cannot be only Yes / No

Users should be able to:

```text
Allow once

Allow for this task

Always allow this capability
```

But:

> Always Allow

Open to low risk capabilities only.

R2/R3/R4 should not be allowed to be permanently approved by the average user without thinking.

---

# 20. Do not move AionUi YOLO over as is

Advanced settings may include:

# Autonomous Mode

But its essence should be:

> Permission Policy

For example:

```text
Automatically approve R0/R1
Still ask R2+
```

instead of:

> All operations are allowed.

---

# 21. Task must become a first-class object of ArcChat

This is the biggest difference between ArcChat and ordinary Chat.

User:

```text
Analyze all device anomalies yesterday,
```

# 25. Task must support Partial Success

This is a very easily overlooked aspect of cross-App Agent.

For example:

```text
ArcScope Analysis     Done

ArcNotes Report       Done

ArcSlate Export       Failed
```

The task cannot just be:

```text
Failed
```

should show:

# Partially Completed

And provide:

```text
Retry ArcSlate step

Open ArcNotes result

Undo completed changes
```

Because it is impossible for cross-process apps to truly perform database-style ACID transactions.

Products must be accepted from day one:

> **Cross-App workflows are compensable transactions, not atomic transactions.**

# 41. There is a very important time now

As of today **2026-07-21**:

The latest official specification of MCP is still the 2025-11-25 series, and the next version `2026-07-28` is currently Release Candidate; it plans to add major changes such as new Stateless Core, Extensions, Tasks, MCP Apps, and there are breaking changes. ([Model Context Protocol Blog][10])

So:

> **Do not hard-bind the ArcChat core architecture to the 2026-07-28 MCP that has not yet been officially released.**

Correct strategy:

* Currently compatible with stable MCP;
* Capability The system itself supports long-running tasks;
* We will add the Adapter after the official version and SDK are stable on 7/28.

This avoids having to follow the breaking spec right after writing it.

# 77. There is another important legal amendment

You have always referred to AionUi as MIT.

But this time I checked directly the **current AionUi main branch**:

README Badge now targets:

# `Apache-2.0`

The current `LICENSE` file in the repository is also clearly:

# Apache License 2.0

So:

> **The current version can no longer be understood as an "MIT project".**

It's one thing if you do an independent C#/Avalonia rewrite and refer to the product idea itself; if you actually copy the current code, resources or other copyrighted content, you need to follow the terms of the current corresponding version of Apache-2.0.

It is best to correct your understanding now to avoid discovering that the license has changed when you release it later.

---

# Stage 6 Finalization

I think ArcChat should ultimately be defined as:

> **ArcForges' AI-native desktop command center.**
>
> **Chat is the communication interface; Agent is the execution engine; Task is the life cycle of the work; Project is the context; Apps are professional capabilities; Artifact is the final result.**

The core relationship is formalized as:

```text
                    User
                      │
                ┌─────┴─────┐
               Chat        Agent
                            │
                          Task
                            │
                     Capability Hub
                            │
           ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
           │                │                │
        ArcNotes         ArcScope         ArcSlate
           │                │                │
           └──────────── Artifacts ──────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
                          User
```

and adhere to these principles:

**ArcChat does not replicate professional apps.**

**Professional apps do not form hidden dependencies on each other.**

**Unify cross-app workflows with ArcChat.**

**Apps not only contribute Tools, but also Actions, Capabilities, Context, Artifacts, and Suggestions.**

**Project saves references rather than copying individual app data.**

**Task and Conversation are separated.**

**Artifact is not equal to file.**

**Agent operations must be visible, pauseable, steerable, and resumable.**

**Accept Partial Success across App Tasks and use Undo/Compensation instead of pretending to have cross-process atomic transactions.**

**Native Arc Capability > Trusted API/MCP > Computer Use.**

**Risk permissions are uniformly managed by ArcChat and do not use YOLO as the default.**

**ArcNotes is the long-term knowledge authority, ArcChat does not build a second knowledge base.**

**Arc Apps must be able to "Ask ArcChat" to form a two-way ecosystem.**

**ArcChat Mobile is a Remote Companion, not a mobile fork of the professional app.**

**Built-in Arc Agent is the main experience; ACP External Agents are advanced extensions.**

**MCP is an external ecological protocol, but it does not limit ArcForges' own stronger Native Capability Protocol.**

**ArcChat can become a backend hub, but it must let users know clearly when it is resident and when Remote/Automation is running.**

Once these are finalized, ArcChat is no longer just "a good open source AI Chat", but the **Agent operation layer** that truly has long-term differentiated value for the entire ArcForges.
