# stage7

---

Now entering **Stage 7: ArcForges Cloud Product Capabilities**.

This stage is very critical, because we have already decided on "how much Cloud charges", "what are the rights and interests", and "how ArcChat serves as the agent entrance". The answer now is:

> **After users purchase ArcForges Cloud, what exactly does the cloud provide? What is uploaded and what is not? How to sync? How to search? Where does the remote Agent run? What can continue after the computer is shut down? What is the relationship between Cloud BYOK and Managed AI? What should I do if I subscribe to expired data?**

If this layer is designed vaguely now, ArcNotes, ArcSlate, ArcScope, ArcChat Mobile, Web, and Remote Agent will all be reworked repeatedly later.

---

# 1. First determine the final positioning of ArcForges Cloud

ArcForges Cloud is **not "moving local software onto a server"**, nor is it simply Dropbox.

Ultimately it should be defined as:

# **ArcForges Cloud = Continuity + Sync + Remote Control Plane + Managed Services**

Four things:

```text
ArcForges Cloud
│
├── Continuity
│   Across devices, Web, Mobile, Task Status continuous
│
├── Sync & Recovery
│   Data synchronization, Version history, restore, cloud storage
│
├── Remote Agent
│   remote tasks, Equipment scheduling, Automation
│
└── Managed Services
    Cloud Search
    Cloud BYOK
    Managed AI
    Notifications
```

The most important principles remain:

> **ArcForges Cloud is never a prerequisite for running local software.**

Cloud is down:

```text
ArcNotes Local       normal
ArcScope Local       normal
ArcSlate Local       normal
ArcChat Local Agent  normal
Local BYOK           normal
Local AI             normal
```

Only:

```text
Sync
Remote
Cloud Search
Cloud BYOK
Managed Cloud Tasks
Web/Mobile continuity
```

affected.

---

# 2. What does the first version of Cloud Plan really sell?

We have already decided:

# `$5.99/month` / `$59/year`

Share:

# `50 GB`

Now you can download the V1 Cloud Bundle completely:

| Ability                           | ArcForges Local | ArcForges Cloud |
| ---------------------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| All desktop apps                     | free              | free              |
| Local Agent                  | free              | free              |
| Local BYOK                   | free              | free              |
| Local AI                     | free              | free              |
| Local Search / Vector        | free              | free              |
| Multi-device Sync                     | -               | **Yes**           |
| 50 GB Cloud Storage          | -               | **Yes**           |
| Version History              | -               | **Yes**           |
| Deleted Item Recovery        | -               | **Yes**           |
| Cloud Search                 | -               | **Yes**           |
| Cloud Vector Search          | -               | **Yes**           |
| ArcChat Web continuity       | -               | **Yes**           |
| ArcChat Mobile continuity    | -               | **Yes**           |
| Remote Desktop Agent         | -               | **Yes**           |
| Cloud Agent tasks            | -               | **Yes**           |
| Cloud Automations            | -               | **Yes**           |
| Cloud BYOK                   | -               | **Yes**           |
| Managed AI Monthly Allowance | -               | **Yes**           |
| Purchased AI Credits         | **Available**        | **Available**        |

This last one I suggest is formalized:

# **Purchased Arc AI Credits are not dependent on Cloud Subscription for survival.**

Users spent real money to purchase:

```text
$25 AI Credits
```

Later canceled Cloud:

> Credits cannot be voided as a result.

Users can still use Arc Managed AI in local ArcChat.

But after no Cloud Subscription:

```text
Cloud BYOK        Not available
Cloud Agent       Not available
Remote Agent      Not available
Web continuity    Not available
Monthly Allowance Never send again
```

This business boundary is very clean.

---

# 3. First solve the easiest thing to rework: Cloud cannot simply "synchronize the entire folder"

Never design ArcForges Sync to:

```text
App data directory
      ↓
Copy all to Cloud
```

This is the plan most likely to cause serious accidents later.

Because:

* ArcNotes are documents;
* ArcScope can produce a large number of telemetry;
* ArcSlate may have dozens of gigabytes of video;
* ArcChat has Conversation/Task;
* App also has cache, log, thumbnail, and index.

They are not the same data at all.

So there must be:

# **Sync Data Classification**

---

# 4. All Arc App data is divided into six categories from the first day

## 1. Canonical User Data

Source data that truly belongs to the user.

For example:

```text
ArcNotes Documents
ArcSlate Project
ArcScope Project
ArcChat Conversations
```

You can enter Sync.

---

## 2. Large User Assets

For example:

```text
Video
Audio
Images
Telemetry Raw Data
Large Attachments
```

Synchronization is possible but must:

# Selective Sync.

---

## 3. Derived Data

For example:

```text
Thumbnail
Waveform
Vector Embedding
Search Index
Preview
Transcode cache
```

Not authoritative user data.

Can:

> Regenerate after deletion.

Therefore it does not need to be synchronized as user data.

---

## 4. Device-local Data

For example:

```text
Window layout
GPU setting
Device path
Local cache
Recent local folder
```

Unable to sync.

---

## 5. Secrets

For example:

```text
Local BYOK key
Device private key
Local credential
```

Cannot enter normal Sync.

Cloud BYOK is another dedicated Secret Vault.

---

## 6. Ephemeral Data

For example:

```text
Temp files
Agent scratch
Logs
Render temp
Task working directory
```

Not part of Sync.

---

# 5. Therefore, ArcForges Cloud must establish a Sync Scope

The user is not:

> "ArcSlate has sync enabled = everything in ArcSlate is uploaded."

Instead:

```text
ArcSlate Project A
    ↓
Sync Scope
```

A Sync Scope should be able to have its own:

```text
Sync Enabled

Protection Mode

Large Asset Policy

Selective Sync Policy

Conflict Policy
```

---

# 6. The default synchronization strategies of different apps must be different.

## ArcChat

Can be synchronized by default:

```text
Conversations
Projects
Task state
Artifacts metadata
Automation definitions
Agent Profiles
User Skills
Selected settings
```

Out of sync:

```text
Local BYOK
Local model files
Device-local paths
Local Agent temp files
```

---

# 7. ArcNotes

Default:

```text
Notes
Documents
Metadata
Attachments
```

All allow synchronization.

This is the most typical Cloud Sync product.

---

# 8. ArcScope

Must be conservative here.

Default sync:

```text
Projects
Session metadata
Annotations
Analysis
Reports
Configurations
```

And:

# Raw Telemetry

Default:

> Local only.

The user explicitly turns on:

```text
Sync raw session data
```

Just uploaded.

Otherwise, a long acquisition session can quickly fill up 50GB.

---

# 9. ArcSlate

Not to mention that all media cannot be uploaded by default.

It is proposed to formally provide three levels:

### Project Only

```text
Timeline
Project metadata
Editing decisions
Text/subtitle
Small assets
```

### Project + Proxies

Added:

```text
Proxy media
```

Convenient for previewing on other devices.

### Full Media

Just uploaded:

```text
Original video/audio
```

Default:

# Project Only

This is the most reasonable.

---

# 10. Sync Scope and ArcChat Project are not the same concept

This must be separated now, otherwise the names will be confused in the future.

Stage 6:

# ArcChat Project

means:

> Agent Context/Work Topic.

Stage 7:

# Sync Scope

means:

> Which batch of App data participates in cloud synchronization.

For example:

```text
ArcChat Project
“Device Research”
│
├── references ArcNotes Notebook
├── references ArcScope Session
└── references ArcSlate Project
```

These three objects can each have different Sync states.

---

# 11. Cloud always uses stable Object Identity

Cannot rely on:

```text
C:\Projects\xxx
```

Identify cloud objects.

Because another device:

```text
/Users/Ryan/Documents/xxx
```

The path is completely different.

So all synchronizable objects must have:

# Stable Object Identity

Conceptually:

```text
Workspace
+
App
+
ObjectId
```

The path is just:

> Local Mapping on a Device.

This is also the basis for Stage 6 Artifact / Deep Link to work across devices.

---

# 12. ArcForges Sync should not uniformly adopt a conflict algorithm

This is another place where it's easy to over-design.

Do not decide:

> "We have everything CRDT."

Also do not:

> All Last-Write-Wins.

Different objects require different Conflict Policies.

---

## Append-only

For example:

```text
Task Events
Audit events
Conversation event log
```

Great for append-only.

---

## Mergeable

For example text:

```text
ArcNotes document
```

Real merge can be implemented in the future.

---

## Optimistic Revision

For example:

```text
Project configuration
Structured metadata
```

Use:

> Base Revision → New Revision.

---

## Conflict Copy / Branch

For example, a complex ArcSlate Project:

Devices A and B have both made modifications that cannot be merged safely:

Do not be silent:

> The one saved later overwrites the previous one.

Should:

```text
Conflict detected

Version from Ryan-PC
Version from MacBook

Review conflict
```

---

## Immutable Blob

For example:

```text
Video
Image
Audio
```

Save by content identity, there is no "modify the same blob in place".

---

# 13. Never Silent Last-Write-Wins User Content

I'll make this a hard rule:

# **Conflicts in user-created content cannot silently lose data.**

Even though the first version did not have advanced Merge:

> Create Conflict Version

All are better than coverage.

---

# 14. Sync status must be understandable to users

Every app should be able to see:

```text
Synced

Syncing

Offline

Local only

Conflict

Waiting for network

Storage full

Error
```

instead of:

> A green Cloud icon.

The settings should also include:

```text
Last successful sync
Current device
Pending uploads
Pending downloads
Conflicts
```

---

# 15. Version history officially added to Cloud V1

Here you can refer to a mature local-first product Obsidian Sync:

It explicitly separates Sync History and Version History and allows the recovery of old versions and deleted files; the current Standard plan retains Notes history for 1 month. ([Obsidian Help][1])

ArcForges First Edition I recommend:

# **30-day Version History**

and:

# **30-day Deleted Item Recovery**

This is a good enough launch spec that's easy enough to understand.

---

# 16. But Version History does not "copy the entire file"

For example ArcSlate:

```text
10GB source.mp4
```

Adjust Timeline:

MUST NOT produce:

```text
source-v1.mp4 10GB
source-v2.mp4 10GB
source-v3.mp4 10GB
```

Video footage should be an Immutable Blob.

The main version changes are:

```text
Project Revision
```

Still citing the same media.

This is the key to whether large professional apps can operate the Cloud for a long time.

---

# 17. How to calculate Storage Quota and decide now

50GB is:

# Workspace Shared Storage

Instead of 50GB per App.

For example:

```text
ArcNotes       4 GB
ArcChat        1 GB
ArcScope      10 GB
ArcSlate      25 GB
------------------
Total         40 GB / 50 GB
```

---

# 18. What counts towards 50GB

Should be taken into account:

```text
Canonical synced user data

Attachments

Original media

Explicitly stored proxies

Deleted items still in Trash

Historical user blobs that remain restorable
```

---

# 19. What is not included?

Generated by ArcForges itself:

```text
Vector index
Embeddings
Search index
Internal DB metadata
Thumbnails
Operational logs
Temporary Agent files
```

It should not consume the user's display credit.

Otherwise:

> The user clearly uploaded 40GB, but the system showed 47GB.

Very poor experience.

---

# 20. Storage UI must have categories

For example:

```text
Cloud Storage

41.2 / 50 GB

ArcSlate          27.4 GB
ArcScope           8.1 GB
ArcNotes           4.2 GB
ArcChat            1.5 GB

Versions & Trash   3.1 GB included above
```

Users can:

```text
Manage storage
```

Instead of not knowing where the space has gone.

---

# 21. Cloud Object Storage still recommends R2

Currently Cloudflare R2 is S3-compatible object storage, and the official currently clearly states that there is no Internet egress bandwidth fee for its object storage; Standard Storage is currently `$0.015/GB-month`. ([Cloudflare Docs][2])

In addition, R2 currently supports multipart upload, and a single object can reach the TiB level. Therefore, there is no principle obstacle to being used as the object layer of ArcSlate large media materials in the future. ([Cloudflare Docs][3])

However:

# ArcForges Cloud Storage abstraction cannot be called `R2Storage`.

Inside it should still be:

```text
ObjectStorage
```

Today:

> R2.

Later:

> B2 / S3 / Azure Blob.

Does not change product semantics.

---

# 22. Cloud Search cannot just "search ArcChat"

I recommend doing:

# **ArcForges Cloud Search**

Search:

```text
ArcChat Conversations

ArcNotes

ArcScope Reports / Metadata

ArcSlate Project metadata

Artifacts
```

Result:

```text
Title
Snippet
Source App
Object Type
Modified
Deep Link
```

Click:

```text
ArcNotes result
→ Open ArcNotes
```

---

# 23. Search indexes are definitely not the authority on data.

Formal relationship:

```text
ArcNotes Document
       │
       │ source of truth
       ▼
Search Document
       ↓
Full-text Index
       ↓
Vector Index
```

Any:

```text
Search Index
Vector Index
Embedding
```

All are:

# Derived Data

Can be deleted and recreated at any time.

It is very important to change the Vector Database in the future.

---

# 24. Cloud Search is divided into three levels

## Metadata Search

```text
Title
Tags
Date
Type
App
```

---

## Full-text Search

Normal text content search.

---

## Semantic Search

Using Embedding:

> "Find previous analysis on USB device jitter."

You can find it even if the original text does not contain exactly the same words.

Cloudflare's Vectorize is currently GA and is used in semantic search, similarity, classification and other scenarios. It can also associate the results back to real data objects such as R2. ([Cloudflare Docs][4])

It can be a good first implementation.

But:

> **The ArcForges Search API cannot expose Vectorize concepts.**

---

# 25. Cloud Search must be strictly Workspace scoped

Stage 1 has been determined:

> Agent Session has an explicit Active Workspace.

So Search must always be:

```text
WorkspaceId
```

as a strong boundary.

Cannot:

> When searching for Personal Workspace, look for Team Workspace.

Even if a user has permissions in both Workspaces, they cannot secretly cross boundaries.

---

# 26. Cloud Search must also respect the data policy of the App

For example:

```text
ArcScope raw telemetry
```

The user did not choose to upload:

> Cloud Search cannot search raw telemetry.

Not for Search:

> All local data is secretly uploaded in the background.

This is a commitment that Local-first products must make very clear.

---

# 27. The big problem of E2EE must be solved now

This is the most important issue in Stage 7 that needs to be decided in advance, otherwise it will have to be reworked later.

You also want:

```text
Cloud Semantic Search
Managed AI
Cloud Agent
Web Access
```

These services usually require a server that can handle the data.

However:

# Zero-knowledge E2EE

means:

> The server cannot see the clear text at all.

The two goals are naturally in conflict.

Obsidian Sync clearly distinguishes between E2EE and Standard Encryption, which manages keys on the server side; its documentation also directly states that zero-knowledge E2EE means that the service provider cannot read the data, and also loses the server's ability to directly process these contents. ([Obsidian Help][5])

---

# 28. So do not lie now and say "Cloud All Zero Knowledge"

ArcForges First Edition Recommendations:

# **Standard Protected Cloud**

That is:

```text
TLS in transit

Encryption at rest

Workspace isolation

Strict service authorization

Secret separation
```

This will provide:

```text
Web
Cloud Search
Semantic Indexing
Cloud Agent
Managed AI context
```

---

# 29. But reserve the second Protection Mode now

The concept must exist:

```text
Standard

EndToEndEncrypted
```

A Sync Scope can be selected in the future:

# E2EE

At this time the server only sees:

> opaque encrypted objects.

---

# 30. E2EE product restrictions must be very clear

E2EE Scope:

Can:

```text
Sync encrypted objects

Version encrypted objects

Download to trusted device
```

However:

```text
Server-side full-text search   Not available

Semantic search                Not available

Cloud-native Agent context     Not available

Cloud server preview           Not available
```

Still possible:

```text
Desktop Local Search

Desktop Local Agent

Remote Desktop Agent
```

Because Desktop owns the decryption key.

Join this way in the future:

# Private Sync

No need to tear down the entire Cloud again.

But:

# V1 does not have to release E2EE Mode.

Get the model right first.

---

# 31. There is another important principle: Sync and AI must be separated

For example, the user is in local ArcChat:

> Send `secret-report.pdf` to Arc Managed AI summary.

This should not mean:

> `secret-report.pdf` Automatically enter Cloud Sync.

Correct relationship:

```text
Local file
   ↓ explicit AI context
Managed AI inference
```

and:

```text
Local file
   ↓ explicit sync
Cloud Storage
```

are two completely independent things.

---

# 32. Product positioning of Managed AI

Managed AI in Cloud should be:

# **Arc Managed AI**

ArcForges is responsible for:

* Model provider access;
* Routing;
* Availability;
* Usage tracking;
* Arc AI Credits;
* Rate Limit;
* Fallback;
* User Privacy Policy.

Users do not need:

> Buy your own OpenAI API Key.

---

# 33. Model and Provider must be decoupled again

Do not write your commercial product as:

```text
Buy Claude Credits
```

Instead:

```text
Arc AI Credits
```

Model:

```text
GPT
Claude
Gemini
...
```

Just execute resources.

In this way, the price, model and provider can all be adjusted in the future.

---

# 34. Cloudflare AI Gateway is still very suitable as the first unified AI Gateway

As of now, Cloudflare AI Gateway already supports analytics, logging, rate limiting, caching, retry, fallback and other controls, and will add Dynamic Routing and unified AI REST API in 2026. ([Cloudflare Docs][6])

Therefore, the direction determined in the previous stage 0 continues to be valid:

```text
ArcForges AI Control
        ↓
Cloudflare AI Gateway
        │
        ├── OpenAI
        ├── Anthropic
        ├── Google
        ├── Workers AI
        └── other providers
```

But still:

> Cloudflare is Infrastructure, not an ArcForges product model.

---

# 35. Workers AI is more suitable for background abilities

Workers AI is currently Cloudflare's serverless GPU inference platform. ([Cloudflare Docs][7])

More suitable for ArcForges use in:

```text
Embeddings

Reranking

Classification

STT / background transforms

Cheap small-model jobs
```

And the real flagship Agent:

> Choose a Frontier Provider based on cost, quality, and availability.

No need to shoehorn all AI into Workers AI.

---

# 36. Be very careful with AI Gateway logs

The formal product strategy for ArcForges should be:

# **Operational metadata can be recorded, Raw Prompt Content is minimized by default.**

Need to save:

```text
Request ID
Model
Provider
Tokens
Latency
Credits
Error
TaskId
WorkspaceId
```

And not for debugging:

> Permanently save all user prompts/responses.

The real Conversation History has been taken care of by ArcChat itself.

The AI Gateway log is just:

> Observability.

Cloudflare AI Gateway currently does offer observability capabilities such as cost, logs, and OpenTelemetry. ([Cloudflare Docs][8])

---

# 37. Cloud BYOK is another path to Managed AI

Formal relationship:

```text
ArcChat
│
├── Local BYOK
│      Client → Provider
│      Free
│
├── Cloud BYOK
│      ArcForges Cloud → Provider
│      Requires Cloud
│
└── Arc Managed AI
       ArcForges credentials
       AI Credits
```

The three must not be mixed.

---

# 38. Cloud BYOK Secret Vault must have these product requirements

Key:

```text
Belong to Workspace

The full text cannot be redisplayed after saving.

OK Replace

OK Revoke

OK Test

can be displayed fingerprint / last 4

Yes Last Used

Yes Audit
```

Never:

```text
GET /apikey
→ Return clear text
```

---

# 39. Cloud BYOK does not increase the price of Token

This has been fixed before and will continue to be fixed now.

User:

> Bear the Provider Token cost yourself.

ArcForges receives:

> Cloud Subscription.

Do not:

```text
BYOK token
+ ArcForges markup
```

This is a strong product selling point.

---

# 40. Remote Agent must now be split into three Execution Modes

This is one of Stage 7's most important Cloud abilities.

# 1. Desktop Execution

For example:

```text
Analyze ArcScope session

Edit ArcSlate project
```

Real execution:

# Ryan Desktop

Cloud is only responsible for:

```text
Task State

Command Relay

Mobile/Web Control

Notification
```

Desktop must be online.

---

# 41. 2. Cloud Execution

For example:

```text
Search synced ArcNotes

Research web

Summarize Cloud Documents

Call Cloud APIs

Generate report
```

Can:

# ArcForges Cloud

Execute directly.

The computer can be shut down completely.

---

# 42. 3. Hybrid Execution

For example:

```text
Analyze web data every day
+
Finally written to the local machine ArcScope project
```

Possible:

```text
Cloud steps
     ↓
Waiting for Ryan Desktop
     ↓
Desktop step
```

This is:

# Hybrid Task.

---

# 43. Users must always know where tasks are performed

Task Details:

```text
Execution

Cloud
```

Or:

```text
Execution

Ryan Desktop
Windows
```

Or:

```text
Hybrid

Cloud + Ryan Desktop
```

Cannot be blurry.

---

# 44. This model has been proven to be very important by real products

Claude Cowork currently has a clear distinction between:

* Remote session can continue to run on the server, even if the computer is turned off;
* When local files, local connectors, and browser/computer use are required, the Desktop App needs to be online. ([Claude Help Center][9])

Anthropic even makes another distinction between Dispatch: sending tasks from the mobile phone, but actually executing them on the Desktop, so the Desktop must remain online. ([Claude Help Center][10])

ArcForges should model this Execution Location clearly from the beginning, rather than patching it up later.

---

# 45. Remote Desktop cannot be implemented through open ports

Do not:

```text
Internet
→ PC:8732
```

This design.

Correct mode:

```text
ArcChat Desktop
      ↓
Take the initiative to establish authenticated outbound connection
      ↓
ArcForges Cloud Relay
      ↑
Mobile/Web
```

User PC:

# The public internet port is not open.

---

# 46. Remote Access default Off

Stage 1 has been decided, continue to be fixed:

User clear:

```text
Enable Remote Access
```

Talent:

* Register Device;
* Create Channel;
* Accept remote tasks;
* Receive approval.

Close:

> Cloud cannot perform tasks to this Device immediately.

---

# 47. Device Presence is also a formal capability of Cloud

Mobile:

```text
Ryan Desktop

Online
Last seen now

ArcChat 1.5.2

Remote enabled

ArcNotes Ready
ArcScope Ready
ArcSlate Offline
```

These are not permanent data, just:

# Presence.

---

# 48. Do not Task Failed when the device is offline

For example:

```text
Run on Ryan Desktop
```

But the computer is off.

Status:

# `WaitingForDevice`

# Stage 7 Finalization

ArcForges Cloud should not be defined as:

> **"50GB network disk + AI."**

Instead it should be formally defined as:

# **The continuity and remote execution layer of ArcForges.**

That is:

> **Local software is always the first citizen; Cloud is responsible for connecting devices, data, agents and services.**

Finally fixed:

**Cloud does not take over local.**

**The end of Cloud Subscription never affects Local Software.**

**50GB is Workspace shared Cloud Storage.**

**Different apps use different Sync Policies, and the entire directory will never be uploaded carelessly.**

**ArcSlate/ArcScope big data defaults to selective sync.**

**Sync does not use global Last-Write-Wins.**

**Conflict always prioritizes data preservation.**

**30-day Version History + 30-day Deleted Recovery.**

**Search Index and Vector Index are always just Derived Data.**

**Cloud Search is strictly Workspace scoped.**

**Standard Protected Cloud is V1; E2EE mode is reserved now and will be released later.**

**Sync and AI Context are completely independent, and using AI does not mean automatically uploading files.**

**Cloud Task is clearly divided into Desktop/Cloud/Hybrid.**

**Desktop connects to the Cloud through outbound authenticated connection and does not expose a public internet port.**

**Cloud Agent Runtime is not a VPS.**

**Cloud Automation must have execution location, budget, concurrency, and Missed Run Policy.**

**ArcChat Web is a Cloud Surface and does not replicate ArcNotes/ArcSlate.**

**ArcChat Mobile is Companion.**

**Cloud BYOK requires Cloud Subscription, but BYOK Token does not charge a commission.**

**Purchased Arc AI Credits will not disappear even if the Cloud Subscription ends.**

**Remote permissions can never override the Stage 6 Risk Permission.**

**Cloud data expires and enters 30-day read/export retention before being deleted; local data is never deleted.**

**Full Export is supported since V1.**

**Official Cloud and Self-host are independent realms.**

**All Cloud data belongs to Workspace from day one, leaving a good foundation for Team in the future.**

After achieving this, the previous **Account → Waffo → Entitlement → Distribution → ArcChat Agent → Cloud** has truly been strung together into a complete product chain, and the key data boundaries, remote boundaries, privacy boundaries and business boundaries have been resolved in advance, and there is no need to wait for the specific App to be launched before rework.

# stage8

---

Now onto **Stage 8: AI Business Cost Model**.

At this stage, I think we need to look deeper than "How many models are connected and how to deduct Credits", because it directly determines whether ArcForges will have this most dangerous situation:

> The more users grow and AI is used, the faster ArcForges loses money.

And AI prices are not stable constants. In recent months alone there have been:

* OpenAI GPT-5.6 re-forms Sol / Terra / Luna three cost files;
* Claude Sonnet 5 now has a temporary discount price, which will return from $2/$10 to $3/$15 per MTok after **2026-08-31**;
* OpenAI, Gemini, and xAI all have Long Context price increases;
* Prompt Cache, Batch, and Priority have different prices;
* Web Search, Computer Use, pictures, videos, and voice are not the same pricing unit at all. ([OpenAI Developers][1])

So the core of stage 8 is not "how much does a token cost for Claude now", but to establish a set of:

# **Provider cost has changed, and ArcForges does not need to redo the AI Cost Engine of the commercial system.**

---

# 1. First, formalize the three business paths of ArcForges AI.

The previous conclusion continues to hold, and now officially enters the cost model.

```text
ArcForges AI
│
├── Local AI
│     User's own computer reasoning
│     ArcForges AI cost ≈ 0
│
├── BYOK
│     ├── Local BYOK
│     │     free
│     │
│     └── Cloud BYOK
│           need Cloud Subscription
│           Token Fees are paid directly by the user Provider
│           ArcForges Not added Token markup
│
└── Arc Managed AI
      ArcForges pay Provider
      ↓
      User consumption Arc AI Credits
```

This business structure is great because:

> **Price-conscious power users always have BYOK.**

So Arc Managed AI **has no need to compete with OpenRouter on "reselling the API at cost"**.

Managed AI sells:

* No need to apply for API Key;
* No need to recharge multiple Providers;
* Automatic model routing;
* Provider fallback;
* Usage / Budget;
* Agent Integration;
* Unified Credits;
* Tool call;
* Model switching;
* Official operations and availability.

Therefore Managed AI should have reasonable profits.

---

# 2. You must not sell "unlimited AI"

The first hard rule:

# **ArcForges will never sell Unlimited Managed AI.**

Even in the future:

```text
ArcForges Cloud Max
$20/month
```

Nor can we promise:

> unlimited GPT / Claude / video generation.

Can give:

> Included Monthly Allowance

After:

> Purchased Credits.

The reason is very simple.

The current GPT-5.6 Sol API is `$5 / MTok input + $30 / MTok output`, Terra is `$2.50/$15`, and Luna is `$1/$6`. The official price for Claude Sonnet 5 will be `$3/$15` and for Opus 4.8 it will be `$5/$25`. The unit cost of different models can vary many times. ([OpenAI Developers][1])

And Agent is not once again:

```text
Prompt → Response
```

Instead it could be:

```text
Model
↓
Tool
↓
Model
↓
Subagent × 4
↓
Search
↓
Model
↓
Retry
↓
Model
```

A "task" can be dozens or even hundreds of times more expensive than an ordinary chat.

So:

> **Subscriptions are responsible for Cloud services, and Credits are responsible for highly variable AI COGS.**

---

# 3. Formal definition of Arc AI Credits

Here I suggest settling on it directly now.

# **1 USD Credits Pack Selling Price = 1,000 Arc AI Credits**

That is to say:

```text
$10  → 10,000 Credits
$25  → 25,000 Credits
$50  → 50,000 Credits
```

But be sure to note:

# **1 Credit is not $0.001 cash.**

The legal and product definition must always be:

> Arc AI Credits are non-transferable prepaid service usage units with no cash value.

That is:

* Cannot withdraw cash;
* Not transferable;
* Not tradable;
* Not currency;
* Not Crypto;
* Only Arc Managed AI services can be consumed.

---

# 4. Why use 1,000 Credits / $1 instead of directly displaying the USD balance?

Because this is easy for users to understand:

```text
10,000 Credits
```

It will not make Arc AI Wallet:

```text
$10.00 cash balance
```

Avoid product concepts that look more and more like Stored Value Wallet.

At the same time, the calculation granularity is sufficient.

For example, one call ends up with:

```text
35.2 Credits
```

The background can record accurately.

---

# 5. The backend cannot really use only integers Credit

Otherwise:

```text
0.2 Credit
```

Every time you round up, there are a lot of hidden charges.

Internally at least:

# MicroCredit

For example:

```text
1 Credit
=
1000 MicroCredits
```

Each Request:

> Accurate accumulation.

UI:

```text
2,431 Credits
```

Just display layer.

Never:

> Each Request individually ceil()s to 1 Credit.

---

# 6. In the first version of Credits Pack, do not do "big package to give away Credits"

Do not start with:

```text
$10  → 10,000
$25  → 27,500
$50  → 60,000
```

The first version remains:

```text
1 : 1000
```

Reason:

* Refunds are easy;
* Credit Lot value is very clear;
* Financial reconciliation is simple;
* There is no need to distinguish between Bonus Credit;
* Will not destroy profits early.

It can be completely deduced after data is available in the future:

```text
$100 → 105,000
```

But not required for V1.

---

# 7. The core: Arc AI cannot directly "Provider cost = User Credits"

There must be two levels of prices:

```text
Provider Cost
      ↓
ArcForges Cost Engine
      ↓
Retail Tariff
      ↓
```

### Managed AI Retail Cost

```text
        ↓

        ↓
```

```text
Per request reservation

Per automation budget

No negative balance
```

The most important thing is:

# **ArcForges does not sell Tokens.**

What it sells is:

> **A unified, budgetable, cross-provider, cross-model, cross-media, managed AI service that is deeply integrated with Agent.**

Model price rises, model retirement, a GPT generation change, Claude changing its tokenizer, Gemini changing its long-context rate, or xAI adding a new media model all require only:

> Update `Upstream Price → Retail Tariff → Routing`

No need to redesign **Waffo, Subscription, Entitlement, Credits, ArcChat, Cloud or user balance system**.

This is Stage 8's true "no rework" business cost model.

# stage9

---

Now onto **Stage 9: Data, Sync, Backup and User Assets**.

I consider this stage one of the layers in all of ArcForges where **"just make it work first" is least acceptable**.

Problems with payment, AI, and UI can most of the time be repaired; however, once the early boundary design of the data system is incorrect, the following are most likely to occur later:

> Synchronization overwrites user files, two devices fight each other, ArcSlate media is lost, deleted and then "resurrected", the data is unknown after Cloud exit, the backup seems to exist but cannot be restored, and the material is completely lost after the user copies the project to another machine.

Therefore, the goal of Stage 9 is not to create a "synchronization function", but to establish a unified ArcForges ecosystem:

# **User Data & Asset Integrity Model**

Let me set down the core principles directly:

> **Sync ≠ Backup ≠ Version History ≠ Trash ≠ Export.**
>
> **User Data ≠ Asset ≠ Cache ≠ Search Index ≠ Secret.**
>
> **ArcForges always gives priority to data preservation, and would rather produce conflicting copies than silently overwrite them.**

---

# 1. First, completely separate the five most confusing concepts.

This is the first hard rule of Stage 9.

## 1. Sync

Answer:

> **How can my multiple devices see the same latest data?**

For example:

```text
Windows ArcNotes
        ↓
      Cloud
        ↓
Mac ArcNotes
```

Sync solves:

* Change propagation
* Device convergence
* Offline changes
* Conflict
* Selective download

---

# 2. Version History

Answer:

> **I changed something, can I go back to yesterday?**

For example:

```text
Report

v14 current
v13
v12
...
```

This is the user-visible history of the data.

Stage 7 has been decided:

# 30-day Version History

Keep it up.

---

# 3. Trash / Deleted Recovery

Answer:

> **I deleted it by mistake, can I restore it?**

Stage 7:

# 30-day Deleted Recovery

Keep it up.

Deletion does not mean immediate physical destruction.

---

# 4. Backup

Answer:

> **Can ArcForges' own Cloud database, object storage or even the entire Provider be restored after a major accident?**

This is operational disaster recovery.

Users typically do not operate Infrastructure Backup directly.

---

# 5. Export

Answer:

> **I no longer use ArcForges, can I take all my data away?**

It solves:

# Portability / No lock-in

Therefore:

```text
Sync      ≠ Backup
Backup    ≠ Version History
Version   ≠ Trash
Trash     ≠ Export
```

You cannot pretend to solve five problems with one feature.

---

# 2. ArcForges must establish a unified data classification

Stage 7 has been initially passed, and I will now officially upgrade it to the entire ecological standard.

All data must fall into one of the following categories.

| Type                  | Example                           |            Whether user assets | Default Cloud |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------: | -------- |
| Canonical User Data | Note, Project, Conversation    |                 Yes | Syncable      |
| Managed Asset       | Pictures, videos, attachments, Telemetry           |                 Yes | by strategy      |
| External Reference  | External video on user disk                   | Yes, but ArcForges does not own | Not uploaded by default    |
| Derived Data        | Thumbnail, Embedding, Waveform |                 No | Rebuildable      |
| Device-local State  | Window position, GPU configuration                  |                 No | Out of sync      |
| Secret              | API Key, Device Private Key   |                sensitive | Specialized Vault |
| Operational Data    | Sync Cursor, Job State        |                system | Cloud    |
| Audit/Commercial    | Billing, Security Audit       |              System logging | independently retained     |

Any new data type added to the App must be answered first:

> Which category does it belong to?

You cannot just "throw it in AppData and sync it all."

---

# 3. The most important data authority boundary

Different systems are responsible for different facts.

## Professional App

Responsible for:

# **Business semantics of data**

For example:

ArcNotes:

> What are Document, Block, Notebook.

ArcScope:

> What are Session, Channel, and Annotation.

ArcSlate:

> What is Timeline, Clip, Track.

---

# Sync System

Only responsible for:

> **Replication, versions, conflicts, device status.**

It should not understand itself:

> Video Timeline How to Merge.

---

# Object Storage

Only responsible for:

> **Blob.**

It should not be the authoritative database of "which project's current version is what".

---

# Search

Just:

# Derived Projection

---

So:

```text
App Domain
   │
   │ defines meaning
   ▼
Canonical Object / Revision
   │
   ├── Sync Metadata
   │
   ├── Blob References
   │
   └── Search Projection
```

Very important:

# **Never infer the user's current data status by enumerating the R2 Bucket.**

R2 is a Blob Store, not an ArcForges Domain Database.

---

# 4. Local priority must be truly implemented into the disk model

The so-called Local-first cannot be just a marketing slogan.

Must mean:

> Even if the user unplugs the network cable, professional apps still have full local state that works.

For example:

```text
ArcNotes Local Store
ArcScope Local Store
ArcSlate Local Project
ArcChat Local Store
```

Cloud is:

> Replica + Coordination + Remote Services.

instead of:

```text
once per operation
↓
The server must be successful
↓
to save
```

---

# 5. Local Save can never fail due to Cloud failure

Formal principles:

```text
Local edit
   ↓
Local durable commit
   ↓
Sync Outbox
   ↓
Cloud when available
```

instead of:

```text
Local edit
   ↓
Cloud API
   ↓
Cloud failed
   ↓
SAVE FAILED
```

This principle is very important.

Cloudflare is down:

> Users can still continue to write ArcNotes, cut ArcSlate, and collect ArcScope.

---

# 6. Each synchronizable object must have a stable identity

Never use a file path as an identity.

Correct:

```text
WorkspaceId

AppId

ObjectId
```

For example:

```text
ObjectId:
01JZ...

Type:
ArcNotes.Document
```

Device A:

```text
C:\Users\...\report.arcnote
```

Device B:

```text
/Users/.../report.arcnote
```

Still the same:

# ObjectId

---

# 7. The file name is not Identity either.

User:

```text
report.md
↓
final-report.md
```

Just:

# Rename

Not:

```text
delete old
+
create unrelated new object
```

Otherwise:

* Version History is broken;
* Deep Link failed;
* ArcChat Artifact is invalid;
* Cross-App Reference is invalid.

---

# 8. All User Objects must have Revision

Conceptually:

```text
Object
│
├── Revision 17
├── Revision 18
└── Revision 19 ← current
```

Every Revision should know at least:

```text
RevisionId

ObjectId

ParentRevision

CreatedAt

Actor

Device

AppVersion

SchemaVersion
```

Agent modifications should also know:

```text
TaskId
Capability
```

In the future users can see:

> Edited by ArcChat Agent
> Jul 21, 15:42

This is very valuable.

---

# 9. Revision is best Immutable

Principles:

# **History Revision Once submitted, it will not be modified.**

New changes:

```text
Revision 19
↓
Revision 20
```

Instead of constantly modifying:

```text
revision-19.json
```

This way:

* Sync is more reliable;
* History Nature;
* Backup is simple;
* Agent Undo is simple;
* Auditing is simple.

---

# 10. User Asset must be formally divided into two core modes

This is the key to whether ArcSlate and ArcScope will be reworked later.

# Managed Asset

User choice:

> Import into ArcForges.

For example:

```text
video.mp4
↓
ArcSlate Managed Library
```

ArcForges is responsible for:

* AssetId
* Life cycle
* Hash
* Sync
* Relocation
* Backup

---

# External Reference

User choice:

> Keep file where it is.

For example:

```text
D:\Videos\movie.mkv
```

ArcSlate just saves:

```text
ExternalAssetReference
```

ArcForges:

# Do not own this file.

---

# 11. You must not copy External Assets into Cloud silently

User opens:

```text
D:\Private\200GB-video.mov
```

Not because:

> ArcSlate Sync is on

Just start uploading 200GB.

It must be clear:

```text
This asset is externally referenced.

[Keep local only]

[Make managed]

[Upload original]
```

This is also a privacy boundary.

---

# 12. How to handle External Asset across devices

For example:

Windows:

```text
D:\Video\source.mov
```

Open the project on Mac.

should show:

# Missing / Unavailable Asset

But the project itself can still be opened.

Provided by:

```text
Locate File

Relink

Find by content

Use proxy
```

instead of:

> Project corrupted.

---

# 13. Asset Relink must support content recognition

It does not matter if the paths are different.

Should be combined with:

```text
AssetId
Expected Size
Content Hash
Metadata
```

After the user selects a new file:

> Verify whether they are the same material.

If the content is different:

> Tell users clearly.

Do not do it just because of the file name:

```text
source.mov
```

The same is considered to be the same.

---

# 14. All Managed Blobs should try to use the Immutable Blob model

For example:

```text
BlobId
ContentHash
Length
```

After one write:

> Not covered in place.

If the user edits the image:

```text
Blob A
↓
Blob B
```

Project Revision references B instead.

Not:

```text
PUT same-key/image.png
```

Constant coverage.

---

# 15. Why is this particularly suitable for R2?

R2 currently provides globally strongly consistent object writing, reading, deletion and listing; but if two clients write the same key at the same time, the last one to complete will still win. ([Cloudflare Docs][1])

So ArcForges' best strategy is not to gamble at all:

> Who PUT last.

Instead:

```text
Blob A → immutable key
Blob B → immutable key

Metadata revision chooses one
```

This conflict occurs when:

# Domain Revision

Instead of Blob Store Last Writer Wins.

---

# 16. Blob Key Do not directly expose user file names

Do not:

```text
workspace123/Ryan Medical Report.pdf
```

It is recommended to use an internal Blob Key that cannot be guessed.

For example logic:

```text
workspace/...
blob/...
```

Filename exists in Domain Metadata.

This way:

* Rename does not move the blob;
* Special character issues reduced;
* Better privacy;
* The URL does not reveal the file title.

---

# 17. Content Hash must become part of asset integrity

It is recommended to formally save:

# SHA-256

At least as a stable cross-platform Integrity Hash.

There can be faster internal fingerprint algorithms, but the public integrity verification is based on mature standard hash.

Need to know:

```text
BlobId
ExpectedSize
SHA256
```

---

# 18. Do not treat Multipart ETag as content Hash

This is very important.

R2 official statement clearly states:

For multipart upload, the final ETag is the value calculated from the MD5 combination of each part, and is not simply "the MD5 of this file". ([Cloudflare Docs][2])

So:

# ETag ≠ ArcForges Content Hash

You must save the real checksum yourself.

R2 itself also supports providing SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-384/SHA-512 and other verification information when uploading. ([Cloudflare Docs][3])

---

# 19. Large files must support resumable uploading

ArcSlate large files cannot:

```text
99% Upload completed
↓
Disconnected
↓
Reupload 40GB
```

Must:

# Multipart / Resumable Upload

R2 current multipart:

* Up to about 5 TiB for a single object;
* Up to 10,000 parts;
* When the upload fails, only the failed part needs to be resent. ([Cloudflare Docs][2])

Perfectly suitable for:

* Video
* Telemetry dataset
* Backup package

---

# 20. But uploading credentials can never give the client a permanent Storage Key.

Correct:

```text
Desktop
  ↓ request upload permission
ArcForges Cloud
  ↓
Short-lived scoped upload authorization
  ↓
R2
```

R2 supports presigned URL, which is essentially a bearer capability with expiration time; the official also clearly reminds anyone who gets the URL to perform corresponding operations within the validity period. ([Cloudflare Docs][4])

Therefore it is necessary to:

* Short TTL;
* Limited object;
* Limited operations;
* Not revealing R2 Permanent Secrets.

---

# 21. Cloud Metadata and Blob upload to solve "semi-successful"

For example:

```text
Blob upload successful

But

Metadata commit failed
```

This produces:

# Orphan Blob

In reverse:

```text
Metadata points to blob

But blob incomplete
```

then produces:

# Broken Reference

Therefore the data system must have clear:

```text
Upload Session

Staged

Verified

Committed

Abandoned
```

life cycle.

Only checksum and integrity verification succeed:

> Only in this way can the official Revision reference this blob.

---

# 22. Orphan Blob must be automatically recycled

For example:

```text
Staged blob

24h / 48h still haven’t been any Revision commit
```

Enter recycling.

Do not store orphan data indefinitely.

R2 itself also terminates unfinished multipart uploads after 7 days by default; lifecycle rules can further control object cleanup. ([Cloudflare Docs][2])

---

# 23. Dedup can be done, but only to a limited extent.

I recommend:

# Workspace-scoped dedup

For example, a user in a Workspace:

```text
Project A
references video X

Project B
references same video X
```

Cloud saves only once.

---

# 24. Do not do cross-user Global Dedup

Do not:

```text
Ryan upload file X

Alice upload file X

→ Share the same security object identity
```

Even though the content hash is the same.

This may produce:

* Privacy side channels;
* Permission complexity;
* Difficulty in deleting;
* Tenant isolation becomes complicated.

It is another matter if the Provider deduplicates the physical storage bottom layer by itself.

ArcForges Domain:

# Workspace isolation first.

---

# 25. Storage Quota is also recommended to be calculated based on the only Managed Content of the Workspace.

For example:

```text
same 10GB video
```

Reused across three projects in a Workspace:

It is recommended to only count:

# 10GB

instead of:

# 30GB

Because real users feel:

> I only uploaded one video.

---

# 26. But Version History may still take up space

For example:

```text
Blob A
Blob B
Blob C
```

These blobs are required for each of the three historical Revisions.

As long as these blobs remain:

* Active
* Version History
* Trash

Recovery scope:

> All are user-recoverable storage.

Stage 7 has decided that such historical user blobs should be included in the quota, and this rule continues to remain.

---

# 27. Derived Asset should never be confused with Canonical Asset

For example ArcSlate:

```text
Original.mov
```

is a User Asset.

And:

```text
thumbnail.jpg
waveform.bin
proxy-360p.mp4
```

Need to distinguish:

### Explicit user-selected Proxy

User asks Cloud to save:

> Can be counted towards quota.

### Pure implementation cache

ArcForges generates it itself:

> Does not count user quota.

---

# 28. Derived Data must always be able to be reconstructed

System design must meet:

```text
delete entire search index
delete all thumbnails
delete all embeddings
```

User data remains intact.

Then:

# Rebuild

That's it.

Deleting a "Cache" will cause the Project to be permanently lost:

> It's not Cache.

---

# 29. Sync Protocol must revolve around Change instead of scanning the entire world

Each startup cannot:

```text
List 1,000,000 cloud objects
↓
Compare with local
```

Must exist:

```text
Sync Cursor

Change Feed
```

For example:

```text
Client has cursor 10582

Server:
10583 update
10584 delete
10585 create
```

Only sync changes.

---

# 30. Each Change must be idempotent

The device network is not good:

```text
Change 10584
```

Received twice.

The result can still only be applied once.

Therefore each change must have:

```text
ChangeId
ObjectId
RevisionId
```

Stable identity.

---

# 31. Local Sync must have Durable Outbox

Local operation:

```text
Edit
↓
Local DB commit
↓
Outbox Entry
```

Even if:

> App crashes immediately after saving

Next startup:

```text
Outbox still there
↓
continue sync
```

Cannot rely on a memory Task.

---

# 32. Cloud also needs Inbox / Idempotency

Same as Stage 3 webhooks.

The same client Change retries 5 times:

> Cloud only generates one Revision.

---

# 33. Sync Conflict cannot cover all apps with one algorithm

Officially reserved:

```text
ConflictPolicy
```

Include at least:

### Append

Suitable for:

```text
Events
Logs
Conversation entries
```

### Merge

Suitable for documents that can be safely merged.

### Revision Compare

Structured Project.

### Conflict Branch

Complex project documents.

### Immutable

Blob.

---

# 34. V1 does not need to use CRDT in order to be "advanced"

This is an over-design direction that I would definitely argue against.

ArcNotes will be able to use CRDT for some data structures in the future.

But:

```text
ArcSlate Timeline
ArcScope Session
Binary Asset
Complex project graph
```

Hard CRDT:

> It's extremely complex and does not necessarily produce better results.

V1 goals:

# **No silent data loss.**

Not:

> Everything works with real-time multiplayer collaboration.

---

# 35. Sync Conflict Minimum Standard

If the system cannot safely merge automatically:

Must:

```text
Original
Device A Version
Device B Version
```

All reserved.

Users see:

# Conflict

instead of:

> Device B wins.

---

# 36. Conflict UI must tell the user what happened

For example:

```text
ArcSlate Project conflict

Ryan Desktop
Edited 15:31

MacBook
Edited 15:34

[Open Desktop Version]

[Open Mac Version]

[Keep Both]

[Resolve]
```

It cannot just be:

> Sync error 409.

---

# 37. Delete must use Tombstone

Device A:

```text
Delete Note X
```

If you just delete the server object:

Device B is now offline and X remains.

B is online:

```text
X exists locally
↓
upload
```

It may be "resurrected" again.

So the delete must become:

# Tombstone

For example:

```text
Object X
DeletedAt
DeleteRevision
```

After all devices are synced to Tombstone:

> Only then did I realize that this was "delete", not "missing files in the cloud".

---

# 38. 30-day Trash is based on Tombstone

Stage 7:

```text
Deleted
↓
Trash 30 days
```

During this period:

* Can be restored;
* Blob reserved;
* History retained;
* Still counts as Storage.

---

# 39. Restore should restore the original Object Identity

For example:

```text
ObjectId 123
```

Restore after deletion:

Still:

```text
ObjectId 123
```

Do not:

```text
new ObjectId 999
```

Otherwise:

* ArcChat Project references;
* Deep Links;
* Artifact Links;

Cut them all off.

Recovery is just:

# A new Revision revokes the Tombstone state.

---

# 40. Permanent Delete is a complete data cleaning process

Definitely not just:

```text
DELETE FROM objects
```

It has to handle at least:

```text
Canonical Metadata

Blob references

Unused blobs

Version references

Search document

Vector index

Preview/cache

Share/access state future

Backup expiry schedule
```

---

# 41. Derived Data cannot remain after deletion

This Stage 7 has been mentioned and is now upgraded to hard acceptance.

Permanently delete:

```text
Medical Report
```

Later:

> Semantic Search can no longer return its excerpts.

Must have:

# Deletion Propagation Tracking

until:

```text
Primary object deleted
Search deleted
Vector deleted
Derived caches deleted
```

All done.

---

# 42. The user is permanently deleted ≠ physically disappears from all Disaster Backups on the same day

This product policy must be honest.

Backup itself needs to prevent:

* Operation and maintenance accidental deletion;
* Ransomware;
* DB corruption.

So a disaster backup may still contain deleted objects for a limited time.

The right policy should:

> Deleted data is immediately inaccessible from the online system and disappears automatically after the backup retention period.

Instead of false promises:

> After pressing Delete, all historical backups in the world will disappear instantly.

---

# 43. Backup Retention I recommend formally adopting a limited window

V1 recommendations:

# **35-day infrastructure backup retention**

It is the same as:

```text
30-day Version/Trash
```

Generally consistent, with a small safety margin.

User Content does not:

> Permanent Disaster Archive.

This way privacy and recovery capabilities are more balanced.

---

# 44. But Billing / Security Audit does not use the same retention as user content

For example:

```text
Invoice
Payment
Refund
Security login record
```

Possible reasons:

* Taxation;
* Anti-fraud;
* Law;

Requires longer retention.

So it must be:

```text
UserContentRetention

≠

CommercialRecordRetention
```

One `RetentionDays` cannot control all data.

---

# 45. Sync is definitely not Backup

This sentence needs to be formally written into the product documentation.

For example user:

```text
Device A accidentally deletes 100 notes
```

Sync does its job very well:

```text
Cloud Delete
↓
Device B Delete
↓
Device C Delete
```

So:

> Sync will even propagate errors very efficiently.

What really saves users is:

# Version History / Trash / Backup

---

# 46. Infrastructure Backup should be divided into two layers

## Metadata Database Backup

Assuming Cloud Core ends up using PostgreSQL:

Must have:

# Continuous WAL / PITR

The current official documentation of PostgreSQL 18 clearly supports restoring the database to a specified point in time through base backup + WAL continuous archiving. ([PostgreSQL][5])

So Cloud Metadata should not just be:

> `pg_dump` once per night.

---

# 47. Objectives of the first version of Metadata Backup

Internal engineering goal recommendations:

# RPO ≤ 5 minutes

That is:

> In extreme accidents, the maximum target loss is about a few minutes of metadata change.

and:

# Critical RTO ≤ 4 hours

These start as:

# Internal Engineering Objective

It is not necessary to immediately commit to SLA on the official website.

It must go through a recovery drill before committing to the outside world.

---

# 48. Blob Backup must also exist

R2 itself already has high durability, and the official currently claims that the design goal is **11 nines of annual durability**, and protects objects through replication/erasure coding and other methods. ([Cloudflare Docs][6])

However:

# High Durability ≠ Backup.

Because it alone cannot protect you from:

* Error deleting script;
* Stolen Cloud credential;
* Error lifecycle;
* Misoperation by administrator;
* Provider/account level disaster.

---

# 49. Now R2 already has Bucket Lock

This is a fact that should be updated in 2026.

R2 currently supports Bucket Locks, which prevent objects from being deleted and overwritten for a specified period of time or permanently. ([Cloudflare Docs][7])

Therefore:

# Primary Provider Internal

Key backup snapshot / backup prefix can be kept immutable.

This is the first layer of protection.

---

# 50. But truly high standards should include cross-Provider Backup

I recommend:

# R2 = Primary

Select again:

# Backblaze B2 = Disaster Backup

The reason is not that R2 is unreliable, but that:

> **True disaster recovery cannot place the Primary and the only Backup in the same Provider/Account fault domain.**

B2 currently provides Object Lock, which can prevent objects from being modified/deleted within the period using governance or compliance retention. ([Backblaze][8])

So ultimately:

```text
Primary
Cloudflare R2
     │
     │ async backup
     ▼
Secondary
Backblaze B2
Object Lock
```

This combination I think is a perfect fit for ArcForges.

---

# 51. Blob Backup should not fully copy 50GB every day × all users

Because we have adopted:

# Immutable Blob

So backup can be done naturally:

```text
New Blob A
→ copy once

New Blob B
→ copy once
```

Immutable Blob:

> No need to re-copy every day.

This is also a huge advantage of the immutable asset model.

---

# 52. Goals of Cross-provider Blob Backup

I recommend:

# Target RPO ≤ 1 hour

That is the new Cloud Blob:

> The target enters the standalone Backup Provider within an hour.

if:

```text
Backup lag > 4h
```

The police must be called.

---

# 53. Do not rush to "copy everything back" after a major R2 failure occurs.

With ObjectStorage abstraction later:

An ideal DR would be:

```text
Primary unavailable
↓
Read selected blobs from backup
```

Or create:

# Restore/Migration Pipeline

But do not make any promises to the outside world in the first stage:

> Cross-cloud switching in seconds.

Be realistic:

# Full Blob Recovery/Switch Target ≤ 24h

Improvement will be made after internal maturity.

---

# 54. Backup is not complete until Restore is proven successful.

This is an operation and maintenance requirement that must be included in Stage 9.

Cannot:

```text
Backup job = green
```

Just think it's safe.

Must:

## automatic

Randomly every day:

```text
restore sample metadata
restore sample blobs
verify checksum
```

---

## regularly

Suggestions:

# Monthly small-scale Restore Drill

---

## complete

# Quarterly Disaster Recovery Exercise

True:

```text
New environment
↓
restore DB
↓
restore/access object backup
↓
verify Workspace
```

---

# 55. Backup Health Dashboard is a must

At least:

```text
Last DB backup

PITR archive lag

Object backup lag

Objects awaiting backup

Checksum failures

Last restore test

Last full DR drill
```

Do not wait until an accident happens to ask:

> Have our Backups been successful recently?

---

# 56. Asset Integrity requires active detection

For Managed Assets:

```text
Expected SHA256
Expected Length
```

After the download is complete:

# Verify

Inconsistencies found:

```text
Corrupted
```

Do not give bad files directly to the app.

---

# 57. Integrity Audit should also be done regularly in the background

No need to rehash all terabytes of video every day.

Can:

* Sample verification;
* Metadata/checksum consistency;
* Random object verification;
* Backup copy verification.

Found:

```text
Primary hash mismatch
```

Available from:

# Backup

Recovery.

---

# 58. R2's Strong Consistency is a good thing, but you cannot be lazy.

R2 currently provides strong consistency for write/read, metadata update, delete, and list. ([Cloudflare Docs][1])

This makes Sync Blob layers easier.

But:

> ArcForges still cannot omit the Revision / Conflict / Transaction Model just because R2 is strongly consistent.

Because the real conflict occurs when:

```text
Device A edits logical object

Device B edits logical object
```

Not just Object Store consistency.

---

# 59. User assets must support Local Availability Policy

After synchronization, it does not mean that each device will download the entire 50GB.

Requires:

```text
Always keep on this device

Available offline

Download on demand

Cloud only
```

---

# 60. But Local-first has a hard rule

# **ArcForges may not automatically delete a user's original local source files to "save space" without explicit user action.**

For example:

User originally:

```text
D:\Video\source.mov
```

After uploading to Cloud:

> ArcForges cannot secretly delete D:\Video\source.mov.

---

# 61. Only Managed Asset can do "Free Up Space"

For example ArcSlate Managed Library:

The user explicitly clicked:

# Free up local space

Talent:

```text
local managed copy delete
↓
cloud placeholder remains
```

Later you will need:

> On-demand hydrate.

# 62. External Reference cannot do automatic offload at all.

Because:

> That is not a file managed by ArcForges.

ArcForges can never delete External References on behalf of the user.

# 63. New device Bootstrap should not download everything first

Log in to the new computer:

```text
Workspace metadata
↓
Object catalog
↓
Project metadata
↓
Small assets
```

Show up first.

Large:

```text
Video
Raw telemetry
```

According to user policy:

# On demand.

Otherwise:

> 50GB full download once logged in.

Very poor experience.

```text
├── Project Data
```

instead of one:

# 68. The data generated by the Agent must have Provenance

Stage 6 Agent operations now officially enter the data layer.

Any Agent Write:

```text
      ↓
ArcNotes Revision
```

```text
Actor = Agent

TaskId

Capability

UserApproval if relevant
```

So from now on:

Can answer.

# 69. Checkpoint should be generated before high-risk modification of Agent

For example:

> "Help me reorganize my entire ArcNotes Notebook."

Before operation:

# Create Recovery Checkpoint

The same goes for large-scale ArcSlate Timeline modifications.

Rather, the underlying data system has safe recovery points.

# 70. Checkpoint and Version History can unify the underlying layer, but the product semantics are different.

For example:

```text

User Version
```

But the UI can identify:

> Before Agent Edit

> Before Upgrade

# 71. Data Schema must be versioned

All syncable Domain Payloads:

```text
ObjectType
SchemaVersion
```

Cannot default to:

> All clients are always on the same version.

Stage 5 has made it clear that each App can be upgraded independently.

So it will definitely appear:

```text
ArcNotes PC 2.1

ArcNotes Mac 2.0
```

Sync simultaneously.

# 72. The new version of data cannot be silently destroyed by the old App

For example:

```text
Schema v4
```

Old client:

```text
Only understand v3
```

Cannot:

> Open → Save → Lost all v4 fields.

# Compatibility Negotiation

```text
Readable

Writable

RequiresUpgrade
```

# 73. Checkpoint must be performed before Breaking Data Migration

For example:

```text
Schema 7 → 8
```

Irreversible migration.

Operation:

```text
Local recovery snapshot
+
Cloud revision checkpoint
↓
Migration
```

Failure:

> Can be restored.

# 74. App Update and Data Migration are not the same transaction

Stage 5 has said:

> Velopack Updater is not responsible for business data migration.

Now officially fixed:

```text
Installer update
       ↓
App starts
       ↓
Data compatibility check
       ↓
Migration
```

And must have:

# Migration Recovery

# 75. Local Path cannot be saved across App Reference

For example ArcChat Project:

```text
references ArcNotes Document
```

```text
ArcNotes.ObjectId
```

instead of:

```text
C:\...\report.arcnotes
```

This way:

> Cloud / Mobile / Mac still understand references.

# 76. Deep Link should also be based on Stable Identity

For example:


instead of:

# 77. Export is the first-class product capability of Stage 9

At least support:

# Per-App Export

For example:

```text
Export ArcNotes Notebook
Export ArcSlate Project
Export ArcScope Session
```

# 78. Workspace Export must also be supported

Stage 7 has been proposed and now officially completed:

```text
Workspace Export
│
├── manifest
├── ArcChat
├── ArcNotes
├── ArcScope
├── ArcSlate
└── Managed Assets
```

---

# 79. Export Manifest must be in documented format

Because ArcForges is open source.

Do not do:

```text
mystery binary .arcbackup
```

No one knows what's inside.

```text
.arcforge
```

Such a convenient container extension.

```text
Manifest
Schema Version
Objects
References
Assets

```

norm.

# 80. Export must be distinguished from External Reference

For example project reference:

```text
D:\movie.mov
```

```text
[No]
```

# 81. Import must prevent malicious files

Because Export Package may come from:

> Internet.

So Import cannot:

* Trust internal absolute paths;
* Allow `../../` Path Traversal;
* Unzip Unlimited Zip Bomb;

Import itself must be as:

# Untrusted Input

processing.

# 82. Cloud Assets cannot be directly used as "executable content"

For example, user uploads:

```text
.exe
.dll
script
```

# Stage 9 Finalization

The data system of ArcForges is officially adopted:

# **Local-first Revisioned Object + Managed/Referenced Asset + Immutable Blob Architecture**

Core relationships:

```text
                  App Domain Object
                         │
                    Stable ObjectId
                         │
                     Revisions
                         │
              ┌──────────┴──────────┐
              │                     │
          Metadata              Blob References
                                    │
                             Immutable Blobs
                                    │
                        ┌───────────┴───────────┐
                        │                       │
                    Primary R2           Disaster Backup
                                            B2 / Object Lock
```

and officially adheres to:

**Sync, Backup, History, Trash, and Export are permanently separated.**

**Local Save always takes precedence over Cloud.**

**Cloud failure cannot prevent local software from being saved.**

**Any synchronizable object has a Stable ObjectId, never a Path/Filename as an identity.**

**User History Revision Try to be Immutable.**

**Managed Asset and External Reference are completely different asset types.**

**External File will never be uploaded secretly just because Sync is turned on.**

**Large Blob immutable, Project Revision only changes the reference.**

**Blob uses content integrity hash; Multipart ETag cannot be used as content hash.**

**Large assets must be resumable multipart.**

**The client never gets the permanent Object Storage credential.**

**Dedup is only considered within the Workspace scope, and cross-user Domain Dedup is not considered.**

**Delete and use Tombstone to prevent offline devices from resurrecting old data.**

**Conflict branches are retained when merge cannot be performed safely and data is never lost silently.**

**V1 does not force everything to CRDT.**

**User data will never be deleted when Storage is full or degraded, and new Cloud writes will only be stopped.**

**New device metadata first, large files hydrate on demand.**

**Search/Embedding/Thumbnail is always just Derived Data and can be completely rebuilt.**

**Each Agent modification has Provenance, and a checkpoint is created before high-risk batch modifications.**

**Data Schema and App Release are versioned independently, and old clients cannot silently destroy the new format.**

**Workspace Export and App Export are V1 basic capabilities, and the format must be documented.**

**Primary Blob Storage uses R2; leverages the R2 Bucket Lock to provide the first layer of immutable protection. ** R2 currently supports Bucket Lock, and the object layer is strongly consistent storage. ([Cloudflare Docs][7])

**Real Disaster Backup is then independently replicated to the second Provider; Backblaze B2 + Object Lock is recommended. ** B2 currently has the ability to prevent backup objects from being modified or deleted during the retention period via the governance/compliance Object Lock. ([Backblaze][8])

**The core Metadata Database must support PITR, not just rely on daily dumps. ** PostgreSQL's current official continuous WAL archive + base backup model can restore to a specified historical point in time. ([PostgreSQL][5])

**A Backup only exists through an actual Restore.**

Internally:

```text
Metadata RPO target      ≤ 5 min
Blob backup RPO target   ≤ 1 hour
Critical service RTO     ≤ 4 hours
Full blob DR target      ≤ 24 hours
Backup retention         ≈ 35 days
```

As an engineering goal, the decision on whether to turn into an external SLA will be made after the actual recovery drill is achieved.

After reaching Stage 9, ArcForges' data is no longer "each app saves a little bit + R2 uploads files", but a user asset system that can truly support **years of professional creation, cross-device synchronization, automatic modification of agents, large media, Self-host, Cloud exit and disaster recovery**.

[1]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/reference/consistency/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Consistency model · Cloudflare R2 docs"
[2]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/objects/upload-objects/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Upload objects · Cloudflare R2 docs"
[3]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/platform/release-notes/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Release notes · Cloudflare R2 docs"
[4]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/presigned-urls/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Presigned URLs · Cloudflare R2 docs"
[5]: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/continuous-archiving.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com "PostgreSQL: Documentation: 18: 25.3. Continuous Archiving and Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)"
[6]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/reference/durability/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Durability · Cloudflare R2 docs"
[7]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/buckets/bucket-locks/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Bucket locks · Cloudflare R2 docs"
[8]: https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Cloud Storage Object Lock"

# stage10

---

Now entering **Stage 10: Production Operations Infrastructure**.

The first 9 stages determine "what ArcForges is". Stage 10 determines:

> **After this thing is actually put on the public internet, how can we not kill the entire product because of a release, an Azure region failure, an OTP that cannot be sent, a queue congestion, an AI Provider 429, or a Cloudflare configuration error.**

At this stage, I will design it according to the **real paid SaaS launch standards** instead of "buy a server and run it first".

# 14. API Origin should not be directly exposed to the public internet

For official Paid Cloud, I recommend:

# `ArcForges.Api` Use internal ingress.

Then:

```text
Cloudflare
    ↓
Tunnel
    ↓
internal ArcForges.Api
```

Cloudflare Tunnel currently actively establishes outbound-only connections to Cloudflare through `cloudflared`, which does not require opening an inbound port for Origin; each connector will establish multiple redundant connections and also supports running multiple connector replicas. ([Cloudflare Docs][6])

Therefore:

> An attacker cannot bypass the Cloudflare WAF and directly find `something.azurecontainerapps.io` and hit Origin.

```text
cloudflared replica B
```

All are connected to the same Tunnel.

Because Tunnel itself supports replica-based HA. ([Cloudflare Docs][6])

This one:

* Container crash;
* ACA replica restart;

The public API entry point will not be directly interrupted.

# 17. WAF, Turnstile and Application Rate Limit layers must exist at the same time

You cannot just do Cloudflare WAF.

Formal structure:

```text
Layer 1
Cloudflare WAF / Network signals

Layer 2
Turnstile
Human/Bot verification

Layer 3
ArcForges application rate limiting
Account / Device / Workspace semantics
```

Cloudflare itself defines WAF, Bot Management and Turnstile as different defense layers: WAF handles network requests, Bot Management does automated identification, and Turnstile does human-computer judgment on the client/browser side. ([Cloudflare Docs][7])

Combined current limit.
