# 21. Production PostgreSQL formal specification principles

# General Purpose

*

# Zone-Redundant HA

Burstable cannot be used as the official core production database.

Azure PostgreSQL's Zone-Redundant HA will create physically separated primary and standby and submit data synchronously; Burstable tier currently does not support this set of Zone-Redundant HA. ([Microsoft Learn][8])

---

# 22. The production PostgreSQL network is never open to the public

Use:

# Private networking / Private Endpoint

Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server currently supports Private Link; traffic can reach the database through Microsoft backbone and does not need to be exposed to the public internet. ([Microsoft Learn][9])

So:

```text
Internet
X
↓
PostgreSQL
```

Does not exist.

Only Cloud workloads:

```text
ACA
↓ private network
PostgreSQL
```

---

# 23. PgBouncer does not need to run another container by itself

Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server currently provides built-in PgBouncer, which uses independent port 6432 by default. ([Microsoft Learn][3])

So when:

```text
API replicas ↑

Worker replicas ↑

Task execution ↑
```

The number of database connections begins to be under pressure:

> Use Managed PgBouncer.

Stop maintaining it yourself:

```text
PgBouncer container
```

As an extra a la carte.

---

# 24. Select the correct PostgreSQL Backup when creating it.

Production:

# 35-day PITR

and:

# Geo-Redundant Backup

Current PostgreSQL Flexible Server:

* Automatic backup;
* PITR;
* retention 7~35 days;
* The storage redundancy selection of Geo-redundant backup must be determined when the server is created, and cannot be switched at will later. ([Microsoft Learn][10])

So production creation is done right the first time.

---

# 25. But Azure PostgreSQL Backup is still not all Backup for Stage 9

Azure official clarification:

> Managed backup files cannot be exported directly. ([Microsoft Learn][10])

So moving on to Stage 9:

```text
Primary fast recovery
=
Azure PostgreSQL PITR

Independent escape backup
=
Encrypted logical pg_dump
        ↓
Backblaze B2
        ↓
Object Lock
```

This way:

> Even if there is a very serious problem with the Azure Subscription itself, ArcForges still has an independent and recoverable copy of the data.

---

# 26. Real-time officially uses Azure SignalR Service

I do not think you need to build your own Redis Backplane for this.

Microsoft's current clear recommendations for ASP.NET Core SignalR applications hosted on Azure are:

> Use Azure SignalR Service.

It is responsible for holding client persistent connections. App Server does not need to expand instances due to the number of connections, nor does it require sticky sessions. ([Microsoft Learn][11])

This is very consistent with:

```text
ArcChat Mobile

ArcChat Web

Desktop ArcChat

Task progress

Entitlement updates

Device presence

Approvals

Remote Agent
```

---

# 27. Production SignalR is recommended to go directly to Premium

The reason is not "more expensive is better".

Instead:

# Real-time/Remote are user-visible core Cloud capabilities.

Azure SignalR's zone redundancy is currently in the Premium tier and is automatically distributed to Availability Zones in supported regions. ([Microsoft Learn][4])

Closed Beta:

> Standard Yes.

Official Paid GA:

# Premium.

And the current Standard → Premium can be upgraded without downtime. ([Microsoft Learn][12])

---

# 28. But SignalR is not a Task State Database

Very important.

SignalR:

```text
Task changed
→ notify
```

PostgreSQL:

```text
Task current state
→ source of truth
```

Missed notifications due to mobile disconnection:

```text
Reconnect
↓
GET Task
↓
Get true status
```

Do not put:

> WebSocket message

When persisting state.

---

# 29. Asynchronous messages: Azure Service Bus

I recommend continuing to choose:

# Azure Service Bus

instead of:

* Kafka;
* RabbitMQ self-built;
* Redis Queue;
* NATS builds itself.

Purpose:

```text
Billing event processing

Notifications

Search indexing

Sync background

Task dispatch

Automation dispatch

Cleanup

Reconciliation
```

---

# 30. But Message Broker can never be a business. Source of Truth

Formal:

```text
Database transaction
    │
    ├── Domain state
    │
    └── Outbox
             ↓
        Service Bus
             ↓
          Worker
             ↓
           Inbox
```

That is:

# Transactional Outbox / Inbox.

This way:

> DB commit succeeded, Queue send failed

Business events will not be lost.

---

# 31. All Queue Consumers must be Idempotent

The reliable reception semantics of Service Bus may still produce redelivery; Microsoft currently explicitly requires consumers to perform idempotent processing according to MessageId/business identifier, and duplicate detection cannot replace receive-side idempotency. ([Microsoft Learn][13])

So:

```text
Message delivered 1 time
Message delivered 5 times
```

Business results:

# Totally consistent.

---

# 32. Use Session only when sequence is required

For example the same one:

```text
SubscriptionId

ObjectId

TaskId
```

Certain events must be ordered.

Service Bus Sessions currently provides per-session FIFO/order processing. ([Microsoft Learn][14])

Do not force Session for all Queues.

Because:

> There is no need to reduce parallelism.

---

# 33. Dead Letter Queue must be a first-class operation object

Not:

> Message failed 10 times → DLQ → No one will ever read it.

Must monitor:

```text
DLQ count

Oldest DLQ age

Message type

Failure reason
```

And provide:

```text
Inspect

Retry

Discard with reason
```

All operations enter Audit.

---

# 34. Service Bus In the first stage, you do not need to get Premium as soon as you get up.

Here I make different choices with SignalR.

Service Bus official current positioning:

* Standard is more suitable for low throughput/development or scenarios that are not particularly sensitive to throttling;
* Premium provides dedicated resources, predictable latency/throughput, and is more suitable for more demanding production workloads. ([Microsoft Learn][15])

So ArcForges V1 can:

# **Service Bus Standard**

Go online first.

Because:

* Queue itself is not directly connected to the user;
* Workers can catch up after backlog;
* Outbox ensures that business facts are not lost;
* Initial throughput is expected to be modest.

---

# 35. When to upgrade Service Bus Premium?

Specify trigger conditions:

```text
need Private Endpoint

Queue latency SLO Unreachable

appear steadily throttling

Throughput significantly improved

Need for stronger network isolation
```

Private Endpoint is currently only supported by Service Bus Premium. ([Microsoft Learn][16])

Application layer:

> There is no need to change the business model at all.

And right from the start:

# Managed Identity + Entra RBAC

connection.

Service Bus currently supports Managed Identity, and SAS/local authentication can be turned off, leaving only Microsoft Entra authentication. ([Microsoft Learn][17])

Upgrading Tier in this way will not cause architecture rework.

---

# 36. V1 cannot be used on Redis

This is my very clear conclusion.

Already have:

```text
PostgreSQL

Service Bus

Azure SignalR
```

There is no irreplaceable responsibility in the first stage of Redis.

Do not do it for:

> "SaaS seems to require Redis"

Add a system.

---

# 37. Especially do not use the old Azure Cache for Redis

Because it's already 2026.

Microsoft has announced legacy Azure Cache for Redis full SKU retirement and recommends migrating to **Azure Managed Redis**; new customers will already be subject to new legacy SKU restrictions starting in April 2026. ([Microsoft Learn][18])

I will actually detect this in the future:

```text
distributed cache required
```

Next:

# Azure Managed Redis

Instead of the old Azure Cache for Redis.

---

# 38. Cloud Task: Trusted work and untrusted code must be separated

Normal:

```text
ArcForges trusted Task code
```

You can run:

# ACA Jobs.

However:

```text
User script

LLM generated Python

Unknown code

Third-party executable
```

Never directly:

> Runs in the ArcForges.Worker container.

---

# 39. Untrusted Code Execution Reserves Azure Dynamic Sessions

Azure Container Apps Dynamic Sessions currently uses Hyper-V isolation to safely run untrusted/user/LLM-generated code in an isolated environment; the current region list also includes Japan East. ([Microsoft Learn][19])

So in the future:

```text
ArcChat Code Interpreter
```

Should:

```text
Agent
 ↓
Dedicated Sandbox Runtime
 ↓
result
```

Not:

```text
Agent
 ↓
Process.Start() inside ArcForges.Api
```

---

# 40. But V1 does not need to be launched on the complex Sandbox platform immediately because of this.

The rules are:

> **V1 does not have arbitrary code execution capabilities, so do not create it at all.**

Other functions really require:

# Dynamic Session Adapter.

That's correct delay complexity, not rework.

---

# 41. Secrets: Unified production into Azure Key Vault

Need to save:

```text
Waffo API credentials

Postmark token

Cloudflare service token when required

AI provider credentials

Backup credentials

Encryption KEKs
```

Cannot:

```text
appsettings.Production.json
```

Nor can it last long:

```text
GitHub Secret
→ Direct injection into all production secret
```

---

# 42. Azure-to-Azure Try not to use Secret at all

ACA:

# Managed Identity

Visit:

```text
Key Vault

Service Bus

ACR

other Azure resources
```

Container Apps currently supports Managed Identity natively and also supports referencing Key Vault secrets through Managed Identity. ([Microsoft Learn][20])

Therefore:

> If you can use Identity, you do not need connection string.

---

# 43. Key Vault officially uses RBAC mode

Microsoft currently defines Key Vault access policies as legacy and clearly recommends Azure RBAC; starting from the 2026-02-01 API version, the new Key Vault also uses RBAC by default. ([Microsoft Learn][21])

Therefore:

# RBAC only.

Each Runtime Role:

Only have the permissions you need.

---

# 44. Production Key Vault opens Purge Protection

Production:

```text
Soft Delete

Purge Protection
```

Both are enabled.

Azure currently also explicitly recommends using both protection features for production environments. ([Microsoft Learn][22])

Avoid:

> After the attacker obtains administrator rights, he directly purges all production keys.

---

# 45. But users' millions of Cloud BYOKs should not be stored one by one Key Vault Secret

This is very easy to design wrong.

User:

```text
Workspace A Claude Key
Workspace B OpenAI Key
...
```

Cannot:

> One million Workspace → One million Azure Key Vault secret objects.

Correct:

```text
Cloud BYOK
 ↓
Application-level encrypted payload
 ↓
DB / secure store

DEK
 ↓ envelope encryption

KEK
 ↓
Azure Key Vault
```

Key Vault Save:

# Key Encryption Keys.

Instead of becoming a business database for each user's Secret.

# 46. The environment must be officially divided into 4 layers

## Local Development

```text
Aspire
local Postgres
local dependencies
mock/test services
```

Development experience is prioritized.

# 47. CI Integration

Short life cycle.

```text
Containers
Test DB
Fake integrations
```

PR finished:

> Delete.

Do not start the entire official Azure Cloud with each PR.

# 48. Staging

exist for a long time.

It must try to match Production:

# Topology-compatible

But on a small scale.

Includes:

```text
ACA

Postgres

Service Bus

SignalR

Waffo Test

AI low-limit credentials

Postmark staging server
```

# 49. Production

Completely independent:

```text
Production Azure Subscription

Production Database

Production R2 Bucket

Production Waffo credentials

Production AI Keys

Production Postmark

Production Key Vault
```

Not shared by Staging/Prod:

> "Just the schema is different".

# 50. Prod and Non-prod are the two best Azure Subscriptions

I formally recommend:

```text
ArcForges-NonProd

ArcForges-Production
```

The same Microsoft Entra tenant works.

But Billing/resource/RBAC blast radius:

# separate.

Especially:

> Staging Terraform errors should never destroy a Production Database.

# 51. Production data will never be copied to Staging

Very important.

Not allowed:

```text
pg_dump prod
→ staging
```

It directly contains:

* Email;
* Notes;
* Chat;
* BYOK;
* User files.

The test requires a real structure:

# Synthetic data.

Special bug debugging:

> Minimize + De-identify + Explicitly controlled Extract.

# 52. Infrastructure as Code: Officially adopt Terraform

The reason is simple:

Your Production is not just Azure.

It also has:

```text
Azure

Cloudflare

Better Stack

B2

Email
```

Azure officially provides two Terraform Providers, AzureRM and AzAPI: AzureRM is a standard typed provider, and AzAPI can cover new resources/APIs that AzureRM does not yet support. ([Microsoft Learn][23])

Cloudflare also has an official Terraform Provider, and the 2026 v5 Provider has been stably and continuously updated. ([Cloudflare Docs][24])

Better Stack also officially provides Terraform provider to manage monitors, on-call, status pages, telemetry, etc. ([BetterStack][25])

So:

# Terraform is best suited as a cross-cloud Production IaC.

---

# 53. Aspire will not be replaced by Terraform

Two responsibilities:

## Aspire

```text
What does ArcForges consist of?

Which services talk to which?

Local development
Developer dashboard
Service defaults
```

---

## Terraform

```text
Where does production run?

How many replicas?

Which VNet?

Which RBAC?

Which DNS?

Which Tunnel?

Which monitor?

Which production storage?
```

Do not try to:

> Become the production Source of Truth for all things Cloudflare/B2/BetterStack with Aspire AppHost.

Aspire currently does have the ability to deploy ACA and generate Bicep, but this is more suitable for Azure-native deployment/workflow. ([Microsoft Learn][26])

---

# 54. Terraform State itself is a Secret

Production Terraform state may contain:

* Resource IDs;
* endpoint;
* sensitive config;
* Sometimes even provider-returned secrets.

So:

# Never commit to Git.

Officially released:

# Dedicated Azure Storage Backend.

The Azure Blob backend currently provides remote state locking/consistency; also supports using OIDC/Entra ID without requiring a SAS secret. ([HashiCorp Developer][27])

---

# 55. Terraform State is also divided into environments

For example:

```text
bootstrap

nonprod

production

cloudflare-production

monitoring
```

Not all Providers:

> A huge `terraform.tfstate`.

Blast radius is too large.

---

# 56. Terraform Provider Version must be Pin

In particular, Cloudflare Terraform Provider updates relatively quickly.

Do not:

```text
latest
```

Each CI automatically eats a new Major/Minor.

Should:

```text
known-good version
```

Then:

> Standalone Renovation PR → plan → review → upgrade.

# 57. Production prohibits "Portal driven infrastructure"

Official rules:

# IaC First.

Normal changes:

```text
Git PR
↓
Terraform Plan
↓
Review
↓
Apply
```

instead of:

```text
Azure Portal
Just click
```

Emergency manual modification:

> Yes.

But after the accident is over, you must:

# Reconcile back into IaC.

---

# 58. Drift Detection must be done regularly

For example every day:

```text
terraform plan
```

Found:

```text
Production differs from Git
```

Call the police.

Do not find out half a year later:

> A certain Firewall Rule was temporarily enabled during the last debugging.

# 59. GitHub Actions to Azure: Only use OIDC

Not saving one:

```text
AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
Valid for two years
```

GitHub Actions can currently use OIDC to exchange short-term tokens from Azure, without the need to store long-term Azure credentials in GitHub. ([GitHub Docs][28])

So:

```text
GitHub
↓ OIDC
Microsoft Entra
↓ short-lived token
Azure
```

# 60. Staging and Production use different Deployment Identity

```text
GitHub → Staging Identity

GitHub → Production Identity
```

Production Identity:

> Only the scope required by Production can be deployed.

Cannot be:

# Subscription Owner.

# 61. Container Image is officially released in Azure Container Registry

Release:

```text
Build once
↓
Push ACR
↓
Image Digest
```

Then:

```text
Staging
↓ same digest
Production
```

# Production is not allowed to build again.

---

# 62. Deployment is based on Digest, not `latest`

Each artifact in ACR's OCI manifest has a unique SHA-256 digest; pulling through the digest ensures that you will get exactly the same image, even if a tag later points to other content. ([Microsoft Learn][29])

So:

```text
arcforges-api@sha256:...
```

This is the real Production Release Identity.

---

# 63. Server Build should also have SBOM + Provenance

Stage 5 Desktop already does this.

The same goes for Cloud Containers:

```text
Commit
↓
GitHub Workflow
↓
Container Digest
↓
SBOM
↓
Build Attestation
```

GitHub Artifact Attestations can currently generate cryptographically signed build provenance for container images, and also supports associated SBOM. ([GitHub Docs][30])

After this I encountered:

> A NuGet CVE

Can know immediately:

> Which Production Image contains it.

# 64. Formal Deployment Pipeline

Recommended to fix:

```text
PR
 ↓
Build
 ↓
Unit Tests
 ↓
Integration Tests
 ↓
Security / Dependency Checks
 ↓
Container Build
 ↓
SBOM
 ↓
Attestation
 ↓
Push ACR
 ↓
Deploy Staging
 ↓
Smoke Tests
 ↓
Synthetic Tests
 ↓
Production approval
 ↓

 ↓
Canary / Blue-Green
 ↓
Observe
 ↓
Full traffic
```

# 65. Production via GitHub Environment

```text
environment:
production
```

GitHub Environments currently supports:

* branch/tag restrictions;
* deployment protection;
* required reviewers, available under corresponding GitHub plan/repository visibility conditions. ([GitHub Docs][31])

Even if some reviewer features are not available due to current plan/private libraries:

> Production deployment policy must still be limited to the official release branch/tag in workflow + OIDC federation conditions.

---

# 66. ACA Revisions are just used for security releases

Azure Container Apps currently:

* Single revision mode can be replaced by zero-downtime by default;
* Multiple revision can traffic splitting;
* Traffic can be directed to different revisions proportionally. ([Microsoft Learn][32])

So:

### Ordinary low risk Release

Single revision zero-downtime.

### Key Release

```text
old 95%
new 5%
```

Observe.

Again:

```text
50 / 50
```

Finally:

```text
100% new
```

During low traffic periods you can use:

> Blue/Green + synthetic test

Instead of mechanically waiting for "5% real users".

---

# 67. Rollback must be one-click level

Error found:

```text
new revision
↓ bad
```

Immediately:

```text
Traffic → previous revision
```

Not:

> Recompile an older version on the spot.

---

# 68. Database Migration is the most dangerous part of the entire Deployment

Must be determined:

# **Disable automatic migration of all App Replica when starting.**

Otherwise:

```text
Replica A
Replica B
Replica C
```

Run migration at the same time.

This is very dangerous in rolling releases.

---

# 69. Migration as an independent Deployment Step

For example:

```text
DB Migration Job
```

Only executed once.

Success:

> Application rollout is allowed.

Failure:

> Deployment Stop.

---

# 70. Database Schema uses Expand/Contract

For example, to:

```text
OldColumn
```

Replace with:

```text
NewColumn
```

Definitely not a release:

```text
DROP OldColumn
+
deploy new app
```

Should:

### Release A

```text
Add NewColumn
```

Old/new apps can still run.

### Release B

Migrate data.

### Release C

The new app no longer relies on OldColumn at all.

### Release D

Finally remove OldColumn.

This way:

> Production App Rollback is where this really works.

---

# 71. Do not understand DB Rollback as "Migration down"

Production bug:

First choice:

# Application rollback / forward fix.

Not:

> Automatically run Down Migration.

Because production schema/data migration is likely to be irreversible.

# 129. A real Game Day must be done before going online

Not just Unit Test.

Active simulation:

### Pull Postgres connectivity

See how the system fails.

### Stop Worker

Check whether the Queue is backlogged and restored.

### Kill cloudflared replica

Confirm another one to continue.

### Disable Postmark sandbox route

Test email failed.

### Simulate Waffo delayed webhook

Confirmation does not revoke Existing Entitlement.

### Make AI provider return 429

Confirm fallback/budget is normal.

### Temporarily block R2

Confirm that the local Sync queue does not lose changes.

### Deploy bad ACA revision

Confirm that rollback can be done quickly.

# The most critical Stage 10 principle

After ArcForges goes online, the design goals of the infrastructure are not:

# **Never fail.**

This is impossible.

The real goal is:

# **No single ordinary provider failure turns into data loss, entitlement corruption, or destruction of the local product experience.**

So:

* If Waffo is down, paid users will not lose their rights;
* AI Provider hangs, local AI/BYOK continues;
* R2 hangs, local save continues;
* SignalR hangs, but Task State is not lost;
* Service Bus repeats messages but does not repeat business operations;
* Postmark is down, but Passkey users can still log in;
* Better Stack is down, but the product runs as usual;
* Production release is broken, Revision can rollback quickly;
* If there is a problem with Azure Region, IaC, PITR and independent B2 backup can be reconstructed;
* **Any Cloud failure will not render the user's local ArcNotes, ArcSlate, ArcScope, ArcChat Local Agent unavailable.**

At this point, Stage 0 to Stage 10 have formed a truly complete commercial production chain:

**Product → Account → Billing → Entitlement → Distribution → Agent Ecosystem → Cloud → AI Economics → User Data → Production Operations**

Stage 10 does not require running a huge "cloud platform team" from day one, yet it still reserves in advance all the **HA, DR, IaC, Queue, Observability, Security, Provider Failover, and data recovery boundaries** that genuinely matter as scale grows.

# stage11

---

Now entering **Stage 11: Legal, Open Source, Privacy and Compliance**.

Your stage really does not need to be as complicated as Stage 9/10. Your direction has naturally simplified many issues:

> **The core software itself is AGPL open source; local functions are free; commercial revenue comes from the official Cloud / Managed AI; Waffo Pancake does MoR.**

So what really needs to be done at this stage is to clearly define several boundaries at once to avoid having to change the product later because of a dependency license, a privacy policy modification or AI compliance requirements.

The following is a compliance baseline at the product and architectural levels and is not a substitute for formal jurisdiction-specific counsel advice.

---

# 1. ArcForges' own license: unified AGPL, no complicated dual licenses

Now that you've made it clear:

# **ArcForges itself is open sourced under AGPL**

Then I suggest that the core code be unified:

# `AGPL-3.0-only`

Includes:

```text
ArcChat Desktop
ArcNotes
ArcScope
ArcSlate
ArcImage ...

ArcForges Cloud Server

Agent Runtime
Capability infrastructure
Sync server
Self-host server
```

If possible, avoid:

```text
ArcChat MIT
Server AGPL
Agent GPL
SDK Apache
Custom license for a certain module
```

Make it a license platter.

---

# 2. Why I prefer `AGPL-3.0-only`

instead of:

```text
AGPL-3.0-or-later
```

`or-later` means that after FSF releases a new version in the future, the license recipient can choose to use subsequent versions; the legal boundaries of `only` are fixed at today's clear AGPLv3.

Your product goal is a long-term commercial Cloud, and you have not shown that you must follow the non-existent AGPLv4 in the future, so:

# **`AGPL-3.0-only` is more predictable.**

This is a product strategy choice, not that there is a problem with `or-later`.

---

# 3. AGPL is exactly in line with ArcForges' business model

One of the biggest differences between AGPL and ordinary GPL is the addition of network interactive source code obligations for software running on the network: if someone modifies an AGPL program and allows users to use the modified version through the network, these network users need to be provided with the opportunity to obtain the corresponding source code. Article 13 of AGPL clearly provides for this. ([GNU][1])

This matches well with ArcForges:

```text
code
→ Open source

Self-host
→ allow

official Cloud
→ Collect money for operating services
```

Therefore your business moat should not be:

> "Server source code hidden."

Instead:

> **Official service stability, infrastructure, AI, storage, synchronization, operations, branding and user experience.**

This is completely consistent with the Stage 0 business model.

---

# 4. The official Cloud also directly provides Source links.

Even though a lot of the code already lives on GitHub, I still recommend:

```text
arcforges.com/open-source

Account / ArcChat Web
About → Source Code
```

Explicitly point to:

> Current ArcForges Server/Web/relevant component source.

AGPL itself specifically requires modified versions of software for network interaction to provide easy access to Corresponding Sources. ([GNU][1])

In this way, even if community contributions are introduced in the future, there is no need to reconsider:

> How exactly does official SaaS satisfy AGPL.

Do more than the bare minimum from day one.

---

# 5. Third-party dependence: Do not be afraid of GPL/AGPL, but you must be afraid of "license incompatibility"

Because you are already AGPL yourself, many copyleft issues that others worry about are not a problem for ArcForges.

I recommend establishing very simple three-level rules.

## Green: OK by default

For example:

```text
MIT

Apache-2.0

BSD-2-Clause

BSD-3-Clause

ISC

0BSD

Zlib
```

Just keep Copyright / License / NOTICE as normal.

Apache 2.0 is compatible with GPLv3, so Apache 2.0 code can enter GPLv3 family projects; Apache officials have also clearly stated this one-way compatibility relationship. ([Apache Software Foundation][2])

---

# 6. Yellow: Yes, but review it

For example:

```text
AGPL-3.0

GPL-3.0

LGPL-3.0

MPL-2.0
```

Since ArcForges itself is already AGPL, the GPLv3/AGPLv3 combination is not a core barrier.

Section 13 of AGPLv3 explicitly allows AGPLv3 to be linked or combined with GPLv3 modules; the GNU FAQ also explicitly states that the two can be combined with each other. ([GNU][1])

So:

> **There is no need to deliberately give up a very good dependency for fear of GPL/AGPL.**

However, you must confirm the specific version, NOTICE, source code provision method and other obligations.

---

# 7. Red: In principle, do not enter core products

The key points to guard against are:

```text
GPL-2.0-only

Non-commercial licenses

Research-only licenses

Source-available but non-open-source licenses

Business Source License / BSL
 (Depends on specific version and conversion terms) 

SSPL

Commons Clause

Elastic License

PolyForm Noncommercial

CC BY-NC for program code/core resources

of unknown origin GitHub code

“Free to use”but not officially LICENSE code
```

Especially:

# `GPL-2.0-only`

GPLv2-only and GPLv3 are not inherently compatible; the official GNU license description and FAQ clearly point out this, and its compatibility matrix states that the same GPLv3 compatibility judgment principles apply to AGPLv3. ([GNU][3])

So do not do it because:

> "We AGPL anyway"

Just think that all copyleft can be mixed casually.

---

# 8. Apache-2.0 projects like AionUi have no license barriers

Stage 6 has confirmed that the current AionUi is Apache-2.0.

For ArcForges AGPL projects:

> Apache-2.0 itself is a very easy source to work with.

What really needs to be done is:

* Retain the original author's copyright statement;
* Keep the Apache License;
* If NOTICE exists upstream, keep NOTICE correctly;
* Make it clear which code comes from/modified from upstream;
* Do not pass it off as an ArcForges original.

The compatibility relationship between Apache 2.0 → GPLv3-based licenses is clear. ([Apache Software Foundation][2])

---

# 9. Automatically perform License Compliance without relying on artificial memory

Stage 5 already requires SBOM.

Now add:

# License Inventory

Each official Release is automatically generated:

```text
Dependency
Version
License
Source
Copyright
Notice
```

Finally formed:

```text
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES
SBOM
```

CI does at least:

```text
Unknown license → Fail

Disallowed license → Fail

License changed since previous version → Review
```

This will not happen in a few years:

> An indirect NuGet dependency changed its license from MIT, and no one noticed it for half a year.

# 11. Contributor: I recommend DCO, do not bother with CLA

Now that you've determined:

> ArcForges long-term AGPL open source.

There is no need to ask the community to grant all copyrights to you for the future "sudden closed source/commercial dual license".

Adopt:

# Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) 

Contributor:

```text
Signed-off-by: Name <email>
```

Indicates that he has the right to contribute the code.

This mode:

* Simple;
* The open source community is easily receptive;
* No need to sign a complicated CLA;
* Contributors are not required to transfer copyright.

Only you decide clearly in the future:

> "I'm going to relicense the community contribution into a proprietary commercial edition."

It would be better to have CLA starting from the first external contributor.

But this and now:

# AGPL + Managed Cloud Business Model

Not required.

So I'm not going to add complexity to a business model that does not exist now.

# 13. Why Brand cannot be copied arbitrarily along with the code

Because otherwise someone could:

```text
fork ArcChat
↓
Change a bunch of malicious code
↓
Still calling ArcChat Official
```

Users cannot tell the difference at all.

Correct policy:

> Code can be forked.

But fork should not have the power:

> Impersonates official ArcForges products and services.

So `TRADEMARKS.md` allows:

```text

“Fork of ArcChat”
```

However, it is prohibited to:

```text
“Official ArcChat”

Use official logo Causing users to have officially sanctioned misunderstandings
```

This does not conflict with true open source at all.

# 24. GDPR data breach response must enter Stage 10 Incident Runbook

Under GDPR, if a personal data leakage may pose a risk to individual rights and freedoms, the Controller is in principle required to notify the supervisory authority without unreasonable delay and within **72 hours** at the latest after becoming aware of it; in high-risk situations, it may also be required to notify affected individuals. ([European Commission][6])

So:

```text
Possible Personal Data Breach
```

Automatically upgrade to:

# SEV0 Legal/Security Incident.

No ordinary bug.

---

# 25. Chinese users should also pay special attention to one thing: your Cloud is currently in Japan East

This means:

> After users in mainland China enable Official Cloud, there is likely to be cross-border processing of personal information.

Article 39 of the "Personal Information Protection Law" clearly requires that when personal information is provided overseas, the overseas recipient needs to be notified, the purpose and method of processing, the type of personal information, and how the user can exercise rights to the recipient, etc., and **separate consent** must be obtained. ([SAMR][7])

So for the first time, Chinese users:

# Enable Official Cloud

It's better to have an explicit:

```text
Cloud data processing / cross-border consent
```

Instead of hiding it in the last paragraph of Terms on page 40.

---

# 26. However, China's data export rules are now more relaxed than before.

The 2024 "Regulations on Promoting and Regulating Cross-Border Data Flows" adjusts the applicable thresholds for security assessments, standard contracts and certifications; for example, non-critical information infrastructure operators that have provided general personal information of less than 100,000 people overseas since January 1 of that year may be exempted from security assessments, standard contracts or certifications under relevant conditions. ([China Anti-Corruption Website][8])

The latest CAC policy Q&A in 2026 continues to make it clear: after reaching higher headcount or involving sensitive personal information, different paths will be entered, such as standard contracts, certification or security assessments. ([China Anti-Corruption Website][9])

So:

# V1 does not need to build mainland data centers for the Chinese market now.

But it must:

```text
Statistics on the scale of user data in China

Distinguish between ordinary/Sensitive personal information

Record cross-border processing

Triggered before reaching the applicable threshold Compliance Review
```

Instead of waiting until the user has exceeded the threshold to know.

# 30. AI compliance has a new point in time that must be paid special attention to now.

Today is:

# **2026-07-21**

The European Commission just yesterday released final transparency implementation guidance for Article 50 of the AI Act.

Relevant transparency obligations:

# **Applicable from 2026-08-02.**

The committee clearly stated:

* When the user directly interacts with the AI system, the user should know that they are interacting with the AI;
* Some AI-generated/manipulated content needs to be identifiable;
* Certain scenarios such as deepfakes require disclosure;
* AI-generated text used to disseminate public interest information without human editing also has specific disclosure requirements. ([Digital Strategy][11])

# 33. Deepfake content needs to be treated separately

The EU AI Act currently clearly requires that, where applicable, when using AI to generate or manipulate images, audio or videos that constitute deepfake, it is necessary to disclose that it is artificially generated or manipulated content; for obvious artistic, creative, satirical, fictional and other works, there are rules that are more suitable for their forms of expression. ([EUR-Lex][14])

So later ArcImage/ArcVideo:

> There is no need to prohibit generating content because of this article.

But it must:

# Provenance / Disclosure capable.

# Stage 11 Finalization

I would fix ArcForges' legal and open source route as:

## Software license

# **AGPL-3.0-only**

The core desktop, server, and agent infrastructure are unified, and no license fragmentation is artificially created.

---

## Third Party License

### Default priority

```text
MIT
Apache-2.0
BSD
ISC
Zlib
```

### GPLv3 / AGPLv3 / LGPLv3

# Can be used.

ArcForges is originally AGPL, so there is no need to exclude good technologies for fear of copyleft. AGPLv3 combined with GPLv3 is expressly licensed. ([GNU][17])

### Principle to avoid

```text
GPLv2-only
Non-commercial
Unknown source
Proprietary-with-unclear-redistribution
Source-available restrictive licenses
```

Unless separate legal review.

---

## Contributors

# DCO

Rather than a complex CLA.

Because the current business model does not require the community code to be secretly closed source in the future.

---

## Trademark

# Brands such as ArcForges / ArcChat / ArcNotes are reserved separately.

Code can be forked.

Do not pretend to be official.

---

## Waffo

# Waffo is responsible for MoR payment/tax/billing side.

ArcForges is responsible for:

# Product / privacy / technical service / IP.

This is consistent with the division of responsibilities in Waffo's current Developer Terms. ([Waffo Pancake][4])

---

## Privacy

Formal commitment:

# Local stays local unless the user enables a Cloud/AI operation that requires transmission.

# Sync ≠ AI upload.

# Private Workspace data is not used to train ArcForges models without separate explicit opt-in.

# No sale of user data.

# No advertising profile.

# Minimal analytics.

---

## Website Analytics

# Cloudflare Web Analytics

Keep using it.

Currently does not rely on cookies/localStorage or cross-site fingerprints to complete website analysis. ([Cloudflare Docs][10])

---

## China

Because Official Cloud is outside the country:

# Clear cross-border notification + corresponding consent flow.

And continue to count:

```text
China users
Personal data volume
Sensitive data volume
```

To handle standard contract/certification/security assessment issues before reaching applicable thresholds. Article 39 of PIPL has clear requirements for notification and separate consent to the overseas provision of personal information. ([China Anti-Corruption Website][18])

---

## EU

Inherited:

# GDPR privacy-by-design.

```text
Export
Delete
Retention
Data minimisation
Security
```

All have been implemented in Stage 1 to 10 systems. GDPR itself requires principles such as purpose limitation, data minimization and storage limitations. ([European Commission][5])

---

## AI

Something to remember here is:

# **2026-08-02**

The transparency obligations of Article 50 of the EU AI Act apply. The European Commission just released the final implementation guidance on 2026-07-20. ([Digital Strategy][11])

Therefore ArcForges remains from now on:

```text
AI interaction disclosure

AI Generated metadata

AI Modified metadata

Content provenance

Export labelling capability
```

There is no need to re-modify the entire Artifact system for ArcImage/ArcVideo in the future.

---

# last word

Stage 11 does not require turning ArcForges into a "law firm."

Your route is actually already clean:

> **AGPL open source all core code, trademarks are retained; Waffo is responsible for transactions and taxation; ArcForges does not sell data, does not do advertising portraits; Local-first, selective Cloud; users own Export/Delete; Managed AI clear data path; AI content retains Provenance; dependent licenses are automatically checked by CI.**

There are only three main categories left that really need to be confirmed by professionals before a specific business goes online:

**Personal business/taxation and cross-border personal information in mainland China, official EU GDPR/AI Act implementation text, and future DPA/SCC for Team/Enterprise.**

For the rest, the architecture of the first 10 stages has actually incorporated most of the legal and privacy requirements into the product design in advance, and there is no need to reconstruct the product for compliance.

# stage12

---

Now onto **Stage 12: The True Growth Loop**.

The biggest difference between this stage and traditional "marketing" is:

> **We are not talking about advertising, buying traffic, or issuing coupons.**
>
> What really needs to be designed is: after a user gains value from ArcForges, how will he naturally generate new uses, new content, new ecological supplies, new users and Cloud conversions, and then these new users will continue to drive the next round of growth.

For ArcForges, I think the most dangerous route is instead:

```text
Free and open source
↓
Crazy bomb Cloud
↓
Referral
↓
buy advertising
↓
chase MAU
```

This not only wastes the biggest advantage of the **AGPL + Local-first + Multi-App + ArcChat Agent + Community** architecture, but also makes it easy to make the product a normal SaaS.

The truly most powerful Growth Engine of ArcForges should be:

# **Free Local → First Value → Ecosystem Value → Create/Share → Discover → New User → Cloud Continuity → Retention → Community Creation**

---

# 1. First determine the final Growth Loop of ArcForges

I suggest that the entire system be formally defined as:

```text
                  Discover
                     │
                     ▼
             Download for Free
                     │
               No account gate
                     │
                     ▼
                 First Value
                     │
                     ▼
             Use another Arc App
                     │
                     ▼
              ArcChat becomes
              more capable
                     │
                     ▼
             Better Work / Result
                     │
          ┌──────────┴───────────┐
          │                      │
          ▼                      ▼
      Share/Create            Need Sync /
      Community Item          Remote / Mobile
          │                      │
          ▼                      ▼
     Public Discovery        ArcForges Cloud
          │                      │
          ▼                      ▼
       New Users              Retention
          │                      │
          └──────────┬───────────┘
                     ▼
              More ArcForges Use
```

This is the long-term growth flywheel.

It does not depend on:

> "What day is the best ad account ROI."

But the more people use the product itself:

> The more valuable ArcForges is.

# Stage 12 Finalization

A true ArcForges Growth strategy should not be based on:

# **Advertising + Paywall + Referral Spam**

On.

Instead, the following six mutually reinforcing flywheels should be formally formed:

---

## ① Open Source Loop

```text
Open Source
→ Discovery
→ Users
→ Contributors
→ Better Product
→ More Discovery
```

---

## ② Ecosystem Loop

```text
One Arc App
→ ArcChat / Another App
→ More Capabilities
→ Better Workflows
→ Deeper ArcForges Usage
```

This is ArcForges' most important differentiated growth mechanism.

---

## ③ Creator Loop

```text
Create Skill / Workflow / Template
→ Publish
→ Discover
→ Install
→ Fork
→ More Creators
→ More ArcForges Value
```

In the first stage, do:

# Free Community Catalog.

Not Paid Marketplace.

---

## ④ Artifact Sharing Loop

Follow-up:

```text
Create professional result
→ Share
→ Recipient discovers ArcForges
→ Open / Install
→ New user
```

Default:

# Unlisted / NoIndex.

Watermarking professional exports is not mandatory.

---

## ⑤ Cloud Continuity Loop

```text
Local User
→ Multiple devices / Remote / Mobile / Backup need
→ Cloud
→ More continuity
→ More usage
→ Higher retention
```

Cloud Conversion requires:

# Contextual.

Never launch Upgrade before starting it.

---

## ⑥ Future Team / Referral Loop

After it truly reaches scale:

```text
Team invitations

Referral promotional credits

Creator commerce
```

Not the core pre-Launch.

---

# The most critical Growth Principle

I would put the following directly as ArcForges long-term product principles:

**Download does not require an Account.**

**First Value occurs before Monetization.**

**Local Free is always a truly complete product, not a trial.**

**Cloud comes when you really need Sync/Remote/Mobile/Cloud Agent.**

**Each Arc App is great on its own; together they are even stronger.**

**ArcChat becomes an ecological capability amplifier rather than forcing dependence.**

**Community content starts with low-risk Skills / Templates / Workflows / Profiles.**

**The first Community Catalog is free, Git-backed, and Curated.**

**Creator must obtain Attribution, Version, Fork lineage and long-term Reputation.**

**Community Package is versioned from day one, with License, Trust and Compatibility.**

**Public Artifact Sharing is Phase 2 and does not destroy the security boundaries of Stage 7 in advance for growth.**

**Share Default Unlisted / NoIndex.**

**ArcForges watermarking of professional output is not mandatory.**

**GitHub Stars, Downloads, and Page Views are not North Stars.**

True North Star:

# **Weekly Successful Outcomes.**

**Product Analytics does not accept prompts, notes, filenames, paths, or user content.**

**Local Analytics is Opt-in.**

**Do not start fingerprinting just because you cannot see all your users.**

**Feature Flag is separate from Experiment.**

**Security, privacy, and price are not used as black box growth experiments.**

**Account creation does not equal consent to Marketing.**

**Do not use Spam Notification / "We miss you" to create Retention.**

**Paid Acquisition is simply an Amplifier that amplifies after the product flywheel is already established.**

---

In this way, after Stage 12 is completed, the entire growth logic of ArcForges will not be:

> "We launch a great product and then figure out how to find users."

And it will gradually become:

> **When a new user enters ArcForges, he or she may add a user, a Workflow, a Template, a Skill, an Extension, a piece of discoverable content, and a cross-App usage scenario; these added values make it easier for the next batch of users to discover, activate, and stay.**

This is the **ArcForges Growth Loop** that can truly enhance each other rather than conflict with the previous **AGPL open source, Local-first, ArcChat Agent, multi-professional App, and Cloud commercialization**.

# Stage 13: Product Topology & Architecture Baseline Freeze

This stage can now be officially done, and only one thing will be done this time:

> **Merging the completed Stages 0 to 12 with the "ArcForges Full C# Future Architecture Outline" into a product/runtime baseline that will not continue to drift.**

This does **not re-select the technology stack**, nor does it reopen whether StreamJsonRpc, Refit, SignalR, AOT, and Avalonia are correct.

These are already technical Constitutions.

The original general outline has been clear: ArcForges is All C# / All .NET; desktop products are independent and autonomous C# processes; ArcChat hosts the native Hub by default, but the Hub is only responsible for directory, routing, permissions, approval, coordination and auditing; each product continues to have its own domain status, database, resources, UI, Undo and recovery log.

What Stage 13 really does is:

# **Freeze what products are currently available, and the boundaries between these products that can never be changed at will.**

---

# 1. The final product portfolio of Stage 13

From now on, the ArcForges Phase 1 official product portfolio is frozen as:

| Products           | Stable product identity     | Positioning                                               | Current priority  |
| ------------ | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| **ArcChat**  | `arcchat`  | AI Agent Command Center / Chat / Task / Hub      | **Core** |
| **ArcNotes** | `arcnotes` | Local-first Knowledge & Document                 | **Core** |
| **ArcScope** | `arcscope` | Local-first Observation / Acquisition / Analysis | **Core** |
| **ArcSlate** | `arcslate` | Professional Video Editing / NLE                 | Second priority    |

These four are the current desktop product collection.

```text
C# / .NET / Avalonia
```

Each product is an autonomous OS Application.

ArcChat Hub is only responsible for coordination and not for professional App Domain.

### Invariant 8

The core local functions of professional apps do not depend on Account/Cloud.

### Invariant 10

Simple user Handoff does not require going through the Agent.

### Invariant 11

Transmit semantic Capability/Reference across apps without remotely operating the UI.

---

### Invariant 12

Most of the resources remain in the respective App, and the Hub does not act as a proxy for the text.

### Invariant 13

Cloud Sync and Remote Agent are different data/control paths.

---

### Invariant 14

Cloud-capable professional apps can directly participate in the Cloud functions of their own data and do not require ArcChat to become a data gateway.

---

### Invariant 15

Remote Desktop Agent is unified through ArcChat Desktop.

### Invariant 16

Mobile/Web currently belongs to ArcChat Companion, not the four professional App Web/Mobile Editions.

### Invariant 17

Product versions and release life cycles are independent.

---

### Invariant 18

Shared Foundation cannot become a shared Domain.

### Invariant 19

Olive is only used as an important reference for rewriting ArcSlate C# and does not change the entire C# technical baseline.

### Invariant 20

Technical exceptions can only exist within controlled boundaries already permitted by the general program, and new exceptions require formal ADR.

# 96. Completion criteria for Stage 13

After completing this phase, any subsequent design should immediately answer these seven questions:

### Which Product does this function belong to?

Must be unique or explicit across App orchestrators.

---

### Who owns its data?

Must be clear.

---

### Is ArcChat Owner or Reference/Orchestrator?

Must be clear.

---

### Can we still do the core work of this product without ArcChat?

Professional apps should:

# Yes.

---

### Can I still work locally without Cloud?

All Desktop Products:

# Yes.

---

### Is this cross-App behavior Handoff or Orchestration?

Must be able to differentiate.

---

### Is this a normal implementation choice, or is it creating a new Architecture Exception?

Must be able to judge.

---

# Stage 13 Formal Conclusion

From now on, the current product topology of ArcForges is officially frozen as:

# **ArcChat + ArcNotes + ArcScope + ArcSlate**

Among them:

### ArcChat

# AI / Agent / Task / Automation / Local Hub / Remote Control Plane.

### ArcNotes

# Local-first Knowledge & Document Authority.

### ArcScope

# Local-first Observation / Acquisition / Telemetry Analysis Authority.

### ArcSlate

# Local-first Professional Video Editing Authority, rewritten in C# + Avalonia with Olive as the key product reference.

---

Four:

# All are independent, autonomous, complete C#/Avalonia desktop applications.

Between the four:

# Writable business databases are not shared.

Professional App:

# Do not rely on ArcChat to do your core local work.

ArcChat:

# Domain responsible for cross-App Agent Orchestration but does not own other products.

Professional App's own Cloud data capabilities:

# ArcChat is not required as a mandatory data gateway.

And Remote Desktop Agent:

# Unified through ArcChat Desktop Hub.

Mobile and Web:

# Currently they are ArcChat Companion/Cloud surface, not the full mobile/Web versions of ArcNotes, ArcScope, and ArcSlate.

The only exceptions allowed for technical realities are to continue to use the existing general outline:

# MAUI Android AOT real boundaries, EF Core strict AOT boundaries, controlled Native Library boundaries, and isolated hosts that can be added through ADR only after sufficient evidence.

**ArcSlate/Olive is not a technical exception.**

At this point, the technical outline of the original `ArcVideo / ArcImage` era can be completely aligned with the current real product planning without overturning any of the established **All C#, Avalonia, Native AOT, StreamJsonRpc, Refit, SignalR, state ownership and product autonomy principles**.

# Stage 14: Shared Desktop Product Experience Foundation

The goals of this stage are very clear:

> **Let ArcChat, ArcNotes, ArcScope, and ArcSlate look, operate, and think as part of the same ArcForges product family, while retaining their respective workspaces and interaction methods as professional software.**

It's not about redesigning the technology Foundation.

The following have been frozen by "ArcForges Full C# Future Architecture Outline" and Stage 13 and will no longer be discussed:

```text
C# / .NET
Avalonia
Native AOT
MVVM/Application/Domain layered
StreamJsonRpc
HTTP/JSON + Refit
SignalR
each App independence and autonomy
each App Have your own status
```

The general outline itself has also been made clear: the desktop product is an independent Avalonia/C# process, and the ViewModel only consumes ViewState and calls application services; there must be clear rules for multiple windows, multiple instances, file associations, life cycles, and recovery.

Stage 14 is to build:

# **ArcForges Desktop Experience Contract**

The next four apps will all follow this experience language.

But:

# **Shared Experience ≠ Shared Shell ≠ Shared Domain.**

This is the first principle of Stage 14.

# 2. ArcForges Desktop Design principles are officially frozen

I recommend that all future Desktop UIs first meet the following principles.

## 1. Professional-first

ArcForges is a productivity/professional tool.

So:

> Content and work objects are always more important than brand decoration.

Prohibited:

```text
Giant gradient welcome page
Over animation
everywhere Upgrade CTA
Marketing that takes up a lot of space Banner
```

After opening the professional software, you should enter it as soon as possible:

# Work.

---

# 2. Calm UI

ArcForges UI should:

```text
low noise
Controllable information density
clear status
animation restraint
Dangerous operation is obvious
```

Especially ArcScope/ArcSlate:

> Users already need to observe a lot of complex information, and the UI itself cannot continue to make noise.

---

# 3. Progressive Complexity

Open for the first time:

> Do not throw all advanced capabilities to users at the same time.

But for advanced users:

> You cannot be castrated for the sake of "simplicity".

Should:

```text
Common workflows
→ obvious

Advanced workflows
→ discoverable

Expert workflows
→ fast
```

That is:

# Easy to start, efficient at depth.

---

# 4. Keyboard + Mouse are equally important

ArcForges is not a pure touch application.

Professional users should be able to:

```text
Mouse
Keyboard
Command Palette
Context Menu
Drag & Drop
```

Mix it up.

Especially:

```text
ArcNotes
ArcScope
ArcSlate
```

An efficient Keyboard Workflow must be established.

---

# 5. Local-first status must be truly visible

Users can never tell the difference:

```text
Saved locally

vs

Synced to Cloud
```

So these two states:

# It must be a different concept.

There can never be just one:

```text
✓ Saved
```

Then the user does not know:

> Has it actually been flushed to local disk, or has it already been uploaded to Cloud?

---

# 3. Design System: What is unified is Semantic Token, not dead colors.

There should be a single Design System established throughout ArcForges.

But the Design System should not become:

```text
Button = #3484FF
Border = #272727
```

This hardcoded table.

should be:

# Semantic Design Tokens.

For example conceptually:

```text
Surface.Primary
Surface.Secondary
Surface.Raised

Text.Primary
Text.Secondary
Text.Disabled

Border.Default
Border.Strong

Accent.Primary

State.Success
State.Warning
State.Danger
State.Info

Selection
Focus
```

Then:

```text
Light Theme

Dark Theme

High Contrast later
```

map separately.

---

# 4. Business UIs are prohibited from inventing color semantics themselves.

For example ArcScope:

```text
red = error
```

ArcSlate:

```text
red = selected clip
```

ArcNotes:

```text
red = destructive
```

In the end the whole product will be messed up.

Business data colors can be used freely, for example:

```text
Signal channel colors
Timeline label colors
Tag colors
```

But:

# Product state colors

Must be unified.

---

# 5. Pography establishes semantic hierarchy

Should not App A:

```text
18px = H1
```

App B:

```text
21px = H1
```

Everyone messes around.

Unified role:

```text
Display

Title

Heading

Body

Secondary

Caption

Code / Monospace

Numeric / Measurement
```

ArcScope specifically requires:

# Stable Numeric Presentation.

For example:

```text
1.000 V
20.3 kHz
14:32:04.231
```

Must be suitable for quick scanning.

---

# 6. Density must become the first-class capability of Design System

This is where the four products differ greatly.

ArcChat can compare:

# Comfortable.

ArcNotes:

# Comfortable / Compact.

ArcScope:

# Compact.

ArcSlate:

# Compact / Professional Dense.

So the Design System itself should support:

```text
Comfortable

Compact
```

instead of:

> ArcScope secretly changes the height of all Controls to smaller sizes.

The same component like this:

```text
Dropdown
Button
Input
List
```

Still maintaining a unified design language.

---

# 7. Iconography must be unified

The entire ArcForges uses a unified semantic Icon System.

For example:

```text
Add
Delete
Search
Settings
Share
Sync
Warning
Info
Undo
Redo
Play
Pause
Stop
```

Same meaning:

# The same visual language.

Ban every app:

> Find a similar icon from different Icon Packs.

---

# 8. Icons cannot be the only source of information

For example:

```text
⚠
```

Critical errors cannot be expressed individually.

Should match:

```text
Warning
Connection lost
```

This will be further stipulated in Stage 27 Accessibility later.

Stage 14 First ensure that the Design System does not create obstacles.

---

# 9. Motion unified restraint

Allowed:

```text
panel transition

selection feedback

expand/collapse

task state transition
```

But:

```text
long time page transition
A lot spring animation
decorative bouncing
```

Not suitable for professional apps.

All core processes:

# Do not rely on animation to understand.

---

# 10. Window Architecture: First unify window type semantics

All apps can have the following types of windows.

## Main Workspace Window

The main window that really works.

For example:

```text
ArcNotes document workspace
ArcScope analysis workspace
ArcSlate editing workspace
ArcChat main window
```

---

## Secondary / Document Window

Need to put something:

```text
Document
Session
Project
Viewer
```

When you become independent.

---

## Utility Window

For example:

```text
Settings

Plugin manager later

Diagnostics

Task details

Preferences
```

But if you can do Panel/Flyout, do not abuse windows.

---

## Dialog

Only use when really needed:

```text
Users make immediate decisions
```

to continue the process.

---

# 11. Do not make all operations into Modal Dialog

In particular, it is prohibited to:

```text
Delete?
OK

Rename?
Dialog

Change color?
Dialog

Export option?
Dialog
```

A large number of professional software Modal:

> Will disrupt workflow.

Priority:

```text
Inline

Inspector

Panel

Flyout

Contextual surface
```

Modal for truly irreversible/important decisions.

---

# 12. Unify the Workspace Region concept

Instead of requiring the four apps to have the same layout, let them use the same set of "spatial semantics."

A professional App can be composed of the following Regions:

```text
Primary Navigation

Secondary Navigation

Main Workspace

Tool Panel

Inspector

Bottom/Timeline Region

Activity / Status Region
```

Each App can be freely combined.

---

# 13. ArcChat recommended layout types

Conceptually:

```text
Navigation
    │
    ├─ Home
    ├─ Projects
    ├─ Tasks
    ├─ Automations
    └─ Apps

Main Content
    │
    └─ Chat / Task / Project

Optional Details
    │
    └─ Artifact / Task Inspector
```

Specifically, Stage 17 will be done again.

---

# 14. ArcNotes recommended layout types

```text
Library / Navigation

Document List / Context

Editor

Optional Inspector
```

Specifically Stage 15.

---

# 15. ArcScope recommends Professional Workspace

Possible:

```text
Source / Session explorer

Main visualization

Measurements

Analysis panels

Inspector / properties

Timeline/status
```

Therefore ArcScope must be able to use:

# Dockable Panel System.

---

# 16. ArcSlate also belongs to Panel-heavy Workspace

For example in the future:

```text
Project Bin

Viewer

Timeline

Inspector

Effects

Scopes

Audio meters
```

So ArcScope and ArcSlate can be shared:

# Docking/Panel Experience Foundation.

But:

> Does not mean they share Domain.

---

# 17. Behaviors officially supported by Dock/Panel Foundation

The underlying product experience supports at least:

```text
Show / Hide

Resize

Split

Tab together

Move between supported zones

Detach / Float where appropriate

Reset layout
```

For professional apps, it should also be allowed to:

# Saved Workspace Layouts.

For example:

```text
Editing
Color
Analysis
Debug
```

Which apps expose this feature are determined by their own stages.

---

# 18. Layout State belongs to Device-local State by default

For example:

```text
Window location

Panel size

Monitor placement

Panel visibility

Dock layout
```

Default:

# Not synchronizing Cloud.

Because:

```text
Desktop 4K monitor

vs

Laptop
```

Completely different.

---

# 19. What can be synchronized in the future is the "Named Layout Definition", not the physical window coordinates.

If future users want to sync:

```text
My Analysis Layout
```

Can be synchronized:

```text
semantic panel configuration
```

But cannot sync:

```text
x=3021
y=212
width=1844
```

This physical state of the machine.

---

# 20. Command System is one of the core foundations of Stage 14

All user operations should be able to:

# Stable Command Identity.

For example concept:

```text
app.file.open

app.file.close

app.edit.undo

app.edit.redo

arcnotes.document.new

arcscope.capture.start

arcslate.timeline.split

arcchat.task.new
```

The specific naming format is not determined yet.

The point is:

# Command is the semantic identity of the action.

---

# 21. Menu / Toolbar / Shortcut should not implement behaviors separately

Correct:

```text
Command
 ├─ Menu Item
 ├─ Toolbar Button
 ├─ Context Menu
 ├─ Keyboard Shortcut
 └─ Command Palette
```

All entry calls:

# Same command.

---

Error schema:

```text
Toolbar_Click()

Menu_Click()

ShortcutHandler()

ContextMenu_Click()
```

Four acts.

---

# 22. Command must know its own availability

For example ArcSlate:

```text
Split Clip
```

Clip is not selected:

```text
CanExecute = false
```

This set of status should uniformly apply to:

```text
Menu
Toolbar
Shortcut
Palette
```

Cannot:

> The Toolbar is grayed out, but the shortcut keys still execute incorrectly.

---

# 23. Command Scope must be clear

Same one:

```text
Delete
```

The meaning is completely different in different locations.

So at least there is:

```text
Global/App

Workspace

Document/Project

Focused Tool

Focused Editor

Modal
```

Wait for Context.

---

# 24. Command resolution priority freezing

Normally:

```text
Modal/Dialog
    ↓
Focused Control/Editor
    ↓
Active Document/Project
    ↓
Workspace
    ↓
Application
```

The more specific context takes precedence.

This way:

```text
Ctrl+C
```

In:

```text
Text editor
```

Copy text.

In:

```text
ArcSlate Timeline
```

Copy Clip.

---

# 25. Undo / Redo uses unified Command Identity, but the status belongs to Owner

For example:

```text
Edit → Undo
```

The visual positions/shortcut keys of the four apps are unified.

However:

```text
ArcNotes Undo
```

Manipulate ArcNotes' own Undo.

ArcSlate operations ArcSlate's own Undo.

There must never be one:

# Global ArcForges Undo Service.

This is exactly the same as Stage 13 / General Outline.

---

# 26. Command Palette should become a common capability of the four desktop apps

Unified entrance suggestions:

```text
Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + P
```

Can be used as the default candidate, and the final shortcut key matrix is then frozen.

It can search for:

```text
Application Commands

Current context commands

Settings commands

Navigation targets
```

---

ArcChat:

# Quick Bar

Not a complete replacement for the regular Command Palette.

Because Quick Bar may also support:

```text
Ask Agent
@Context
Open resource
```

Stage 17 specific design.

But the normal Command Palette:

# All four apps should be available.

---

# 27. The shortcut key system must be Projection of Command System

Shortcut keys cannot be directly bound to specific UI callbacks.

Each shortcut key:

```text
Key Gesture
→ CommandId
```

---

# 28. Shortcut keys are divided into four levels

## Platform Standard

For example:

```text
Copy
Paste
Undo
Redo
Save
Find
```

Respect:

```text
Windows/Linux Ctrl
macOS Cmd
```

---

## ArcForges Shared

For example:

```text
Command Palette

Settings

Search
```

Try to be consistent across apps.

---

## Product-specific

For example:

```text
ArcScope Start Capture

ArcSlate Split Clip
```

---

## User Custom

Allow modification by advanced users.

---

# 29. The shortcut key Conflict must be managed by the system

For example user settings:

```text
Ctrl+K
```

Already belongs to another Command.

Cannot:

> Both are saved and then run randomly.

Requires:

```text
Conflict detected

Existing:
...

Replace / Cancel
```

---

# 30. Shortcut key Context Conflict is allowed

For example:

```text
K
```

In ArcSlate Timeline and a Text Editor:

Can have different meanings.

Just:

# Contexts do not overlap.

So Conflict judgment cannot only compare strings.

---

# 31. No grabbing OS Reserved Shortcut

The system should maintain:

# Reserved / unsafe shortcuts.

Especially different platforms:

```text
Windows
macOS
Linux desktop environments
```

There are differences.

---

# 32. Settings is the second very important Shared Foundation

The Settings of the four Apps must have a unified concept.

But the most important thing is:

# **Settings is not a flat Dictionary.**

---

# 33. Settings are at least divided into these Scope

## Account Preference

For example:

```text
Preferred UI language
Certain account-level preference
```

Follow Account.

---

## Workspace Setting

For example:

```text
Cloud behavior

Knowledge policy

Workspace-specific preferences
```

Belongs to Workspace.

---

## Device Setting

For example:

```text
Hardware acceleration preference

Cache location

Download location

Background startup

Device-specific performance
```

Should not sync to another machine.

---

## Product/App Setting

For example:

```text
ArcNotes editor preference

ArcScope visualization preference

ArcSlate playback preference
```

---

## Project / Document Setting

truly belongs to:

```text
specific Project/Document
```

behavior.

---

## Session Setting

Temporary status.

It can disappear after closing.

---

# 34. Do not build a system where "all Settings are covered at the same level"

For example:

```text
Account
<
Workspace
<
Device
<
App
<
Project
```

This unified precedence seems simple, but in fact it is easy to make mistakes.

Correct way:

# Each Setting defines which Scope it is allowed to appear in, as well as its own Resolution Rule.

For example:

```text
UI Language
```

and:

```text
ArcScope Sampling configuration
```

Not the same thing at all.

---

# 35. Each Setting must know its own Source

The Settings UI should be able to explain in the future:

```text
Value: Dark

Source:
This Device
```

Or:

```text
Managed by Workspace Policy
```

The latter's real remote Policy mechanism is in Stage 25.

Stage 14 first ensures that the Settings model can express:

# Effective Value + Source.

---

# 36. Settings and Policy are always separated

Very important:

### Settings

User choice:

```text
Dark Theme
```

### Policy

System/Workspace regulations:

```text
Remote Agent disabled
```

Policy cannot be disguised as:

```text
Settings checkbox
```

Then users think they can change it.

Stage 25 deals specifically with Policy.

---

# 37. Secret is never an ordinary Setting

For example:

```text
OpenAI API Key

Connector Token

Cloud BYOK
```

Cannot:

```text
settings.json
```

Inside as an ordinary string.

Product UI can be managed near Settings.

Domain semantics must be:

# Secret.

Stage 26 ends completely.

---

# 38. Settings UX must be unified

Four apps support at least:

```text
Search Settings

Category navigation

Reset individual setting

Reset category where safe

Show changed/default state
```

---

# 39. Reset Do not delete business data by mistake

For example:

# Reset ArcNotes Settings

Cannot:

```text
delete notebook
```

Therefore:

```text
Settings
```

and:

```text
Data
```

Must be clearly separated at the UX layer.

---

# 40. Notification should not just be Toast

ArcForges needs to be unified:

# Attention Model.

At least the following Surfaces exist.

---

## 1. Inline State

closest to where the problem occurs.

For example:

```text
This source is disconnected.
```

Priority is given to displaying in ArcScope related areas.

---

## 2. Toast

Information that is short-lived and does not require future processing.

For example:

```text
Copied link

Export started

Settings saved
```

---

## 3. Persistent Attention Item

The user needs to process it later:

```text
Task needs approval

Sync conflict

Device unavailable

Automation failed
```

Toast cannot disappear after 5 seconds.

---

## 4. OS Notification

When the app is not in the foreground and really needs the user's attention.

---

## 5. Email / Push

Belongs to the Cloud/Remote layer.

Stage 7/10 has been defined.

---

# 41. Notifications must be classified by Durability, not Severity alone

For example:

```text
Task completed
```

May be:

# Info

But the user needs to know the results.

So:

```text
Severity
```

and:

```text
Persistence / Attention Requirement
```

Must be in two dimensions.

---

# 42. Unified Severity

Recommended:

```text
Informational

Success

Warning

Error

Critical/Security
```

But:

# Do not overuse Error red.

For example:

```text
Offline
```

In Local-first App many times it is just:

# Informational state.

Not a "system failure".

---

# 43. Notification deduplication

For example, Cloud is disconnected:

Cannot:

```text
Disconnected
Disconnected
Disconnected
Disconnected
```

Retry playing Toast each time.

Should:

# A status Item is continuously updated.

---

# 44. ArcChat can aggregate cross-App Attention, but cannot grab Ownership

For example:

```text
ArcScope capture interrupted
```

Authoritative Attention:

# ArcScope.

ArcChat can display:

```text
ArcScope needs attention
```

and link to it.

But you cannot modify it yourself:

> ArcScope internal error status.

Stage 21 will define this Contribution.

---

# 45. Error experience must be unified

Users should never see:

```text
System.NullReferenceException...
```

as a normal product error.

Unifying Error UX requires at least:

```text
Human-readable summary

What was affected

Whether user data is safe

What the user can do

Retry if safe

Details

Correlation / Error ID
```

---

# 46. Error classification suggestion freezing

## Validation

User input does not meet requirements.

Display:

# Inline.

---

## Conflict

For example:

```text
Document changed elsewhere.
```

Display:

# Resolve.

instead of:

```text
Error 409
```

---

## Dependency unavailable

For example:

```text
ArcScope device disconnected

Cloud unavailable

AI provider unavailable
```

The product tells users:

> Which part is unavailable.

---

## Recoverable Operation Failure

For example:

```text
Upload failed.
```

Can Retry.

---

## Partial Success

For example, across App Tasks:

```text
Analysis completed,
document creation failed.
```

Accurate presentation is required.

Stage 19 further defines.

---

## Document/Project Recovery Problem

It is of high severity.

Key points:

# User data state.

---

## Fatal App Failure

Enter Crash Recovery / Diagnostics.

Stage 27 continues design.

---

# 47. "Retry" cannot be a universal button

Only operations are defined as:

# Safe to retry

before showing.

For example:

```text
Download
```

Generally safe.

Some:

```text
External publish/send
```

You cannot Retry without confirming.

The underlying CommandId/idempotency has been designed in the main program.

Stage 14 only stipulates UX:

> **Cannot pretend that all failures are repeatable.**

---

# 48. Error Details are divided into two levels

Ordinary users see:

```text
Cloud sync temporarily unavailable.
Your local work is safe.
```

Advanced details:

```text
Error code
Time
Provider
Correlation ID
```

---

Not shown by default:

```text
raw stack trace
local absolute path
secret
internal server information
```

---

# 49. Deep Link must become a unified experience protocol for the entire ArcForges

Use uniformly:

# `arcforges://`

Deep Link Namespace as a product family.

Do not:

```text
arcnotes://
arcscope://
arcslate://
```

Each independently developed into four sets of protocols.

---

# 50. Deep Link needs to express at least four types of semantics

## Open Product

```text
Open ArcNotes
```

---

## Navigate

```text
Open ArcScope → specific session
```

---

## Resource

```text
Open specific ArcNotes document
```

---

## Handoff

For example:

```text
Open generated artifact in ArcNotes
```

---

Specific URL schema and fields:

# Stage 21

Freeze again.

Stage 14 only freezes the unified experience.

---

# 51. Deep Link must not become invisible Remote Execution API

Particularly important.

A web page:

```text
arcforges://...
```

Cannot be triggered directly:

```text
Delete document

Publish video

Execute shell

Send email
```

High-risk Deep Link can only:

# Open the corresponding UI + prefilled intent.

The actual execution still goes through the normal Permission / Confirmation / Capability.

---

# 52. Deep Link from outside is always regarded as Untrusted Input

Requires:

```text
Validate

Normalize

Check resource access

Check realm/workspace

Check product/version
```

URL parameters cannot be trusted.

---

# 53. It is forbidden to embed Secret in Deep Link

Never:

```text
arcforges://...?apiKey=...
```

---

# 54. Deep Link should be based on Stable Identity, not based on absolute path

Continue to Stage 9:

Correct:

```text
Resource identity
```

instead of:

```text
C:\Users\Ryan\...
```

---

# 55. The product must be downgraded gracefully when it is not installed.

For example, the user clicks:

```text
Open in ArcScope
```

But ArcScope is not installed.

Should:

```text
ArcScope is required

[Get ArcScope]
```

instead of:

> Unknown protocol.

---

# 56. File association must have a unified principle

Each App can later have its own:

# Native Project/Document Format.

Specific extension:

# Stage 22

Determine again.

---

# 57. ArcForges should only register Native Format that it really owns by default.

For example in the future:

```text
ArcScope Project

ArcSlate Project
```

Normal file association is possible.

---

But do not install ArcNotes later:

```text
grab .md Default program
```

After installing ArcSlate:

```text
grab .mp4 Default player
```

This behavior is very bad.

---

# 58. Common format use Open With

For example:

```text
Markdown
CSV
MP4
JSON
```

Should:

# Support opening/importing.

But by default, it does not actively modify the system default applications for users.

---

# 59. There must be a difference between "Open" and "Import"

For example, drag in:

```text
report.csv
```

to ArcScope.

May be:

```text
Open as data source

Import into project
```

The two are not the same thing.

Products must display semantics.

---

# 60. When a Native Project is opened, it will be routed to existing instances first.

OS:

```text
Double click project
```

If you already have a suitable ArcSlate instance:

> Priority is given to existing instances.

No:

> Start.

This is consistent with the existing multi-instance/file association principle of the general program.

---

# 61. Drag & Drop need to unify Data Transfer semantics

ArcForges supports at least four Drop Payloads:

```text
External File

External URL/Text

ArcForges Resource

App-specific object
```

---

# 62. Drop cannot be equal to Copy by default

It must be decided based on semantics:

```text
Open

Import

Copy

Move

Link / Reference

Attach
```

---

For example:

# ArcNotes ← Image

Possible:

```text
Attach managed copy

or

Reference external file
```

---

# ArcSlate ← Video

Possible:

```text
Import/reference media
```

---

# ArcNotes ← ArcScope Report

Priorities may be:

```text
Reference

or

Create editable document from report
```

You cannot decide secretly.

---

# 63. Cross-App Drag must be Non-destructive by default

Never:

> After dragging something from ArcScope to ArcNotes, the original ArcScope object is Moved away.

Cross-App should default to:

# Reference / Copy / Import.

Unless there are very clear Move semantics.

---

# 64. Dragging large files does not mean copying bytes

For example:

```text
50GB video
```

Drag ArcSlate to an ArcChat Task.

Cannot:

> Copy 50GB via Drag payload.

Should pass:

# ResourceRef / Controlled Reference.

---

# 65. The Drag to Cloud function cannot be uploaded secretly

For example, the user puts:

```text
PrivateVideo.mov
```

Drag into an interface.

Not because of this goal:

> Support Cloud

It will be uploaded automatically.

Continue to Stage 9:

# Cloud transmission must be an explicit behavior.

---

# 66. Drag Target must clearly display the action

Displayed when dragging:

```text
Import

Link

Add to Project

Open

Not supported
```

Rather than the user finding out what happened after the mouse is put down.

---

# 67. Clipboard should also belong to Shared Experience

Cross-App Clipboard can:

```text
Rich ArcForges representation
+
standard OS fallback
```

For example ArcNotes copy content:

```text
Arc-specific structure

HTML

Plain text
```

ArcSlate/Scope is similar, each according to its own domain.

---

# 68. Clipboard must not carry Secret

and:

> Absolute local internal paths should not be used as the only available payloads.

---

# 69. Lifecycle must be defined uniformly instead of hard-coding "Close window = exit"

Each App distinguishes at least:

```text
Window Close

Application Quit

Background Work

OS Shutdown

Update Restart

Crash
```

---

# 70. Ordinary professional apps should not secretly run in the background for a long time by default

For example:

```text
ArcNotes
```

The user closes the last window:

You should usually exit.

---

# 71. ArcChat is the main Background/Tray Exception

Stage 6 has been decided:

> ArcChat Local Hub can run in the background/Tray.

However:

# Users must know.

First time enabled:

```text
Remote Agent
Automation
Keep ArcChat running
```

clearly stated.

---

# 72. ArcScope / ArcSlate can continue in the background when there is real work

For example:

```text
ArcScope recording

ArcSlate rendering
```

When the user closes the window:

Can appear:

```text
Work is still running.

Keep running in background

Cancel work and quit

Keep window open
```

---

Not:

> Turn ArcScope into a Tray App permanently.

The reason for the existence of the background must be:

# Active explicit work.

---

# 73. Closing the window cannot destroy the confirmed data

If current changes:

# Already Local Durable

Close directly.

If there is still:

```text
non-durable operation
```

Must:

> Wait/confirm.

But do not worry because Cloud has not synced yet:

> Prevent exit.

Cloud Sync continues in the background or resumes next time.

---

# 74. Cloud Pending ≠ Unsaved

This is a very important UX principle.

For example:

```text
Saved locally
Cloud sync pending
```
