# 117. Stage 14 Architecture Invariants

Once completed, these should become four hard rules for desktop apps.

### Invariant 1

The four products share the Design Language, but not the mandatory Shell Layout.

### Invariant 2

Professional products allow different Density and Workspace Composition.

### Invariant 3

Menu, Toolbar, Shortcut, and Palette must revolve around unified Command semantics.

### Invariant 4

The same user operation cannot produce different business logic due to different entrances.

### Invariant 5

Command has Context/Scope and does not use the global shortcut trash can.

### Invariant 6

User shortcut keys support conflict detection and remapping.

### Invariant 7

Settings must have a clear Scope, not a global Dictionary.

### Invariant 8

Secret does not belong to ordinary Settings.

### Invariant 9

Settings are strictly separate from Stage 25 Policy.

### Invariant 10

Local Saved and Cloud Synced are always two different states.

### Invariant 11

Toast does not assume attention that requires long-term processing by the user.

### Invariant 12

Errors must explain the impact and recovery method, and the normal product path does not directly expose the exception stack.

### Invariant 13

Deep Link uses the unified ArcForges Namespace.

### Invariant 14

Deep Link cannot directly bypass confirmation to perform dangerous operations.

### Invariant 15

Ordinary file formats do not rob the system of default associations.

### Invariant 16

Drag & Drop must specify Open/Import/Copy/Reference/Move semantics.

### Invariant 17

Cross-App Drop is non-destructive by default.

### Invariant 18

Drag/Clipboard cannot directly move large text across apps.

### Invariant 19

Window Close, App Quit and Background Work are different concepts.

### Invariant 20

Apps cannot secretly reside in the background for long periods of time, except for ArcChat or explicitly active tasks.

### Invariant 21

Multi-window is a formal capability and does not require `MainWindow singleton` as an architectural prerequisite.

### Invariant 22

Multi-window takes precedence, and multi-process is an explicit expansion capability.

### Invariant 23

The same Resource cannot produce two local writable owners without coordination mechanism.

### Invariant 24

The default physical state of Window/Layout is Device-local.

### Invariant 25

Account is not First Launch Gate.

### Invariant 26

Cloud failure cannot render the Local-first App completely unavailable.

### Invariant 27

Cross-App UI always displays the Owner App that actually performs the work.

### Invariant 28

Shared UI can only share mechanism and experience, not professional domain state.

---

# Stage 14 officially finalized

The four ArcForges Desktop Apps from now on should not be understood as:

> **Four sets of UI created by four completely independent design teams.**

Nor can it be understood as:

> **The same Shared Shell can be replaced with four sets of business content.**

The final pattern is:

# **One Design Language, Four Professional Workspaces.**

That is:

**ArcChat** can be a Conversation/Task centered Agent Command Center.

**ArcNotes** can be a Document/Knowledge-centric writing environment.

**ArcScope** is a highly configurable, panel-heavy, real-time analysis workbench.

**ArcSlate** can be a high-density Viewer / Timeline / Inspector type NLE workbench.

But after the user switches between the four apps:

* Know where Settings are;
* Know how to use Command Palette;
* The shortcut keys are logically consistent;
* Undo/Redo behavior conforms to the principle of unity;
* Notification does not have four styles;
* Error can tell him whether the data is safe;
* There is no confusion between Local Save and Cloud Sync;
* Deep Link behaves consistently;
* Drag & Drop is predictable;
* Account/Workspace have the same meaning;
* Update and Crash Recovery experience are consistent;
* Closing a window does not result in four completely different lifecycle logics.

At this point, the task of **Stage 14 has been closed**.

In the following stages 15~17/20, you can safely design the specific interfaces and workflows of four real products, because they already have the **Desktop Product Experience Foundation** that is unified and will not in turn limit the capabilities of professional software.

---

# stage15

---

# Stage 15: ArcNotes Complete Product Specification

The goal of this stage is not to say:

> "ArcNotes is a knowledge note-taking software."

Instead push it to:

# **Have been able to continue designing the ArcNotes Domain Model, Persistence, Application Service, Local RPC, and UI based on this without having to re-decide what the product is.**

The original "Future C# Architecture Outline" has actually left a very good technical skeleton for ArcNotes:

* `Notebook`
* `Document`
* `Block`
* `Link`
* `Tag`
* `Index`
* `Attachment ResourceRef`
* Local database
* Search/Vector Index
* Undo / Recovery
* Multi-window/multi-instance
* Local RPC
* ArcChat capability call

And it is clear that ArcNotes can still be edited offline, and restarting the Hub will not affect its local work.

What Stage 15 does is:

> **Turn these technical skeletons into a complete, clear, non-overlapping final product model.**

# 1. Final product definition of ArcNotes

I propose to officially freeze it as:

# **ArcNotes = Local-first Professional Knowledge & Document Workspace**

It is not simple:

* Markdown Editor;
* Notion Clone;
* Obsidian Clone;
* Wiki;
* Word alternative;
* AI Chat shell.

Instead:

> **A local priority knowledge and document application used for rapid recording, long-term knowledge management, professional document writing, data organization, knowledge retrieval, and can be safely called by ArcChat Agent.**

```text

   ↓

   ↓

   ↓
```

Document should have its own:

# Title.

This way:

* Internal Link;
* Search;
* Window title;
* Deep Link;
* Artifact;

All have stable meanings.

The new Document can temporarily:

```text
Untitled
```

Or use the user's first line as a suggested title.

But you cannot rely on AI automatic generation to save.

---

# 21. Block is the basic editable unit of Document content.

Formal:

# **Document = Ordered Block Structure.**

Block has stability:

# Block Identity.

The reasons are very important:

```text
Block link

Agent edit

Selection context

Citation

History

Artifact provenance
```

All will be needed.

---

# 22. BlockId should not change with ordinary editing

For example:

```text
Paragraph Block 123

"Hello"
↓
"Hello world"
```

Still:

```text
Block 123
```

Instead of regenerating the BlockId.

---

# 23. Block supports hierarchical structure

Suggestions:

```text
Block
├─ Content
└─ Children
```

This way:

```text
Lists
Indented content
Toggle sections
```

There is no need to invent a second tree structure.

---

# 24. ArcNotes V1 First-party Block Types

I recommend supporting these basic blocks from the start:

### Text

```text
Paragraph

Heading 1/2/3...

Quote

Callout
```

---

### Lists

```text
Bullet List

Numbered List

Checklist
```

Pay special attention here:

# Checklist Item ≠ ArcChat Agent Task.

User hook:

```text
☐ Buy hardware
```

Does not automatically appear in ArcChat Task Center.

Only the user explicitly:

> Convert/Create Agent Task

Only then create the Agent Task.

---

### Technical Content

```text
Code Block

Math Block

Table
```

ArcNotes targets professional/technical users, and these three should be core capabilities.

---

### Structure

```text
Divider

Toggle/Collapsible Section
```

---

### Assets

```text
Image

File Attachment

PDF

Bookmark / Link Preview
```

---

### References

```text
Document Reference

Block Reference / Embed
```

---

# 25. Open Arbitrary HTML / Script Block without V1

Otherwise:

* Security;
* portability;
* export;
* rendering;
* Cloud preview;

It will be much more complicated.

Later expansion content:

# Stage 24 Extension Model

solved.

---

# 26. Inline Content

Text Block supports:

```text
Bold
Italic
Underline
Strikethrough
Inline Code
Highlight
Link
Internal Reference
```

and as appropriate:

```text
Subscript / Superscript
```

Can be used as professional writing skills.

---

# 27. The core positioning of Editor

ArcNotes Editor should be:

# **Rich Block Editor with Markdown-friendly interaction**

Not:

# Markdown Source Editor.

---

# 28. Support Markdown Keyboard Syntax

For example user input:

```text
# 
## 
- 
1.
> 
```

Should be quickly converted to the corresponding Block.

Code fence, inline code, etc.:

Natural input is also supported.

# 29. Support Slash Command

For example:

```text
/
```

Open:

```text
Paragraph
Heading
Checklist
Code
Table
Image
File
...
```

This is perfect for Block Editor.

---

# 30. But Command Palette and Slash Menu are not the same thing

Stage 14:

# Command Palette

Used throughout App Command.

ArcNotes:

# Slash Menu

Used to insert content into the current Document.

These two cannot mix.

# 31. Block requires complete editing operation

At least:

```text
Select

Multi-select

Move

Drag

Duplicate

Delete

Convert type

Indent

Outdent

Copy

Cut

Paste
```

# 32. Multi-Block Selection must be a first-class ability

Because in the future:

```text
Move several blocks

Apply formatting

Ask AI

Agent rewrite preview
```

All are needed.

You cannot make the editor:

> Only one Block can be operated at a time.

# 33. Block Drag & Drop

Inside Document:

# Move.

Cross Document:

By default:

```text
Move
or
Copy
```

Based on user actions.

Across Apps:

Continue to Stage 14:

# Reference / Copy / Import

And non-destructive by default.

# 34. Table is a document table, not a Notion Database

This boundary should now be clear.

ArcNotes allows:

```text
Rows
Columns
Cells
Basic formatting
```

An ordinary Table.

However:

# V1 does not turn the Table Block into an independent relational database engine.

# 35. Ped Properties are different from Table

The Document itself can have:

# Typed Properties.

This is metadata.

For example:

```text
Status
Author
Created
Topic
Priority
Date
URL
```

# 36. Property type

At least the model allows:

```text
Text

Number

Boolean

Date

DateTime

Select

Multi-select

URL
```

Later:

```text
Relation

Person

Formula
```

Can be expanded.

But V1 is not required to implement all high-level types at once.

# 37. Separate System Properties and User Properties

System:

```text
CreatedAt

ModifiedAt

CreatedBy

ModifiedBy

Revision
```

Users cannot put:

```text
ModifiedAt
```

Redefined as normal Text.

---

User Properties:

Created by users themselves.

---

# 38. Property should not destroy the experience of "normal notes are very light"

Create a new normal Document:

> There is no need to fill in any Property.

Only users need:

```text
Research Database-like view

Meeting collection

Design docs
```

Only used when.

---

# 39. ArcNotes should not become Notion Database Clone

This is an important Non-goal.

We reserve:

```text
Typed Properties

Saved Views

Filtering

Sorting
```

This already satisfies a large amount of professional knowledge management.

But do not introduce it immediately in the first stage:

```text
Relational database pages

Formula engine

Board engine

Project management database

Complex rollup
```

Otherwise the core of the product will be out of focus.

# 40. Definition of Tag

# **Tag = Cross-cutting classification.**

Document can have multiple Tags.

For example:

```text
#architecture

#research

#csharp
```

---

# 41. Tag does not bear hierarchical position

Folder replied:

> Where is it placed?

Tag answered:

> What topics does it belong to?

Both must remain clear.

---

# 42. Deleting Tag will not delete Document

It's just:

# Remove classification.

This is completely different behavior from Folder deletion.

---

# 43. Tag Scope

Tag should belong to the same one:

# Data ownership scope.

That is to say, multiple Notebooks in the same Workspace/local scope:

Tags can be shared.

Do not regenerate in each Notebook:

```text
#research
```

Three completely unrelated tags.

The specific identity model is further refined in Stage 22.

---

# 44. Internal Link is the core of the knowledge system

ArcNotes must support:

# Document Link.

Users can:

```text
[[Architecture Design]]
```

Or via Link Picker.

But what is actually stored is:

# Stable Document Reference.

Not a title string.

---

# 45. Document Rename cannot destroy Link

For example:

```text
Architecture Design
↓
ArcForges Architecture
```

Links to other Documents:

Still valid.

---

# 46. Link Display supports Alias

For example:

Goal:

```text
ArcForges Architecture
```

Text display:

```text
architecture document
```

It should also be supported.

Therefore:

# Target Identity is separate from Display Text.

---

# 47. Block Link

Must support linking to:

```text
Specific Heading

Specific Block
```

This way:

* Citation;
* ArcChat;
* Research;
* Technical reference;

will be very useful.

---

# 48. Backlink

Backlink is:

# Derived Relationship.

When Document A:

```text
→ links Document B
```

Backlinks for Document B:

A appears automatically.

---

# 49. Backlink should not be written into the Document body

Otherwise, after the link is deleted:

> Two copies of the backlink status must be maintained simultaneously.

Correct:

# Derived from Link Index.

---

# 50. Broken Link must have a clear status

If Target:

```text
Deleted
Unavailable
Other workspace
```

```text
Unavailable reference
```

Rather than directly converting Link into ordinary text.

Restore after this:

> Link can be valid again.

---

# 51. Reference Embed

ArcNotes should allow:

```text
Embed Document

Embed Block
```

But the default should be:

# Reference View.

Not copying content.

---

# 52. The editing authority of Embedded Reference still belongs to the original object

For example:

Document A embed:

```text
Block B
```

Display B.

Do not create secretly:

# The second writable Block.

If you want to edit:

> Edit the original Block.

This avoids future data conflicts.

# 53. Backlinks Panel

Recommended to become the standard view of Document Inspector.

At the same time, the Inspector can have:

```text
Outline

Properties

Backlinks

Attachments

History
```

The actual Tab layout will be decided upon implementation of Stage 14/15 UI.

# 54. Document Outline

Heading is automatically generated:

# Outline.

Outline:

> Derived.

Does not become a second document structure.

Click:

> Jump to Block.

# 55. Saved View

This is a capability that I think is worth adding now without turning the product into a Notion Clone.

# **Saved View = Saved Query + Sort/Filter/View Configuration.**

For example:

```text
All documents tagged #research
Modified this week
Status = Draft
```

---

# 56. Saved View does not own Document

Therefore:

```text
Document A
```

Can appear simultaneously in:

```text
Research

Recently Modified

Draft Documents
```

Three views.

No copying.

# 57. V1 Saved View can first provide only List

Can be expanded in the future:

```text
Table View

Card View

Calendar View
```

But the bottom layer is still:

# Query Projection.

No need to re-change Document Ownership.

---

# 58. Favorites

Favorite is also:

# User-level presentation state.

Not a Document Folder.

A Document can:

```text
Normal existence Notebook
+
Favorite
```

---

# 59. Recent

Likewise:

# Derived.

Do not add: to Document:

```text
IsRecent
```

Such business fields.

# 60. Template

ArcNotes should support:

# Document Template.

Template contains:

```text
Block structure

Property defaults

Optional naming suggestion
```

---

# 61. After applying Template, the default is "Copy content"

instead of:

> The new Document is always bound to the Template in real time.

Otherwise:

```text
Template updated
↓
1000 documents unexpectedly change
```

Very dangerous.

# 62. Template can become Stage 24 Community Item

So from now on make sure:

```text
Official Template

User Template

Community Template
```

It is the same type of product concept.

But Publication/Package will be designed later.

# 63. Attachment models must be formally divided into two categories

Continue to Stage 9:

# Managed Attachment

and:

# External Reference.

---

# 64. Managed Attachment

For example user:

```text
Drag image.png
```

Select/Default:

# Add to ArcNotes.

ArcNotes is responsible for:

```text
Asset identity

Lifecycle

Integrity

Sync if notebook syncs

Backup
```

---

# 65. External Attachment

For example:

```text
Link to D:\Research\data.csv
```

ArcNotes only saves:

# Reference.

Will not:

* Unauthorized copying;
* Upload without permission;
* Unauthorized deletion.

# 66. Drag ordinary small attachments into Document

By default, you can use:

# Managed Attachment

Because users typically expect:

> "I inserted the picture into the note."

# 67. Large files or obviously external information

It should be clear to the user:

```text
Add a copy to ArcNotes

Link to original file
```

Do not do it for convenience:

> Secretly copy dozens of GB files into Notebook.

The specific threshold Stage 22/27 is set based on actual performance.

---

# 68. Attachment cannot embed Base64 into Document

Unify:

```text
Block
↓
Attachment Resource
```

This way:

* Undo;
* Sync;
* Dedup;
* Version;
* Download-on-demand;

It will be much cleaner.

# 69. Image Block

At least support:

```text
Preview

Resize

Caption

Alt Text
```

# Not part of ArcNotes.

# 70. PDF

ArcNotes is supposed to be a PDF-friendly knowledge application.

Support:

```text
Attach

Preview

Search extracted text where supported

Reference specific document
```

```text
Page citation
```

Stage 23 further completes Knowledge Citation.

# 71. The extracted text of PDF is Derived Data

Delete:

```text
PDF text index
```

# 72. Attachment Availability

The same attachment may:

```text
Available locally

Cloud-only

Downloading

Unavailable
```

Cannot:

> Attachment is not available → Document cannot be opened.

# 73. Search is a first-level capability of ArcNotes

First level entrance on the left:

# Search.

Not hidden in:

```text
Ctrl+F
```

inside.

# 74. ArcNotes Search is divided into three Scope

## Current Document

Normal:

# Find.

---

## Notebook Search

Current scope of knowledge.

---

## All Accessible Notes

Search all currently locally accessible notebooks.

# 75. Basic search never needs AI

At least support:

```text
Full text

Title

Tag

Property

Notebook

Folder

Date

Attachment
```

Wait for search.

# 76. Search Filter

At least the product layer should be able to express:

```text
Notebook

Folder

Tag

Property

Created

Modified

Has attachment

Document type/state
```

Specific Query Engine Stage 23.

# 77. Search Result must try to locate the specific Block

Not:

```text
Architecture.md
```

Instead:

```text
Architecture
> "The Hub does not own..."
```

Click:

> Open + Highlight corresponding block.

# 78. Semantic Search is an enhancement and does not replace ordinary Search.

User search:

```text
hub state ownership
```

Semantically relevant results can be obtained.

But:

# Semantic Index is down

Normal Search still works.

---

# 79. Semantic Search can be local or cloud

In line with previous product models:

### Local

local embedding/index.

Free.

---

### Cloud

Cloud semantic search for synced data.

Need to correspond to Cloud entitlement.

---

# 80. Users should know the Knowledge status of a notebook

For example:

```text
Searchable locally        Yes

Available to AI retrieval Yes

Cloud indexed             No
```

AI Knowledge cannot be allowed to become an invisible black box.

---

# 81. Knowledge is the core of ArcNotes, but it is not the second data

Formal:

# Document / Attachment is Source.

Knowledge Index:

# Projection.

---

# 82. Knowledge Participation

Notebooks can have defaults:

```text
Available to AI Knowledge

Excluded from AI Knowledge
```

Document can:

# Override.

---

# 83. This is separate from ordinary Search permissions

User:

```text
Exclude this notebook from AI
```

Does not mean:

> ArcNotes itself cannot search.

So:

```text
Normal Search Visibility

AI Knowledge Eligibility
```

It must be a different concept.

---

# 84. Cloud Knowledge cannot be automatically enabled either.

The user puts Notebook:

```text
Sync to Cloud
```

should not necessarily mean:

```text
Send entire notebook to Managed AI
```

Stage 7 has clarified:

# Sync transmission ≠ AI transmission.

ArcNotes UX must maintain this principle.

---

# 85. Correct positioning of ArcNotes AI

ArcNotes should not evolve by itself into:

# Second ArcChat.

It has three layers of AI capabilities.

---

# First layer: Editor AI Actions

Belongs to ArcNotes itself.

For example:

```text
Rewrite

Summarize selection

Translate

Change tone

Explain

Extract structure

Turn text into checklist

Generate outline
```

These features:

```text
single document
short-lived
clear scope
```

---

# Second level: Ask ArcChat

When users need:

```text
Conversation

Deep reasoning

Multi-step work

Cross-document

Cross-app

Agent task
```

Use:

# ArcChat.

---

# The third layer: Agent-driven ArcNotes Capability

ArcChat can:

```text
Search notes

Read referenced blocks

Create document

Insert content

Update document

Generate report

Set properties
```

Operate ArcNotes with controlled capabilities.

---

# 86. ArcNotes Native AI does not require ArcChat to be installed.

This is consistent with Stage 13 independence.

If the user has configured:

```text
Local AI

Local BYOK
```

ArcNotes can perform AI Actions within its own scope.

---

Managed AI:

According to Stage 8:

```text
Arc Account
+
Arc AI Credits
```

Billing.

---

# 87. But complex Agent Orchestration does not copy to ArcNotes

ArcNotes can no longer appear on its own:

```text
Agents
Skills
MCP
Automations
Task Center
```

The entire platform.

These belong to:

# ArcChat.

---

# 88. Ask ArcChat must pass Context Reference instead of blindly Copy Everything

For example:

The user selects three Blocks:

```text
Ask ArcChat
```

ArcNotes provides:

```text
DocumentRef

SelectedBlockRefs

Selection context
```

ArcChat reads the data it really needs based on permissions.

---

# 89. You cannot upload the entire Notebook just because the user clicks Ask ArcChat once.

Context must:

# Minimum necessary.

Users can understand:

```text
Using:
Current selection
Current document
```

Need to expand:

```text
Search this notebook
```

Expand clearly.

---

# 90. AI modification must have Provenance

For example:

```text
Edited by ArcChat
Task ...
```

Document History can identify:

```text
Human

ArcNotes AI Action

ArcChat Agent
```

---

# 91. Create Checkpoint before large-scale modification of Agent

For example:

> "Reorganize the entire design document."

ArcNotes is created first:

# Before Agent Edit

Checkpoint.

Then operate.

---

# 92. Complex AI Edit should support Review Changes

Especially:

```text
Replace many blocks

Delete/move sections

Change properties
```

should render:

```text
Before

After

Accept

Reject
```

Or review block by block.

---

# 93. Small AI Insert does not require huge Diff UI every time

For example:

```text
Insert summary below selection
```

The user has explicitly requested it.

Can be inserted directly and:

# Undoable.

Therefore, the intensity of review is based on the scope of operations and risks.

---

# 94. ArcChat Context Providers

The product layer should formally include at least:

```text
CurrentDocument

CurrentSelection

CurrentBlock

CurrentNotebook

OpenDocuments

CurrentSearchResults
```

Specifically Local RPC Contract Stage 21.

# 95. Core capability categories provided by ArcNotes to ArcChat

Rather than finalizing the RPC method now, freeze the scope of semantic capabilities.

## Query

```text
SearchDocuments

FindByTag

FindByProperty

GetDocumentSummary/metadata
```

---

## Read

```text
ReadDocument

ReadBlocks

ReadSelection
```

---

## Create

```text
CreateDocument

CreateFromArtifact
```

---

## Edit

```text
InsertBlocks

ReplaceBlocks

AppendBlocks

UpdateProperties

AddTags
```

---

## Organization

```text
MoveDocument

LinkDocuments
```

---

## Artifact

```text
OpenArtifact

ImportText/Markdown/Report
```

# 96. Delete This type of capability exists, but it is a high-risk Capability

It cannot be because the Agent supports:

```text
DeleteDocument
```

It is called automatically by default.

It must continue Stage 6/26:

# Risk / Permission / Approval.

---

# 97. ArcNotes Artifact Handler

ArcChat produces:

```text
Technical Report

Research Draft

Structured Text
```

When:

Can:

```text
Open/Create in ArcNotes
```

and produces really:

# ArcNotes Document.

---

# 98. ArcScope → ArcNotes

This is a very important ecological scenario.

For example:

```text
ArcScope Session
    ↓
ArcChat Analysis
    ↓
Technical Report
    ↓
ArcNotes Document
```

Final ArcNotes Document:

Can be retained:

```text
Source ArcScope Session Ref

Task provenance

Generated time
```

---

# 99. ArcNotes Document can reference ArcScope Resource

For example in the report:

```text
Source session
```

Keep:

# Resource Reference.

Instead of copying the entire Session data.

---

# 100. History must be officially divided into four levels

In ArcNotes:

# Undo, Revision History, Checkpoint, Trash

Cannot be mixed into one thing.

---

# 101. Undo / Redo

Answer:

> Can the edit I just made be undone?

Belongs to the current Document Editing Session.

High frequency and fast.

---

# 102. Document Revision History

Answer:

> What did this document look like yesterday?

It is lasting history.

---

# 103. Checkpoint

Answer:

> Are there clear recovery points before major changes?

For example:

```text
Before Agent Edit

Before Migration

Manual Checkpoint
```

---

# 104. Trash

Answer:

> I deleted the entire Document, can it be restored?

Different from editing history.

---

# 105. History UI should display Actor

For example:

```text
Today 14:36
Ryan

Today 14:31
ArcChat - Task "Reorganize document"

Yesterday
ArcNotes AI - Rewrite
```

This will be very valuable.

---

# 106. Restore History should not "delete the subsequent history"

User Recovery Revision 15:

Correct:

```text
Revision 26
=
content based on Revision 15
```

Not:

```text
erase revisions 16–25
```

History remains immutable.

This continues the Stage 9 Immutable Revision principle.

---

# 107. Local History is not an exclusive capability of Cloud

Very important.

Stage 0 said:

# Local features free.

So:

```text
Undo
Local revision/history
Local checkpoint/recovery
```

It should be local product capabilities.

---

What Cloud brings is:

```text
server-side version/recovery

cross-device history

backup continuity
```

instead of:

> If you do not pay, you will not even have history.

---

# 108. Trash

Trash is also available locally.

Synced Notebook:

Continue to Stage 7/9:

# Cloud Deleted Recovery 30 days.

---

# 109. Restore maintains DocumentId

Continue to Stage 9:

> Deleting and restoring does not create a new Document.

So Links, Backlinks, ArcChat References:

Still valid.

---

# 110. Folder deletion semantics

If there are Documents in the Folder:

Delete Folder:

# Folder + descendants enter Trash.

Do not be secretive:

> Move all Documents inside to Root.

Because this may cause users to think that a batch of content has been deleted, but in fact it still exists.

Confirmation UI must clearly show impact.

---

# 111. Tag deletion has completely different semantics

Delete Tag:

```text
Remove tag from documents
```

# Document is not deleted.

---

# 112. Saved View Delete

Delete only:

# View definition.

Does not affect any Document.

These semantics must be fixed from the product stage.

---

# 113. Import is the first-class capability of ArcNotes

Because open source/Local-first products cannot only consider:

> New users start with a blank slate.

Users often have profiles that are several years old.

---

# 114. The first batch of official Import Families

I recommend planning at least:

### Generic

```text
Markdown file

Markdown directory

Plain Text

HTML
```

---

### Obsidian

# Obsidian Vault Import

Because:

```text
Markdown
Wiki Links
Attachments
Tags
```

All are highly related to ArcNotes.

---

### Notion

Support:

# Notion Export Import.

It is not necessary to connect to the Notion Cloud API first.

Instead, the user exported from Notion:

```text
Markdown / HTML / CSV + assets
```

Perform structured import.

---

# 115. Other Import Adapter

Later:

```text
Evernote ENEX

OneNote migration

other note formats
```

Can be added through unified Import Pipeline.

No need to change the Document Domain.

---

# 116. Import must generate Report

For example:

```text
342 documents imported

17 links converted

3 unsupported embeds replaced with attachments

2 files could not be imported
```

Cannot:

> finished

But the user has no idea what is missing.

---

# 117. Import is always Non-destructive

Import Obsidian:

> The original vault is not modified.

After user confirmation:

# Create ArcNotes objects.

---

# 118. Import try to preserve the relationship

For example Obsidian:

```text
[[Doc A]]
```

If Doc A is also imported:

> Convert to a true ArcNotes DocumentRef.

Instead of retaining:

```text
string "[[Doc A]]"
```

---

# 119. Repeated Import must be able to identify Origin

When the user imports the same source again in the future:

The system should at least be able to know:

```text
ImportedFrom
```

This provides:

```text
Import as new

Update previous import
```

Instead of creating duplicate documents forever.

Specific Origin model Stage 22.

---

# 120. Do not use V1 to do "real-time two-way Markdown Folder Mirror"

This is very important.

For example:

```text
ArcNotes internal document
↔
arbitrary external Markdown directory
```

Real-time two-way synchronization:

will appear immediately:

* BlockId is lost;
* property round-trip;
* attachment mapping;
* rename;
* conflict;
* external editor write;
* unsupported rich blocks.

This would drag the core of the product into an extremely complex synchronization system.

---

So V1:

# Import / Export is a clear boundary.

If you really do it in the future:

# Linked Vault Mode

Must be designed individually.

It cannot be added casually.

---

# 121. Export must be more reliable than Import

Because it determines:

# User Exit Freedom.

---

# 122. Native Full-fidelity Export

Must have:

# ArcNotes Native Package / Workspace-compatible export.

Specific format Stage 22.

Able to maintain:

```text
Documents

Blocks

Properties

Links

Attachments

Metadata

History where appropriate
```

---

# 123. Markdown Export

Support:

```text
One Document

Notebook

Selected documents
```

and output:

```text
Markdown
+
assets
```

---

# 124. Content that cannot be represented by Markdown

Must:

> Use stable, documented fallbacks.

For example:

```text
callout syntax

front matter

HTML fallback where appropriate
```

But not:

> Delete silently.

---

# 125. HTML Export

Used for:

```text
high-fidelity portable document
```

---

# 126. PDF Export

Used for:

# Stage 15 finalized

ArcNotes is officially defined from now on as:

# **A Document-first, Block-based, Local-first professional knowledge and documentation system.**

Core content level:

```text
Notebook
    ↓
Folder
    ↓
Document
    ↓
Block
```

Auxiliary organizations:

```text
Tag
Property
Link
Saved View
Template
```

Assets:

```text
Managed Attachment
External Reference
```

Knowledge:

```text
Document / Attachment
        ↓
Derived Search / Knowledge Index
```

AI:

```text
ArcNotes Editor AI
        │
        ├── Single-document assistance
        │
        └── Local and lightweight

ArcChat
        │
        └── Conversation / Agent / Multi-step / Cross-App
```

ArcNotes will not become:

* Markdown file shell;
* Notion Database Clone;
* ArcChat Clone;
* Cloud-first document app;
* All user information is uploaded to AI's black box knowledge base by default.

Instead:

> **Lightweight recording is fast enough, and long-form professional documents are strong enough. After several years of knowledge accumulation, they can still be managed, searchable, cited, and exportable, and can naturally be understood and operated safely by ArcChat Agent.**

Therefore, the `Notebook / Document / Block / Link / Tag / Index / Attachment ResourceRef`, Undo/Recovery, Local-first and strongly typed ArcChat capability boundaries in the original general outline can continue to be retained, and Stage 15 has supplemented these concepts into a complete set of actual products.

At this point, the product direction layer of **ArcNotes can be considered complete**. Next time we will discuss how `Document`, `Block`, Property, Link, and Revision fall into Domain/Persistence/RPC for ArcNotes. This already belongs to the detailed architecture design later, rather than rework because there is still a missing piece in the product definition.

---

# stage16

---

# Stage 16: ArcScope Complete Product Specification

The goals of this stage are the same as Stage 15:

> **It is not about designing SQLite tables now, or deciding `IArcScopeLocalRpc` that there are several methods now, but about advancing ArcScope from the architectural positioning of "Telemetry/Session/Capture/Analysis" to a truly complete professional product.**

After completing Stage 16, you should be able to continue designing directly:

```text
ArcScope Domain Model
→ Local Persistence
→ Capture Pipeline
→ Application Services
→ Local RPC / Capability
→ UI ViewState
→ Cloud Sync Projection
```

Without re-arguing:

* What is the difference between Session and Capture;
* Are Device and DataSource the same thing?
* Are Channel and Signal the same thing?
* Whether real-time monitoring and Recording are the same;
* Decoder output is raw data;
* Can AI directly read several GB of Capture?
* Does Compare copy Session?
* Does Report belong to ArcScope or ArcNotes?

The original outline has determined that each professional App is an autonomous product, with its own domain state, database, resources, UI, Undo and recovery mechanism, and collaborates across applications through semantic capabilities, instead of ArcChat taking over its internal state. This principle applies entirely to ArcScope.

---

# 1. ArcScope final product definition

Officially frozen:

# **ArcScope = Local-first Professional Data Acquisition, Observation & Telemetry Analysis Workspace**

Chinese can be understood as:

> **Local priority professional data collection, real-time observation, timing/telemetry analysis workbench.**

The core processes it solves are:

```text
Data Source / Device
        ↓
Connect
        ↓
Observe
        ↓
Capture
        ↓
Decode
        ↓
Visualize
        ↓
Measure
        ↓
Analyze
        ↓
Annotate / Find
        ↓
Compare
        ↓
Report / Export
```

At its core, ArcScope is not:

> "Draw some real-time polylines".

Instead:

> **Turn time series data and events from devices, networks, software, files and other data sources into professional sessions that can be analyzed repeatedly, quoted, compared and reported.**

---

# 2. The target users of ArcScope cannot be locked into a certain industry.

ArcScope should prioritize serving:

* Software/Systems Developer;
* Embedded Developer;
* IoT/Hardware engineering staff;
* Test and verification personnel;
* People who need to analyze device telemetry;
* People who need to observe time series data, event streams, and protocol data.

But the product Domain should not be written directly:

```text
ArcScope = Serial Monitor
```

Nor should it be hard-coded:

```text
ArcScope = Oscilloscope Software
```

Not to mention writing to death:

```text
ArcScope = IoT Dashboard
```

These are just one of the usage scenarios that ArcScope can cover.

---

# 3. The real core of the product is "time-related data"

ArcScope must be able to handle two main data modalities from the beginning:

## Continuous / Sampled Data

For example:

```text
Voltage
Temperature
CPU usage
Pressure
RPM
Frame time
Sensor value
```

---

## Discrete Events

For example:

```text
Packet received
State changed
Error occurred
Protocol frame
Log event
Trigger fired
Device disconnected
```

So the product cannot be built on a false premise:

> Everything is `double[]`.

ArcScope must understand both:

# Signal + Event.

---

# 4. ArcScope's formal top-level domain relationship

I recommend freezing as:

```text
ArcScope Project
       │
       ├── Source Definitions
       │
       ├── Sessions
       │      │
       │      ├── Connections snapshot
       │      ├── Captures
       │      ├── Signals / Events
       │      ├── Annotations
       │      ├── Measurements
       │      └── Analysis Results
       │
       ├── Comparisons
       │
       ├── Analysis Recipes
       │
       └── Reports
```

Note:

# ArcScope Project ≠ ArcForges Workspace.

Stage 1:

```text
ArcForges Workspace
```

is the Cloud ownership/authorization boundary.

ArcScope Project:

> It is a professional work object.

---

# 5. Formal definition of Project

# **Project = a long-term professional container for a set of related observations, collections, analyzes and reports.**

For example:

```text
Motor Controller Development

Robot Arm Validation

Temperature Sensor Investigation

Game Server Performance Investigation
```

Project can save:

* Source configuration;
* Source references;
* Capture presets;
* Decoder configuration;
* Trigger presets;
* Visualization configurations;
* Analysis recipes;
* Sessions;
* Comparisons;
* Reports.

---

# 6. But you cannot sacrifice Quick Capture for Project

Users just want to:

> Connect the serial port and see the current data.

Must not appear first:

```text
Create Project
Project Name
Project Folder
Project Template
Project Metadata
```

Therefore, the ArcScope homepage must support:

# **Quick Session / Quick Capture**

The user immediately:

```text
Add / choose source
↓
Connect
↓
Observe
```

If data needs to be retained:

> The system turns it into a normal persistent Session and allows the user to later join a Project.

Therefore:

# Session can exist in Project, or it can be temporarily Unfiled.

This way Quick Capture does not need a weird "Magic Project".

---

# 7. The core objects of ArcScope must be clearly distinguished

This is the most critical part of Stage 16.

Formal distinction:

| concept                     | meaning                                 |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| **Device**             | Recognized external physical/logical device, optional                   |
| **DataSource**         | ArcScope can read logical sources of data               |
| **Connection Profile** | How to connect a reusable configuration of a DataSource           |
| **Connection**         | The currently existing runtime connection                       |
| **Session**            | Complete observation/test/analysis work context at once                  |
| **Capture**            | A data collection segment actually recorded in the Session            |
| **Channel**            | Logical data channel provided by Source                   |
| **Signal**             | Continuous/sampled values with type, time, and unit semantics               |
| **Event**              | Discrete structured records on timeline                       |
| **Derived Signal**     | Derived signals generated by Decoder/Transform/Analysis |
| **Annotation**         | Description added to the data by the user or Agent                 |
| **Measurement**        | Reproducible measurements performed on a specified data range                    |
| **Analysis Result**    | Derived results from analysis operations                        |
| **Comparison**         | Comparative view/analysis between multiple Sessions/Captures      |
| **Report**             | ArcScope internal structured analysis results                 |

These concepts should never be combined into one:

```text
TelemetryData
```

Large objects.

---

# 8. Device is not DataSource

This must be fixed now.

For example:

```text
Device:
Oscilloscope A
```

It may provide:

```text
DataSource:
Analog Input
Digital Input
Protocol stream
```

In reverse:

```text
CSV file
TCP endpoint
Recorded trace
```

There may be no Device at all.

So:

# Device is Optional Identity.

And:

# DataSource is the real data entry point of ArcScope.

---

# 9. Product semantics of Device

If the Adapter recognizes the device:

ArcScope knows:

```text
Device name
Model
Stable identity where available
Capabilities
Connection availability
```

But not by being fragile:

```text
USB port number
```

When the device identity is permanent.

The real recognition ability depends on the corresponding Adapter.

---

# 10. DataSource formal definition

# **DataSource = A logical source that can provide time-related data, events, or raw streams to ArcScope.**

Typical Source Family:

```text
Serial / stream

TCP

UDP

Device SDK

Hardware acquisition

File / replay

Structured telemetry

Software instrumentation
```

The specific Adapters that V1 comes with will be determined during subsequent implementation.

But the Domain must support these types.

---

# 11. File Replay is also a DataSource

This is a very important design.

User opens:

```text
recording.csv
trace.bin
previous capture
```

should be able to:

> Enter unified analytics workflows like Live Source.

So should not exist:

```text
Live Analysis System

and

completely different File Analysis System
```

Two sets of products.

Unify:

# Source → Session → Analysis.

---

# 12. Connection Profile and Connection must be separated

For example:

```text
Serial Sensor
COM5
115200
8N1
```

This is:

# Connection Profile.

And:

```text
current 14:03 Open connection established
```

is:

# Connection.

---

Connection:

```text
Runtime-only
```

Can:

* Connect;
* Disconnect;
* Lose connection;
* Reconnect.

Profile:

> It is a persistent and reusable configuration.

---

# 13. Connection Profile changes cannot rewrite historical Session

This is extremely important.

Let us say today:

```text
Sampling = 1 kHz
```

Tomorrow the user will modify Profile:

```text
Sampling = 2 kHz
```

Yesterday's session:

# It is still important to know that 1 kHz was actually used at the time.

Therefore each Capture/Session must be saved:

# Effective Configuration Snapshot.

Instead of always referencing the "current Profile".

---

# 14. The same Session supports multiple DataSources

This is a product capability that must be supported from day one.

For example:

```text
Source A:
temperature

Source B:
motor RPM

Source C:
controller messages
```

Same test:

> It should be possible to observe together.

Therefore:

# Session is not an alias for Connection.

---

# 15. Formal definition of Session

# **Session = a complete unit of work with a common observation goal, temporal context, and analysis context.**

For example:

```text
Motor start test – Run 42
```

It can contain:

```text
multiple sources
multiple captures
annotations
measurements
analysis
findings
reports
```

---

# 16. Session and Capture must be separated

This is the easiest place to rework later.

## Session

means:

> A test/observation job.

## Capture

means:

> A continuous data segment that is actually recorded.

---

For example:

```text
Session: Motor startup test
│
├── Capture 1
│   10:00:00 – 10:03:42
│
├── disconnection gap
│
└── Capture 2
    10:03:47 – 10:10:00
```

Still:

# A Session.

---

# 17. Why is Capture Segment necessary?

Because in reality it will definitely happen:

```text
Pause
Reconnect
Trigger
Dropped connection
Source restart
Recording restart
```

If you put:

```text
Session == one huge contiguous byte stream
```

Write to death:

These scenarios will all be difficult to handle in the future.

---

# 18. Live Observation and Capture must also be separated

After the user Connect:

Can:

# Live Observe.

But:

> Complete data is not necessarily being saved.

At this time you can use:

# Rolling Buffer.

---

User clicks:

# Record / Capture

Only then did durable acquisition really begin.

Therefore the three states are completely different:

```text
Connected

Monitoring

Recording
```

The UI must be clear.

---

# 19. Pause View ≠ Pause Capture

This is one of the most important professional UX rules for ArcScope.

The user may be:

# Recording

But to look at past data:

```text
Pause live follow
```

This can only:

# Stop automatic scrolling of the screen.

The underlying Capture cannot be paused.

---

The interface should be clear:

```text
Recording ●

Live Follow: Paused
```

Avoid disastrous misunderstandings.

---

# 20. Capture's product life cycle

There is no need to write code for a state machine now, but the product must be able to express:

```text
Preparing

Armed

Recording

Finalizing

Completed

Interrupted

Recovered

Failed
```

---

# 21. Interrupted is different from Failed

For example:

```text
Device disconnected after 8 minutes
```

Data for the first 8 minutes:

# is valid data.

Capture:

```text
Interrupted
```

instead of:

```text
Failed → everything useless
```

Users should still be able to analyze already saved sections.

---

# 22. The recorded data cannot be discarded after Crash Recovery.

Next time ArcScope starts:

```text
The previous capture was interrupted.

18m 23s of confirmed data was recovered.
```

Then:

```text
Open recovered session
```

This is completely consistent with the general Journal/Recovery principle.

---

# 23. Gap must be clearly generated when disconnecting and reconnecting

Assumptions:

```text
10:00 – 10:04 data
10:04 – 10:05 disconnected
10:05 – 10:10 data
```

Cannot be drawn as:

```text
a continuous waveform
```

Let the user think that there are real samples in the middle.

Must produce:

# Explicit Gap.

---

# 24. No Silent Data Loss

This is the principle that ArcScope should write directly into the product Constitution:

# **Any data loss that cannot be confirmed as recorded must be explicitly indicated.**

For example:

```text
Dropped samples

Buffer overflow

Network packet loss

Source discontinuity

Decoder error
```

Curves cannot be hidden to make them "pretty."

---

# 25. If the system collection speed cannot keep up

ArcScope cannot:

> Quietly throw away half of the data and continue displaying it.

Must:

```text
Data loss detected
12,481 samples dropped
```

Or at least:

```text
Capture contains gaps.
```

The specific low-level counting capabilities depend on Source.

---

# 26. Raw Captured Data Once Finalized, it is immutable by default.

This is a very important product principle.

# **Raw Capture = Evidence / Source of Truth.**

Users cannot:

```text
Manually modify the 8274 a sample
```

And then called it the original Capture.

---

Users want to:

```text
Filter
Crop
Normalize
Offset
Smooth
Remove noise
```

should produce:

# Derived Data.

Instead of overwriting Raw.

---

# 27. Trim also defaults to Non-destructive

User choice:

```text
00:10 – 00:40
```

Can:

* Focus selection;
* Export selection;
* Create derived capture;
* Create new session from selection.

But the original Capture:

# Not being secretly laid off.

---

# 28. Time Model is something that ArcScope must design from the product stage.

All data should not be just one:

```text
DateTime timestamp
```

Because real device data will appear:

```text
Host time

Device time

Monotonic elapsed time

Capture-relative time
```

---

# 29. ArcScope retains at least three time semantics

## Session-relative Time

For example:

```text
00:02:13.421
```

The most stable axis of analysis.

---

## Host / Wall Clock Time

For example:

```text
2026-07-21 16:32:15.124
```

Used for cross-system event correlation.

---

## Source / Device Time

If the device provides it itself:

```text
DeviceTimestamp
```

Must be retained.

---

# 30. Do not force Source Time to equal Host Time

Device clock:

Possible:

* drift;
* offset;
* reset;
* invalid;
* wrap around.

ArcScope should save:

# Clock relationship / mapping.

The original SourceTimestamp cannot be overwritten as soon as it is received.

---

# 31. Multiple Source Sessions must support time alignment

For example:

```text
Sensor A

Sensor B

Application log
```

The three clocks may be different.

ArcScope needs to be able to:

```text
Automatic alignment when reliable

Manual offset

Align by trigger

Align by marker

Align by known event
```

---

# 32. Time alignment cannot overwrite Raw Timestamp

Alignment:

# is Analysis/View Transformation.

instead of:

> Change the original Capture.

---

# 33. Time accuracy and credibility should be able to express

For example:

```text
Exact

Estimated

Source-provided

Host-arrival based
```

At least the underlying product semantics must allow it.

Do not all data claim:

> "Nanosecond accuracy."

---

# 34. Formal definition of Channel

# **Channel = Logical data channel exposed by DataSource.**

For example:

```text
CH1

CH2

Temperature

Motor speed stream

Serial RX

Packet stream
```

Channel is:

# Source-level concept.

---

# 35. The formal definition of Signal

# **Signal = a temporal value with type, time and semantics.**

For example:

```text
Temperature [°C]

RPM

Voltage [V]

CPU utilization [%]

Digital state
```

---

A Channel:

A Signal can be generated directly.

Also possible:

```text
Raw Channel
↓
Decoder
↓
Multiple Signal
```

---

# 36. Channel ≠ Signal

For example:

```text
CAN Bus Channel
```

Decoder may get:

```text
EngineRPM

CoolantTemperature

ThrottlePosition
```

Three Signals.

So the two cannot be combined.

---

# 37. Event is the third type of core data

# Event = Discrete timestamped structured occurrence.

For example:

```text
Trigger fired

Packet received

State → ERROR

Device reconnect

User marker
```

---

Signal and Event can:

> Shown simultaneously in the same Timeline.

But it cannot be forced into:

```text
Signal NaN value
```

to simulate events.

---

# 38. The Packet/Frame output by the Decoder can be modeled as a Structured Event

Not all Decoder outputs so-called:

# Packet.

So the generic Domain should be:

# Structured Event / Decoded Record.

Specific protocol UI can display:

```text
Packet
Frame
Message
```

---

# 39. The Signal type cannot only support Floating Point.

At least the product model should support:

```text
Numeric

Boolean / Digital

Categorical / Enum

String / Text state
```

Complex Vector/Matrix can be expanded later.

---

# 40. Sample Rate cannot be assumed to be constant

Must support:

```text
Fixed-rate

Variable-rate

Event-driven

Unknown-rate
```

Otherwise a large number of network/software Telemetry will be modeled incorrectly.

---

# 41. Units are the first-class metadata of Signal

For example:

```text
V

mV

°C

Hz

rpm

%
```

Products must understand:

> Signals have Quantity/Unit.

---

# 42. The display unit conversion does not change the Raw Value by default.

For example:

```text
1.2 V
```

User switching:

```text
1200 mV
```

This should:

# is Display Conversion.

Does not create another copy of data.

---

If the user actually does:

```text
x * calibrationCoefficient
```

then produces:

# Derived Signal.

---

# 43. Derived Signal formal definition

# **Any new time series data generated through Decoder, Transform, Analysis, Math, etc., is Derived Signal.**

It must know:

```text
Source input

Parameters

Operation/version
```

This way you can:

# Reproduce.

---

# 44. Derived Signal can be recalculated

Therefore:

# It's not Raw Authority.

If Cache is deleted:

> Can be regenerated from Source Capture.

This is consistent with the Stage 9 Derived Data principles.

---

organization.

For example:

```text
RPM

Current
```

Common timeline.

# 51. Signal with completely different dimensions should not have a Y Axis inserted by default

For example:

```text
V

°C

rpm
```

# 52. View ≠ Signal Ownership

User puts Signal:

```text
Hide
```

Just:

# Not displayed.

Does not mean:

# Delete data.

# 53. Display Decimation and real data must be strictly separated

Large Capture:

It is impossible for the UI to draw every frame:

```text
10billions sample
```

So the display can be:

# Level-of-detail / Decimation.

But:

# **Measurement and Analysis are based on Canonical Data by default, rather than sampled pixels on the screen.**

This is an extremely important principle of professional credibility.

# 54. If a Measurement is Approximate

Must be clearly marked:

```text
Approximate
```

Users cannot be led to believe that the results are accurate for all data.

# 55. Zoom/Pan is a core capability

Support:

```text
Wheel zoom

Box zoom

Zoom to fit

Go to time

Follow live
```

# 56. Cursor is the core of professional analysis

At least support:

```text
Single cursor

Dual cursor / range
```

Display:

```text
Time

ΔTime

Value

ΔValue
```

# 57. Selection is the core of ArcScope Agent Context

User selects in Timeline:

```text
12.5s – 14.8s
```

This should become:

# Stable Selected Time Range Context.

Later:

```text
Measure

Analyze

Annotate

Ask ArcChat
```

All operate within this range.

---

# 58. Multiple Signal Selection must also be supported

For example:

```text
RPM

Current

Voltage
```

Select together.

So:

```text
Compare correlation
```

There is a clear Scope.

# 59. Trigger's formal product positioning

# **Trigger = Rules that control Capture or generate important time events based on data/event conditions.**

It does not just mean:

> oscilloscope edge trigger.

---

# 60. Trigger Family at least supports model expansion

```text
Manual

Threshold

Edge

Condition

Event match

Decoder match

Time-based
```

V1 does not need to be implemented all at once.

But Product Model must be able to cover it.

# 61. Triggered Capture supports Pre-trigger / Post-trigger

Typical:

```text
[ pre-trigger buffer ]
        ↓
Trigger
        ↓
[ post-trigger recording ]
```

This requires Live Observation to exist:

# Rolling Buffer.

# 62. Separation of Trigger Definition and Trigger Occurrence

For example rules:

```text
RPM > 8000
```

is:

# Trigger Definition.

Occurs:

```text
Run 42
13.248s
```

is:

# Trigger Occurrence.

---

Occurrence:

> Should be used as an Event of the Session Timeline.

---

# 63. Trigger should not automatically modify data

It:

* Control Recording;
* Create Event;
* Create Marker;

But:

# Sample is not changed.

# 64. Measurement is officially divided into two categories

## Transient Cursor Measurement

Users temporarily view:

```text
Value
Δt
Δv
```

No need to save.

---

## Pinned Measurement

For example:

```text
Average RPM from 10–14 sec
```

Requires:

# Persistence, repeatable calculation, and report placement.

---

# 65. Measurement must save Scope

For example:

```text
Signal
Time range
Measurement type
Parameters
```

Instead of just saving:

```text
Average = 7234
```

Otherwise it cannot be verified and recalculated later.

---

# 66. Basic Measurement Family

Depending on the Signal type, at least the product model supports:

```text

Max

Average

Median

RMS

Peak-to-peak

Count

Duration

Frequency

Period

Duty cycle

Rate
```

Not all types are available for all Signals.

# 67. Measurement Result must contain Unit

For example:

```text
Frequency:
12.31 kHz
```

Cannot:

```text
12310
```

Then the UI guesses what it is.

# 68. Analysis and Measurement are different

Measurement:

> Answer a relatively clear question.

Analysis:

> Perform more complex processing on data and produce derived results.

# 69. Analysis can generate

```text
Derived Signal

Spectrum

Statistics

Detected Events

Anomalies

Correlation

Model result

Comparison result
```

# 70. Basic Analysis Family

ArcScope should be able to extend to:

```text
Filtering

Smoothing

Resampling

Normalization

Calibration

FFT / Spectrum

Correlation

Statistics

Peak detection

Anomaly detection
```

The specific first releases will be ranked according to actual user needs.

# 71. Analysis must be Non-destructive

For example:

```text
Low-pass filter
```

Result:

```text
Filtered Signal
```

instead of:

> Overwrite the original Signal.

---

# 72. Analysis must be Reproducible

Every saved Analysis logically knows at least:

```text
Input

Parameters

Operation type

Operation version
```

Later:

> Can be re-run.

# 73. Analysis Recipe

This is a concept well worth supporting from the start.

# **Analysis Recipe = A set of Analysis/Measurement configurations that can be applied repeatedly.**

For example:

```text
Motor Startup Validation
```

Automatic execution:

```text
1. smooth current
2. calculate startup time
3. find peak
4. measure steady-state RPM
```

---

This is perfect for:

# Automation / Community / ArcChat.

But it's not a complete scripting language just yet.

---

# 74. Analysis Recipe does not save old results as templates

It saves:

# Process Definition.

Apply to:

```text
Session 42
```

Generate a new Result.

---

# 75. The formal definition of Decoder

# **Decoder = Semantic processor that converts Raw Channel / Raw Event Stream into structured events, fields and signals.**

For example:

```text
Raw serial bytes
        ↓
Protocol Decoder
        ↓
Message type
Temperature
RPM
State
```

---

# 76. Decoder output is all Derived Data

Raw:

# Keep it forever.

After Decoder upgrade:

> Can be re-Decoded.

---

# 77. Decoder must be Versioned

Because:

```text
Decoder 1.0
```

and:

```text
Decoder 2.0
```

May produce different results.

The old Session must know:

> Which version was used at that time.

---

# 78. Decoder Configuration Same as Snapshot

For example:

```text
Endian
Field map
Protocol version
```

Later it was changed:

> The old Session interpretation results cannot be allowed to change secretly.

---

# 79. Support Decoder Chain

Conceptually:

```text
Raw bytes
↓
Framing Decoder
↓
Protocol Decoder
↓
Field Extraction
↓
Signals / Events
```

But each layer must be able to track Provenance.

---

# 80. Decoder Error must be displayed

For example:

```text
12 frames could not be decoded
```

Cannot:

> Lost in silence.

---

# 81. Decoder is not device control

This is an important boundary.

Decoder:

# Interpret the data.

Equipment:

```text
Send command
Change firmware
Change actuator
```

Belongs to:

# Device Control.

You cannot use Decoder to do it secretly.

---

# 82. ArcScope V1 is mainly Observation-first

That is to say:

# Read / Acquire / Analyze

It's the core.

Source needs to be configured to collect:

The connection configuration can be written normally.

But:

> General device control, actuator operation, remote commands

Should not be V1 core.

In the future, if an Adapter provides:

# Device Command Capability

The security level needs to be clarified.

Stage 26 processing.

```text
Here is the spike.
```

a time frame.

```text
=
```

# 112. Core principles of ArcScope AI

This is different from ArcNotes.

ArcScope's top AI questions are:

# **Numerical grounding.**

LLM must not be allowed to:

> Look at a waveform screenshot, guess "the peak value is about 7.3V", and then measure it as a professional.

# 113. Deterministic tools are responsible for numbers, LLM is responsible for understanding and orchestration

```text
User:

 ↓
select tools
 ↓
ArcScope Measurement / Analysis
 ↓
Structured Results
 ↓
LLM explains
```

instead of:

```text
↓
Stuff into prompt
↓
```

# 160. ArcScope core Non-goals

In order not to expand infinitely in the future, it is clear now.

## Not a complete Device Control Platform

## Not ArcChat

Complex Agent, MCP, Automation Center:

# Leave it to ArcChat.

Core:

# Raw immutable + Derived analysis.

# 164. The complete scene that must be passed

## Source / Connection

1. Create a new Source.
2. Save the Connection Profile.
3. Connect.
4. Disconnect.
5. Reconnect.
6. Profile was later modified.
7. The old Session still retains the old configuration.
8. File Replay works normally without Device.

## Session

9. Quick Session.
10. You can quickly observe without Project.
11. Later joined Project.
12. Multiple Sources for one Session.
13. Session is closed and reopened.
14. Session metadata is complete.

## Live / Capture

15. Connect but not Record.
16. Live View works.
17. Start Recording.
18. Clear Recording status.
19. Pause View.
20. Capture continues.
21. Resume Follow.
22. Stop Recording.
23. Capture Finalize.

---

## Disconnect

24. The Capture process is interrupted.
25. Data retention confirmed.
26. Gap is clear.
27. Reconnect.
28. New Capture Segment continues.
29. Session is still the same.

---

## Recovery

30. The process crashed during Capture.
31. Restart.
32. Lost data recovery.
33. Capture marked Interrupted/Recovered.
34. Do not forge unwritten data.

---

## Signals

35. Fixed-rate Signal.
36. Variable-rate Signal.
37. Boolean Signal.
38. Categorical Signal.
39. Event.
40. Unit conversion.
41. Raw values ​​remain unchanged.

## Time

42. Host time.
43. Device time.
44. Relative time.
45. Multi-source has offset.
46. Manual alignment.
47. Raw timestamp is not modified.

---

## Visualization

48. Billion-level data still does not require full loading into the UI.
49. Display decimation.
50. Measurement still uses real data.
51. Zoom.
52. Pan.
53. Cursor.
54. Multi-signal.
55. Hide Signal does not delete data.

## Trigger

56. Manual Trigger.
57. Threshold Trigger.
58. Pre-trigger buffer.
59. Trigger occurrences are displayed in Timeline.
60. Trigger config was modified later.
61. The old Session maintains historical configuration.

## Measurement

62. Cursor measurement.
63. Pinned measurement.
64. Recalculate after changing the time range.
65. Measurement with Unit.
66. Put in Report.

---

## Analysis

67. Apply filter.
68. Raw Signal remains unchanged.
69. Derived Signal is generated.
70. Delete Derived Cache.
71. Can be regenerated.

## Decoder

74. Raw stream.
75. Decoder generates Event/Signal.

## Annotation

81. Marker.
82. Region.
83. Finding.
84. Created by Human.

86. Actors are displayed correctly.

## Compare

88. Start-time alignment.

## Import / Export

## AI

# Stage 16 finalized

ArcScope is now more than just:

> "A Telemetry Software".

It officially becomes:

# **A Local-first professional data collection and analysis workbench that uses Session as the working context, Capture as the original evidence, supports both Signal and Event, and performs real-time observation, recording, decoding, measurement, analysis, comparison and reporting around the timeline.**

Its core chain is fixed as:

```text
Device? / DataSource
        ↓
Connection
        ↓
Session
        ↓
Capture
        ↓
Channel
        ↓
Signal / Event
        ↓
Decoder / Measurement / Analysis
        ↓
Annotation / Finding
        ↓
Comparison
        ↓
Report
```

Among them:

# **Raw Capture is always authoritative data.**

Decoder, Calibration, Filter, Derived Signal, Anomaly, Measurement, Comparison:

# All are traceable derived layers.

AI:

# Does not assume an authoritative role for precise numerical calculations.

The real numbers are calculated by ArcScope's Measurement/Analysis tools, with AI taking care of it:

* Understand;
* Select tool;
* Arrangement;
* Summary;
* Explain.

Complex cross-session, cross-app, automated work:

# Leave it to ArcChat.

ArcNotes:

# Responsible for long-term technical documentation and knowledge writing.

Cloud:

# Project/Session metadata, Annotations, Analysis and Reports are synchronized by default, while Raw Capture still defaults to Local and will only be uploaded if the user explicitly chooses to do so.

In this way, no matter how ArcScope adds:

* Serial port;
* TCP/UDP;
* CAN;
* Modbus;
* Logic Analyzer;
* Oscilloscope;
* Software performance Telemetry;
* Custom hardware;
* New Decoder;
* New Analysis;
* New AI Workflow;

There is no need to re-change ArcScope's basic domain architecture.

This is the most important closed loop of Stage 16.

---

# stage17

---

# Stage 17: ArcChat Complete Product Specification

Stage 6 has already answered:

> **What should ArcChat be?**

The answer has been frozen:

# **ArcChat = AI Agent Command Center / Local Hub / Task Center / Cross-App Orchestrator for ArcForges.**

At this stage, we will no longer discuss whether this direction is correct or not.

Stage 17 to answer is:

> **After users actually install ArcChat, how do they use it every day?**
>
> What is the relationship between Home, Chat, Agent, Project, Task, Artifact, Apps, Skills, MCP, Provider, Search, History, Memory, Automation, and Settings?
>
> What is ArcChat's own data, and what is just a reference to other apps?
>
> How are conversation editing, branches, tasks, model switching, context, AI cost, Cloud, and local data presented?

After completing Stage 17, you should be able to proceed directly to:

```text
Conversation Domain
Project Domain
Agent Profile Domain
Artifact Domain
Search Projection
Provider Configuration
UI ViewState
```

The specific operating state machine, Retry/Resume/Compensation, etc. of the Agent are left to Stage 19.

---

# 1. ArcChat final product definition

Officially frozen:

# **ArcChat = Chat-first interface + Agent execution surface + Task control center + ArcForges App capability hub.**

Users can understand it as:

```text
Ask
↓
Understand
↓
Act
↓
Coordinate
↓
Track
↓
Deliver
```

But ArcChat is not:

```text
ArcNotes inside ArcChat

ArcScope inside ArcChat

ArcSlate inside ArcChat

Universal file manager

Universal database
```

Professional content is ultimately owned by the corresponding professional app.

---

# 2. ArcChat must serve three depths of use at the same time

## Level 1: Ordinary Chat

User:

> "Explain what this code means?"

Or:

> "Summary this PDF."

ArcChat should be as simple as a good AI Chat.

---

## Second layer: Context-aware Assistant

For example:

> "Explain this anomaly based on my current ArcScope selection of 20 seconds of data."

It starts with:

```text
Current Selection
Current Document
Current Session
Project Context
Knowledge
```

---

## The third layer: Agent

For example:

> "Analyze these three ArcScope Sessions to find out the reasons for degradation, create a technical report in ArcNotes, and sort out the issues that need to be addressed."

At this time:

```text
User intent
↓
Task
↓
ArcChat Agent
↓
ArcScope capabilities
↓
ArcNotes capabilities
↓
Artifacts
```

But three experiences must be:

# **Same ArcChat**

Instead of three different products.

---

# 3. The final level of Information Architecture

I recommend freezing as:

```text
Home

Chats

Projects

Tasks

Artifacts

Automations

Apps
```

Global capabilities:

```text

Quick Bar

Settings
```

Stage 6 has designated Artifact as a first-class object.

```text
code file
pictures

Export
```

If the Artifact can only be obtained from:

> "A chat from three months ago"

Look inside again,

Products will become increasingly difficult to use.

So:

# Artifacts should have a global Library.

ArcChat Search is better suited for:

```text
+
Keyboard
+
```

Search to enter the full Results Surface.

Mainly used for:


Rather than simply equaling:

# Recent Files.

---

# 11. Conversation is the core interactive object of ArcChat

Formal definition:

# **Conversation = A continuous human-computer interaction context.**

It has:

```text
Messages

Context references

AI response metadata

Linked tasks

Linked artifacts
```

---

# 12. Conversation does not need to belong to Project

Users readily:

> "Explain the problem."

It is possible to create:

# Unfiled Conversation.

Project must not be a mandatory prerequisite for Chat.

---

# 13. Conversation has at most one Primary Project

If it belongs to:

```text
Project A
```

Then:

* Inherits Project Instructions by default;
* The default recommendation is Project Context;
* Task/Artifact can be automatically classified into Project.

Do not allow:

```text
Conversation
belong to 7 a Project
```

Otherwise Context and Ownership will be very difficult to explain.

---

# 14. This does not prevent Conversation from citing other resources.

For example, Project A's Conversation:

Can be quoted explicitly:

```text
ArcNotes Document
ArcScope Session
Local File
```

But these are:

# Context References.

Does not change Project ownership.

---

# 15. Life cycle of Conversation

At least:

```text
Active

Archived

Deleted / Trash
```

And the Presentation state:

```text
Pinned
```

---

# 16. Archive ≠ Delete

Archive:

> Hide from daily list but remain intact and searchable.

Delete:

> Enter the delete/restore mechanism.

You cannot make both buttons:

```text
Remove
```

---

# 17. Conversation Title

Support:

```text
Automatic title

Manual rename
```

Auto-titles are just a helper.

After the user changes the title:

> Models are no longer allowed to be automatically overwritten.

---

# 18. Conversation History cannot be silently rewritten by Edit

This is very important for long-term design.

If the user modifies a past prompt:

# **Create a new Conversation Branch.**

instead of:

```text
Put the old Message In-situ coverage
↓
Pretend the past was never what it was
```

---

# 19. Regenerate also forms Alternative Branch

For example:

```text
Assistant answer A
Assistant answer B
```

Both are candidate branches of a certain node of the same Conversation.

The default UI does not need to display complex DAGs.

Only when a branch occurs:

```text
< 1 / 2 >
```

Just a simple tip like that.

---

# 20. Explicit Fork Conversation

Users can:

```text
Fork into new chat
```

This is different from Branch.

## Branch

Still part of the current Conversation lineage.

## Fork

Create one:

# New Conversation.

And inherit the necessary context from that point.

---

# 21. Why must this semantics be supported?

Otherwise future:

* message edit;
* regenerate;
* retry with another model;
* compare models;

will continue to:

> Rewrite history.

The problem becomes more serious after the Agent is executed, because old Messages may have caused real-world operations.

So:

# Conversation History defaults to append/branch, not rewrite.

---

# 22. Even if a certain piece of historical content is deleted, it cannot be rewritten without trace.

The product model should allow:

# Redaction / Tombstone.

For example:

```text
Message removed by user
```

Instead of forcing the entire subsequent causal chain to become:

> "The message never existed."

Specific persistence is designed after Stage 22.

---

# 23. Message and Task should not be mixed into one type

Can appear in ArcChat Conversation:

```text
User message

Assistant response

Task card

Approval card

Artifact card

Citation
```

But:

# Task itself is not a Message.

---

For example:

```text
User:
Help me analyze these Session.

Assistant:
OK, I started processing.
```

```text
Read context
```

```text
Target
```

# Side-effect Contract.

# Stage 17 finalized

ArcChat is now more than just:

> **"Have Chat, and then add Agent later."**

It officially becomes a complete product composed of the following core objects that are independent but cooperating in a unified way:

```text
Conversation
        │
        ├── Context
        ├── Messages
        └── Linked Tasks
                │
                ▼
              Task
                │
                ├── Apps / Capabilities
                ├── Approvals
                └── Artifacts
```

Long term organization:

```text
Project
├── Instructions
├── References
├── Conversations
├── Tasks
├── Artifacts
└── Automations
```

Agent configuration:

```text
Agent Profile
├── Instructions
├── AI Policy
├── Skills
├── Capability policy
├── Permission policy
└── Budget
```

AI:

```text
AI Source
↓
Provider
↓
Model
```

Ecology:

```text
Arc Apps
Native Capabilities
MCP
Skills
External integrations later
```

The user's real operation logic is ultimately:

# **Chat when you want an answer.**

# **Agent when you want work done.**

# **Tasks when work outlives the conversation.**

# **Projects when work has long-term context.**

# **Artifacts when work produces something valuable.**

# **Arc Apps when specialist tools should own the real professional result.**

The most important thing is that although ArcChat has become the Agent entrance to the entire ArcForges ecosystem, it has still not become:

> Central database, universal editor, second ArcNotes, second ArcScope or UI Shell for all professional apps.

This makes the platform direction of Stage 6 truly finalized into a complete finished ArcChat that can continue to enter specific Domain Design such as **Conversation/Project/Agent Profile/Artifact/Provider**.

**Stage 17 At this point, the product definition layer can be considered closed.**

---

# stage18

---

# Stage 18: ArcChat Mobile & Web Companion Specification

At this stage, the previously frozen principles must be truly transformed into products:

> **ArcChat Mobile and ArcChat Web are both Companion/Continuity Surface of ArcChat, rather than moving four desktop apps to mobile phones and browsers.**

The core value of their existence is not:

> "I can operate all the UI on my computer on my phone."

Instead:

# **See → Approve → Steer → Continue → Start Remote Work → Receive Results**

That is:

```text
Desktop
Responsible for complete professional work

Mobile / Web
responsible for continuity, remote control, task supervision, Light interaction and result consumption
```

After Stage 18 is completed, you should be able to proceed directly to:

```text
Mobile/Web ViewState
Remote Session Domain
Device Presence
Approval UX
Notification Routing
Continuity State
Cloud Task UI
```

The actual runtime details of how Agent executes, recovers, Retry, and Compensation are left to Stage 19.

# **Remote Task = ArcChat Task initiated by the user from Mobile/Web, and the actual execution location may be on Desktop, Cloud or Hybrid.**

```text
DEKU Desktop

ArcNotes → create report
```

```text
remote click
```

# Semantic Remote Agent.
