# 97. Durable Integration Event and Ephemeral Signal must be distinguished

This is an important rework prevention decision.

---

## Durable Integration Event

For example:

```text
DocumentCreated

CaptureCompleted

RenderCompleted

ArtifactCreated
```

It has stable business significance.

Available for:

```text
Automation

Audit correlation

Cross-App integration
```

---

## Ephemeral Signal

For example:

```text
Mouse selection changed

Playback position changed

Current hover changed

Realtime progress update
```

Only used for:

# Real time experience.

---

# 98. Automation only subscribes to Durable Events by default

Otherwise the user moves the ArcSlate Playhead:

```text
60times/seconds
```

Possible:

> Trigger Automation 60 times.

This is a disaster.

---

# 99. Some high-speed signals need to be explicitly promoted to become Automation Events

For example:

```text
ArcScope trigger fired
```

If this is an explicitly professional event:

# Can become a Durable Event.

And:

```text
CurrentSignalValueChanged
```

Usually it should not.

---

# 100. Do not expose the universal event "Changed" as the main ecological contract.

RPC Events in the master program can be used for low-level notifications.

However, Stage 21 cross-App ecological events should try to:

# Semantic.

For example:

```text
DocumentRevisionCommitted

SessionCompleted

FindingCreated

RenderCompleted
```

instead of:

```text
Changed
```

The consumer then guesses what happened.

---

# 101. Event Ordering, do not make illusions about global ordering

Not created:

# Global ArcForges Event Sequence.

This is very expensive and unnecessary.

---

It is guaranteed that:

```text
Source instance sequence

Resource revision

Task sequence
```

etc. local order.

Between different apps:

# There is no pretense that there is an absolute global sequence of events.

---

# 102. Event loss cannot destroy the state

Continuing with the general principles:

> SignalR/real-time events are not the only reliable truth; state must be resynchronized via Revision/Sequence after disconnection.

Therefore:

```text
missed event
↓
query current snapshot/revision
↓
recover
```

---

# 103. Health cannot have only one green dot

Cross-App running status must distinguish at least five different dimensions:

```text
Installation

Presence

Health

Readiness

Compatibility
```

---

# 104. Installation

For example:

```text
Installed

Not Installed
```

This is the long-term status of the device.

---

# 105. Presence

For example:

```text
Running

Not Running

Offline / disappeared
```

Answer:

> Is Instance here now?

---

# 106. Health

It is recommended to unify:

```text
Healthy

Degraded

Unhealthy
```

Answer:

> Is the instance itself normal?

---

# 107. Readiness

For example:

```text
Ready

Busy

Not Ready
```

Answer:

> Are you currently available for a new job?

---

# 108. Compatibility

Answer:

> Can the current caller and this Instance understand the same Capability Contract?

Possible:

```text
Compatible

Partially Compatible

Incompatible
```

---

# 109. These dimensions cannot be combined

For example:

```text
ArcSlate
Running
Healthy
Busy rendering
Compatible
```

Totally legal.

---

Another example:

```text
ArcNotes
Running
Healthy
Ready
But Capability v3 incompatible
```

It's entirely possible.

---

# 110. Health ≠ Trust

An Instance can:

```text
Healthy
```

But:

```text
Untrusted / unauthorized
```

This is safe.

Failure to pass health check due to:

> Capability is granted.

---

# 111. Health ≠ Capability Availability

For example ArcScope overall:

```text
Healthy
```

But:

```text
StartCapture
Unavailable because device disconnected
```

So:

# Capability Availability

Still a separate Projection.

---

# 112. Health Snapshot cannot become a business status image

Hub can know:

```text
healthy
busy
active resources routing hints
```

But not:

> Stuff the entire Timeline/Document/Capture state into Heartbeat.

---

# 113. Out-of-contact Instances are evicted by Lease

This basic outline has been determined:

> The Hub evicts out-of-contact instances by lease; they reconnect and re-register; the App itself does not depend on the Hub for normal local use.

Stage 21 continues direct inheritance.

---

# 114. Compatibility must be negotiated based on Capability

This is a very important conclusion of Stage 21.

Error:

```text
ArcChat 2.4
ArcNotes 2.3

version mismatch
→ cannot connect
```

---

Correct:

```text
ArcNotes supports:
Capability A v1/v2
Capability B v3

ArcChat supports:
A v2
B v2/v3

Result:
A v2
B v3
```

---

# 115. App Version is just information, not the only compatibility criterion

For example:

```text
ArcNotes 3.1.2
```

Users can understand it.

However, machine compatibility judgment should be based on:

# Contract / Capability versions.

---

# 116. Compatibility layering

At least logically:

```text
Foundation contract compatibility

Hub/control contract compatibility

Product capability contract compatibility

Individual capability version/features

Event contract compatibility
```

---

# 117. Not all version changes affect the entire App

For example, ArcSlate adds:

```text
AdvancedColorCapability v2
```

```text

```

Also suddenly unavailable.

For example:

```text
Unsupported
```

```text

TrimClip

```

# 119. Destructive Contract Change

The general outline has stipulated:

> Destructive changes use the new version interface and allow V1/V2 to coexist in the migration window; carry contractSet/version/features when registering, and perform Capability/version negotiation before calling.

Stage 21 officially upgrades this to:

# Semantic Versioning Rule.

---

# 120. CapabilityId should not be changed casually due to Additive Change

For example:

```text
CreateDocument
```

Add an optional capability:

> Still the same Capability.

---

Really changing the semantics:

For example:

> The input/effect meaning is destructively changed.

Requires:

```text
New major contract version
```

Even if necessary:

# new CapabilityId.

---

# 121. Feature Flag and Capability Version are different

Capability:

> What App compilation/implementation supports.

Feature Policy:

> Whether it is currently enabled.

Stage 25 is responsible for:

```text
Feature flag
Kill switch
Remote policy
```

The function cannot be temporarily turned off:

> Pretend the version is incompatible.

# 122. Contract organizations must avoid lock-step

The original general outline has been clarified:

> Do not use a giant `ArcForges.Contracts` to couple all products. At the same time, Foundation only retains basic concepts such as stable ID, Revision, Result, ResourceRef, and TaskSnapshot.

Stage 21 further freezes:

# **Shared Foundation is small and stable; Product Capability Contracts are independently owned and versioned by product owners.**

---

That is to say logically:

```text
Foundation
│
├── Hub / Platform Control Contracts
│
├── ArcChat semantic contracts
├── ArcNotes capability contracts
├── ArcScope capability contracts
└── ArcSlate capability contracts
```

---

# 123. Do not let an ArcNotes upgrade force an ArcSlate re-release

If only:

```text

```

Upgrade:

ArcSlate:

# Should not be forced to recompile/release.

---

So in the future, even if there is a larger LocalRpc contracts project in the physical Solution layout stage:

> Semantic ownership and version boundaries still have to be broken down by product.

This is not a change to StreamJsonRpc.

This is:

# Contract Governance.

For example:

```text
AppId

InstanceId

ResourceId

TaskId

CommandId

Revision

Result/Error

```

The general outline has also been defined in this way.

# 125. Foundation is prohibited from appearing

```text
ArcNotesDocumentDto
```

# 126. The formal definition of Invocation

# **Invocation = A complete semantic invocation that actually requests the execution of a Capability.**

It connects Stage 21 and Stage 19.

# 127. Invocation at least logically includes

```text
Invocation identity

Capability identity + negotiated version

Actor

Authority / Workspace scope

Target App / Instance

Resource bindings

Context bindings

Task / Run / Step / Attempt correlation when applicable

Command identity for writes

Expected revision when applicable

Approval reference when applicable

Deadline / cancellation context
```

It's not that these all turn into one giant do-it-all DTO.

Owner-specific request still:

# Strongly Typed.

The common envelope only carries platform semantics.

# 128. InvocationId and CommandId are strictly separated again

Stage 19 has been frozen:

## InvocationId

# This time the actual call is made.

Try again:

> newInvocationId.

---

## CommandId

# This is a logical writing action.

Technical retry:

> Continue with the same CommandId.

---

For example:

```text
Create Document

CommandId = C1

Invocation 1
timeout

Invocation 2
same CommandId C1
```

Owner finds that C1 has completed:

> Return the original result.

Instead of creating a second Document.

So:

# Step ≠ Invocation.

```text
↓
Negotiate
↓
Bind Context/Resources
↓
Validate
↓
Authorize / Preflight
↓
Invoke
↓
Immediate Result
or
TaskHandle
```

# 131. Resolve

```text
ArcNotes
```

```text
Instance B
```

# 132. Routing priority is officially frozen.

Continue the existing rules of the general outline and generalize to Resource:

### 1. Explicit Instance

The call explicitly specifies:

# InstanceId.

### 2. Resource-affine Instance

For example, the current authoritative writable Session of Document X is:

# ArcNotes Instance A.

Priority A.

---

### 3. Explicit User Preferred Instance

The user has selected:

# Executed in this Instance.

---

### 4. Single Healthy Compatible Instance

There is only one:

> Use directly.

---

### 5. Launchable App

Installed but not running:

> Can be started on demand.

---

### 6. Ambiguous

Return:

# Selection Required.

It cannot be random.

This is fully consistent with the current multi-instance routing principles of the master plan.

## Artifact

## Handler

## Deep Link

57. Click Open ArcScope Session.

## Event

62. ArcScope CaptureCompleted.

64. Raw Capture not included.

## Realtime Recovery

68. SignalR/Event connection disconnected.

## Health

73. ArcSlate Running/Healthy/Busy.

## Compatibility

## Independence

95. Hub recovery.

98. Do not lose your status.

# Stage 21 finalized

From this stage onwards, the common business language between the four ArcForges apps is officially frozen as:

# **App / Instance / Contribution**

Description:

> Who is in the ecology and what it can contribute.

---

# **Capability**

Description:

> What an app can be safely called by a machine to do.

---

# **Action**

Description:

> What the user can do in the current context.

---

# **Context Provider**

Description:

> What the user is looking at, selecting, and working on now.

---

# **ResourceRef**

Description:

> Who is the object actually owned by an App?

It only normalizes:

# Identity.

Never attempt to standardize content domains across all apps.

---

# **Artifact**

Description:

> What valuable results did a piece of work produce?

It can reference the professional Resource, but does not take over the Ownership of the professional Resource.

---

# **Deep Link**

Description:

> Where the user should be navigated.

It is not:

# Side-effect Command.

---

# **Event**

Description:

> What business facts have occurred.

It is not a command, nor does it turn SignalR/Callback into a database.

---

# **Health / Presence / Readiness / Compatibility**

Describe respectively:

> Is the App present? Is it working properly? Can it take on new jobs? Can both parties understand the same Capability?

No more using a fuzzy green dot to carry all the semantics.

---

# **Invocation**

Description:

> An Actor makes an actual call to a certain Capability on a certain Instance/Resource.

And with Stage 19:

```text
Task
Run
Step
Attempt
CommandId
ExpectedRevision
Approval
Correlation
Causation
```

Complete connection.

---

The final cross-App relationship therefore becomes:

```text
Human / Agent
      │
      ▼
    Action
      │
      ▼
   Capability
      │
      ├──── Context Binding
      │
      ├──── ResourceRef
      │
      ▼
   Invocation
      │
      ▼
 Owning App Instance
      │
      ▼
 Application / Domain
      │
      ├── Revision
      ├── Resource
      ├── Artifact
      ├── Event
      └── TaskHandle when long-running
```

The most critical long-term principles are:

> **App identity is not equal to process.**

> **Action is not equal to Capability.**

> **Context is not equal to Resource.**

> **ResourceRef only standardizes identity, not professional content.**

> **Artifact does not take over the ownership of professional resources.**

> **Event expresses the fact that it has happened, rather than secretly sending the Command.**

> **Deep Link only does navigation/Handoff and does not become a dangerous operation API.**

> **Compatibility is negotiated based on Capability, rather than requiring four App versions to be locked in step.**

> **The same App will never be routed randomly when there are multiple instances.**

> **All write calls continue to follow CommandId, Revision, Permission and Owner final verification.**

> **All large resources continue to stay on the Owner side.**

> **All professional payloads continue to be strongly typed and will not degenerate into `Dictionary<string, object>` universal protocols.**

This enables the **StreamJsonRpc Interface Code First RPC** that has been identified in the "Full C# General Outline" to truly have complete upper-layer business semantics without redesigning the Transport at all. The original general outline `AppId / InstanceId / ResourceRef / CommandId / TaskHandle / Revision / capability negotiation` has now been condensed by Stage 21 into a unified Cross-App Semantic Model that can carry **ArcChat, ArcNotes, ArcScope, ArcSlate and the fifth Arc App** in the future for a long time.

**Stage 21 At this point, it can be considered that the cross-App semantic layer is officially closed.**

# Stage 22: Local Data / Project Format / Interoperability Architecture

This stage solves a problem that is easily underestimated, but will actually determine whether ArcForges can live for more than ten years:

# **What is the user's real data, where is it placed, how is it saved, how is it migrated, how is it restored, and how is it taken away.**

Stage 9 has been resolved:

> How does Local-first data enter the Cloud, how does Blob synchronization occur, how does multiple devices recover, and which Raw Capture/Media data are not uploaded to the Cloud by default?

Stage 15/16/20 defined respectively:

* Document/Block/Attachment/History of ArcNotes;
* ArcScope's Session/Capture/Raw/Derived Data;
* Project/Sequence/Timeline/Media/Proxy/Cache for ArcSlate.

Stage 22 must now wrap this all up into:

# **ArcForges Local Data Constitution**

It cannot appear in the future:

```text
ArcNotes:
SQLiteIt’s the document format

ArcScope:
CaptureThe file isProject

ArcSlate:
ProjectThe database isExportFormat

ArcChat:
Conversation JSONThat’s all the status
```

This kind of handle:

# Runtime Storage

and:

# User Data Format

Mixed design.

The original outline has made it clear "who owns the data and who is responsible for their own transactions, versions, undos, logs, snapshots and resource life cycles", and the ArcNotes baseline itself has clearly included AOT-safe SQLite, journal/snapshot, Undo/Redo and crash recovery; it also requires database migration rehearsal, data format reader/writer version, and safe read-only/recovery mode if migration fails.

Therefore, Stage 22 does not overturn these, but completes the upper data system.

---

# 1. First freeze the most important five-layer concepts

From now on, ArcForges must strictly distinguish between:

```text
Domain Model
    ↓
Working Store
    ↓
Native Portable Format
    ↓
Interchange Format
    ↓
Derived Projection / Cache
```

They are not the same thing.

---

# 2. Domain Model

Answer:

> **What the product thinks the user's data is.**

For example:

### ArcNotes

```text
Notebook
Document
Block
Property
Link
Attachment
Revision
```

### ArcScope

```text
Project
Session
Capture
Signal
Event
Annotation
Analysis
```

### ArcSlate

```text
Project
Sequence
Track
Clip
Effect
MediaAsset
Marker
```

This is product authority semantics.

---

# 3. Working Store

Answer:

> **How to save these Domain States efficiently and transactionally safely when the App is running normally.**

You can use:

```text
SQLite

structured files

blob files

append-only capture chunks

journal
```

Wait.

It is:

# Implementation-oriented durable representation.

---

# 4. Native Portable Format

Answer:

> **How users can bring an ArcForges native object intact to another machine, back it up, archive it, or re-import it.**

It must:

```text
Versioned

Self-describing

Validated

Portable
```

And can maintain the unique semantics of ArcForges to the greatest extent.

---

# 5. Interchange Format

Answer:

> **How to exchange data with the ecosystem outside ArcForges.**

For example:

```text
Markdown

HTML

CSV

JSON

SRT

PDF

common media formats
```

It usually:

# Full Fidelity is not guaranteed.

---

# 6. Derived Projection/Cache

Answer:

> **What data is generated that can be restructured for search, display, AI, performance.**

For example:

```text
Search index

Embedding index

Thumbnail

Waveform

Proxy

Render cache

Decoded projection

FFT result cache
```

All:

# Not the authority on user data.

---

# 7. The highest principle of Stage 22

Officially frozen:

# **Runtime Storage Format ≠ User Interchange Format.**

SQLite works well with ArcNotes.

But this does not mean:

> "Giving `.db` files to users is the ArcNotes document format."

Similarly, ArcSlate can use efficient databases internally,

But:

> Users should not have to understand SQLite to back up video projects.

---

# 8. The second highest principle

# **The logical format of user data is independent of current database technology.**

Inside today:

```text
SQLite
```

A future module:

```text
new embedded store
```

As long as Domain and Native Format remain stable:

# Should not cause the user's format to completely change.

---

# 9. The third highest principle

# **Do not sacrifice transaction security and editing performance for the sake of "Git friendliness".**

This is a very clear decision that must be made at this stage.

Error:

> "Git does not diff SQLite very well, so all edit status changes to a bunch of JSON files."

In the end it is likely to produce:

```text
partial writes
thousands of tiny files
cross-file invariants
slow save
hard migration
merge corruption
```

Therefore:

# The Runtime Store serves correctness first.

Git friendliness:

# Solved by explicit text formatting, Repository Projection and Interchange.

Detailed definition later.

---

# 10. Unify Local Data classification

The local data of the four apps is now unified into the following categories:

```text
Canonical Structured State

Managed Assets

External References

Append-only / Large Data

Revision / Recovery State

Derived Data

Device-local Presentation State

Secrets

Temporary Data
```

This is better than:

```text
db/
files/
cache/
```

This purely physical classification is far more important.

---

# 11. Canonical Structured State

The data that truly determines what a user's work is.

For example:

### ArcNotes

```text
Document blocks
Links
Tags
Properties
Notebook structure
```

### ArcScope

```text
Sessions
Annotations
Analysis definitions
Report structure
```

### ArcSlate

```text
Sequences
Timeline
Clips
Effects
Markers
```

These:

# Must enter reliable Durable Store.

---

# 12. Managed Assets

Owner App is clearly responsible for the life cycle of files.

For example:

```text
ArcNotes managed attachment

ArcScope imported managed dataset

ArcSlate managed source media
```

App is responsible for:

```text
identity
integrity
storage
migration
backup/export
sync policy
```

---

# 13. External References

The user explicitly chooses:

> Keep the original file external.

App only saves:

```text
Stable logical asset identity

Location hint

Fingerprint

Metadata
```

Do not own the original file.

---

# 14. Append-only / Large Data

Especially ArcScope:

```text
Raw Capture
```

This kind of data:

# Should not be stuffed into normal relational table blobs.

Should be used:

```text
chunked files
append-oriented data segments
```

Or equivalent big data storage method.

---

Reason:

```text
Continuous writing

GB/TBscale

partial recovery

rangeread

Avoid huge databasesBlobaffairs
```

---

# 15. Revision/Recovery State

For example:

```text
Journal

WAL

Revision metadata

Checkpoint

Recovery manifest
```

This is:

# Reliability infrastructure.

Not the user's main content itself,

But it is necessary for recovering user data.

---

# 16. Derived Data

Unification principle:

# **Delete and rebuild.**

For example:

```text
index
thumbnail
embedding
proxy
waveform
FFT cache
decoded cache
```

If an item of Derived Data is deleted:

> Project is permanently damaged,

Explain the design error.

---

# 17. Device-local Presentation State

For example:

```text
Window position

Panel layout

last opened tab

zoom

monitor placement
```

Stage 14 has been confirmed:

# Default is Device-local.

It must not contaminate:

# Native Project portability.

---

# 18. Secrets

For example:

```text
API key

OAuth token

credential
```

Forever:

# Not entering Project/Document Native Format.

Even if a Project references:

```text
Provider X
```

Also only save:

# Secret reference.

Stage 26 then completes the security implementation.

---

# 19. Temporary Data

For example:

```text
unfinished drag preview

clipboard staging

temporary render frames

temporary download
```

After App crashes:

# Can be cleaned directly.

It should never be allowed to be the sole source of a work.

# 20. Final Storage Strategy of Four Products

Officially freezing the general direction below:

| Product      | Working Store Principle        | big object                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| **ArcChat**  | DB-centric Hybrid      | attachments/artifacts/blob store        |
| **ArcNotes** | DB-centric Hybrid      | managed attachments/blob store          |
| **ArcScope** | Project-centric Hybrid | chunked raw captures                    |
| **ArcSlate** | Project-centric Hybrid | external/managed media + derived caches |

This does not mean that four apps use the same database schema.

Quite the opposite:

# Each App has its own Local Store.

ArcChat local authority status:

```text
Conversations

Projects

Automations

Memory
```

Suitable for:

# Embedded transactional DB.

---

Attachments/Artifact files:


Not to:

```text
500MB PDF
4GB generated video
```

Normal user experience:

```text
ArcChat Local Library
```

Automatic maintenance.

> Select the `.arcchat` file first for each chat.

```text
Document != Markdown File
```

```text
Folder

Tags
```

For example:

```text
FTS

Semantic index

Embedding vectors

Extracted PDF text
```

```text
rebuild
```

Continue to Stage 15.

Because otherwise these would lose their full expression:

```text
Stable BlockId

Typed Properties

Block references

Revision

Agent provenance

Managed attachment identity
```

# 26. But Markdown must be first-class Interchange

So:

```text
ArcNotes Domain
        ↓
Markdown Export
```

instead of:

# 27. ArcScope: Project-centric Hybrid

ArcScope is better suited than ArcNotes for:

# **A clearly identifiable Project Store.**

Logic:

```text
ArcScope Project
│
├── Project metadata / DB
├── Raw Capture data
├── Managed assets
├── Analysis state
└── optional portable resources
```

---

# 28. ArcScope Structured State

You can enter the Project-local embedded DB:

```text
Project configuration

Session metadata

Capture metadata

Channel/Signal definitions

Annotations

Measurements

Analysis definitions

Reports
```

---

# 29. Raw Capture must not be designed as an ordinary Blob in a database

Officially frozen:

# **Raw Capture uses independent, chunked, and verifiable large-scale data storage.**

For example logic:

```text
captures/
    capture-A/
        chunk-0001
        chunk-0002
        ...
```

Only the data shape is explained here, the actual file name is not fixed.

---

# 30. Why does Capture need Chunk?

This way you can:

```text
continueappend

partial recovery

partial read

range upload

Broken segment

damage isolation

large scale data
```

---

if:

```text
100GB capture
```

is a single file that must be rewritten atomically in its entirety:

> It will be very painful later.

---

# 31. Capture Segment and physical Chunk are not equivalent

Stage 16:

```text
CaptureSegment
```

It is Domain concept.

And:

```text
Storage Chunk
```

It is a storage implementation.

---

A CaptureSegment:

> Can contain multiple Chunks.

Do not let file boundaries control Domains in turn.

---

# 32. Default is Immutable after Raw Capture Finalize

Stage 16 has been frozen:

# Raw Capture is the evidence.

So Finalized Capture:

> Normal analysis is not modified in place.

---

If the underlying layer needs to be compressed/repackaged:

Must maintain:

```text
same logical raw evidence
+
verified transformation provenance
```

Or produce:

# New managed representation.

Cannot be changed without trace.

---

# 33. ArcScope Decoder Result does not enter the Raw Store

Decoder:

```text
Raw
↓
Decoded Events / Signals
```

Belongs to:

# Derived / Reproducible.

Can be cached,

But Raw still exists.

ArcSlate is also officially adopted:

Canonical Structured State of Project:

# 35. ArcSlate Project State does not insert Original Media into the core DB

```text
or
```

# 36. Proxy/Cache independent

```text
Proxy

Render Cache

Thumbnail Cache

Waveform Cache

Analysis Cache
```

All:

# Derived.

---

Delete:

```text
cache/
```

Maximum:

> Regeneration is slow.

# 37. Project Working Store and Portable Project Package must be separated

This is one of the most important designs of Stage 22.

During normal operation:

# **Working Project Store**

Can be used for:

```text
transactions

autosave

large data

incremental update
```

Use structures appropriate to the runtime.

---

User needs:

```text
Transfer

Archive

Backup

Share privately

Move machine
```

When:

# **Portable Package / Bundle**

Responsible for portability.

---

# 38. Do not force every project to be a giant ZIP.

Especially:

```text
ArcScope 500GB Capture

ArcSlate 1TB Media
```

If you need to save every time:

> Rewrite one archive

Totally unacceptable.

---

Therefore it was officially decided:

# **The Working Store of large projects defaults to a directory-backed bundle instead of a single compression container.**

---

# 39. Portable Export can select a single file Archive

if:

```text
metadata + small managed assets
```

Suitable for:

> Pack a file.

Can:

# Archive Container.

---

But large media/Raw data:

The default is better suited for:

# Folder Bundle.

Therefore:

```text
Portable Format
```

Describes the logical layout,

Not:

# Must ZIP.

---

# 40. Composition principles of Portable Bundle

Concept:

```text
Manifest

Canonical data

Managed assets

Optional history

Integrity metadata
```

---

Cannot contain:

```text
Machine paths as authority

Secrets

Temporary files

Render cache

Search cache

Window coordinates
```

---

# 41. Portable Manifest must exist

Each Native Portable Format contains at least:

```text
Format family

Format version

Producer product

Producer version

Resource identity

Required features

Managed assets

External references

Integrity information
```

---

# 42. Manifest should be able to be read without loading the entire Project

This is very important.

This way:

```text
File picker

Importer

Migration tool

Compatibility check
```

You can quickly know:

> What's this.

Without opening it first:

```text
400GB data
```

---

# 43. The Manifest itself should not become a duplicate copy of the entire Project content

For example:

```text
Timeline
```

Already in the Project Store.

Manifest:

# The full Timeline is no longer copied.

Otherwise the two authorities will drift.

---

# 44. Native Format must be Versioned

Formally distinguish at least three version concepts:

```text
Storage Schema Version

Native Format Version

Product Version
```

They cannot mix.

---

# 45. Storage Schema Version

means:

> The current internal structure of Working DB/Store.

Only for:

# App itself/migrator

important.

---

# 46. Native Format Version

means:

> A structured version of the user-portable Package.

Import/Export tools require understanding.

---

# 47. Product Version

For example:

```text
ArcNotes 2.7
```

Just the app version.

Cannot:

```text
ArcNotes 2.7
=
Format Version 2.7
=
DB schema 2.7
```

All tied to death.

---

# 48. Reader Version and Writer Version

The general outline already requires that the document format has a reader/writer version and migration tests, and requires that data format upgrades cannot allow old versions to mistakenly write semi-upgraded data.

Stage 22 is officially expanded to:

Each Native Format should be able to determine:

```text
Can Read?

Can Write?

Can Upgrade?

Can Open Read-only?
```

---

# 49. Backward Read and Backward Write must be separated

For example the new ArcSlate:

```text
Can readv3
```

Does not mean:

```text
Safe to write backv3
```

---

So it's possible:

```text
Read v3
Upgrade on edit
```

Or:

```text
Read-only legacy mode
```

---

# 50. When a new version opens old data, it must not immediately destroy the old compatibility without prompting.

Ideal process:

```text
Open
↓
Inspect format
↓
Can migrate?
↓
Create recovery point
↓
Migrate
↓
Validate
↓
Commit format upgrade
```

---

# 51. Format Upgrade is separated from ordinary App Startup

Cannot:

```text
App starts
↓
automatically alters 300 projects
```

Only migrate:

# Data that is actually opened or explicitly batch migrated.

---

# 52. Schema Migration principle officially frozen

Migration must:

```text
Versioned

Deterministic

Idempotent where practical

Testable

Recoverable

Auditable
```

---

# 53. Small DB Schema Migration

ideal:

# Transactional.

For example:

```text
begin
alter/create/backfill
validate
commit
```

Failure:

# Rollback.

---

# 54. Large-scale migration cannot pretend that one database transaction solves everything

For example:

```text
ArcScopeReindex2TB Capture
```

Cannot:

> Lock the library for 4 hours.

Correct:

```text
Schema migration
↓
new format ready
↓
background derived rebuild
```

---

User data:

# It can be safely opened first.

Derived Data:

# Backstage rebuild.

---

# 55. Derived Data usually does not migrate at all

if:

```text
Search Index v3
```

becomes:

```text
Search Index v4
```

Usually:

# Delete + Rebuild.

---

Do not write:

```text
Migration 1→2→3→4
```

Specifically migrate dozens of GB Cache.

---

# 56. Canonical User Data cannot be so rough

For example:

```text
ArcSlate Timeline
```

Must:

# Real migration.

Cannot:

> "If it's not compatible, delete it and rebuild it."

---

# 57. Recovery Point must be established before destructive migration

At least:

```text
Metadata snapshot
DB backup/checkpoint
Manifest
```

---

For very large projects:

> It is not necessary to copy 500GB Raw Data.

Because Raw itself may not change.

Just make sure:

# Modified data has a recovery path.

---

# 58. Migration Recovery Point ≠ Normal Undo

Migration failed:

> The entire storage structure needs to be restored.

This is:

# System Recovery.

Not a user:

```text
Ctrl+Z
```

---

# 59. Migration must be verified after completion

For example:

```text
foreign keys/logical constraints

resource references

asset integrity

revision chain

required manifests
```

Cannot:

> No error is reported during SQL execution = Migration is successful.

---

# 60. Enter Safe Mode when Migration fails

Formal:

# **Never continue to write half-and-half upgrade data.**

Enter:

```text
Read-only

Recovery

Restore previous

Export data
```

one.

The general outline also already requires that migration failures enter safe read-only/recovery mode instead of continuing to write semi-upgraded data.

---

# 61. App Binary Rollback and Data Rollback must be separated

For example:

```text
ArcSlate 3
↓
upgrades project format
```

User rollback:

```text
ArcSlate 2
```

Old App:

> You cannot pretend that you can write a new version of Project.

---

Can:

```text
Refuse write

Read-only if safe

Restore pre-upgrade recovery copy
```

---

# 62. This is why Updater must know Data Compatibility

Stage 5:

```text
keep previous executable
```

does not automatically equal:

# User data can be rolled back.

Stage 22 explicitly adds this.

---

# 63. Formal semantics of Autosave

From now on all ArcForges professional apps use:

# **Durable Local Commit First.**

The user completes a confirmed edit:

```text
Domain Command
↓
validate
↓
commit canonical state
↓
acknowledge saved
↓
cloud/outbox later
```

---

# 64. "Saved" can only be displayed after it is truly Durable.

Cannot:

```text
ViewModel changed
↓
UI immediately shows Saved
↓
database still pending
```

---

Product promises to users:

# Saved locally

means:

> Under the normal supported fault model, this change has entered the Durable Local State.

---

# 65. Autosave ≠ Copy the entire Project every time you type on the keyboard

For example, ArcNotes type a character:

Cannot:

```text
serialize entire Notebook
```

ArcSlate drags a Clip:

Cannot:

```text
rewrite entire Project package
```

---

An implementation of Autosave must:

# Incremental / Transactional.

---

# 66. UI Transient State and Committed Edit are separated

For example, the user drags an ArcSlate Clip:

```text
Mouse move
Mouse move
Mouse move
...
```

These:

# Preview State.

---

Drop:

```text
MoveClip Command
```

To become:

# Durable Edit.

---

# 67. ArcNotes continuous text input can be merged in a short time

For example:

```text
typing "hello world"
```

Not required:

> 11 independent user Revision.

Can:

# Coalesced Edit Transaction.

---

But not for merging:

> Did not settle for 5 minutes.

Requires:

```text
short durability interval
+
focus/change boundary
+
safe flush
```

The specific number of milliseconds is determined by Stage 27 actual measurement.

---

# 68. The final semantics of Ctrl/Cmd+S

After Autosave exists:

# Save remains.

But the meaning becomes:

```text
Flush pending durable writes

Create/advance explicit checkpoint where product supports

Confirm local durable state
```

---

It is not:

> "Nothing is saved without pressing Ctrl+S."

---

# 69. Cloud Pending never triggers Unsaved Prompt

Continue to Stage 14.

For example:

```text
Local
✓ Saved

Cloud
3 changes pending
```

Close:

# Yes.

---

# 70. Undo, Revision, Checkpoint, and Recovery must be completely separated.

This is another set of concepts that are most critical to Stage 22.

```text
Undo
≠
Revision
≠
Checkpoint
≠
Recovery Journal
```

---

# 71. Undo

Answer:

> **Can the user operation I just performed be reversed?**

Features:

```text
Command-oriented

User-facing

Short/medium horizon

Semantic
```

For example:

```text
MoveClip

DeleteBlock

AddAnnotation
```

---

# 72. Undo must be based on semantic Command

Not:

```text
DB row before/after bytes
```

Otherwise complex operations:

```text
Ripple Delete
```

Cannot be a user action.

---

# 73. Redo

Based on Undo Branch.

But once:

```text
Undo
↓
new edit
```

Traditional Redo chain can fail.

---

# 74. Revision

Answer:

> **What committed versions does a persistent object have in its history?**

It is:

# Durable History.

---

For example:

```text
Revision 41
Revision 42
Revision 43
```

---

# 75. Undo will not delete Revision

User:

```text
Revision 43
↓
Undo
```

The result is usually:

```text
Revision 44
```

It expresses:

> A semantic undo of 43.

instead of:

```text
43disappear
```

---

This is what Stage 15 has frozen:

> Restore the old Revision to generate a new Revision instead of deleting the subsequent history

Totally consistent.

---

# 76. Checkpoint

Answer:

> **Is this a safe boundary worth explicitly restoring?**

For example:

```text
Before Agent Edit

Before Format Migration

Before Major Timeline Rewrite

User-created checkpoint
```

---

Checkpoint usually refers to:

# A stable Revision/Snapshot.

---

# 77. Checkpoint is not created every time Command is issued.

Otherwise:

> Duplicate with Revision.

Checkpoint is:

# Named Recovery Landmark.

---

# 78. Recovery Journal

Answer:

> **How to rebuild the final confirmation status after the process exits abnormally?**

It is:

# Persistence Infrastructure.

Not the user history UI.

---

# 79. Users should not browse 1 million Storage Journal Entries

Normal UI display:

```text
History

Revision

Checkpoint
```

Internal:

```text
WAL/journal
```

Only used for:

# Recovery and Diagnosis.

---

# 80. The principle of Undo History across restarts

This cannot be ambiguous.

Official decision:

# **Revision History must be Durable; Undo Continuity can be persisted by product, but cannot be used as the only recovery mechanism.**

---

ArcNotes / ArcSlate:

> A certain range of semantic Undo history can be saved to improve the restart experience.

But if a certain Undo cannot be safely restarted:

> Does not affect Revision/Recovery integrity.

---

# 81. Therefore it can never be claimed

```text
Undo Stack
=
Crash Recovery
```

Completely different.

---

# 82. Minimum guarantee of Crash Recovery

Any App happens:

```text
power loss
process crash
native library crash
forced termination
```

After restarting:

# **All confirmed Durable Commits must be maintained.**

---

The only things that may be lost are:

```text
uncommitted instantUIStatus
```

---

# 83. Crash Recovery cannot rely on "Save when App exits normally"

This is a fundamental mistake.

Because:

> There is no Exit during Crash.

Must rely on:

```text
transactional store
journal/WAL
append durability
```

and other mechanisms.

---

# 84. Startup Recovery Pipeline

It is recommended to formally freeze as:

```text
Open Store
↓
Detect clean/unclean shutdown
↓
Validate storage metadata
↓
Replay/rollback storage journal
↓
Verify canonical state
↓
Reconcile incomplete operations
↓
Quarantine/rebuild derived data
↓
Open normally
```

---

# 85. Derived Cache is damaged and the App cannot enter Project Corrupt.

For example:

# 200. The complete scene that must be passed in Stage 22

## Autosave

1. ArcNotes input text.
2. UI editing occurs.
3. Durable commit is successful.
4. Show Saved locally.
5. Kill the process immediately.
6. The restart content is still there.

---

## Cloud Independence

7. Cloud is disconnected.
8. Editing continues.
9. Local Saved.
10. Cloud Pending.
11. Exit the App.
12. No "Unsaved changes" false prompt appears.

---

## Undo / Revision

13. Document Revision 10.
14. Edit→Revision 11.
15. Undo.
16. Produce Revision 12.
17. Revision 11 still exists.
18. History is complete.

---

## Checkpoint

19. Agent is ready for major changes.
20. Create Checkpoint.
21. Agent changes 100 Blocks.
22. Users are not satisfied.
23. Restore checkpoint.
24. A new Revision is generated.
25. History has not been deleted.

---

## Crash

26. ArcSlate is editing.
27. The confirmed Command has been flushed to disk.
28. Native library causes process crash.
29. Restart.
30. Timeline status has been confirmed to be complete.
31. Cache needs to be rebuilt but Project is normal.

---

## ArcScope Capture

32. Continuous Capture.
33. Write multiple Chunks.
34. The process exited abnormally.
35. Finally, Chunk retention has been confirmed.
36. Unfinished Chunk is identified.
37. Capture marked Interrupted/Recovered.
38. Other Chunks are intact.

---

## Migration

39. Old Project v3.
40. A new app opens.
41. Establish a Recovery Point.
42. Migration begins.
43. Failed midway.
44. Do not continue to write a semi-upgraded store.
45. Restore old data.
46. Users can still use the old version.

---

## Derived Migration

47. Search index version changes.
48. Old Index is not migrated.
49. Delete.
50. Backstage rebuild.
51. Canonical data does not need to be changed.

---

## Portable Package

52. ArcScope Project export.
53. Copy to another machine.
54. There is no Original external resource.
55. Project can still be opened.
56. Missing resource is clear.
57. Restore after Relink.

---

## ArcSlate Media

58. External video path changes.
59. AssetId remains.
60. Relink.
61. Timeline ClipIds are all maintained.

---

## Changed External Media

62. The same Path file is replaced.
63. Fingerprint changes.
64. ArcSlate prompts Source Changed.
65. New content is not used silently.
66. User clearly Accept/Relink.

---

## ArcNotes Markdown

67. Export Notebook Markdown.
68. Edit externally.
69. There are no mysterious real-time changes to the Document inside ArcNotes.
70. User explicit import.
71. Import Report is generated.
72. The new state enters the normal Domain.

---

## Import Failure

73. Import 1000 items.
74. Item 800 damaged.
75. Canonical Store leaves no unexplained semi-imported data.
76. Staging clean/recoverable.

---

## Lossy Export

77. Document exists and Markdown cannot represent the content.
78. Export detection.
79. Display Loss Report.
80. The user chooses to continue.
81. The output is clearly marked Fallback.
82. Do not lose data silently.

---

## Git

83. User exports Repository Projection.
84. Export without change twice in a row.
85. Git diff is close to zero.
86. Modify a Document.
87. Diff mainly focuses on corresponding content.
88. Cache/DB/WAL does not enter Git.

---

## Restore from Git

89. Checkout past versions.
90. Import to Staging.
91. Validate.
92. Materialize.
93. Create normal ArcForges new Revision/Restore state.
94. Do not directly hot replace the open DB.

---

## Multiple Writers

95. ArcSlate Project has been opened writably by Instance A.
96. Instance B opens.
97. Enter Read-only/Clear Take Ownership.
98. Do not generate two uncoordinated Writers.

---

## Backup

99. App is running.
100. Create consistent Snapshots.
101. The half-written DB is not copied directly.
102. Restore to new location.
103. Validate succeeded.
104. Open normally.

---

## Corruption

105. Thumbnail cache is damaged.

106. Delete and rebuild.

107. Project is normal.

108. Canonical DB is corrupted.

109. Stop writing.

110. Save a corrupted copy.

111. Recovery Mode.

112. Recover Checkpoint or readable data.

---

# Stage 22 finalized

From now on, ArcForges will no longer include:

# "What database do I use?"

Treat as:

# "My User Data Format".

The final data system is officially divided into:

```text
Domain
↓
Reliable Working Store
↓
Versioned Native Portable Format
↓
Interchange Adapters
```

At the same time, all products use the same:

```text
Canonical State
Managed Assets
External References
Revision/Recovery
Derived Data
Device-local State
```

This set of classifications.

---

The final directions of the four products are:

### ArcChat

# DB-centric Hybrid

Mainly local Library, Attachments/Artifacts independent resource storage.

---

### ArcNotes

# DB-centric Hybrid

The Canonical Block/Link/Property model is in the structured Store, and the attachments are independent; Markdown is First-class Interchange, but not Canonical Runtime Format.

---

### ArcScope

# Project-centric Hybrid

Structured Project Metadata + Blocked Raw Capture Store; Raw immutable, Decode/Analysis is Derived.

---

### ArcSlate

# Project-centric Hybrid

Timeline/Edit State + External/Managed Media; Proxy, Render Cache, Waveform, and Thumbnail are all Derived.

---

All professional apps comply with:

# **Local durable commit first.**

Users see:

```text
Saved locally
```

, the data has actually entered the local Durable State.

Cloud status is always displayed separately.

---

Historical system unification:

```text
Undo
    =
semantic edit reversal

Revision
    =
durable committed history

Checkpoint
    =
explicit recovery landmark

Journal
    =
crash recovery infrastructure
```

The four are no longer confused.

---

Format upgrade and unification:

```text
Preflight
↓
Recovery Point
↓
Migration
↓
Validation
↓
Commit
```

Failure:

# Safe Read-only / Recovery Mode.

Never continue to write:

# Half-migrated Data.

This is completely consistent with the `journal/snapshot`, crash recovery, migration rehearsal, reader/writer version and safe recovery principles already required by the original general outline.

---

Portability unification:

> **Resource Identity does not rely on absolute paths.**

> **Managed resources follow Package.**

> **External resources remain Reference and Collect when necessary.**

> **Secrets, Cache, and Window State do not enter Portable Format.**

---

Git friendliness also officially closed as:

# **Git-friendly representation, not Git-driven runtime architecture.**

Something suitable for text:

# Direct Git.

Complex Transactional Domain:

# Deterministic Repository Projection.

Large assets:

# Git LFS / External Store.

Runtime DB / WAL / Cache:

# Does not participate in Git merge.

Therefore, the transaction reliability of ArcNotes, ArcScope, and ArcSlate will not be sacrificed for Git, nor will users be locked into a black box database that cannot be versioned or exported at all.

**Stage 22 At this point, local data, Project/Document Format, Autosave, Undo/Revision, Crash Recovery, Migration, Import/Export, External Editing, Portability and Git friendliness have formed a unified data architecture that does not fight with each other.**

# Stage 23: Knowledge / Search / Retrieval Architecture

This stage solves a problem in ArcForges that can easily end up becoming a "second central database":

# **Knowledge exactly what it is, who owns it, and how Search and AI Retrieval use it without duplicating data from professional apps.**

Stage 7 has been confirmed:

* Cloud can provide Cloud Search;
* Mobile/Web can only access Cloud visible range;
* Desktop-local data is not secretly uploaded for search purposes.

Stage 9 has been confirmed:

* Search Index, Embedding, Thumbnail, etc. belong to Derived Data;
* Sync ≠ AI transmission;
* Cloud replica is not the second Domain Owner.

The original "Full C# General Outline" has also made it clear that ArcNotes itself has "notebooks, documents, blocks, links, tags and indexes", with local search and optional vector indexing; Cloud can maintain cloud resource indexes. At the same time, the outline insists that all products have unique state owners, caches/indexes must be discardable, sourced and revised, and cannot become new authoritative write points.

Stage 23 brings these foundations into completeness:

# **Knowledge Source → Scope → Index → Search → Retrieval → Evidence → Citation → AI Context**

And make it clear:

# **ArcNotes is the long-term knowledge authority and ArcChat is the cross-source retrieval and Agent Retrieval Orchestrator.**

Not the other way around.

---

# 1. Freeze the seven most important concepts first

From now on strict distinction:

```text
Knowledge Source
        ↓
Knowledge Scope
        ↓
Index
        ↓
Search
        ↓
Retrieval
        ↓
Evidence
        ↓
Citation
```

These seven things should never be mixed together:

```text
Vector Database
```

a concept.

---

# 2. Formal definition of Knowledge Source

# **Knowledge Source = An authoritative source of content that can be discovered, retrieved, or used for knowledge answers.**

Itself:

# Not necessarily a copy of the data.

Usually just:

```text
Owner
+
Resource / Resource Set
+
Knowledge Policy
```

---

# 3. The most typical Knowledge Source

## ArcNotes

```text
Notebook

Document collection

Document

Managed attachments
```

ArcNotes is the most complete long-term knowledge source.

## ArcChat

```text
Conversation History

Project-owned ArcChat data

Artifacts

Saved research
```

But ArcChat's old Chat:

# It is not equal to the user's real long-term knowledge base.

---

## ArcScope

```text
Reports

Findings

Annotations

Measurements

Session metadata

Decoded textual events
```

---

## ArcSlate

```text
Project metadata

Transcript

Subtitle

Marker

Clip metadata

Render/report metadata
```

---

# 4. Raw ArcScope Data does not directly become ordinary text Knowledge Source

For example:


Cannot:

```text
split into chunks
→ embed everything
→ vector search
```

# **Should be retrieved via ArcScope Professional Query / Measurement / Analysis Capability.**

# 5. ArcSlate Raw Video Same reason

For example:

```text

Transcript

Markers

User annotations
```

Can be expanded.

But:

# It cannot be a basic dependency of V1 Knowledge.

# 6. Knowledge Source ≠ Context Provider

Stage 21 already has:

# Context Provider

means:

> What the user is looking at now.

For example:

```text
Current ArcNotes Selection

Current ArcScope Time Range
```

---

Knowledge Source:

> Is a set of content that can be retrieved over a long period of time.

Therefore:

```text
Current Selection
≠
Knowledge Source
```

But Current Selection:

# Can point to a Resource in a Knowledge Source.

---

# 7. Knowledge Source ≠ Import

For example the user said:

> "Enable ArcChat to search this ArcNotes Notebook."

It cannot be understood as:

```text
Copy Notebook
→ ArcChat database
```

Instead:

```text
ArcNotes Notebook
        ↓
Knowledge eligibility/reference
        ↓
ArcNotes Search Capability / Index
```

# 8. Knowledge Source does not change Ownership

This is one of the most important rules in all of Stage 23.

```text
ArcNotes Document
```

After becoming AI Knowledge:

# Still owned by ArcNotes.

ArcChat will not get:

```text
ArcChatDocumentCopy
```

# 9. Knowledge Source Definition

In the long term, you should be able to express:

```text
Source identity

Owner App

Root Resource / selector

Realm / Workspace

Search policy

AI retrieval policy

Cloud indexing policy

Availability
```

---

Not:

> A Source = a copy of the full text.

Not required:

```text
Salary Information
Exclude from AI
```

# 12. Formal definition of Knowledge Scope

# **Knowledge Scope = A Search / Retrieval allows the boundaries of which Knowledge Sources / Resources to be considered.**

# Index.

```text
Current Notebook
```

```text

+
```

Real runtime analysis.

121. Scope analysis.
122. Evidence is fixed to this Run.
123. Adding a new Document during task execution does not secretly change the selected Evidence.

---

# 252. Long Source

124. Notebook contains 100000Documents.
125. Query first generates candidate refs through Index.
126. Only a small amount of final evidence is read.
127. Do not load the entire Notebook into the model Context.

---

# 253. AI Pollution Prevention

128. The agent generates a temporary guess.
129. Ordinary Chat Response is saved.
130. It does not automatically become Long-term Knowledge.
131. User explicitly Save as ArcNotes.
132. The new Document becomes the official Knowledge Source content.

---

# 254. Stage 23 final system

After completing this stage, ArcForges' Knowledge architecture officially becomes:

```text
                AUTHORITY
                   │
                   ▼
              Knowledge Source
                   │
                   ▼
              Resource / Revision
                   │
                   │
            ┌──────┴──────┐
            ▼             ▼
       Local Index     Cloud Index
            │             │
            └──────┬──────┘
                   ▼
               Search
                   │
                   ▼
           Candidate Results
                   │
             Scope + Policy
                   │
             Permission Check
                   │
             Freshness Check
                   │
                   ▼
                Evidence
                   │
                   ▼
             Context Pack
                   │
                   ▼
                  AI
                   │
                   ▼
                Answer
                   │
                   ▼
               Citations
                   │
                   ▼
        ResourceRef + Revision + Anchor
```

---

# Stage 23 finalized

From now on:

# **ArcNotes is the long-standing intellectual authority on ArcForges.**

It has:

```text
Documents
Attachments
Links
Knowledge policies
Local indexes
```

---

# **ArcChat is the Knowledge Retrieval Orchestrator.**

It is responsible for:

```text
Federated Search
Knowledge Scope
Hybrid Retrieval
Evidence selection
Context packing
Citation
Agent retrieval
```

But:

# ArcNotes Knowledge Database is not copied.

---

# **ArcScope and ArcSlate are Specialist Knowledge Providers.**

They are exposed through their most suitable domain capabilities:

```text
Reports
Findings
Measurements
Transcript
Markers
Metadata
```

Instead of forcing all huge numerical data and videos to become Text Embedding.

---

# **Cloud Search is Derived Cloud Projection.**

It only covers:

```text
Cloud-visible
+
Cloud-index-allowed
+
Authorized
```

data.

---

And finally freeze the following extremely important boundaries:

> **Knowledge Source is not equal to data copy.**

> **Search Index is never the business authority.**

> **Keyword Search never relies on generative AI.**

> **Semantic Search can enhance Search but never replace Keyword Search.**

> **Cloud Sync is not equal to Cloud Index.**

> **Cloud Index is not equal to AI Retrieval.**

> **Exclude from AI will not invalidate the user's own normal search.**

> **AI Retrieval can only run within an explicit Knowledge Scope and cannot silently search everything the user has access to.**

> **Retrieval Candidate must be re-verified by permission and Revision before it can become a real Evidence.**

> **Citation always refers to Owner Resource + Revision + Typed Anchor, not Vector DB Chunk ID.**

> **The temporary conclusions generated by AI will not automatically pollute long-term knowledge.**

> **ArcChat Personal Memory is not ArcNotes Knowledge.**

> **Web Search results are not long-term knowledge unless the user explicitly saves it.**

> **Raw ArcScope Capture and ArcSlate video will not be Embedding or uploaded by default for so-called RAG.**

That way, however ArcForges later changes its search engine, Embedding Model, Vector Store, or Reranker, adds OCR, Multimodal Search, Knowledge Graph, or GitHub/Drive/Confluence Connectors, or even introduces a fifth professional App, **none of it requires overturning the Ownership, Scope, Index, Evidence, and Citation models of Knowledge.**

This is the long-term Knowledge Architecture that Stage 23 really needs to freeze.

---

# stage24

---

# Stage 24: Extension / Integration / Developer Platform

This stage is where ArcForges truly moves from a "suite of four products" to:

# **Scalable Platform**

critical step.

Already existing separately:

* Stage 6: Skill, MCP, ACP, App Capability;
* Stage 12: Community / Catalog / ecosystem;
* Stage 17: Agent Profile, Skill, MCP management;
* Stage 19: Unified running model required for Task/Workflow execution;
* Stage 21: Capability, Action, Context, ResourceRef, Artifact, Event;
* Stage 23: Knowledge Source/Search/Connector future entrance.

They must now be consolidated into **a single developer platform**.

Otherwise it can easily become:

```text
Skills There is a store
MCP Another configuration system
Connector Another plug-in framework
Agent Another one Agent Store
ArcNotes A set of plug-ins
ArcScope Decoder a set
ArcSlate Effect a set
Community Catalog Apply another layer
```

Finally:

* The installation mechanisms are different;
* Different permissions;
* Different versions;
* Updates are different;
* Trust is different;
* Publishing is different;
* SDK is different;
* Users simply do not know the difference between "Extension" and "Integration".

This stage is about completely stopping this fragmentation.

At the same time, we must continue to abide by the technical constitution of the "Full C# General Outline": the main desktop host targets Native AOT and cannot rely on any assembly scanning, dynamic proxy, Reflection.

---

# 1. Freeze the final overall developer platform model first

ArcForges Extension Platform will now be understood as:

```text
                         ArcForges Developer Platform
                                      │
         ┌────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┐
         │                            │                            │
         ▼                            ▼                            ▼
   Content Extensions           Integrations               Executable Extensions
         │                            │                            │
         ├─ Skill                     ├─ MCP                      ├─ Extension App
         ├─ Template                  ├─ Connector                ├─ Third-party Arc App
         └─ Workflow                  └─ External Agent / ACP     └─ Product Extension Provider
                                      │
                                      ▼
                            External Resources /
                            Capabilities / Events /
                            Knowledge Sources

                                      │
                                      ▼
                                Arc Package
                                      │
                                      ├─ Manifest
                                      ├─ Version
                                      ├─ Contributions
                                      ├─ Compatibility
                                      ├─ Permissions
                                      ├─ Publisher
                                      └─ Signature / Integrity

                                      │
                                      ▼
                               Community Catalog
```

All of which ultimately share:

```text
Package
Manifest
Publisher
Version
Compatibility
Trust
Permissions
Install / Enable
Update
Uninstall
Catalog
SDK
CLI
```

Instead of redesigning each one.

---

# 2. First, separate the most confusing concepts at once.

This is the most important set of definitions for Stage 24.

| concept                      | Answered questions                                        |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| **Skill**               | "How" Agent should do                                |
| **Template**            | "What initial structure to start with" when creating something?                           |
| **Workflow**            | A piece of work "executed according to what reusable process"                             |
| **Automation**          | "When" a job is automatically created                               |
| **Capability**          | What the system actually "can do"                                  |
| **MCP**                 | How external systems contribute Tool/Resource capabilities                 |
| **Connector**           | How ArcForges establishes long-term integration with an external service/data source                |
| **External Agent**      | Which external Agent Runtime to delegate Agent work to              |
| **ACP**                 | A protocol adaptation boundary for External Agent                     |
| **Extension**           | Installable extensions that add execution capabilities to ArcForges                    |
| **Third-party Arc App** | Independent and complete App, join the ecosystem through Stage 21 Contribution Model |
| **Package**             | How are the above things distributed and installed?                               |
| **Catalog**             | Where users go to discover Packages                              |
| **SDK**                 | How developers build them                                    |
| **CLI**                 | Tool chain for development, verification, packaging, testing, and release                           |

In the future, these concepts can no longer be substituted for each other.

A third party wants to contribute a new capability that the platform has never seen before:

Therefore adopt:

# **Schema-described Extension Capability Protocol.**

# 70. This is not a universal recovery `Dictionary<string, object>`

# Fixed, closed, AOT-safe Structured Value Model.

```text

Boolean

Integer

Decimal/Number

String

Binary reference

Date/Time

ResourceRef

List

Record
```

And clarify the Schema.

```text
arbitrary CLR object

runtime Type

assembly-qualified typename

native pointer
```


# Stage 24 finalized

From this stage forward, ArcForges no longer has:

> "Skills system, MCP system, Connector system, Agent plug-in system, and Community plug-in system develop independently."

They all fall into one unified:

# **ArcForges Extension / Integration / Developer Platform**

The final relationship is:

```text
                    ARC PACKAGE
                         │
          ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
          │              │              │
          ▼              ▼              ▼
       Content       Integration     Executable
          │              │              │
       Skill             MCP          Extension
       Template        Connector      Third-party App
       Workflow        External Agent
                           │
                           ACP
```

---

Among them:

# **Skill**

Representative:

> How Agent does it.

No code executed, no permissions granted.

---

# **Template**

Representative:

> What structure to start with when creating a Resource.

Materialize will be independent from Template in the future.

---

# **Workflow**

Representative:

> How to perform a reusable job.

Enter when executing:

```text
Task → Run → Step → Capability
```

---

# **Automation**

Continue to represent individually:

> When to create the Task.

Will not be merged with Workflow.

---

# **MCP**

is:

> External Capability Adapter.

Does not replace Native Arc Capability.

---

# **Connector**

is:

> Long-term identity, Resource, Search, Event and Capability integration with external systems.

MCP is just one of its possible implementations.

---

# **External Agent / ACP**

Representative:

> Delegate Agent work to external Agent Runtime.

External Session does not replace ArcChat's Task/Run Authority.

---

# **Extension**

Default:

# **Out-of-process.**

No longer used:

```text
arbitrary DLL
+
Assembly.Load
+
runtime XAML
```

As a Community Plugin architecture.

This gives:

```text
Native AOT
Security
Crash isolation
Version isolation
Native dependency isolation
```

can be established at the same time.

---

When dynamic third-party capabilities are really needed:

Adopt:

# **Fixed Extension Protocol + Schema-described Capability**

instead of:

```text
Dictionary<string, object>
```

The C# SDK continues to provide developers with:

# Code First experience.

At the same time, ArcForges NativeAOT Host does not need to know third-party CLR types during compilation.

This solves the core structural contradiction between **Native AOT and the open plug-in ecosystem**, while not destroying the first-party strong type Capability system that has been frozen in Stage 21.

---

All extensions ultimately have:

```text
PackageId
Publisher
Version
Manifest
Compatibility
Permissions
Trust
Signature
Dependencies
Install
Enable
Update
Rollback
Uninstall
```

---

Community Catalog is also officially just:

# **Discovery & Distribution Catalog**

instead of:

# Paid Marketplace.

Do not build commercial plug-in billing, taxation, and revenue sharing into the current platform foundation in advance.

---

The official Developer Platform finally consists of:

```text
C# SDK
Source Generators
arcforge CLI
Test Host
Package Validator
Package Builder
Publisher / Catalog
```

composition.

And the most important long-term principles were finally frozen as:

> **Skill is not code.**

> **Template is not a runtime.**

> **Workflow is not Automation.**

> **Automation is not the second set of Task Engine.**

> **MCP is not an ArcForges internal protocol.**

> **Connector is not an alias of MCP Server.**

> **ACP is just an External Agent Adapter and will not become another Conversation/Task system.**

> **Third-party Extension does not enter the main process by default.**

> **Third-party Native Code is isolated in the Extension Process by default.**

> **Public SDK does not expose internal LocalRpc/database implementation.**

> **First-party core capabilities continue to be strongly typed; dynamic third-party capabilities only use Schema Contract in explicit Extension Boundary.**

> **Package installation does not automatically grant Capability Permission.**

> **Publisher signature proves source, not security.**

> **Trust, Permission, Compatibility, and Health are always separated.**

> **Extension uninstallation will not delete user resources owned by professional apps.**

> **When Community Catalog is unavailable, installed local Extensions can still work.**

> **Any fifth Arc App, future Connector, External Agent, MCP Server, Skill, Workflow or professional Extension will enter this common platform instead of establishing a sixth plug-in system.**

**Stage 24 At this point, ArcForges' Skill / Template / Workflow / MCP / Connector / ACP / External Agent / Third-party App / Extension / SDK / CLI / Package / Catalog / Trust / Compatibility has officially formed a unified and long-term scalable Developer Platform.**

# stage25

---

# Stage 25: Dynamic Configuration & Product Policy Control Plane

What needs to be solved at this stage is not ordinary Settings or subscription permissions, but:

# **ArcForges How to safely, explain, and rollback changes to "how the current product is allowed to run" without redistributing the client.**

There are actually many places where it is needed:

```text
A new feature is only available 5%

someone Provider Temporary serious failure

Quality regression of a certain model, Pause new tasks

An old client version needs to be discontinued Cloud Sync

A certain function is only available Beta Channel

someone Remote Agent Capacity needs urgent Kill Switch

A certain default model needs to be dynamically adjusted

someone UI / Agent Behavior is experimenting

someone Cloud Features need to be turned off by region
```

If these were all hardcoded separately to:

```text
ArcChat

ArcNotes

ArcScope

ArcSlate

Mobile

Web

Cloud
```

Inside, there will eventually be six or seven sets of Feature Flag, Model Availability and Minimum Version systems.

Stage 25 is about unifying them.

---

# 1. Stage 25 final definition

Officially frozen:

# **Dynamic Configuration & Product Policy Control Plane**

is:

> **Server-published, versioned, cacheable, deterministically evaluated product run policy.**

It controls:

```text
Feature Availability

Feature Rollout

Emergency Kill Switch

Remote Configuration

Compatibility Policy

Minimum Client Version

Provider Availability

Model Availability

Experiment Assignment

Managed Product Constraints
```

---

It expressly **is not responsible** for:

```text
User Settings                     → Stage 14

Subscription / Entitlement        → Stage 4 / Stage 8

Permissions / Approval / Trust    → Stage 26

Local Domain State                → Product owner

Project/File migration            → Stage 22

Runtime Health                    → Stage 21 / Infrastructure
```

---

# 2. The most important first boundary

It must always be true in the future:

# **Policy ≠ Entitlement**

For example GPT-X model:

```text
Entitlement:
User's plan includes GPT-X
```

Just explain:

> User is eligible.

But currently it is possible to:

```text
Policy:
GPT-X temporarily disabled
```

Result:

# Temporarily unavailable.

---

The reverse is also possible:

```text
Policy:
GPT-X available
```

But:

```text
Entitlement:
not included in this subscription
```

Result:

# Upgrade required.

---

The two UIs must also be different:

### Entitlement

```text
Upgrade to use this model
```

### Policy Availability

```text
This model is temporarily unavailable
```

Definitely not all displayed:

# "Not available".

---

# 3. The second boundary

# **Policy ≠ Settings**

Settings answer:

> How users want to use the product.

Policy answer:

> How the current product is allowed to run.

---

For example:

```text
User Setting:
Use cloud AI = Off
```

This is a user choice.

---

```text
Policy:
Cloud AI disabled for this Workspace
```

This is a control plane limitation.

---

If the user:

```text
Use cloud AI = On
```

But Policy:

```text
Cloud AI = Disabled
```

Finally:

# Disabled.

UI according to Stage 14:

```text
Managed by Workspace Policy
```

Or:

```text
Unavailable by current product policy
```

---

# 4. The third boundary

# **Policy ≠ Runtime Health**

For example:

```text
Policy:
Claude Sonnet available
```

Provider at this moment:

```text
Health:
Outage
```

Finally still:

# Not currently enforceable.

---

In reverse:

```text
Provider:
Healthy
```

But Policy:

```text
Model disabled because of quality regression
```

Also cannot be executed.

So:

```text
Policy Availability
≠
Runtime Health
```

---

# 5. The fourth boundary

# **Policy Control Plane ≠ Request Data Plane**

This is a point in the architecture that must be frozen.

Cannot:

```text
User clicks button
↓
ArcChat calls Policy Server
↓
Can I use this?
↓
Every single operation
```

Otherwise:

> Policy Service hangs, and the entire product hangs.

---

Formal mode:

```text
Policy Control Plane
        ↓
Published Policy Snapshot
        ↓
Client / Cloud Runtime Cache
        ↓
Local deterministic evaluation
```

For Cloud's truly sensitive operations:

# The Cloud Service itself performs server-side policy checking again.

---

So:

> Desktop does not need to connect to the Internet to ask the Policy Server for every operation.

---

# 6. The entire system is finally unified into the following layers

```text
Built-in Product Invariants
           ↓
Compatibility
           ↓
Emergency Kill Switch
           ↓
Product Availability Policy
           ↓
Rollout
           ↓
Experiment Assignment
           ↓
Remote Configuration
```

Then when truly judging whether a user can use the function, combine it with other independent systems:

```text
Policy Decision
       +
Entitlement Decision
       +
User Setting
       +
Permission
       +
Runtime Health
       =
Effective Product Behavior
```

---

# 7. This cannot be implemented as a universal Boolean

Error:

```text
CanUseFeature = true
```

And no one knows why.

Correct must be retained:

# Decision Dimensions.

For example:

```text
SupportedByBinary        Yes

Compatible               Yes

Killed                    No

PolicyAvailable           Yes

RolloutEligible           Yes

Entitled                  No

UserEnabled               Yes

Permission                Yes

RuntimeHealthy            Yes
```

Finally:

```text
Unavailable
Reason:
EntitlementRequired
```

---

# 8. Formal definition of Feature

# **Feature = a stable product capability identity.**

For example conceptually:

```text
arcchat.remote-agent

arcchat.cloud-agent

arcchat.agent.parallel-work

arcnotes.semantic-search

arcscope.cloud-capture-upload

arcslate.ai-transcription
```

The specific final ID will be defined later in the implementation phase.

---

# 9. FeatureId must be stable and Namespaced

Cannot:

```text
NewFeature1

test2026

fooEnabled
```

This temporary variable becomes the long-term control plane identity.

---

Feature name can be changed:

```text
AI Search
↓
Semantic Search
```

But if the essence of business capabilities remains unchanged:

# FeatureId does not need to be changed.

---

# 10. Formal definition of Feature Flag

# **Feature Flag = Dynamic Gate indicating whether a Feature is currently allowed to be activated.**

It is not the Feature itself.

Therefore:

```text
Feature
≠
Feature Flag
```

---

After a mature Feature:

> It is completely possible to delete the Rollout Flag.

Feature still exists.

---

# 11. Feature Flag cannot become a permanent architecture layer

This is the most common disaster for Feature Flag systems.

Code at the end:

```text
if flagA
if flagB
if legacyFlag
if experimentalFlag
```

No one will dare to delete it after five years.

So each Flag must have:

```text
Owner

Purpose

Created

Lifecycle

Expected removal/review
```

---

# 12. Feature Lifecycle

Officially supported:

```text
Internal

Canary

Preview

General Availability

Deprecated

Retired
```

---

After Rollout is completed:

```text
General Availability
```

Percent Flag is no longer needed:

# Temporary code paths should be removed gradually.

---

# 13. Feature Flag can never replace the real version design

Error:

```text
if flag:
    write Project Format v5
else:
    write v4
```

Then a large number of users generate two kinds of incompatible data at the same time.

---

Involving:

```text
Persistent Schema

Project Format

Cross-App Contract

Cloud Sync Protocol
```

Must first use:

```text
Format Version
Contract Version
Migration
Compatibility
```

Stage 21/22 mechanism.

Rollout can only control:

# Whether capabilities that already have security compatibility are exposed.

---

# 14. Feature Rollout formal definition

# **Rollout = A release strategy in which a Feature gradually expands from a small number of objects to more objects.**

It can be based on:

```text
Percentage

Release Channel

App Version

OS

Architecture

Region

Realm

Workspace

User

Installation

Device capability
```

Safe and clear context.

---

# 15. The percentage Rollout must be Deterministic

Cannot:

```text
per request random() < 0.05
```

Otherwise:

> The user has it this time, but not next time.

---

Correct:

```text
Stable Subject
+
Feature Rollout Salt
↓
Deterministic Bucket
```

---

For example:

```text
bucket = 2741 / 10000
```

If 5%:

> Not entering.

If 30%:

> Enter.

stable.

---

# 16. Rollout Subject must be clear

Different Features can use different Assignment Units:

```text
User

Workspace

Installation

Device
```

---

For example, common personal UI functions:

# User.

---

Collaboration/Workspace level behavior:

# Workspace.

Otherwise:

```text
User ASee the new collaboration model

User Bsee old model
```

Serious inconsistencies may arise.

---

Hardware features:

# Device / Installation.

---

# 17. You cannot use email for Bucket Identity

Should use:

```text
opaque stable identifier
```

For example:

```text
UserId

WorkspaceId

InstallationId
```

Not used:

```text
email

display name
```

# 18. Experiment/Rollout identities cannot be shared between different Realms.

Continue to Stage 1:

```text
Official Cloud UserId
≠
Self-host Realm UserId
```

Even if:

> Same as Email.

# 19. Signed-out users

For fully local, anonymously testable Features:

You can use:

# InstallationId.

---

But if Experiment is defined:

```text
AssignmentUnit = User
```

Then:

# Signed-out user does not participate at all.

Do not install bucket first,

After logging in, suddenly switching the User bucket causes the Variant to jump randomly.

# 20. Rollout can have Allowlist

For example:

```text
Internal team

Design partners

Selected beta workspaces
```

---

Also possible:

# Denylist.

But:

Even if allowedlist:

Still possible:

# Not eligible for subscription.

# 21. Release Channel and Rollout are independent

Stage 5 already has:

```text
Stable
Beta
```

Rollout can:

```text
Beta 100%

Stable 10%
```

This is reasonable.

---

But:

```text
Release Channel
≠
```

# 22. Rollout must be able to stop expanding immediately

For example:

```text
5%
↓
25%
↓
50%
```

Exception found:

# Hold at 50%.

Or:

# 23. Rollout rollback must not destroy existing user data

Suppose Feature creates some kind of user object.

Feature Rollout from:

```text
20%
→
0%
```

Cannot:

> The existing object disappears and cannot be opened.

---

At least required:

```text
Read existing data

Preserve existing state

Disable creation of new data
```

Here's why:

# Rollout cannot replace Format Compatibility.

# 24. Officially introduce Kill Switch

# **Kill Switch = The highest priority dynamic switch used to quickly prevent a new execution or dangerous behavior under abnormal circumstances.**

Typical:

```text
Provider quality incident

Model severe regression

Remote Agent vulnerability

Broken Cloud capability

Data corruption risk

External API incident
```

---

# 25. Kill Switch is different from ordinary Feature Flag

Normal Flag:

> Product release management.

Kill Switch:

# Emergency Control.

---

It has higher priority:

```text
Rollout says Enabled
```

But:

```text
Kill Switch = Active
```

Result:

# Disabled.

---

# 26. Kill Switch must define stop semantics

You cannot just write:

```text
Disabled = true
```

Need to be clear:

```text
BlockNew

DrainExisting

StopAtSafePoint

ReadOnly

DisableExternalEffect
```

---

# 27. BlockNew

For example:

```text
New ArcSlate Cloud Render
```

Stop creating new tasks.

Already running:

# It can be done.

---

# 28. DrainExisting

stop new work,

Existing:

# Complete normally.

Suitable for:

```text
provider migration
```

---

# 29. StopAtSafePoint

For example found:

```text
someoneAgentAbility to potentially generate dangerous writes
```

Existing tasks:

```text
finish current safe operation
↓
stop before next dangerous invocation
```

---

With Stage 19:

# Cooperative cancellation / safe point

consistent.

---

# 30. ReadOnly

For example:

```text
Cloud sync write path bug
```

Can:

```text
Cloud reads allowed

New cloud writes blocked
```

---

Local:

# Continue saving.

Sync Outbox continues to wait.

---

# 31. Kill Switch never automatically deletes data

Hard rules:

```text
Disable feature
≠
Delete feature data
```

---

# 32. Kill Switch with cloud capabilities must be Server-side enforced

Client display:

```text
Disabled
```

Just UX.

Real Cloud API:

# Still refused.

Cannot believe it:

> Old clients will respect the new Flag.

---

# 33. Remote Kill Switch cannot be the only way to fix local security vulnerabilities.

This is a very important point for Local-first products.

If a:

```text
offline local feature
```

There is a serious Security Bug,

User is completely offline:

> Cannot receive Kill Switch.

So a true security fix still requires:

# Application Update.

Remote Policy:

> It can only reduce the risk for Connected users.

cannot be:

# Local security boundary only relies on.

# **Remote Config = Product parameters dynamically issued by the server and constrained by Schema.**

For example:

```text
default model recommendation
```

```text
Typed Value

Default

Validation

Staleness Behavior
```

# 36. The supported Config Value should be a closed type

For example:

```text
Boolean

Integer

String
```

Not:

For example user settings:

### Policy Constraint

Clear management:

---

instead of:

# 41. Setting itself must declare whether it can be controlled by Policy

NumericLimit:

# 55. Compatibility Policy formal definition

# **Compatibility Policy = Whether the platform allows a client/capability to continue to access online services even though technical protocols may still currently work.**

This is it with Stage 21:

# Capability Negotiation

difference.

```text
2.1
```

At least:

# 59. Recommended Version

Just:
