# Stage 25 finalized

From this stage forward, ArcForges has a unified:

# **Dynamic Product Policy Control Plane**

It is responsible for:

```text
Feature Flag
Rollout
Kill Switch
Remote Config
Compatibility Policy
Minimum Version
Provider Availability
Model Availability
Experiment Assignment
```

## Feature Rollout

Must:

# Deterministic + Sticky.

It will not randomly change every request.

---

## Kill Switch

is:

# Emergency override.

Able to:

```text
Block New

Drain

Stop at Safe Point

Read-only
```

But:

> **User data is never automatically deleted.**

---

## Remote Config

is:

# Typed, Validated, Bounded Data.

Not:

# arbitrary JSON / arbitrary code.

Each Key has:

```text
Default
Scope
Resolver
Validation
Application Timing
Staleness Policy
```

---

## Compatibility

Press:

# Product Capability / Cloud Service

Precise control.

instead of:

> If a certain App version is lower, the entire software cannot be used.

The most important Local-first principle continues:

> **Cloud Minimum Version cannot lock the user's own local Document, Project and Export capabilities.**

---

## Provider / Model Availability

Formal with:

```text
Catalog
Health
Entitlement
User Selection
```

All separated.

User Pin exact Model:

> Policies are not allowed to change models silently.

Auto mode:

> Recommendations can be changed by dynamic Routing Policy, but the actual execution Model must be recorded.

---

## Experiment

Only used for:

# Compatible Product Variant.

Cannot experiment:

```text
Security guarantees

Permission bypass

Entitlement

Irreversible data semantics

Incompatible file formats
```

---

## Policy release

Officially adopted:

```text
Draft
→ Validate
→ Stage
→ Publish
→ Immutable Revision
```

Fallback:

# Publish a new Revision.

Do not modify history.

---

## Runtime

Application and Cloud Service usage:

# Immutable Policy Snapshot.

The Control Plane is not requested in real time for every operation.

Client:

```text
Built-in Default
+
Last Known Good
+
Background Refresh
```

So even if the Policy Control Plane is temporarily unavailable:

# Local-first products still work fine.

---

And the most critical long-term boundary finally freezes as:

> **Policy is not Settings.**

> **Policy is not Entitlement.**

> **Policy is not Permission.**

> **Policy is not Runtime Health.**

> **Feature is not a Flag.**

> **Rollout is not an Experiment.**

> **Kill Switch is not a data deletion mechanism.**

> **Remote Config is not dynamic code deployment.**

> **Minimum Cloud Version cannot become a local data lock.**

> **Model Availability cannot be disguised as a subscription level.**

> **Remote Policy cannot change the frozen architecture constitution of ArcForges.**

> **Feature Flag cannot be a substitute for Project Format, Contract Version, or Database Migration.**

> **All Policy decisions must be able to explain "why" and cannot just return a Boolean.**

> **All dynamic controls must have security Default, LKG, Revision, Validation and Rollback.**

That way, even with dozens of Cloud features, dozens of Providers/Models, multiple Stable/Beta/Preview release stages, self-hosted Realms, a large number of Workspaces, and continuous product experiments, ArcForges only ever maintains **one set of dynamic product control semantics** — rather than a fragmented world with one set of Flags for ArcChat, another Remote Config for ArcNotes, a separate Minimum Version for Cloud, and yet another Model Switch for AI.

**Stage 25 At this point, it can be considered that the Dynamic Configuration / Feature Rollout / Compatibility / Provider & Model Availability / Experiment Control Plane is officially closed.**

# Stage 26: Product Security / Permission / Trust Closure

At this stage, the parts of ArcForges that are most likely to get out of control after Agent, Automation, Remote, MCP, and third-party Extension all enter are completely sealed:

# **Who is doing it, who is doing it on behalf of, what it can do, what it can do, why it can be done, when it must be confirmed again, how trustworthy the third-party code is, whether Secret can be used, whether Remote can replace local confirmation, and whether it can be explained clearly afterwards.**

Here **not re-discuss** what Stage 10 is already responsible for:

```text
TLS
WAF
Key Vault infrastructure
Network topology
Cloud firewall
DDoS
Server hardening
```

Nor do we need to redo Stage 25:

```text
Feature Flag
Kill Switch
Dynamic Product Policy
Minimum Version
```

Stage 26 completes:

# **ArcForges Product Security Model**

Final core chain:

```text
Identity
   ↓
Security Principal
   ↓
Actor / Delegation Chain
   ↓
Trust Eligibility
   ↓
Capability Permission
   ↓
Resource Authorization
   ↓
Data / Secret / Egress Constraints
   ↓
Effective Risk
   ↓
Approval / Step-up / Local Presence
   ↓
Owner Final Enforcement
   ↓
Invocation
   ↓
Audit
```

---

# 1. First, freeze a few concepts that must never be mixed up again.

It always holds true henceforth:

```text
Identity
≠
Actor
≠
Executor
≠
Caller Process
```

and:

```text
Permission
≠
Approval
≠
Trust
≠
Entitlement
≠
Product Policy
```

and:

```text
ResourceRef
≠
Permission Token
```

These three sets of boundaries are the root of the entire Stage 26.

---

# 2. Formal definition of Security Principal

# **Security Principal = A security principal that can be granted or denied permissions.**

ArcForges exists at least:

```text
Human Principal

Automation Principal

Workspace Service Principal

Extension / Integration Principal

Trusted Device Principal
```

Not all "execution stuff" is a Principal.

---

# 3. Human Principal

Represents real users.

For example:

```text
Ryan
```

It binds:

```text
Realm

Account / Local Profile

Workspace Membership

Roles / Grants
```

---

It can also exist when you are not logged in to the Cloud:

# Local Human Principal.

For example:

```text
LocalProfile: Ryan
```

Therefore:

> The Permission Model does not depend on Cloud.

---

# 4. Agent Profile is not Security Principal

This must be officially frozen.

```text
Engineering Agent
```

Just:

# Agent Configuration.

It cannot have a permanent set of superpowers independent of the user.

Correct relationship:

```text
Ryan
  ↓ delegates
Engineering Agent
  ↓ executes
Capability
```

---

So:

# **Agent acts on behalf of a Principal.**

---

# 5. Ordinary Agent cannot exceed the authority of Delegating Principal

If Ryan does not have read permission:

```text
Workspace Secret Document
```

Then his Agent:

# No rights either.

Not because:

> "This is AI, so all the data is needed in the background."

Ultra vires.

---

# 6. The Tool configuration in Agent Profile is not Permission

For example Profile:

```text
Tools:
ArcNotes
GitHub
ArcScope
```

means:

> Allow the Agent to consider using these Tools.

does not mean:

# Authorization Granted.

---

Ultimately you still need:

```text
Actor rights
+
Capability permission
+
Resource authorization
+
Approval when required
```

---

# 7. Automation Principal

Stage 19 has made it clear that Automation will automatically generate Tasks in the future.

Must now be resolved:

> Who will Automation be running on behalf of six months later?

Two security models are officially supported.

---

## 1. Run As Creator

For example:

```text
Automation:
Weekly Report

Run As:
Ryan
```

Then every time you run:

# Reuse Ryan's current permissions.

---

If Ryan later:

```text
loses Workspace access
```

Automation:

# Needs Attention.

Old permissions that were saved six months ago will not be used again.

---

# 8. User administrator rights cannot be permanently frozen when creating Automation

Prohibited:

```text
Ryan was admin when automation created
↓
Ryan removed from workspace
↓
Automation still admin forever
```

This is seriously Privilege Zombie.

---

# 9. The second type is Workspace Service Principal

For truly enterprise-level unattended work:

```text
Nightly Compliance Report
```

Can be created explicitly:

# Workspace Service Principal.

---

It has:

```text
own identity

explicit grants

owner/admin

lifecycle

audit identity
```

---

This is not:

> "Automation itself is the administrator."

---

# 10. Service Principal must be created explicitly

Not every Automation automatically:

```text
create invisible super-user
```

---

Ordinary individual users:

# By default, Service Principal is not required at all.

---

# 11. Automation Definition ≠ Automation Principal

An Automation is just:

# Enforce the rules.

What exactly does it:

```text
Run as Creator
```

Or:

```text
Run as Service Principal
```

Is a separate security attribute.

---

# 12. External Agent is not an independent Principal by default.

For example ACP Coding Agent.

Typical relationship:

```text
Human Ryan
     ↓ delegates
ArcChat Task
     ↓ delegates limited work
External Coding Agent
```

External Agent:

# Executor.

It gets:

# Scoped Delegation Lease.

---

Not:

> Once the External Agent is connected, it becomes a Workspace Member.

---

# 13. The formal definition of Actor

# **Actor = This time the business operation is "who did it" in terms of security semantics.**

For example:

```text
Human Actor
Agent Actor
Automation Actor
Service Actor
```

---

# 14. Formal definition of Executor

# **Executor = the software/process that actually performs the operation.**

For example:

```text
ArcChat Desktop

ArcNotes Instance

Cloud Task Worker

External Coding Agent

Extension Process
```

---

# 15. Caller Instance is also reserved

For example:

```text
Actor:
Ryan

Delegated Actor:
Engineering Agent

Caller:
ArcChat Desktop

Executor:
ArcNotes Instance
```

Four identities:

# All different.

---

# 16. Why must this be separated?

Because Audit if only shows:

```text
ArcNotes modified document.
```

Totally meaningless.

What you really need to know:

```text
Ryan
through Engineering Agent
through ArcChat Desktop
used ArcNotes
to modify Document X.
```

---

# 17. Official introduction of Actor Chain

All delegated operations can express:

```text
Initiator
   ↓
Delegator
   ↓
Agent / Automation
   ↓
Caller
   ↓
Executor
```

For example:

```text
Ryan
↓
Weekly Report Automation
↓
ArcChat
↓
ArcNotes
```

---

Or:

```text
Ryan
↓
Engineering Agent
↓
External Coding Agent
↓
GitHub Connector
```

---

# 18. Actor Chain cannot be lost due to cross-App

if:

```text
ArcChat
→ ArcScope
→ ArcNotes
```

ArcNotes ultimately sees more than just:

```text
Caller = ArcChat
```

Also must know:

```text
Original Actor

Task

Delegation

Command
```

---

# 19. App Identity itself does not represent user authority

This is very important.

Even if:

```text
ArcChat
```

It is a first-party App.

Nor can it say to ArcNotes:

> "I am the official App, give me all the Documents."

---

ArcChat is just:

# Trusted software identity.

Business authorization still comes from:

# Actor Chain.

---

# 20. First-party App Trust ≠ Unlimited Permission

Continue to freeze:

```text
First-party
≠
All-access
```

Otherwise, all cross-App permission designs will be invalid.

---

# 21. Capability Permission becomes the core of authorization

ArcForges does not use:

# "Can the plug-in access the entire App?"

This coarse-grained mode.

The core units are:

# **Capability.**

For example:

```text
arcnotes.document.read

arcnotes.document.create

arcnotes.document.delete

arcscope.session.read

arcscope.capture.start

arcslate.timeline.edit

arcslate.render.start
```

---

# 22. Formal definition of Permission

# **Permission = Authorization for a Principal to use a Capability under a certain Scope and Constraint.**

It at least semantically includes:

```text
Principal

Capability

Resource Scope

Workspace / Realm Scope

Constraints

Grant Source

Validity

Expiry

Revocation state
```

---

# 23. Permission cannot just be

```text
CanUseArcNotes = true
```

This kind of authority must eventually be too broad.

---

For example, an agent might:

```text
Read ArcNotes Technical Notebook
```

But:

```text
Cannot delete anything
```

This is reasonable.

---

# 24. Capability Permission and Resource Authorization are separated

For example:

```text
Ryan has:
arcnotes.document.read
```

Not equal to:

> Ryan can read all Documents in all Workspaces.

Also required:

```text
Resource authorization
```

---

So ultimately:

```text
Capability Permission
+
Resource Access
=
Eligible
```

---

# 25. Resource Owner is the final Authorization Authority

Continue to Stage 13/21:

ArcNotes owns Document.

So:

```text
ArcNotes
```

Final verdict:

> Whether this Actor can read/write this Document.

---

Hub can coordinate.

ArcChat can carry Grant.

But:

# Owner App must be inspected eventually.

---

# 26. The Hub cannot be made into a universal ACL Database

Hub can have:

```text
delegation coordination

approval state

cross-app grant metadata
```

But:

# Professional Resource access rules are still maintained by the Owner.

---

Otherwise it will become:

> The central Service owns all business access models.

Violation of Stage 13.

---

# 27. Default Owner of Local Personal Resource

For local mode without Workspace:

```text
Local Human Principal
```

By default, you have a local Resource created by yourself.

So:

# Users can directly edit normally without popping up Permission every time.

---

However:

```text
Agent
Automation
Extension
External Agent
```

Still only get:

# Delegated Authority.

---

# 28. Role's official position

ArcForges can have:

```text
Role

Group
```

But:

# Role is just Permission Assignment Convenience.

---

Cannot design:

```text
if Admin
    allow everything forever
```

All over the product code.

---

Correct:

```text
Role
↓
Grants
↓
Capabilities + Resource scopes
```

---

# 29. The final authorization model is Capability-based + Scoped

instead of:

# Pure RBAC.

Role can reduce management costs,

But the real decision still revolves around:

```text
Actor

Capability

Resource

Context
```

---

# 30. Life cycle of Permission Grant

Officially supports at least:

```text
One Invocation

Current Task / Run

Current Session

Resource / Project Scope

Workspace Persistent Grant

Time-limited Grant
```

---

# 31. Do not make all prompts "Allow Once / Always Allow"

Because:

# What exactly does Always Allow allow?

Scope must be specified.

For example:

```text
Allow this task

Allow this notebook

Allow this ArcNotes project

Allow for this workspace
```

---

instead of:

```text
Always allow ArcChat.
```

Such a dangerous sledgehammer.

---

# 32. Grant must be minimized

For example, the user allows Agent:

> "Create reports for Engineering Notebook."

Reasonable Grant:

```text
Capability:
CreateDocument

Scope:
Engineering Notebook
```

---

Not:

```text
All ArcNotes write forever
```

---

# 33. Permission Grant can have Conditions

For example:

```text
only while Task X is active

only selected repository

only selected device

only documents tagged public

only outputs under Folder X
```

---

Concretely express the subsequent Domain design.

But the model must allow it.

---

# 34. Permission Grant ≠ Approval

Officially frozen again.

## Permission

Answer:

> Is this Actor generally qualified to perform such operations?

## Approval

Answer:

> Is this specific action approved now?

---

# 35. Having Permission may still require Approval

For example:

```text
Agent has permission:
arcnotes.document.delete
```

But specifically to delete:

```text
384 documents
```

Effective Risk is raised.

Still need:

# Approval.

---

# 36. Formal definition of Approval

Stage 19 has the basics, and now the complete summary is:

# **Approval = A provisional authorization decision for a clear enforcement intention.**

Must be bound:

```text
Actor

Task / Run

Capability

Target Resources

Resource Revision when relevant

Proposed Effect

Effective Risk

Expiry

Requested Scope

Approval Decision
```

---

# 37. Approval cannot just be written

```text
Approve this action?
```

A good Approval must tell the user:

```text
Who

What

Where

How much

External effect?

Can it be undone?

What data leaves the device?
```

---

# 38. Pical Approval

For example:

> Engineering Agent wants to replace 42 blocks in
> `ArcNotes / Architecture`.

Display:

```text
42 blocks will be changed

Checkpoint will be created

No data leaves this device

Reversible through checkpoint
```

---

Only users can truly judge.

---

# 39. Bulk Approval must display Scope

For example:

```text
Create markers in 183 clips.
```

Cannot:

> Play each item 183 times.

---

But you cannot:

> "Approve changes"

Cannot tell the scale.

---

Support:

```text
Approve all 183 proposed changes
```

and displays:

```text
sample
count
affected resource
risk
```

---

# 40. Approval binding Resource Revision

Continue to Stage 19:

```text
Approval based on Revision 42
```

Found before execution:

```text
Current Revision 49
```

Cannot continue.

Requires:

```text
re-evaluate
↓
new preview
↓
reapproval where necessary
```

---

# 41. Approval has Expiry by default

Cannot:

> The task approved two months ago suddenly resumed execution today.

---

# 42. Approval Decision at least

```text
Approved

Denied

Expired

Invalidated

Canceled
```

---

Not just:

```text
true / false
```

---

# 43. Approval can generate Transient Grant

For example user approval:

```text
Allow this task to modify Document X.
```

can generate:

# Task-scoped temporary grant.

Task ends:

# Automatically invalid.

---

# 44. Approval cannot be automatically upgraded to Persistent Permission

Unless the user explicitly chooses:

```text
Always allow within this scope
```

And the Risk level allows it.

---

# 45. Capability Risk officially uses R0–R4

Stage 6 already has R0–R4, and it is now officially closed.

Important:

# **Risk is Capability baseline + Runtime modifiers.**

Not every Capability always has a fixed number.

---

# 46. R0 - Passive / Harmless

Typical:

```text
Navigate

Read non-sensitive metadata

Query status

Open local resource
```

Principles:

# Approval is usually not required.

---

But still need:

# Normal Resource authorization.

---

# 47. R1 - Normal Reversible Local Action

Typical:

```text
Create marker

Add tag

Create ordinary local note

Rename non-sensitive resource

Small reversible edit
```

Direct Human:

# Execute normally.

Agent:

> This can usually be done automatically within an explicitly authorized Scope.

---

# 48. R2 - Significant / Sensitive but Recoverable

Typical:

```text
Bulk document edits

Large timeline edits

Read sensitive workspace data

Generate large number of resources

Modify important project structure
```

---

Usually requires:

```text
explicit task grant

impact preview

checkpoint
```

At least some of these scenarios:

# Approval.

---

# 49. R3 - External / Secret / Persistent Side Effect

Typical:

```text
Send data to external provider

Publish content

Post GitHub comment

Use sensitive secret

Enable persistent automation with write permissions

Upload local resource externally
```

---

Default:

# Explicit Approval.

---

Persistent Grant only allows:

# Narrow Scope + Explicit User Consent.

---

# 50. R4 - Critical / Irreversible / Security Administration

For example:

```text
Permanently destroy large canonical data

Change security ownership

Reveal credential plaintext

Enable unverified privileged extension

Transfer sensitive data across trust boundary

Disable security controls

High-impact irreversible external action
```

---

Principles:

# Always explicit.

Usually also required:

```text
Step-up authentication

Local presence

or Workspace admin authority
```

Specifically, press Capability.

---

# 51. R4 cannot have the ordinary "Always Allow Everything"

This is a hard rule.

---

Can exist:

> Enterprise administrators pre-authorize extremely narrow machine workflows through explicit security policies.

But this is not:

# User clicks "Always allow R4".

---

# 52. Effective Risk can be dynamically improved

For example:

```text
DeleteDocument
```

Delete:

```text
1 recently-created local draft
```

and:

```text
12,000 workspace documents
```

Definitely not the same risk.

---

Therefore Runtime Modifiers include:

```text
Target sensitivity

Resource count

Irreversibility

Data volume

External egress

Secret use

Remote origin

Automation origin

Third-party executor

Background execution
```

---

# 53. Risk can only be raised and cannot be lowered by a third party.

Extension cannot be declared:

```text
“DeleteEverything is R0”
```

Then circumvent Approval.

---

Final minimum risk:

# Determined by Host/Owner Capability Contract.

Third-party statements are simply:

# Metadata input.

---

# 54. Stage 25 Product Policy can be more stringent

For example:

```text
Workspace:
All external uploads require approval.
```

The actual requirements can be:

# improve.

---

But not:

> Reduce R4 to R1.

---

# 55. Official introduction of Approval Requirement

Capability can be defined:

```text
Never

Conditional

Always

LocalPresenceRequired

AdminRequired
```

Wait for the request.

---

Real Decision:

# Combined with Effective Risk.

---

# 56. Step-up Authentication

Certain high-risk operations require users to:

```text
re-authenticate
```

For example:

```text
Passkey

password

platform authentication
```

The specific implementation will be determined later.

---

It answers:

> Is the current person operating this really the Human Principal?

---

# 57. Step-up ≠ Approval

Users may:

```text
Approve action
```

Also required:

# Reauthenticate.

Two things.

---

# 58. Local Presence officially becomes a security attribute

Certain capabilities can be declared:

# **Requires Local Presence on Target Device**

For example:

```text
Reveal local credential

Enable Developer Mode

Install unverified privileged extension

Change remote-control trust

Certain destructive local operations
```

---

Then:

> Click Approve on Mobile

Nor is it a substitute for local confirmation on the target Desktop.

# 59. Remote Approval and Local Presence must be separated

This is the key to preventing Remote Agent from causing accidents in the future.

For example:

```text

```

Mobile:

# Yes.

---

And:

```text
Reveal API key plaintext on DEKU
```

Even if Mobile is a Trusted Device:

# Still cannot replace Local Presence.

Stage 18 has completed the Remote Task product.

The Remote security chain is now officially frozen as:

```text
Authenticated User
↓
Trusted Session / Device
↓

↓

↓

↓

↓
```

# 61. Mobile/Web can never directly become a local professional App super administrator

Cannot:

```text
Mobile
→ direct ArcNotes DB
```

Nor can:

```text
Cloud
→ arbitrary desktop command
```

All Remote execution:

# Continue past ArcChat Desktop + Hub + Capability.

# 62. The official position of Trusted Device

A Device can:

```text
Registered
```

But not necessarily:

# Trusted for remote control.

It is recommended to distinguish:

```text
Registered

Trusted

Restricted

Revoked
```

---

# 63. Device Presence ≠ Device Trust

Stage 21 already has:

```text
Online
Offline
```

Here it only explains:

# Presence.

a:

```text
Revoked Device
```

Even online:

# Nor can I send Remote Command.

# 64. Remote Permission is a separate ability

For example:

```text
Local:
Agent may edit ArcNotes

Remote:

```

Can be independently restricted.

Not because Local Agent is allowed:

# 65. Remote Origin is Risk Modifier

Same Capability:

```text
Delete 5 notes
```

Operate in front of local users,

and:

> User initiates remotely via the Web in another country

The risks vary.

So Remote can trigger:

# Higher Approval requirements.

---

# 66. Remote Session must be revocable

User:

```text
Revoke device
```

Later:

```text
new remote invocations
```

Immediate rejection.

---

Existing tasks:

According to the security policy:

```text
Continue

Pause

Stop at safe point
```

---

High-risk Remote Task:

# Default pause/safe termination is more reasonable.

# 67. Cloud Remote Channel itself does not carry permanent business permissions

It's just:

# Transported authenticated request.

Finally:

# Desktop reauthorization.

# 68. The formal definition of Secret

# **Secret = Sensitive credentials that are not allowed to be spread as ordinary business data, Settings, Task Content or AI Context.**

---

At least classify:

```text
Personal Provider Secret

OAuth Credential

Connector Credential

Workspace Managed Secret

Device Identity Secret

Extension Credential

Ephemeral Session Secret
```

---

# 69. SecretRef is the only common business reference method

Ordinary Domain/Settings only save:

```text
SecretRef
```

Never save:

```text
sk-xxxx
```

Such value.

---

# 70. SecretRef ≠ Secret Value

It only means:

> Which Secret to use.

# 71. The most important Secret permissions must be divided into

# **Use ≠ Reveal**

This must be frozen.

For example Agent:

```text
Use OpenAI Key
```

But:

```text
Reveal Key
```

Must:

# Prohibited.

# 72. Most businesses always only need Use Without Reveal

For example:

```text
Call GitHub API

Refresh OAuth
```

Neither requires:

> Agent sees the Token string.

# 73. AI Model should never see Secret plain text

Regardless of:

```text
System prompt

Tool input generated by model

Conversation

Task trace

Artifact
```

Neither can appear.

---

# 74. Secret must not be entered either

```text
Deep Link

Clipboard by default

Logs

Audit message

Crash report

Search Index

Embedding

Package Manifest

Export
```

# 75. Product Semantics of Secret Broker

Executor that really needs Secret:

```text
Capability Invocation
↓
Secret authorization
↓
Secret Broker
↓
Use
```

The business layer takes:

# SecretRef.

# 76. Secret strategy of Out-of-process Extension

Default priority:

# **Brokered Use**

For example, the Host proxy is completed:

```text
authenticated request
```

Or generate:

# short-lived scoped credential.

Try not to put long-term Secret:

# 77. Some Integration do require original Credential

For example, a third-party Protocol Client can only send requests by itself.

At this time:

```text
Secret Use By Extension
```

> "This extension will receive credential X."


# 78. Extension can only obtain the Secret it has been granted.

Cannot:

---

Even if the user installs:


```text
OpenAI API key
```

exists.

# 79. Workspace Secret and Personal Secret are not automatically interchangeable

For example:

```text
Company GitHub credential
```

Cannot be called by Personal Workspace Task.

---

Realm/Workspace isolation:

# Hard borders.

---

# 80. Secret Rotation does not change the business configuration identity

For example:

```text
SecretRef = github-work
```

Credential rotation behind.

Connector configuration:

# No need to change everything.

# 81. Secret was revoked

Use it for:

```text
Automation
Connector
Agent Profile
```

Not deleted.

Instead:

# Needs Attention.

# 82. Data Read Permission ≠ Data Egress Permission

This is one of the most important security principles in the Agent era.

For example, Agent has the right to:

```text
Read ArcNotes Document X
```

does not mean:

> The full text of X can be sent to any MCP Server.

Officially introduced:

# **Data Egress Boundary**

---

# 83. Any operation that sends data across Trust Boundary must be authorized separately

For example:

```text
Local → Managed AI

Local → External AI Provider

Local → MCP Server

Local → External Agent

Workspace → Public Internet

Workspace A → External SaaS
```

---

Need to meet:

```text
Source read permission
+
Egress permission
+
Destination permission
+
Knowledge/AI policy
```

# 84. Stage 23 AI Retrieval Policy is not a replacement for Permission

For example Document:

```text
AI Retrieval Allowed = Yes
```

Just explain:

# 85. Managed AI and BYOK External AI can have different Egress Rules

# 86. Egress must know Destination Identity

```text
to OpenAI Provider connection X
for this task.
```

# 87. The same applies to third-party Extension Network Permission

Manifest at least states:

```text
No Network

Declared Destinations

General Network Access
```

Among them:

# General Network Access

# 88. Package cannot circumvent Network Permission indirectly through Backend.

If Extension:

```text
sends data to publisher's API
```

This is it:

Must be declared.

---

# 89. MCP Security Model

MCP Server is not trustworthy just because it "uses the MCP protocol".

It is still:

# External Integration Principal / Trust Boundary.

---

Which:

```text
Tool descriptions

Resource text

Prompt text
```

All from:

# External Source.

# 90. MCP Tool Description cannot obtain Instruction Authority

This is the key rule to prevent prompt injection.

For example, MCP returns:

```text
Permission Scope

System Rules
```

# 91. Retrieved Knowledge Content is also not Trusted Instruction

Agent Runtime must know:

```text
Platform Security Instruction

Direct User Instruction

Approved Skill / Workflow Instruction

Tool / Integration Metadata

Retrieved Content

External Web Content
```

The sources are different.

---

# 93. Instruction Authority cannot just look at the text content

Even if the Retrieved Document writes:

```text
SYSTEM OVERRIDE
```

# Retrieved Content.

---

# 94. Skill's Instruction Trust

Stage 24 Skill by users:

```text
Install / Enable / Assign
```

It can then become:

# Agent Guidance.

But still below:

```text
Platform Security Invariants

Workspace Security Policy

User current explicit instruction
```

> Grant permissions, reveal secrets, or close Approvals.

# 95. Community Workflow is the same

Workflow can decide:

# 96. Connector Content must prevent Data-to-Instruction Confusion

For example GitHub Issue:


# 97. The Delegation of External Agent must be Capability Lease

Formal definition:

# **Capability Lease = A set of capabilities temporarily granted to the External Executor within a specific Task, Period, and Scope.**

At least bind:

```text
Task / Run

External Agent identity

Capabilities

Resource Scope

Data Egress Constraints

Expiry

Secret access if any
```

# 98. The Lease automatically expires after the Task ends

# 99. External Agent can no longer be delegated beyond the capabilities of the Lease.

If it's inside a Delegate:

Principles:

# 100. Capability Lease is also suitable for Extension temporary high-privilege calls.

```text
Read only
```

```text
write selected resource
```

can generate:

# 101. Package Trust must be separated from all other Trusts

# 179. Security Decision Pipeline finally frozen

A real Capability Invocation must be experienced at least once:

```text
1. Binary / capability exists

2. Stage25 product policy allows feature

3. Actor identity is valid

4. Realm / Workspace scope valid

5. Software / package trust is eligible

6. Capability permission exists

7. Resource authorization succeeds

8. Secret / data-egress requirements succeed

9. Effective risk is calculated

10. Approval / Step-up / local-presence requirement satisfied

11. Owner performs final validation

12. Invocation executes

13. Result / effect certainty recorded

14. Relevant audit event written
```

Note:

# Entitlement also exists in the real product Gate.

But it keeps Stage 4 independent Decision.

Permission must not be deposited.

2. Engineering Agent is started by Ryan.

4. Allowed.

6. Agent tries Finance.
7. Refuse.

# 201. Automation permission scenario

9. Ryan creates Weekly Report Automation.
10. Run As Ryan.
11. Ryan currently has ArcScope Read.
12. Automation is normal.
13. Later Ryan lost ArcScope permissions.
14. Trigger re-authorizes next time.
15. Automation enters Needs Attention.
16. Do not continue to use the old permissions.

# 202. Service Principal scene

17. Enterprises need unattended Nightly Report.
18. Create Workspace Service Principal.
19. EXPRESSLY GRANTED:

    * Read Project X;
    * Create report in Notebook Y.
20. Automation Run As This Principal.
21. Ryan resigned.
22. Automation can still run.
23. Audit clearly shows the Service Principal instead of pretending that Ryan is still operating.

# 203. Approval Revision scene

24. Agent plans to modify Document Revision 42.
25. User Approve.
26. Users themselves continue editing to Revision 47.
27. Agent detects Revision changes before execution.
28. Original Approval Invalidated.
29. Regenerate Preview.
30. Need to Approve again.

31. `DeleteDocument` The baseline is higher.
32. Delete 1 recoverable Draft.
33. Ordinary Confirm.
34. Delete 5000 Workspace Documents.
35. Effective Risk increased to R4.
36. Force explicit Approval/Admin/Step-up.
37. Grants with "small deletions" cannot be reused.

# 205. Agent Editor

38. Agent needs to modify 120 Clips of ArcSlate.
39. Generate Impact Preview.
40. Create Checkpoint.
41. The user approves the entire explicit batch.
42. Execute.

# 206. Secret Use

45. ArcChat uses user OpenAI BYOK.
46. Agent only holds SecretRef.
47. Provider Client obtains the Secret to make a request.
48. Model Prompt does not contain Key.
49. Task Trace does not contain Key.
50. Audit only records that SecretRef is used.

# 207. Secret Reveal

51. Extension request displays OpenAI Key plain text.
52. `Use` Permission cannot be satisfied.
53. Requires separate `Reveal` high-risk capabilities.
54. Step-up/Local Presence is triggered according to rules.
55. Most extension requests of this type should be denied by default.

# 208. Extension Credential

56. GitHub Extension must use Credential directly.
57. Manifest declares Secret access.

59. Extension only obtains this Secret.
60. Other Secrets cannot be enumerated.
61. Audit record usage.

# 209. Data Egress

62. Agent can read ArcNotes Document X.
63. Agent wants to send it to MCP Server.
64. Read Permission exists.
65. Egress Permission does not exist.
66. The call was blocked.
67. The user explicitly approves this Task to send selected content to this MCP.
68. Task-scoped Egress Grant is generated.
69. Other Documents still cannot be sent.

# 210. Managed AI Policy and Permission

70. Document allows AI Retrieval.
71. User has Read Permission.
72. Workspace prohibits External BYOK.
73. Managed AI allows.
74. Managed AI paths are available.
75. External BYOK path denied.
76. Knowledge Policy and Authorization both work correctly.

# 211. Remote Approval

77. Desktop Agent is required to create a normal ArcNotes Report.
78. Users receive Approval on Mobile.
79. Mobile is Authenticated/Trusted.
80. Approval is bound to a specific Task/Resource.
81. User Approve.
82. Desktop execution.

# 212. Local Presence

83. Remote Task requests Reveal local Secret.
84. Mobile users Approve.
85. Capability statementRequiresLocalPresence.
86. Desktop is still waiting for local confirmation.
87. Mobile cannot be replaced.

# 213. Device Revocation

88. Laptop was stolen.
89. User Revoke in Security Center.
90. New Remote Requests are rejected immediately.

92. Device cannot continue even if it is Online.

# 214. MCP Prompt Injection

93. MCP Resource includes:

94. Retrieval marks it as External Content.
95. Agent cannot promote it to Security Instruction.
96. Secret will not be revealed.
97. Content can still be processed as ordinary Evidence.

# 215. GitHub Issue Injection

98. The Issue body requires the Agent to upload Workspace documents.
99. Issue Content does not possess Instruction Authority.
100. The Agent only executes the user's Task target and has authorized capabilities.
101. Egress rules continue to take effect.

# 216. MCP Tool Expansion

102. MCP only had Search yesterday.
103. Delete is added today.
104. There is no Delete Grant for Existing connection.
105. Agent cannot be called automatically.
106. User/administrator re-Review.

# 217. Package Update

107. Extension 1.0 Read only.
108. 2.0 adds Write + Network.
109. Auto Update is turned on.

111. Update awaits user confirmation.
112. Rights cannot be expanded silently.

# 218. Revoked Extension

113. Community Extension is Revoked.
114. All new Invocations are blocked.
115. Background process stopped.
116. ArcNotes/ArcSlate user data is retained.
117. Missing extension state is reserved.
118. Secure Audit records.

# 219. Developer Mode

119. User enables Developer Mode.
120. Install Unsigned Extension.
121. The UI continues to identify the Development Trust.

123. WorkspacePolicy is still in effect.

# 220. External Agent Lease

125. Coding Agent Task requires:
     - repo read;
     - create branch;
     - run tests.
126. ArcChat creates Task-scopedCapability Lease.

128. It tries to read ArcNotes.
129. rejected.

# 221. Cross-Workspace

132. Agent reads the Document in Workspace A.
133. Want to create Workspace B Document and copy the content.
134. Even if Human has permissions on both sides.
135. Ordinary Read/Create Permission is insufficient.
136. Cross-Workspace Transfer must be explicit.
137. Generate independent Approval/Audit.
138. Silent mixing of Realm data is not allowed.

# 222. Audit

139. User asked:
     > "Which Agent changed this Document yesterday?"
140. Audit can display:
     - Human Actor;
     - Agent;

     - ArcChat caller;
     - ArcNotes executor;
     - Capability;
     - Revision;
     - Approval.
141. No need to parse Debug Logs.

# 223. Permission Revocation

142. Agent has Notebook Write.
143. User revoked.
144. New Invocation fails immediately.
145. Documents that have been successfully written will not be rolled back.
146. If you need to cancel the result, use Undo/Compensation.
147. The concept of safety is not confused.

# 224. Policy vs Permission

148. Stage 25 Policy allows Remote Agent.

150. Eventually banned.

151. The UI displays the Permission reason.

152. User has Remote Permission.

154. Eventually banned.

155. The UI displays the Managed Policy reason.

The two sources of Decision are clear.

# 225. Final security system

After Stage 26, the security relationship of ArcForges officially becomes:

```text
                    HUMAN / SERVICE PRINCIPAL
                              │
                         Delegates to
                              │
                              ▼
                 Agent / Automation / App
                              │
                              ▼
                         ACTOR CHAIN
                              │
                              ▼
                     Capability Request
                              │
          ┌───────────────────┼────────────────────┐
          ▼                   ▼                    ▼
     Product Policy      Package Trust       Entitlement
       Stage 25             eligibility          Stage 4
          │                   │                    │
          └───────────────────┼────────────────────┘
                              ▼
                    Capability Permission
                              │
                              ▼
                     Resource Authorization
                              │
                   ┌──────────┴──────────┐
                   ▼                     ▼
              Secret Access         Data Egress
                   │                     │
                   └──────────┬──────────┘
                              ▼
                       Effective Risk
                              │
                ┌─────────────┼──────────────┐
                ▼             ▼              ▼
            Approval       Step-up      Local Presence
                │             │              │
                └─────────────┼──────────────┘
                              ▼
                     OWNER FINAL CHECK
                              │
                              ▼
                         Invocation
                              │
                              ▼
                     Effect / Resource
                              │
                              ▼
                           Audit
```

# Stage 26 finalized

From now on, ArcForges does not exist:

> "Agent permissions", "plug-in permissions", "Remote permissions", "MCP permissions", and "Automation permissions" are developed independently.

They are all built on the same set:

# **Actor → Delegation → Capability → Resource → Risk → Approval → Audit**

above semantics.

---

## Actor

Human, Agent, Automation, and Service are clearly separated.

Agent always:

# Executed on behalf of a Principal.

Will not become a super user with unlimited permissions.

---

## Automation

Normally:

# Run As Creator.

Only use it for truly unattended enterprise tasks:

# Explicit Workspace Service Principal.

The creator's past administrator privileges are not permanently inherited.

---

## Permission

Officially becomes:

# **Capability + Resource Scope + Constraints + Lifetime**

instead of:

```text
CanUseApp = true
```

---

## Approval

Approval only:

# A specific Action Snapshot.

and bind:

```text
Task
Capability
Resource
Revision
Effect
Expiry
```

It will not become a vague permanent authorization.

---

## Risk

Officially unified as:

```text
R0
R1
R2
R3
R4
```

But in the end Risk consists of:

```text
Capability baseline
+
Target
+
Scale
+
Sensitivity
+
External egress
+
Secret use
+
Remote
+
Automation
+
Third-party execution
```

Decide together.

---

## Remote

Remote Device:

# Presence is not equal to Trust.

Remote Approval:

# Not equal to Local Presence.

Mobile/Web cannot be the universal remote administrator of local professional apps.

---

## Secret

ArcForges officially implements:

# **Use Secret ≠ Reveal Secret**

Business systems only propagate:

```text
SecretRef
```

AI, Task Trace, Audit, Deep Link, Artifact, Clipboard, and Search cannot leak secrets.

---

## Data Egress

Officially a first-class security perimeter:

> **Being able to read data does not mean that it can send data to external systems.**

Therefore:

```text
Read Permission
+
Destination Egress Permission
```

Both are indispensable.

This pair:

```text
Managed AI
BYOK
MCP
External Agent
Extension
Connector
```

All unified.

---

## Trust

No more creating a ridiculous universal Trust integer.

Formal distinction:

```text
Package Trust

Publisher Trust

Device Trust

Software Identity Trust

Instruction Provenance
```

Because:

# **Trust is typed.**

---

Especially:

> **The text in MCP, Web, GitHub Issue, and ArcNotes documents is Content. It does not obtain Instruction Authority just because "IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS" is written.**

This became the long-term basis for ArcForges' Prompt Injection protection.

---

## Third-party ecosystem

Stage 24:

```text
Skill
Workflow
MCP
Connector
External Agent
Extension
Third-party App
```

All enter the same Security Model.

And:

> **Skill will not grant permission.**

> **Workflow will not grant permission.**

> **MCP protocol does not mean trustworthy.**

> **External Agent only takes Task-scoped Capability Lease.**

> **Extension's default Out-of-process still does not mean automatically safe.**

> **Package signature proves the source, but does not prove the absence of malicious intent.**

> **Added Permission always requires re-Consent.**

---

## Audit

Ultimately safe behavior can answer:

> **Who, on behalf of whom, through which App/Agent/Extension, with what Capability, to which Resource, under what Permission and Approval, what was done, and what was the result.**

But Audit:

# It does not become Debug Log, it does not become Telemetry, it does not become another Domain History database.

---

After achieving this level, even if ArcForges increases in the future:

```text
dozens Agent
hundreds MCP Tool
third party Extension
Enterprise Automation
Remote Desktop Control
More Connector
external Agent Runtime
fifth major Arc App
```

There is no need to reinvent a security system.

All of them can only be accessed if they are already frozen:

# **Principal / Actor Chain / Capability Permission / Resource Authorization / Risk / Approval / Trust / Secret / Egress / Audit**

This set of safety language.

**Stage 26 At this point, ArcForges' Product Security / Permission / Trust Model is officially closed.**

# Stage 27: Product Quality & Compatibility Contract

What needs to be solved at this stage is:

> **The functions of ArcForges can continue to be increased, but "easy to use, stable, fast, recoverable, upgradable, accessible, and cross-platform run" cannot drift as implementers and versions change.**

The previous stages 13 to 26 have frozen product boundaries, data, tasks, cross-app, extensions, security and dynamic policies.

Stage 27 Now add a real layer to these things:

# **Quality Constitution**

It is not about "testing a bit more before launch"; it turns quality itself into **a versioned, machine-verifiable, release-blocking product contract**.

The existing technical outline has given several very important starting points: local UI input to the visible state P95 target `<50ms`, UI main thread single work as much as possible `<8ms`, lightweight native RPC P95 `<10–20ms`, submitted commands must be able to be recovered after a process crash; at the same time, the desktop requires true Native AOT publish, rather than just running ordinary JIT tests. Stage 27 officially elevates these from "technical targets" to quality contracts for the entire product range.

---

# 1. Freeze the most important principles first

From now on:

# **Quality Requirement ≠ Engineering Suggestion**

For example:

```text
ArcNotes startup P95 <= budget
```

Not:

> "There will be time to optimize."

Instead:

# Release Gate.

---

Likewise:

```text
Supported old project must migrate successfully
```

Not:

> "It should be fine in most cases."

Instead:

# Compatibility Contract.

---

# 2. Each product must have a Versioned Quality Contract

Officially established:

# **Product Quality Contract**

Currently covers at least:

```text
ArcChat Desktop
ArcNotes
ArcScope
ArcSlate

ArcChat Mobile
ArcChat Web
```

and the quality of Cloud interactions as directly perceived by users.

Each Product Quality Contract contains at least:

```text
Performance Budget

Memory Budget

Startup Budget

Background Resource Budget

Responsiveness Budget

Scale / Soak Scenarios

Accessibility Contract

Localization Contract

Units / Time / Number Contract

AOT Contract

Supported Platform Matrix

Compatibility Matrix

Migration Matrix

Recovery Contract

Diagnostics Contract

Test Matrix
```

---

# 3. Quality Contract must be placed in the repository and version controlled

Cannot just exist:

```text
Notion
Wiki
in someone's mind
```

At least logically:

```text
quality/
  arcchat/
  arcnotes/
  arcscope/
  arcslate/
  mobile/
  web/
  compatibility/
```

Among them, budgets that can be judged by machines should include:

# Machine-readable representation.

---

In this way, CI can directly determine:

```text
Baseline
Current
Regression
Hard Ceiling
```

Instead of relying on people to look at Benchmark screenshots.

---

# 4. It is forbidden to secretly increase the quality threshold in ordinary PR.

For example the test fails:

```text
Startup budget:
2.0s
```

Developers cannot directly:

```text
→ 4.0s
```

Then the test came back green.

---

Quality Budget changes must go:

# **Quality ADR / Explicit Quality Review**

At least state:

```text
why change

User impact

Measurement data

alternative

Is it permanent?

recovery plan
```

---

# 5. Official adoption of two-tier performance thresholds

Each key metric exists at the same time:

## Absolute Budget

The product regardless of its history:

# This hard upper limit cannot be exceeded.

---

## Regression Budget

Even if the hard cap has not been reached yet:

# It cannot continue to get worse.

---

For example:

```text
Absolute Startup Ceiling:
2.0s

Previous release:
1.30s

New build:
1.72s
```

Although it has not exceeded 2 seconds,

But already:

```text
+32%
```

Not because:

> "Not more than 2 seconds"

Just let it go.

---

# 6. Default Regression Gate

Formal recommendation to freeze:

For the key P50/P95 in the stable benchmark:

# **A repeatable regression of approximately 10% above the last stable baseline must enter a blocking review.**

Memory:

# A retreat warning line of about 10% is also adopted.

But because Benchmark is noisy:

> Requires repeated sampling and statistical stability rather than failure on a single machine fluctuation.

---

Real Hard Ceiling:

# Unconditional Blocking.

---

# 7. Unify the concept of Reference Hardware

Performance Contract cannot say:

> "It's fast on my 4090 computer."

Must define:

# **Reference Hardware Class**

Rather than binding a specific CPU model.

Desktop V1 Reference Class at least:

```text
Supported 64-bit architecture

8+ logical CPU cores

16 GB RAM

NVMe-class SSD

supported GPU where product requires it

release build

no debugger

production AOT artifact
```

---

Also maintain:

# Lower-bound Supported Hardware Class

Used to discover:

> Is it completely unavailable on ordinary machines?

---

# 8. Benchmark must test real released products

It is forbidden to test only:

```text
dotnet run
Debug
JIT
```

Then treat the results as Native AOT product performance.

Desktop benchmark:

# Production Native AOT package.

Mobile:

# Release AOT package.

Web:

# Production WASM build.

---

# 9. Desktop global interaction quality bottom line

Stage 27 officially freezes the following common goals.

| Metric                           |      V1 Quality Contract |
| -------------------------------- | -----------------------: |
| **Input → visible feedback P95** |              **≤ 50 ms** |
| UI thread single synchronization work target               |               **< 8 ms** |
| High frequency path continuous UI thread block           | **Must not last more than one frame budget** |
| Commonly used Command to start feedback P95              |             **≤ 100 ms** |
| Operation expected >200 ms                     |                 Clear feedback must appear |
| Operation expected >1 s                        |   Progress/activity status should be displayed |
| working long hours                            |      Must enter Activity/Task semantics |
| UI confirmation after Cancel request                   | Enter `Canceling...` immediately, cannot pretend to have canceled |

This is consistent with the `<50ms` input feedback and `<8ms` UI main thread work budget that the existing master outline already has.

---

# 10. Do not use animation to cover up real slowness

For example, after clicking the button:

```text
300ms
```

do nothing,

Then play a beautiful animation:

> Not counting responsiveness.

Real requirements:

# The user knows immediately that the operation has been accepted.

---

# 11. Synchronous blocking for more than 50ms is a serious problem

In particular:

```text
DB query

filesystem enumeration

network

RPC

media decode

AI request

search rebuild
```

Must not be executed synchronously on the UI thread.

---

Can be stably reproduced in the core path:

```text
>50ms UI freeze
```

Should:

# Release Blocking.

---

# 12. Start-up quality is officially divided into three time points

Cannot have just one blur:

# "Startup Time".

Formal distinction:

```text
Process Start

First Window Visible

First Usable Workspace
```

---

Real product indicators:

# **Time To Usable**

Users can already do core work.

---

# 13. Desktop V1 Startup Budget

In Reference Hardware, Release Native AOT, and normal local state:

| Product      | Cold Process → Usable Workspace P95 |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------: |
| **ArcChat**  |                         **≤ 2.0 s** |
| **ArcNotes** |                         **≤ 2.0 s** |
| **ArcScope** |                         **≤ 2.5 s** |
| **ArcSlate** |                         **≤ 3.0 s** |

ArcScope/ArcSlate can:

> The background continues to scan the device, index Media, and load Derived Cache.

But:

# You cannot block the Workspace from being available for the first time for these tasks.

---

# 14. Startup cannot wait for Cloud

This is the quality expression of Stage 13 Local-first.

Start:

```text
Open local store
↓
show local workspace
↓
refresh Cloud / Policy / Sync asynchronously
```

Prohibited:

```text
Wait for account
Wait for cloud
Wait for feature policy
Wait for model catalog
↓
finally open app
```

---

# 15. Startup cannot require ArcChat to be online

ArcNotes / ArcScope / ArcSlate:

# The core Workspace is started first.

Hub connection:

# Background recovery.

---

# 16. Desktop Base Memory Budget

In order to prevent the number from completely inflating with development, the **Initial Release Ceiling** is officially set.

Measurement conditions:

```text
Release AOT
main workspace open
no large project loaded
60s quiescent
derived transient startup work finished
```

Includes:

# Managed + relevant native resident memory.

Initial budget:

| Product                 | Quiescent Base Memory Ceiling |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------: |
| **ArcChat + local Hub** |                 **≤ 250 MiB** |
| **ArcNotes**            |                 **≤ 250 MiB** |
| **ArcScope**            |                 **≤ 320 MiB** |
| **ArcSlate**            |                 **≤ 450 MiB** |

This is not a "marketing promise".

Instead:

# Initial project Release Budget.

If the first real Vertical Slice proves that a certain budget is unreasonable, it can be adjusted through Quality ADR; thereafter drifting without evidence is prohibited.

---

# 17. You cannot cheat through "Cache is not counted as Memory"

All of the following are included:

```text
Managed heap

Native heap

Pinned buffers

Media buffers

RPC buffers

Image buffers

Index working memory
```

GPU Memory is measured separately,

But:

# It cannot be ignored just because it is not in the managed heap.

The existing general outline also clearly requires that native memory, LOH, pinned objects, and SignalR/HTTP/RPC buffers all enter capacity testing.

---

# 18. Memory Pressure must be surrenderable

Especially ArcSlate:

```text
thumbnail cache
render cache
frame cache
waveform
proxy working data
```

ArcScope:

```text
decoded data
analysis cache
visualization buffers
```

Must:

# Have budget + eviction.

---

Memory Pressure appears on the OS:

Priority release:

# Derived / Rebuildable memory.

Cannot:

> In order to protect the Cache, the entire App is killed by the OS.

---

# 19. Leak/Soak Contract

"Starting with small memory" means nothing at all.

All Desktop Apps must run:

# Long-running Soak Test.

---

Minimum test:

```text
8 hour application soak
```

and execute it repeatedly:

```text
Open

Work

Close resource

GC / settle naturally

Repeat
```

---

After returning to the same Quiescent state:

```text
retained baseline growth <= 10%
```

and:

# Handle/Native Resource/Thread/Subscription that continues to grow monotonically is not allowed.

---

Anything unexplainable:

```text
>50 MiB persistent growth
```

An investigation must be entered.

---

# 20. Product Special Soak

## ArcChat

At least:

```text
Long conversation

Agent tasks

MCP reconnect

App registrations

Cloud reconnect
```

Run repeatedly.

---

## ArcNotes

At least:

```text
Open/close hundreds of documents

Search

edit

history

attachments
```

---

## ArcScope

Must:

# Continuous Capture/visualization test for more than 8 hours.

Monitor:

```text
Memory

CPU

Buffer growth

Dropped data

File growth

UI responsiveness
```

---

## ArcSlate

Must have:

```text
long playback

seek loop

effect changes

proxy

render

project open/close
```

Soak.

---

# 21. Background Resource Contract

Local-first professional apps are not allowed to be:

# Permanent CPU burning tool.

---

When there is no active work:

### ArcChat Background / Hub

Average:

# ≤ 0.5% of one logical core

as an initial budget.

---

### ArcNotes / ArcScope / ArcSlate

None is executing:

```text
capture
render
index
sync
```

Backstage Quiescent:

# Should be close to zero, with an initial target of ≤0.2% of a logical core average.

---

# 22. Busy Polling is prohibited

Cannot:

```text
while (true)
{
    CheckSomething();
    Thread.Sleep(50);
}
```

Long polling.

Priority:

```text
event
wait handle
async notification
bounded timer
```

---

Background Work must have:

```text
Reason

Owner

Lifetime

Cancellation

Resource budget
```

---

# 23. The backend network is also controlled

Idle status:

> Pointless persistent HTTP polling is not allowed.

Realtime:

# SignalR/explicit heartbeat.

Sync:

# event/outbox-driven + bounded retry.

---

# 24. Task resource competition must have priority

ArcSlate generates Proxy in the background:

Not allowed:

# Timeline drag stuck.

ArcScope background Index:

Not allowed:

# Capture loses data.

ArcNotes Semantic Index:

Not allowed:

# Typing lags.

Formal priority:

```text
Real-time / User Interaction
>
Durability
>
Active User Task
>
Background Sync
>
Derived Index / Cache Build
```

# 25. The performance budget must be based on "user work" rather than only measuring function benchmarks.

Two types of testing are required:

## Micro Benchmark

For example:

```text
serialize
RPC
index lookup
timeline operation
```

---

## Product Scenario Benchmark

For example:

```text
Open 20k-document library
Search
Open result
Edit
Save
```

The latter:

# More important.

---

# 26. Establish Scale Corpus

Formally establish product-level Reference Scale data.

It is not the product Maximum,

Instead:

# The scale that each Release must support.

V1 recommended minimum test file:

| Product  | Reference Scale Corpus                                                  |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ArcChat  | 100k messages + thousands of Tasks/Artifacts                            |
| ArcNotes | 50k documents / ~1M blocks + large attachment corpus                    |
| ArcScope | 8h continuous capture + multi-GB/100GB-class raw dataset                |
| ArcSlate | 10k media assets + multi-hour project + several thousand timeline items |

This does not mean:

> ArcNotes can only have a maximum of 50k.

# 27. Separate Search Quality and Performance

For example Search:

```text
20ms
```

But the result is completely wrong:

```text
Latency

Recall

Ranking Quality

Freshness

Citation Correctness
```

test.

# 28. Accessibility becomes Release Contract

Official goal:

# **All major user workflows reach the WCAG 2.2 AA semantic level and correctly connect to the target platform Accessibility APIs.**

This does not mean that Desktop UI must mechanically follow the rules of web pages.

Instead, we use AA-level principles as a common bottom line.

---

# 29. Keyboard Accessibility

All core workflows must be able to:

# Do not rely on Mouse to complete.

For example ArcNotes:

```text
Navigate

Open

Edit

Search

Save

Properties
```

---

Professional Direct Manipulation exists for ArcSlate/ArcScope,

But at least:

```text
All key operations
```

Both must exist:

# Command / keyboard-accessible semantic path.

---

Not a requirement:

> Every pixel dragged in the Timeline has the exact same keyboard gesture.

Instead it requires:

> Users cannot completely lose core functionality just because they cannot use Mouse.

---

# 30. Focus Contract

It must always be possible to know:

```text
What has keyboard focus
```

and:

# Focus ≠ Selection.

Continue to Stage 14.

---

Prohibited:

```text
invisible focus
focus trapped permanently
focus jumps randomly
```

---

After Modal is closed:

# Restore reasonable source Focus.

# 31. Screen Reader Contract

Key controls must have:

```text
Accessible Name

Role

State

Value

Description where needed
```

---

Cannot:

```text
Button
Name=""
```

Or make Screen Reader read-only:

```text
“button button button”
```

# 32. Icon-only Controls

Must:

# Accessible Name.

Tooltip:

# 33. Color cannot be the only source of information

For example ArcScope:

```text
Red signal
```

You cannot just rely on red to say:

> Error.

Also required:

```text
icon
label
pattern
state
```

in a reasonable manner.

---

ArcSlate Track/Marker color:

# Stage 27 finalized

From this stage on, ArcForges' "quality" is no longer just a vague goal, but is defined by:

# **Budget + Matrix + Fixture + Test + Release Gate**

Mutually defined long-term contracts.

---

## Performance

Unified ownership:

```text
Startup

Time To Usable

Input Latency

Command Responsiveness

Memory

CPU

Background Work

Scale

Soak
```

Budget.

and adopt:

# Absolute Ceiling + Regression Gate.

---

## Desktop basic interaction bottom line

Officially:

```text
Input → visible P95 <= 50ms

UI thread synchronous work target <8ms
```

as a common starting point.

And ArcChat/ArcNotes/ArcScope/ArcSlate all have clear initial budgets for Startup and Base Memory. The performance starting point in the existing technical master plan is therefore no longer just a suggestion, but has entered the formal Product Quality Contract.

## Accessibility

It's not about "fixing the problem later".

From the first edition:

```text
Keyboard

Focus

Screen Reader

High Contrast

Reduced Motion

Text Scaling

No color-only meaning
```

Enter Release Matrix.

## Localization

Formal insistence:

> **Display can be localized, Identifier and Persistent Data cannot be localized.**

and pass:

```text
pseudo-localization
RTL testing
locale-aware formatting
```

Prevents UI and data formatting from being reworked later.

---

## Units

ArcScope and other professional products officially adopt:

# **Typed Quantity / Dimension-safe Unit Model**

Display Unit and Canonical Value are separated.

ArcSlate's Frame/Sample/Timecode continues to use Stage 20's Rational Time system and does not degenerate into `double seconds`.

---

## AOT

Officially becomes:

# Release Contract.

Not:

> "The code should be AOT-friendly".

Every official host must test the real Production Publish path; AOT/trimming warnings are blocked by default, and problems cannot be covered up by large-area Suppression. The existing technical outline has clarified the realistic boundaries of desktop Native AOT and Android Mono AOT as well as the real release testing requirements. Stage 27 has fully incorporated this into the quality gate.

---

## Compatibility

ArcForges no longer has a blur:

# "version compatible".

Instead, make a clear distinction between:

```text
App
Contract
Capability
Format
Schema
Native ABI
Policy
Extension Protocol
Package
```

version.

The four Desktop Apps can still be Independent Released.

But:

# Mixed-version Matrix must actually pass.

---

## Migration

All old Native Formats still supported:

# Must have permanent Golden Fixtures.

Every Release:

```text
read
migrate
validate
write
reopen
```

All tested.

It's not "Migration code can be compiled".

---

## Crash / Recovery

From now on:

# Actively killing processes is a formal testing method.

Wherever the UI has been confirmed:

```text
Saved locally
```

data,

Crash must exist in the future.

This is:

# P0 level quality contract.

---

## Diagnostics

Unified to form:

```text
User Diagnostics

Support Diagnostic Bundle

Developer Diagnostics
```

and defaults to:

# No secrets, no hidden user-content upload.

---

## Cross-platform

"Windows/macOS/Linux supported" no longer means:

> "Theoretically Avalonia supports it".

And means:

# These platforms truly enter Build, AOT, Install, UI, Recovery, Compatibility, Performance and Release Matrix.

ArcScope/ArcSlate must also enter:

# Real Hardware Lab.

---

Ultimately the most important rule is:

> **Any new feature cannot be "traded for development speed" by quietly slowing down startup, increasing memory, breaking AOT, shortening the compatibility window, reducing accessibility, breaking old data migration, or reducing Crash Recovery guarantees.**

When you really need to change the Quality Budget:

# Must be specified, measured, reviewed, versioned.

Cannot drift silently.

That way, however many Agents, Providers, Extensions, professional features, Cloud services, or fifth products ArcForges adds later, **product quality itself is governed by a long-term contract that does not shift as the implementers change.**

**Stage 27 At this point, Performance / Responsiveness / Memory / Accessibility / Localization / Units / AOT / Compatibility / Migration / Contract / Recovery / Diagnostics / Cross-platform Quality Contract are officially closed.**

# stage28

# Stage 28: Support / Feedback / Operator / Trust & Safety Operations

This stage is the last piece of the entire Stage 0~28.

Already solved before:

* What is the product;
* To whom user data belongs;
* How Cloud, Sync, Agent, and Automation operate;
* How to access Extension / MCP / Connector;
* How Permission / Trust / Audit works;
* Quality / Recovery / Diagnostics How to guarantee.

Stage 28 now solves the last real-life problem:

# **After the product is actually launched, how to deal with user problems, data corruption, third-party packages doing evil, service failures, security vulnerabilities, community reports, and copyright complaints?**

This is not a simple matter of adding:

```text
support@arcforges.com
```

It's over.

If this layer is not defined in advance, it will easily appear after commercialization:

```text
Customer service directly logs in to the user account to troubleshoot

OperatorChange the database directly

User reportsBugUpload all logs and chat content

ExtensionIf reported, user files will be deleted remotely

SupportandTrust & SafetyShared universalAdminAccount number

maliciousPackageRemoved from the shelves, However, the installed version can continue to execute

CopyrightComplaints will directly delete the user's local works.

Security Advisory, Incident, Bug, Abuse ReportMix allTicket

Directly overwrite the original damaged files when recovering data
```

These must be banned now.

The general outline of the existing technology has been made clear: Hub is only responsible for platform coordination, permissions, approval and auditing, and does not take over the business status of professional products; Cloud itself already has independent platform modules such as Audit; remote desktop capabilities must be authorized, approved and revoked by the device visible to the user. Stage 28 continues this ownership model rather than creating a "super backend" that bypasses all product boundaries.

---

# 1. The highest principle of Stage 28

Final freeze:

# **Support is assistance, not impersonation.**

# **Operator is an Actor, not the User.**

# **Recovery repairs data through product semantics, not arbitrary database mutation.**

# **Trust & Safety enforcement acts on distribution/access surfaces, not silently on users' local canonical data.**

# **Security emergency powers remain scoped, attributable and auditable.**

---

# 2. First, completely separate all operating objects.

In the future, ArcForges will have at least the following completely different concepts:

| object                     | What to solve                                  |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| **Feedback**           | User feedback on the product                              |
| **Bug Report**         | User believes there is a software defect                           |
| **Feature Request**    | Users put forward product capability requirements                            |
| **Support Case**       | User needs personal help                              |
| **Engineering Defect** | Software defects that engineering teams actually track                         |
| **Known Issue**        | Confirmed issues that require public clarification to users                      |
| **Incident**           | A service-level failure that is currently occurring                          |
| **Recovery Case**      | Dedicated support process for data recovery efforts                         |
| **Community Report**   | Reports on Package, Publisher, Public Content, etc. |
| **Security Report**    | Report security vulnerabilities privately                              |
| **Enforcement Action** | Restriction/removal/withdrawal decisions made by the platform                       |
| **Appeal**             | Review request for Enforcement                     |
| **Security Advisory**  | Public security advisory for users/admins                       |

These objects:

# They cannot all be called "Ticket".

---

# 3. Feedback and Support Case must be separated

User said:

> "ArcSlate would be better off adding a Timeline tool."

This is:

# Feature Feedback.

Support personnel are not necessarily required to handle it.

---

User said:

> "ArcSlate Project cannot be opened today. I have important projects."

This is:

# Private Support Case.

---

User said:

> "I found this operation to bypass the Workspace Permission."

This is:

# Security Report.

---

User said:

> "This Extension in the Catalog is suspected of stealing API Key."

This is:

# Community / Security Package Report.

The entrance can be unified,

But:

# Backend workflows should never be lumped into one category.

---

# 4. The "Report a Problem" entrance in the product is officially unified

The four Desktop Apps and ArcChat Mobile/Web should be unified:

# **Report a Problem**

entrance.

At least you have the option of:

```text
Report a Bug

Request a Feature

Send Product Feedback

Get Private Support

Report an Extension / Package

Report a Security Issue
```

---

# 5. Security Issue must be clearly directed to Private Channel

Users cannot be allowed to default to:

```text

```

Report:

> A remote execution vulnerability that has not yet been patched.

---

Open source projects can of course have Public GitHub Issues.

But the product must clearly:

```text
OrdinaryBug
→ can be discussed openly

Potential Security Vulnerability
→ Private Security Report
```

---

# 6. In-app Bug Report defaults to Private

Because common bugs may include:

```text

Task IDs

Error metadata
```

---

Users can:

# Actively select "Create public issue".

But users must be clearly told:

> What information will be made public.

User clicks:

```text
Basic error code

User description
```

Diagnostic Bundle:

# Explicit opt-in.

---

Screenshot:

# Explicit opt-in.

---

Current Document / Conversation:

# Explicit opt-in.

---

Prompt / Agent Context:

# Explicit opt-in.

Cannot:

> "For convenience and support" will upload all the user's stuff together by default.

should not produce:

Correct:

instead of:

```text
version
```

proceed on.

# 74. Formal Enforcement Ladder

From mild to severe it can include:

```text
No Action

Warning

Catalog Delisting

Block New Install

Quarantine Version

Revoke Package Version

Suspend Package

Suspend Publisher Publishing

Restrict Account / Cloud Service
```

Different Targets use different subsets.

# 75. Delist ≠ Revoke

## Delist

Package no longer:

# Catalog Discovery.

Already installed:

> Normal operation unless otherwise required for safety reasons.

---

## Revoke

Package Version:

# It was judged that execution should not continue.

Runtime:

```text
No new invocations
No background restart
```

Continue to Stage 24/26.

---

# 76. Yank ≠ Moderation Removal

Stage 24:

# Yank

Usually the Publisher itself:

> Stop new installations of a version.

# Enforcement Removal

is a platform based on:

```text
security
abuse
policy
```

operational decisions made.

Audit and UI must be different for both.

```text
Report / Detection
↓
Triage
↓
Reproduce / Analyze
↓
Determine affected versions
↓

↓
Enforcement
↓

↓

↓
Fixed version review
↓
```

```text
credential stealer
```

Running.

instead of:

if:

# Publisher / Package.

# 153. Must pass: Ordinary Bug Report

1. An error occurred in ArcNotes.
2. The user clicks Report a Problem.
3. Fill in the description.
4. By default, only Version/Error metadata is attached.
5. Document text is not uploaded.
6. API Key is not uploaded.
7. Users can choose to attach the Diagnostic Bundle.
8. Generate Private Bug Report.

---

# 154. Must pass: Public GitHub Issue

9. The user explicitly selects Open Public Issue.
10. The system displays the information that will be made public.
11. Private Case Attachment is not automatically attached.
12. Public content is created only after User confirmation.

---

# 155. Must pass: Bug Dedupe

13. 500 users reported the same crash.
14. The Support system forms 500 user reports.
15. Engineering only tracks one main Defect.
16. Each Case can still receive Fix Version notification.

---

# 156. Must pass: Support Privacy

17. The user opens a case.
18. Support can see Product Version and Sync status.
19. User ArcNotes Documents cannot be opened directly.
20. Support requests additional information.
21. The user only shares Document X.
22. Support can only access this Scope.
23. Access becomes invalid after Grant expires.

---

# 157. Must pass: Impersonation prohibited

24. Support Operator wants to reproduce the problem.
25. Operator Console does not exist `Login as User`.
26. Use Support Projection or user-shared snapshot.
27. All Operator Actions record the Operator identity.

---

# 158. Must pass: Recovery

28. ArcNotes local store is damaged.
29. The user first enters Recovery Mode.
30. Self-service recovery failed.
31. Generate Recovery Package.
32. The original damaged files are retained.
33. Support analyzes on copies.
34. Restore a valid Document.
35. Returned as Recovered Copy/Revision.
36. The original data is not silently overwritten.

---

# 159. Must pass: unable to recover

37. The user's External ArcSlate Original has been completely deleted.
38. Never managed.
39. Never Backup.
40. Support clearly states that the original media cannot be restored.
41. No fake "Cloud Restore".

---

# 160. Must pass: Operator Repair

42. Cloud Search Projection is corrupted.
43. Recovery Specialist calls Rebuild Projection Capability.
44. Does not directly execute arbitrary SQL.
45. Canonical ArcNotes data remains unchanged.
46. Operator Audit records.

---

# 161. Must pass: Canonical Recovery

47. Cloud-sideResource does need to be restored.
48. Explicit request by the user.
49. Recovery Capability execution.
50. New Revision/Recovery provenance is generated.
51. The recovery source is visible to the user.
52. Support does not pretend to be a user to modify.

---

# 162. Must pass: Remote Support

53. The user starts a Remote Support Session.
54. The product continues to display Support Connected.
55. Default View-only.
56. The user can only input after clearing Grant control.
57. The user stops at any time.
58. Invalid immediately after the session ends.
59. There is no background permanent Support connection.

# 163. Must pass: Community Report

60. User reports Package v2.3.
61. Report records the exact Version.
62. 100 reports were received.
63. Publisher will not be automatically and permanently blocked.
64. T&S investigates.
65. It is judged that only 2.3 has a problem.
66. Action is only for 2.3.

# 164. Must pass: Confirmed Malware

67. Package v2.3 was confirmed to steal Credential.
68. Emergency Revocation.
69. New Invocation is prohibited.
70. Background process no longer restarts.
71. Catalog blocks new installations.
72. The user receives a Security Warning.
73. Professional data such as ArcNotes/ArcSlate continue to exist.
74. Package status/parameters can still be used for recovery or forensics.

# 165. Must pass: Fixed Package

75. Publisher fixed.
76. Release 2.3.1.

78. The new version has been re-security reviewed.
79. Users upgraded to 2.3.1.
80. 2.3 Continue to maintain Revoked history.

85. Publisher restores Catalog Distribution.

109. Catalog status is restored.

```text
 Known Issue
        │
        ▼
      Release

                       ▼
```

# Stage 28 finalized

From this stage onwards, ArcForges no longer understands "customer service backend" as:

> **An Admin page that can see everything.**

Instead, it is formally formed:

# **Purpose-bound Operator Capabilities**

Each Staff behavior has:

```text
Operator identity
Role
Reason
Case / Incident
Scope
Capability
Result
Audit
```

---

## Support

Officially follows:

# **Support is assistance, not impersonation.**

Users themselves are still users.

Operator always starts with:

# Operator Principal

Execute.

There is no silence:

```text
Login as user
```

---

## Diagnostics

Stage 27 defines content,

Stage 28 freezes operation path:

# **Generate → Review → Explicit Share → Case Attachment**

All logs, chats, and projects will not be automatically uploaded just because the user clicks Bug Report.

---

## Recovery

Officially follows:

# **Preserve Original → Work on Copy → Validate → Produce Recovery Result**

Not passed directly:

```text
SQL UPDATE
```

Modify user Domain.

Canonical Data Recovery:

# Through Owner Application/Recovery Capability.

---

## Operator Console

Officially not:

```text
SQL Console
Shell
User Impersonation Tool
```

Instead:

# Support/Operations/T&S/Security control plane with clear capability boundaries.

It will never become the fifth business state owner.

---

## Trust & Safety

Officially adopted:

```text
Report
≠
Investigation
≠
Enforcement
≠
Appeal
```

The number of reports will not directly equal the penalty.

Serious security incidents can be Contained first.

But:

# All Actions still have Scope, Reason and Audit.

---

## Malicious Package

Officially follows:

# **Minimum necessary range processing.**

Priority:

```text
Affected Version
```

instead of:

> First, block the entire Publisher.

Confirmed malicious version can:

```text
Block New Install
Quarantine
Revoke Runtime
```

But:

> **User Resources owned by professional apps will never be deleted for this reason.**

---

## Copyright / Abuse

Officially used for:

# Distribution / Public / Community Surface.

Not:

> Because there is a problem with Public Share, the user's own local Document is deleted remotely.

Ownership and distribution status are officially separated.

---

## Appeal

The past will not be rewritten.

```text
Old Enforcement
+
New Appeal Decision
```

Together they make history.

---

## Security

Security Report:

# Private.

Security Advisory:

# Public, stable and versioned.

And:

```text
Stage 5 Update
Stage 24 Package Revocation
Stage 25 Kill Switch / Minimum Version
Stage 26 Permission / Session Response
Stage 27 Compatibility / Release Quality
```

Complete closed loop.

---

## Self-host

Officially confirmed:

> **There is no ArcForges official hidden Support Backdoor.**

Official Support cannot see independent Self-host user data,

Unless:

# Unsolicited by user/administrator.

Official Advisory can be subscribed,

But:

# Advisory ≠ Remote Policy Authority.

```text
Recovery
Operator
Incidents

```

---

So after Stage 28, **Stages 29, 30, and 31 should not keep being added mechanically for the sake of "completeness".**

There is no obvious missing product-level/platform-level high-level architecture aspect.

The following work should be formally entered into:

# **Detailed Architecture / Domain Design / Contracts / Storage Schema / APIs / Implementation Plans / ADRs**

Rather than continuing to expand the high-level stage.

Only when a new problem is discovered in the future that truly cannot fall into any of the boundaries of Stage 0 to 28, a high-level Architecture Amendment should be added.

**Stage 28 is officially closed here, which also means that the complete product, platform, data, security, quality and operational architecture of ArcForges Stage 0~28 have completed the first round of overall design closed loop.**
